Heading: Babloo Srivastava hearing: Senior govt officer does a volte face - Indian Express
Content:
The Samajwadi Party on Saturday demanded the arrest of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati and District Magistrate of Pratapgarh Sainthal Pandiyan C for allegedly razing a statue of India's first Home Minister Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel.

"A statue of Sardar Patel was to be unveiled on his birth anniversary on October 31. But the district magistrate ordered that the statue and the platform on which it was built be razed. We want the Centre to arrest the district magistrate and the chief minister," SP chief Mulayam Singh Yadav told reporters.

Yadav alleged that Pandiyan had issued the order at Mayawati's behest. He alleged that though the land on which the statue was built belongs to the gram sabha, the state government has

tried to create an issue out of it. "The process of putting up the statue was started four months ago but nobody had objected then," he said.

SP general secretary Amar Singh, who was also present at the press conference, read out a letter written by Pratapgarh MP Akshay Pratap Singh, in which the latter maintained that the gram sabha had given permission for using the land. Yadav said if his party came to power, "It would jail the district magistrate and Mayawati for this act".

Principal commits suicide

Allahabad: The principal of a prominent school of the city committed suicide by shooting himself with his pistol in the Civil lines area, while the body of a youth was found in Yamuna river.

In the first incidence, the principal of YMCA school Anurag Massih shot at himself late on Friday night. The reason behind the suicide could not be known as Massih's relatives refused to say anything. According to the police, some family problem may have forced the principal to take this extreme step. His body has been sent for postmortem.

In the second incident, the body of one Ravi Nishad, who was reported missing since October 29, was found in the Yamuna. The Kydganj police recovered the body. Nishad was a resident of Meerapur under the Attersuiya police station. Nishad's family members gheraoed the office of the superintendent of police and demanded immediate arrest of his murderers. They also filed an FIR against two persons in this connection. Superintendent of Police Awdhesh Singh Vijeta said a police team was sent to arrest the accused.

Heading: Gorakhpur police defy HC order, do not file FIR against Yogi - Indian Express
Content:
A senior government officer was declared hostile by a court on the request of the CBI prosecutor in a case, in which don Om Prakash Srivastava alias Babloo Srivastava was named as accused.

Vice Chairman (VC) of Rae Bareli Development Authority, Satya Narain Srivastava was a witness in a case lodged against the don and a few others. On Saturday, the case came up before the Special Judge Anti-Corruption in Lucknow, but the VC resiled from his earlier statements made before the CBI during the investigation.

Subsequently, CBI prosecutor K P Singh wrote a letter to the CBI Superintendent of Police, New Delhi, requesting him to take action against Satya Narain. Singh cited a December 2005 directive of the Chief Vigilance Commissioner which would empower them to take action against any government officer, if he or she turned hostile in a court case.

Singh also said, "After Satya Narain turned hostile, I filed an application before the court praying for cross-examination."

The case dates back to 1998, when Satya Narain was posted as Additional District Magistrate (ADM) in Allahabad. Official records state that on December 14, 1998, the then Allahabad District Magistrate Alok Tandon had asked the ADM to conduct a search at the Naini Jail, following the reports of jailed Babloo Srivastava using cell phone in the prison.

Subsequently, Satya Narain and Allahabad Chief Medical Officer K K Srivastava had visited the cell where Babloo and his associate K K Saini were lodged. According to Singh, Satya Narain had told the CBI that he found several objectionable items such as foreign-made track suits, cigarettes and lots of edibles in the cell. Court records also confirm that he had told Tandon over phone that the jail staff seemed to provide favours to the don.

On Saturday, however, the ADM denied making such comments to the CBI, Singh added.

The Naini jail visit in 1998 was prompted by a complaint lodged by one Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava. He had alleged that a few associates of Babloo had taken his cellphone by fraud and supplied it to the don in the prison, who was using it from the jail premises. On the directives of the Allahabad High Court, the case was transferred to CBI for investigation.

Satya Narain, however, denied that he backtracked from his earlier statements and said, "I told the court what the truth was."

Heading: Experts urge citizens to replace kerosene lamps with solar panels - Indian Express
Content:
Despite instructions by the Allahabad High Court, the Gorakhpur police failed to lodge an FIR against firebrand BJP parliamentarian Yogi Adityanath for his alleged involvement in spreading communal violence in nearly a dozen districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh in 2007.

During a hearing of a writ petition on September 26, the HC had directed the chief judicial magistrate of Gorakhpur to ensure that an FIR is lodged against the MP within 24 hours. After receiving the order's copy on October 16, CJM Ajay Kumar Tripathi had directed the Cantt police to lodge the FIR within 24 hours and inform the court accordingly.

Parwez Parwaaz, a Gorakhpur-based journalist, had filed the writ in the Allahabad High Court against Adityanath for allegedly spreading communal violence, which claimed about half a dozen lives. "Even after HC instructions and orders from the chief judicial magistrate, the Gorakhpur police could not muster courage to lodge an FIR against Adityanath," said Parwaaz.

On January 27, 2007, the MP had allegedly conspired communal violence, which began from the DAV college

Gorakhpur and lasted for nearly two weeks.

Parwaaz said he had submitted a video CD in the High Court. The CD showed that the MP had incited crowds in his public meetings at various places including the meeting

at the DAV college on January 27. "The High Court had instructed that besides the MP, FIR should also be lodged against MLC Y D Singh, legislator Radha Mohan Das Agrawal, Mayor Anju Chaowdhry and former minister Shiv Pratap Shukla," said the journalist.

Radhey Ram, the Senior Sub-Inspector at the Cantt police station, said, "We have a copy of the court's order, but I cannot comment on the issue because SHO Inspector Mangla Tiwari, who was handling the case, has been transferred."

Gorakhpur Senior Superintendent of Police R K Shrivastava said," It is a high profile case. We cannot file a FIR directly. We are examining the court's order and it will take time."

Heading: Lucknow woman was strangled in Tehri: postmortem report - Indian Express
Content:
To encourage the state's rural populace to replace kerosene lamps with solar panels, industry experts converged on Friday to discuss the benefits of clean development mechanism.

Speaking at the seminar organised by Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry and IBS, Professor Rakesh Goel of Business School of Institute of Chartered Financial Analysts of India, Lucknow branch, said: " By eliminating approximately 100 million kerosene lamps used in rural India for lighting and by adopting solar panels to produce electricity, carbon dioxide emissions can be reduced and rural health improved simultaneously."

Currently around 60 million households use 100 million kerosene lanterns. By adopting alternate sources of energy such as solar power and biogas, India can prevent 100 kg of carbon dioxide emissions per year. In order to spread awareness about the process of obtaining carbon credits and claiming them, lectures on Kyoto Protocol and clean development mechanisms were conducted during the seminar.

Clean development mechanisms, one of the three methods in the Kyoto Protocol, encourage cleaner development in growing countries and also brings an infusion of investments and technologies. "Considering the need to reduce pollution levels and save energy, we must opt

for clean development mechanisms and reap its benefits," said Sudhir Kumar, Principal Secretary, NEDA, department of additional sources of energy.

Talking about recent advancements in the sustainable energy sector, Goel said the government could now avoid Rs 15,000 crore on subsidies every year due to the new initiatives undertaken by banks and solar energy firms such as Tata BP Solar. According to Goel, solar energy mechanisms were now available to the average villager at an economical rate. "The per unit cost of electricity is Rs 265, which can now be replaced with solar panels," he said.

Solar energy being cleaner and greener will enable users to receive carbon credits — using the Kyoto Protocol — which can then be exchanged with developed countries.

Heading: Society to hold RTI gun to government’s head - Indian Express
Content:
The postmortem report of a Lucknow resident Archana Sharma (32), who was found dead in an ashram in Uttarakhand, has confirmed strangulation as the cause of death. The body had injury marks on hands, neck and face, which made the police believe that murder took place in a fit of anger.

The police are now hunting for the absconding youth, who had visited the ashram with Sharma. According to the ashram records, she had entered the youth's credentials as that of her husband, Ashok Kumar. A resident of Alambagh area in Lucknow, she used to work with Jan Vishleshan Sansthan in the city. 

On Friday morning, the Uttarakhand police had recovered her body from an ashram in Munighirati area of Tehri district. The police identified her body by an identity card found in her bag. Subsequently, the policemen informed her husband Alok Sharma and brother Santosh Sharma, both in Lucknow.

The deceased had booked a room in the ashram for two-days. "The booking was done after the ashram received a courier on October 23, requesting for the booking. The courier was sent from Lucknow," Munighirati police station in-charge S C Bhandare told The Indian Express. He added Sharma was not taken forcibly to Uttarakhand because her husband had confirmed that the note in the courier was written by his wife.

According to the police, the ashram staff failed to provide any concrete information about Sharma and the youth. They, however, claimed that earlier also the duo had stayed in the ashram.

Her brother Santosh, a medical representative, said, "My sister had gone to Tehri for some official work".

Circle Officer Alambagh Virendra Kumar said: "Neighbours of the deceased in Alambagh informed us after her brother and husband received a call from the Uttarakhand police."

Heading: Lucky 13 - Indian Express
Content:
So the sun finally sets on the Virani household. Eight long years and 1800 episodes after Tulsi (then a lithe, shy, young bride) walked into our lives, after displaying unflinching resolve to solve each and every real and imaginary problem of her husband's entire clan, a much-changed Tulsi finally makes a somewhat unceremonious exit from our lives later this week. Across India, men put up ads in matrimonial columns that read "She should be like Tulsi in Kyunki…", and women take their wedding benarasis to their local tailors to get Kyunki Saas zardozi work done on them, in their effort to emulate their favourite character's look. Of course ,the series has more than its fair share of detractors. Yet, even as Ekta Kapoor cries hoarse over breach of contract, it's time to go beyond knee-jerk snobbery and take stock.

The Feminine Gaze

"As a regular viewer of the series I can say that Kyunki…, being a woman-centric serial, has actually managed to sideline the male characters. So much so that they end up being mere objects of the attention of the women," says Madhurima Mukhopadhyay, a teacher with Cambridge School. Within the domain of the domestic set up, a role reversal of sorts takes place. "Though the situations are very regressive, the truth remains that the women are the proactive figures in this series. The men are the side players," adds documentary filmmaker Paromita Vohra. Lead players like Tulsi are icons, pretty much like the angry young man of the 1970s, who the audience identified with. "The way she stoically resists worldly pleasures and negotiates the scheming, vampish obstacles in her path in the form of interfering sisters-in-law, fiendish ex-girlfriends and the all-important mother-in-law, is what makes her an aspirational figure,"Vohra adds.

Slo-Mo Icons

To Kyunki … goes the dubious distinction of introducing Slo-Mo to Indian Television. Slo-Mo for the uninitiated is the technique which makes the characters walk in slow motion and is apparently used for the dramatic effect. That it proves to be a handy tool to stretch a 10 minute episode to an hour is entirely incidental. "No matter what we say Ekta Kapoor and Balaji Telefilms know their stuff. We may say they lack aesthetics but what they have managed to create through Kyunki… and other such serials is an episode-churning factory which uses all possible dramatic devices to carry the story forward," says filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt. The other innovation is the "reaction" technique. Where a sensational statement made by a character is followed by reaction shots of close to dozen characters. "The camera zooms into their faces and there are thunder-claps for a soundtrack. This is a very Kyunki... innovation," adds Bhatt.

Fashion Victims

When designer Nil, of Dev R Nil duo, was approached by a Bengali housewife who wanted him to rev up her wedding Benarasi sari to make it look more "contemporary", he thought he had an interesting assignment at hand. " But I realised that she wanted a Saas-Bahu sari. And despite my efforts she insisted that she wanted the sari to look like that of Tulsi's," says Nil. Given the fact that any Balaji heroine, at any given point of time is dripping diamonds and is sheathed in gold, makes the look that most Indian women aspire for, very bling. "It's bling all the way. And very North Indian. Though I have nothing against women sporting gaudy saris and jewelry, it's disillusioning to find that women from different parts of the country are discarding their own distinctive styles to embrace this look," says Nil.

Heading: Life’s Like That - Indian Express
Content:
In its thirteenth year, The Great Indian Rock gets a bunch of foreign bands and travels to seven cities

Thirteen years ago, a festival called The Great Indian Rock began with bands from across the country competing at Delhi's open-air theatre Hamsadhwani. This season, with the name tweaked a little to The Fuel Great Indian Rock, the fest will have a new avatar as it transforms into a national concert tour, spanning seven cities — Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad and Shillong— with 21 Indian bands and three international acts. "The festival has always aimed at providing local bands a platform to write and perform good, original music. It is not a competition anymore, it is purely bands in concert," says Amit Saigal, founder of the festival.

After the fest kicked off at Mumbai's Andheri Sports Complex on Friday, it plays out in Delhi on November 1 and 2 with myriad subgenres of rock spelt out by bands such as Them Clones, Kryptos, Undying Inc and Frequency alongside the hard rock act put forth by the Swedish band Freak Kitchen (in the picture) and the Norwegian black metal bands Sahg and Satyricon. "The foreign bands and the Indian bands together will add to the festival since it's always good to mix things and see what comes out of it," says Saigal. "Well, to be honest there is nothing super happening in the western hemisphere. It is here that all the energy is happening," says Mattias Eklundh, vocalist and

guitarist of Freak Kitchen, which also performed at the fest last year and have been so smitten by the country's rock and raga that in their upcoming album they have Indian classical musicians like flautist V Selvaganesh playing. But it is a first for Sahg and most of the Indian bands. Saigal says all that mattered in choosing them was a good, original song. "It doesn't matter how fast you play, it is all about good song writing," he says. And with bands putting out their originals and pushing the envelope, this season seems to be bigger than ever.

Heading: Just Qawwali - Indian Express
Content:
Loneliness and chaos collide in the exhibition "Zeitgeist" at Gallery Romain Roland at Alliance Francaise. The photographs, paintings, sculptures and video-installation of eight artists show a withering streak of hopelessness, sometimes even nihilism. If Kriti Arora's photograph has a light-eyed girl clutching a barbwire fence in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, Gauri Gill goes far out to New Jersey to show a dull matrimonial conference in progress.

Delhi-based Gill's work is from her exhibition "The Americans" that is currently going on at the Chicago Cultural Center and shows a slice of life of NRIs in the US. "I moved to the US in the mid-1990s and much of my work springs from my personal experiences," says the 38-year-old. Meanwhile, Arora used the camera as her canvas when she escorted her journalist mother to strife-torn Kashmir. "The camera serves as a notebook, recording events," says Arora, 38.

If Vibha Galhotra's White Noise (bottom) has the rampant construction in metros embossed on paper, Manil Gupta's delightfully eerie Malfunctioning Phantasmagoria series (left), all watercolours on archival paper, highlights a malfunctioning growth on a man's body.

"The works are multi-layered and cut across the medium," says Latika Gupta, curator of the show, who brought together the artists, including environmentalist Ravi Agarwal, Nicola Durvasula, Kumar Kanti Sen and Mithu Sen. The works begin at Rs 40,000 and go up to Rs 6 lakh.

Heading: Insider View - Indian Express
Content:
The sunny colours of citrine make it a much cherished stone

Fondly known as the 'Merchant's Stone', Citrine resembling the glorious shades of sun is as warm as a Van Gogh painting of sunflowers. Citrine, a semi-precious stone in jewellery is a mineral variety of crystalline Quartz family. It is named after the French word 'Citrin' meaning yellow. Citrine's colour palette ranges from a straw to sun yellow to sparkling honey tones and reddish Madeira wine colour. Natural bright yellow citrine is the rarest of Quartz family. It has a vitreous lustre and carries the warmth and glow of a golden sunset. Most commercial citrine is Amethyst or Smokey Quartz artificially heated to attain permanent citrine colour, hence it is abundant and inexpensive availability. Typical cutting styles are faceted, cabochons, beads and carvings. Most of citrine's world supply comes from Brazil. Other sources include France, Madagascar and Russia.

Citrine is both the traditional and modern birthstone of November. The Naphtali tribe of Israel is associated with citrine. It has been used in Greece since the Hellenistic Age (323-146 BC). Dionysis, a famed Greek poet, historian, geographer and author of 'Description of the inhabited earth' wrote about Indian gems and claims that every one of the gems he noted including citrine was at least once found in Southern India. Beginning of 17th century witnessed citrine's use as pure decoration e.g Scottish daggers. Advent of Romantic Period (c.1837-1860) citrine was more widely available and set in jewellery and it was this Romantic Period that citrine started gaining its modern day popularity. But it was Queen Victoria (c.1837-1901) who instigated the fashionistas towards romantically Scottish jewellery settings showcasing citrine. It may be safely concluded that prized jewellery pieces with gracious notes of citrine have been admired right through the Georgian Period across the Victorian era, the Art Deco Period up till today's Modern Period.

Besides Hollywood biggies like Greta Garbo and Joan Crawford's love for citrine jewels many of us till date enjoy citrine also for the rich legacy of its positive attributes and beliefs. The sunshine personality of the stone promotes financial growth and protects against depression and unnecessary introspection. Tough enough for everyday wear one must protect all stones from scratches. Citrine should be avoided from heat and prolonged sunlight. Natural citrine becomes dark brown when exposed to X-rays and white when heated. Citrine may be cleaned with soap, warm water and soft brush. Be sure to rinse and dry. Citrine weighing three carat and more demands higher price. It looks glorious set solo in basket setting and equally luxurious and chic set with diamonds or other complementing stones. Diwali might be over but you may ignite your attire with citrine accessories any night and shoot like a proud, sparkling cracker.

(The writer is a city-based researcher specialising in jewellery art and can be contacted at sameeraahaan02@gmail.com)

Heading: Armyman arrested for bid on wife’s life: police - Indian Express
Content:
A top model and a designer deconstruct Madhur Bhandarkar's film Fashion

In his movie Fashion that released this week, Madhur Bhandarkar plays himself in a cameo. The frame catches him sitting in the front row of a fashion show, while characters whisper in awestruck tones that he is there researching his latest project — the fashion industry. This self-congratulatory pat on his back is possibly the least irksome part of Bhandarkar's three-hour-fifteen-minute-long movie. Watching it in PVR Saket, top model Sonalika Sahay and designer Vineet Bahl protest vehemently about the movie and Bhandarkar, who has built a reputation as a hard-hitting filmmaker who doesn't dumb down to appease the audience. "It is very clichéd. He has strung together a few sensational events and tried to filter an opinion through them," says Sahay.

Sahay's ire is directed at the screenplay of the movie — the story of three models: a small-town beauty pageant winner, played by Priyanka Chopra, who makes it big very fast, a supermodel played by Kangana Ranaut who is addicted to drugs and alcohol and a second-rung model, Mugdha Godse, who figures out how to hold her own in the big, bad world of modelling. Bhandarkar's disclaimer at the beginning of the movie that all the characters and events are fictitious doesn't ring true as a doped-out Ranaut lands up on the footpath a la Gitanjali Nagpal, and Chopra's character descends into the allegedly murky side of fashion — dope, alcohol and rehab, much like England-educated Shivani Kapur did a couple of years back. "Bhandarkar should have given the movie a broader perspective. This whole thing about small-town girls losing their heads in modelling is so insulting. I'm from Bihar and let me tell you, exploitation is a matter of choice," says Sahay. "There's a nicer side to the industry as well, like friendships and creativity."

The stress on supermodels and showstoppers throughout the movie, says Sahay, is also dated. "It's something that used to happen in the initial stages of the industry. We are way past those days when a show was only about the showstopper. The only believable bit about the movie is Mugdha, probably because being part of the industry, she knows how it works and makes it look a little more credible," she says.

Newbie designer Vineet Bahl agrees in part with Sahay. While he is impressed with the histrionics of Chopra and Ranaut, his grouse is about the male characters, most of whom have been stereotyped as gay designers and exploitative agency owners. "Bhandarkar could have done without gross generalisations. It makes the movie shallow and over-dramatic. Also, there is nothing about the clothes. Whatever they show on the ramp in the movie is extremely amateurish, straight out of some fashion student's costume fantasy," says Bahl. "What is credible about the movie is the rise and fall of the two lead characters — Priyanka and Kangana. Their attempt to hold onto 15 minutes of fame is something you see in the industry all the time," he says.

The final verdict: "I think Page 3 was a success because Bhandarkar was an insider in the circuit and knew it well. This one, by and large, doesn't ring true," signs off Sahay.

Heading: No respite from school bags for city students - Indian Express
Content:
Baljinder had claimed his wife received an electric shock from a water immersion rod

The Panchkula police arrested an army personnel working at Chandi Mandir cantonment, near Panchkula, on Saturday for allegedly attempting to murder his wife.

The accused has been identified as Baljinder Singh.

The victim, Ranjit Kaur, is, meanwhile, undergoing treatment at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of the Command Hospital, Panchkula.

"On October 27, the father of the victim received a telephone call from Baljinder saying that Ranjit had received an electric shock from a water immersion rod and was hospitalised," said a police officer, on condition of anonymity.

On reaching the hospital, the victim was found to have sustained strangulation injuries and burns, added the officer.

Gurmit, the victim's father, a resident of Nangal Lubana near Begowal in Kapurthala district, stated that he got his daughter married off to Baljinder in January earlier this year.

He claimed to have spent nearly Rs 15 lakh on the marriage, which included a Maruti 800 car as part of the dowry.

"The victim's father also stated that soon after the marriage, the accused started demanding a Hyundai Accent car and when he could not meet his demand, he started harassing Ranjit," added the police official.

Heading: Five generations get together to celebrate an ageless bond - Indian Express
Content:
It has been more than two years since the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) issued instructions to phase out school bags. Stating that it found the size of the school bag to be one of the major contributors of stress among schoolchildren, the board had asked all affiliated schools to take this load off the students, especially those in the primary sections.

Most of the schools have, however, failed to comply with the directions. As a result, students in the city are still reeling under the burden of heavy bags. While students of some private schools like Strawberry Field, Gurukul, Carmel Convent, St. John's and a few others do not have to carry too many books, their counterparts in government schools are yet to get the luxury.

At the beginning of this year, the UT Education department had decided to do away with school bags for students up to Class V. The proposal was launched with much fanfare, but has failed to see the light of day yet.

Aruna Bhardwaj, principal of Gurukul School, said: "Childhood cannot be burdened under the heavy bags. It is wrong to weigh them with any kind of pressure, whether physical or psychological. To ensure this, our students carry only those things that are required."

In its directions issued in 2006, the CBSE had said the number of books and notebooks prescribed to Classes I and II should be as minimal as possible. To ensure this, the schools were asked to make adequate arrangements on the campus to keep the bags of students so that they do not have to carry them back home.

"We do not have any place where students can deposit their bags. We have also not received any instructions from the department to provide the students with such facilities," said a teacher of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 46.

Talking to Newsline, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools), said: "We are in the process of implementing the board's instructions. The department is thinking of providing students with desks where they can keep their books. We also want the students to attend school without any extra pressure, but this will take some time."

Heading: 3 held for ‘manhandling’ doctors at hospital - Indian Express
Content:
It was a family get-together, but there was something so special about this family affair that the entire Mansa Devi Complex was talking about it on Saturday.

The get-together saw five generations celebrating the vast spectrum of life. A 95-year-old Meena Kumari, the oldest member of the family, travelled all the way from Saharanpur in Uttar Pradesh, along with her 78-year-old daughter Pushpa Sharma, to meet the other generations at her great granddaughter Reena Rambani's (30) house. The occasion was very special. It was the first birthday of little Riya, Reena's daughter. Reena's mother Sarita (56), too, came down to bless the one-year-old.

Reena played host to 40 relatives at the function. And according to the family, the number was very less as everybody couldn't come. Meena Kumari has four sons and four daughters — all live in Saharanpur — with the branches of the family settled in other parts of the country.

Fifteen years ago, there was a similar get-together at the family's ancestral house in Saharanpur that had brought four generations together. Meena Kumari stays there with her elder son.

"It was fun to see all five generations of our family together, which is otherwise a rare phenomenon. Though we make it a point of be in touch, meeting up in person was no less than a dream come true," says Reena.

For Meena Kumari, it was the biggest achievement of her life to watch her four generations grow and prosper before her eyes.

As for Pushpa Sharma, the bond among them has got stronger with age. "Life took a full circle for us today. This was the first time that all five generations got together for a function in the family. When we met more than 15 years ago, we did not know God would give us an opportunity to be with our fifth generation too," she says.

"Though my mother is 95 years old, she has the heart of a 30-year-old and loves watching cricket and latest Bollywood movies. And it is this spirit of hers that helps us all forget the generation gap," Pushpa adds.

The family now plans to unite every year to celebrate the festival called life and enjoy the togetherness.

Heading: Glaucoma experts from India and abroad converge on the city for annual conference - Indian Express
Content:
The Panchkula police arrested three persons on Saturday for creating a ruckus and manhandling hospital staffers at the emergency ward of General Hospital, Sector 6, late on Thursday night.

The three — Vibhor Batra, Bhupinder alias Vishu and Sunil — were arrested after Dr Amarjeet and Dr Rakesh Saini along with the other staff members, lodged a complaint.

The trio was, however, released on bail, today after being produced before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM).

"On Thursday night, following a group clash, three injured youths were brought to the General Hospital for first aid. The moment they reached, a group of nearly 25 youths came to the hospital and manhandled the hospital staff," said Dr Amarjeet.

Sources added that while in the complaint, the names of three identified youths have been mentioned, another two unidentified youths were also involved in the case.

A police officer, on condition of anonymity, said, "While Batra, a resident of Sector 4, runs a restaurant in the Sector 8 market, his accomplices, Vishu and Sunil, are residents of Sectors 16 and 9 respectively. Many other accused in the case are yet to be identified."

While no case was registered on Thursday as the groups had agreed to a compromise, the police registered a case under Section 107/151 of the CrPC on the complaint lodged by the doctors on Saturday.

Heading: Soldiers killed in 1984 riots: ex-servicemen to approach judiciary against Congress - Indian Express
Content:
Latest surgical techniques, improvement in the quality of a patient's life and better disease management were the key areas of discussion at the 18th Annual Conference of the Glaucoma Society of India which began at the PGI today.

The two-day conference has been organised by the Advanced Eye Centre, PGI. Over 40 glaucoma experts took part in the discussions on the inaugural day, which included participants from India and abroad.

After inaugurating the conference, PGI Director Professor K K Talwar highlighted the excellent work being done by the Advanced Eye Centre.

"At present, the Advanced Eye Centre is equipped with all the latest technology, including a state-of-the-art clinic and an electronically managed clinical medical database to facilitate advanced treatment of glaucoma patients," he added.

The programme started with guest lectures from Dr Allan Robin, USA, Dr Bill Morgan, Australia, and Dr G Chandrashekhar, Hyderabad.

They emphasised the need for regular treatment for glaucoma and the difficulty being faced by ophthalmologists in using glaucoma drugs over a long period of time. They also highlighted various new techniques being developed for early diagnosis of glaucoma.

Dr Ramanjit Sihota from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, deliberated on the adverse effects of glaucoma on the lifestyle of patients.

In the afternoon session various surgical methods for treating glaucoma patients were discussed in detail. Dr Vijaya, president of the Glaucoma Society of India, discussed the latest techniques by which one can avoid complications of glaucoma surgery.

Heading: CHB razes unauthorised constructions in Sector 55 - Indian Express
Content:
Ex-servicemen in Punjab have decided to approach the judiciary against the Congress for allegedly hiding the names of armymen who were killed in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

The decision was taken after the Army recently admitted for the first time that 34 soldiers were killed in the aftermath of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984.

Col Partap Singh Phoolka (retd), president of the ex-servicemen wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal and who has been leading the campaign, said over 200 Sikh soldiers were killed in the riots in northern India.

"The Congress was aware of the fact but tried to hide it. The then Congress government did not allow the Army to reveal the names," he said.

He further added that the government had hatched a conspiracy to sweep the matter under the carpet by labeling the soldiers as deserters.

He said there is a need to conduct a thorough probe in the case and he would take up the matter with the authorities.

On October 24, the Rehabilitation and Welfare Section of Ceremonial and Welfare Directorate, Adjutant General's branch in the Army Headquarters in Delhi, sent a note to various Commands and Regiments that 34 Army personnel (including one ex-serviceman) were killed in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

The note stated that all efforts be made to report on the progress of their compensation cases with respective state governments in tune with the package announced by the Centre in January 2006.

Heading: ‘For the ordinary Punjabi, PU is his Harvard and Cambridge’ - Indian Express
Content:
The enforcement wing of the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) demolished illegal construction in 54 houses in Sector 55 on Saturday.

Out of these, 40 were existing constructions on government land. In three cases, the owners had unauthorisedly constructed an additional floor.

Seven ongoing illegal constructions were also demolished. Four of the owners had had already been served notices.

Housing Board secretary Kamlesh Kumar and the Additional SHO of the Sector 39 police station were present at the demolition drive.

The demolitions were conducted under the supervision of Executive Engineer (Enforcement) Sunil Malik.

More such anti-encroachment drives are to be conducted on Monday.

Heading: Inadequate security, poor hygiene plague Sector 19 - Indian Express
Content:
All departments at the Panjab University participated on the final day of the yearlong Diamond Jubilee celebrations on Saturday.

While Haryana Governor A R Kidwai was the chief guest, the other dignitaries present at the function included Minister of State for Finance Pawan Bansal and member of Rajya Sabha Prof Ram Parkash.

A series of academic activities in the form of special lectures, alumni meets, essay-writing competitions and cultural programmes were held throughout the day.

The celebrations culminated with a special function organised at the University Law Auditorium.

Kidwai congratulated the university for what he termed as its "consistent record of growth and development" in the field of higher education. Recounting his association with the university, the Governor appreciated the way the institution has maintained its standards of excellence, despite financial constraints. He described the Diamond Jubilee as the "beginning of a new era".

Prof Ram Parkash exhorted the fraternity at the university to compete with global players to help it rise to the international standards in research and teaching. He said, "For the ordinary Punjabi, PU is his Harvard and Cambridge. Let us not fail him."

Panjab University Vice-Chancellor Prof R C Sobti said that 48 new courses have been started by the university over the last three years.

A book titled-The Flight of the Phoenix — co-authored by Prof DVS Jain, Professor Emeritus, and Dr V K Anand, chief librarian, AC Joshi Library, was also released at the function. The book chronicles the history of Panjab University since its inception in 1882 as one of the four federal universities in India.

Festive mood on campus as all depts hold functions

Centre for Emerging Areas in Social Sciences: A special talk — Human Rights that have a bearing on Police Administration and Social Work — was delivered by V K Bhawra, IG Police, Punjab. A poster exhibition on various themes — female foeticide, environment, smart policing, women empowerment, say no to drugs and no-smoking — was held. A documentary — Ek Tha Bachpan: The Lost Childhood — was also screened.

English Department: Former and current students of the department joined hands with the faculty to give shape to an alumni association, said Dr Rana Nayar, a senior professor in the department and a functionary of the organisation. Apart from a quiz contest, a speech on the Right to Information Act was delivered by Rajan Kashyap, IAS, who was a member of the RTI committee till recently.

Institute of Educational Technology and Vocational Education: Nearly 17 students participated in poster-making and slogan-writing competitions. Richa Sharma, Lecturer of Arts, Dev Samaj College of Education judged the events.

Department of Sociology: The faculty and staffers felicitated the former teaching and non-teaching members of the department. Various presentations were made on the subject 'Relevance of Sociology in the Globalised World'.

University Institute of Fashion Technology and Vocational Development: The institute organised a 'Paint Your T-shirt' and 'Paint the Classroom Wall' contest on the theme — Save the Planet.

History Department: A lecture — Looking back at History, the relevance of History today — was delivered by Meeta Rajivlochan (IAS) controller, Semi Conductor Laboratory, Mohali. An interactive session was held with the students on critical questions on history as well as the role of bureaucracy in contemporary India.

Department of Laws: Apart from an alumni meet, the department also organised a lecture by Prof Varindra Kumar on the topic 'Law Teacher and the Legal Order — Reminiscences and Reflections of a Teacher'. The alumni members were felicitated on the occasion.

Music Department: A seminar on 'Various Forms of Music' was held as several students, faculty members, staff presented the various forms of music — Classical, Semi-Classical and Folk among others.

Department of Psychology: Prof B S Chavan, Head, Department of Psychiatry, Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32, Chandigarh and Prof Jitendra Mohan, Emeritus Professor, delivered various lectures on the theme — Stress at the Workplace.

Department of Indian Theatre: Nearly 36 saplings were planted to mark the completion of 36 years of its existence. Zulfiqar Khan, an alumnus, was honoured for his work with underprivileged children.

Heading: PU may re-employ retired professors to address issue of faculty crunch - Indian Express
Content:
A visit to Sector 19 invariably makes one encounter heaps of garbage and construction waste. Apart from hygiene, the inadequate security in the area also generates a sense of apprehension among residents.

G S Bhatwa, a resident of the area says, "There is a path adjoining my house which is meant for pedestrians to walk. The path, however, is now being used as a pass road for vehicles. This provides an easy escape for notorious elements active in the area."

Another resident, Bhupender Bakshi, adds that snatchers are common in the area and that his wife has been on the receiving end a couple of times. He says, "Security is a major concern in the sector. We are senior citizens and such incidents can prove fatal for us."

As construction waste can be found dumped at various places, residents allege that while stern action is taken against them for dumping the waste, officers from government offices face no action for committing the same.

The sector houses several offices apart from the Le Corbusier Centre. With potholes present at almost every corner, the roads here leave a lot to be desired.

The inadequate parking facility is also exposed during rush hours.

Heading: Scribe arrest: journalists protest police highhandedness - Indian Express
Content:
After the Punjab and Haryana High Court dismissed the petitions seeking enhancement in the retirement age of professors from 60 to 62 years, the Panjab University Syndicate called for an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss the status of the 58 retired professors who were relieved from duty on Friday.

The issue of accommodation for these professors formed the core agenda of the meeting.

According to a decision taken earlier, the retiring professors had been given six months' time to vacate the official residences allotted to them.

On Saturday, it was decided that since nearly 21 professors had already attained the age of 63 years, they should not be given more than two months to vacate their houses.

Others who do not fall under the category of those whose permissible time span has expired have been given a time of four months.

In another decision taken at the Syndicate meeting, the members said the status of Professor Emeritus would be conferred on former Dean University Instructions Prof S K Kulkarni.

On the issue of faculty crunch being faced by the university, the members decided to consider the re-employment scheme and said they would lay down a specific time span for the eligible professors to apply under the scheme.

Talking to Newsline, Prof Mahajan said: "We discussed the issue related to re-employing the retired professors.

"It will be finalised soon. It is the best way to deal with the problem of faculty crunch."

The authorities have, meanwhile, dispatched relieving letters to all 58 professors.

While it was earlier speculated that the university will not relieve the 58 professors till it received written orders from

the High Court, the authorities decided to relieve the professors after seeking legal opinion on Friday evening.

With 58 professors on their way out, the university will have to face a crunch of over 300 faculty members.

It is already largely dependent on guest faculty.

Heading: ‘Skin allergy’ drives man to suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Journalists protested against the highhandedness of the Punjab Police on Saturday in arresting Ashwini Malhotra, a reporter with NDTV, in Jalandhar recently.

The protestors said the Kapurthala police had hastily registered a criminal case against the reporter, charging him with trespassing and extortion, on the complaint of the management of the Lovely Professional University.

"The arrest was made without conducting any inquiry, thus violating the standing orders of the Punjab Chief Minister in this regard," said a journalist.

The media fraternity demanded that the state government immediately re-issue instructions to the SSPs about conducting thorough inquiry by a DSP-rank official whenever a complaint is submitted against a journalist.

"We don't support corrupt journalists. In case, the police come across any evidence of extortion against the journalist, he should be brought to book," added another journalist.

Heading: Civil medical services body rings alarm bell on dengue - Indian Express
Content:
In his suicide note, engineer wrote he was suffering from an incurable skin disease that had 'made life humiliating'

A 24-year-old Junior Engineer with the Punjab Water Supply and Sewerage Board allegedly committed suicide by hanging himself from the ceiling fan at his residence in village Kishangarh on Saturday.

The police have recovered a suicide note from his room.

The victim, identified as Dilbag Singh, said in his note that he was suffering from an incurable skin allergy, which had made life humiliating for him.

According to the police, Singh was alone in the house in the afternoon. "When the family members returned around 2 pm, they found his room locked. They knocked on the door but Dilbag did not respond. The family members gained entry into the room by breaking down the door and found him hanging from the fan," said a police officer.

The victim's father, Pal Singh, a police constable, said his son was depressed as the skin disease was aggravating.

The police have initiated inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC. The body was kept at the hospital and will be handed over to the family members after conducting the postmortem.

Heading: ‘A balance between spiritualism and science is essential’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Civil Medical Services Association (PCMSA) has described the ground situation on the outbreak of dengue in the state as "very serious and alarming" and deplored the "casual and negligent" approach of departments concerned.

The association disapproved of the lack of coordination between the various state departments who were indulging in a "blame game" rather than taking the required measures at a war footing.

President of the association, D S Gill, and Manjit Singh, general secretary, in a joint statement appealed to the Chief Minister and Chief Secretary to take immediate stock of the "grave situation".

"We urge the authorities to coordinate and direct the departments concerned to take extensive measures, including proper fogging operations without delay to control further spread of this epidemic," he said.

The association also urged the health department to immediately declare the dengue epidemic as a medical emergency so that innocent lives are saved.

Heading: Realty reality - Indian Express
Content:
"The concept of Hindu nationalism is not any political ideology," said Mohan Bhagwat, general secretary of the Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh (RSS) at a lecture organised by Chandigarh-based Panchnad Research Institute today. "It should be understood as a way of life that leads to ideal coordination between man and his environment," he added.

Highlighting the four phases of an individual's life, Bhagwat said that the scientists of ancient India — the rishis and munis — had comprehended the reality of the universe and devised a way of life that was in tune with nature.

Bhagwat said neither spiritualism nor scientific developments alone can bring peace and harmony to humanity — "a balanced combination of both is essential".

Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, Prem Kumar Dhumal, presided over the lecture and released a souvenir to mark the occasion. Dhumal emphasised the need to create universal brotherhood based on ancient Indian wisdom.

Heading: Octogenarians felicitated by Air Force Association - Indian Express
Content:
Owning a home has now got easier. Left with no buyer in the real estate market, builders and developers are now targeting the middle-class and its 'affordability' factor with slashed rates and attractive offers

The middle-class buyer perpetually on a hunt for an "affordable" property may finally see an end to the wait to own a home. The realty market is waking up to the reality that overpricing does not pay for long. With the market gripped by fears of recession and thanks to a general slowdown in the demand for real estate, the seller — builders and developers — is now forced to look beyond the investors. Hence, the target is now the middle-class buyer whose priority is affordability, which translates into a dip in the prices.

The realty developers are either advertising the slashed prices or are open to negotiations. Some realtors are even going one step further and offering innovative schemes to lure the prospective middle-class buyer.

The open offer

It's all over the newspapers and local radio stations. Prominent builders are openly offering their products at substantially lower rates, targeting the "affordability" factor. For Rs 12 to 15 lakh, a price unheard of till recently, you can now own a two-bedroom flat in the periphery — Kharar, Banur and Dera Bassi.  

Open to negotiations

Some builders are, however, not open to the idea of advertising that the prices are being slashed. But they are ready for a 10 to 20 per cent cut on the total price of the flats, built-up houses, and even plots.

"We had to shelve our plan to buy a house two years ago as the builder was not ready to compromise on the price. The same builder called up a few days ago and requested us to meet him if we are still interested in the flat. This time around, he is very flexible on the price issue. He says we can discuss the matter and settle on a price that suits both of us. Other builders and property dealers, too, are offering such flexibility. Our options as buyers have increased manifold," said Manmohan Dhindsa, a resident of Panchkula.

"The hike in the interest rates for home loans, and the general increase in the construction costs in the last one year had made owning a house a very expensive proposition. As a result, there was no buyer left in the market. To woo them back, we are forced to offer discounts. We cannot openly say this, but are slashing prices during individual negotiations with each buyer," said a builder based in Dhakoli, Zirakpur, who did not want to be named.

Innovative inducements

Suffering from the acute liquidity crunch, and consequently forced to stop the construction work on their projects, the builders are now willing to cut down on the rates (by 10 to 20 per cent) if the buyer pays a substantial part of the total price in cash as down payment.

"The prospective buyers know that the developers, both local and the national ones, are now ready to negotiate the prices. They enquire about the projects accordingly," said Gurpreet Singh, a property consultant in Chandigarh.

A residential project coming up in Mohali on the Landran-Kharar road is offering a discount of up to Rs 400 per square feet if the buyer opts to pay a large chunk at the time of buying the property.

Projects in the same area are even offering to pay the equated monthly instalments (EMI) on a home loan for two years on behalf of the buyer. In this case, the buyer has to pay 20 per cent of total price in cash at the time of booking. The buyer will have the option to either sell the property after two years, or start paying the EMI, depending upon its current market value.

Re-launch

The growing trend of re-launching a project gives another opportunity to the buyer to get properties at comparatively lower rates. Several projects have been re-packaged according to the changed market situation with lowered prices and attractive offers for the buyers to choose from.

Heading: Curry Trail - Indian Express
Content:
Retired Air Force personnel from Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Himachal Pradesh were felicitated at an annual meet organised by Air Force Association (AFA), North Zone, at 12 Wing Air Force, Chandigarh, on Saturday.

Air Commodore S R K Nair, AOC 12 Wing, presided over the meeting. All octogenarians were given a shawl and a memento.

Speaking on the occasion, Air Commodore Nair said: "The present generation of the Air Force is the contribution of these dedicated soldiers, who by means of their devotion and hard work have made the organisation stand tall."

AFA secretary Wing Commander Satish Bhatia briefed all the members about the latest policies adopted by the Defence Ministry and the Air Force for ex-servicemen.

He emphasised the need of becoming a member of the Ex-servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) and the AFA. He also enlightened the members about resettlement schemes for ex-servicemen and war widows.

Heading: Monks and Meditation - Indian Express
Content:
With the nip in the air, the season is just right to relish a bowlful of greasy butter chicken or piping hot tandoori tikkas. Northern Spice, a new restaurant in Gurgaon, opens just in time to offer some interesting Indian and Pakistani dishes laden with warm spices, best suited for this weather. Set up by the owners of Oz, a popular Mediterranean restaurant in MGF Mega City Mall, their new venture Northern Spice is located at Central Plaza Mall and serves North Indian fare. "Gurgaon is dotted with restaurants serving international cuisines. I wanted to offer flavours from closer home," says owner Daman Sodhi.

The interiors at Northern Spice are a mix of contemporary furnishing paired with traditional Indian motifs. A collage of beautifully carved tiles is buttoned across the walls, adding elegance to the setup and tall wooden lamps add a distinct glow. The restaurant also boasts of a neatly furbished lounge area, which will soon serve a variety of single malts paired with tikkas, once the liquor license comes in.

Must Try

The restaurant claims to hold fort in kebabs, and they serve them char grilled with smoky flavours. Our order of Lal Surkh Tangri (Rs 345) served four spicy chicken drumsticks laden with a distinct smoky aroma. Dohre Kebab (Rs 375) is a delicious starter with chicken mince wrapped in mutton seekh. Among the soups, you can try Dahi ka Shorba (Rs 175), a delicious broth of beaten yogurt tempered with cumin seeds and green chillies. The restaurant's tall claim of serving exquisite Pakistani dishes falters a bit. There are a few pointers to Pakistani recipes with Balti Chicken (Rs 375) and Dal Gosht (Rs 395) in the menu, but both these items are common offerings at most Indian restaurants. At Northern Spice, Balti Chicken is a lot like kadhai chicken, but sumptuous, nevertheless. Dal Gosht excels with tender pieces of mutton in thick lentil gravy. Among entrees Mughul Khopra (Rs 375), cooked in spicy Kari gravy and creamed coconut, is interestingly different. Low on spice, the dish was a refreshing shift from the regular tomato-onion curries. Among vegetarian dishes, Paneer Tikka Lababdar (Rs 325) is exceptionally well done. Dal Makhanwali (Rs 275), with a tender aroma of charcoal fire, is lip-smacking. The restaurant also serves a variety of biryanis with Dum Gosht Hyderabadi (Rs 365), Dum Murg Luckhnowi (Rs 365) and Peshwari Biryani (Rs 325).

Give a Miss

The Boti Kebab (Rs 375) turns out to be a bit chewy and fails to offer any distinct flavours.

Heading: A New Cut - Indian Express
Content:
The season for theatre has begun. Look out for some original scripts

In the haphazard world of Delhi theatre, very little original work has emerged over the years. The few plays staged are usually based on works by the greats, Shakespeare, Brecht and Premchand. However, this year the season kicks off with some fresh scripts and new voices. Lokesh Jain's Hamay Naaz Hai, his second original proscenium production in a career spanning 25 years, was staged on October 31. First City Theatre Foundation will stage A Brief History of Pantomimes on November 14, while Hungry Heart Foundation's Mahim Junction will have its India premiere in December, six years after it was staged at the Edinburgh Festival. And Traitors, which was tested with a small show a few months ago, will travel to Pakistan before a major opening in January.

This is welcome news to theatre lovers, most of whom wonder when they last came across a good, original play. Neel Chaudhuri of the First City Theatre Foundation can't remember. "Few and far between," says Sohaila Kapur of the Hungry Heart Festival, adding that the drama company "made a policy decision a year ago to produce original scripts in order to encourage creative Indian writing."

"The reason people just pick up scripts like bedroom farces and comedy is simply convenience," says Chaudhari. It's a long, painstaking process to produce an original play.

NSD faculty member Tripurari Sharma spent a year writing Traitors, before holding a public reading of the play to get feedback. "Based on tips from the listeners, the period script was pruned to make it more effective," says Sharma. The process is far from over as Traitors undergoes further tightening.

Kapur's play Mahim Junction will open in India only now, largely because "the audience is more sophisticated and will accept a retro play about Bollywood." Mahim Junction, a reworked version of Yeh Hai Mumbai Meri Jaan, takes the action to the slums of Bandra and packs in original music, 1960s costumes and a cast of "heroes, youngsters in love and call girls, all the joie de vivre of Hindi movies." "Delhi is the right place for the play now," she says.

Lokesh Jain defiantly states that his new production is as grim as real life and he couldn't care less that there are no corporate sponsors. But then, Jain, a veteran of several street plays, has always gone against the tide. "Hamay Naaz Hai is drawn from life, from a year of wandering around the streets of Old Delhi learning about the deprived and the homeless," he says.

A Brief History of Pantomimes is equally defiant, especially since Chaudhuri, the playwright, didn't even have a concrete script when he auditioned actors.

"Why should an actor give his time to an unknown playwright when he can work with an established script by a popular playwright? But, I was keen to create my own work," he says.

The play works on a novel concept —it is the fictional biography of a group of people who don't speak out of choice. "They live their lives, attend social gatherings and raise families without uttering a single word," he says.

Chaudhuri adds "Only four-five actors turned up to audition for my earlier play Mouse. With A Brief History there were 40 hopefuls. Clearly, actors are now more open to original plays." And so is the audience.

Heading: Tricks and Treats - Indian Express
Content:
After playing many roles, Mansi Joshi Roy now takes the director's seat

After actor Mansi Joshi Roy turned producer, she insisted on adding 'creative' as suffix to her new role. "I always believe that I'm a creative producer and not just a producer. I like designing my complete show, which I'm doing with Cinemascope," says Joshi.

Joshi Roy's prowess as a director will come to the fore today when Zee Music launches a new season of Cinemascope. The Bollywood-based show hosted by Roshni Chopra will take the viewers through new releases and their making, besides filling them in with all the gossip related to films. It will also package reviews, previews and the box-office outcome. The small screen might experience a surfeit of such programmes but the newly-turned director claims that her show, replete with trivia, will stand out. "Apart from trivia, interviews with actors and behind-the-scene footage will be our USP," she says.

Though direction is very fulfilling, Joshi Roy doesn't want to take more assignments right now. After setting the template of Cinemascope and directing its initial episodes, her focus will shift to acting — which remains her abiding passion. Production will also take up her time. She has launched a production house, called Magic Works, with husband Rohit Roy. Both of them are involved in the creative process while administration remains Joshi Roy's domain.

However the actor, who won hearts as Sudha in Saaya, has no plans of appearing on the small screen. "Not until I get something exciting," she says. Next summer, she will appear on the big screen in Alibaug. The year 2009 will also see the release of Pankh, which is co-produced by the Roys. "We are very happy to have made a non-mainstream film like Pankh," she says.

After mapping a successful journey in the world of entertainment, the actor — who has her roots in theatre — still longs to go back to stage. "I wish to do some plays sometime soon," says the daughter of Arvind Joshi, an eminent Gujarati theatre personality.

Heading: After Apollo, consumer panel faults Max hospital for negligence - Indian Express
Content: In these hard times, restaurants make a hullabaloo over the kid's festival, Halloween, in a feeble effort to lure customers to spend. On Friday night, all roads led to the Tabula Rasa, the Middle Eastern resto-bar that rocked Delhi all of last year, but has recently fallen off the party map. About 500 revellers in pirate patches, bleeding gloves, dark fairy wings, black capes and lantern bags ploughed the dance floor, whipping to house music cranked out by Devil DJ's from House Kandy until 1.30 am. The décor — a mélange of skeletons, spider webs, pumpkin faces and images from the movie Omen — added to the comically sinister ambience. While alcohol flowed freely, chef KP Singh prepared delicious Lebanese shawarma and grilled prawns. "We were the first to host a Halloween bash and start the concept. Last year, about 1,500 people, mostly expatriates, trooped in for the party," says Sohrab Sitaram, owner of Tabula Rasa, who came sans the Halloween costume. However, his partner Rohan Gupta (top left, in the picture with Kim) showed up in a police uniform and two streaks across the face.

Heading: All in the family: Father of MCD councillor gets BJP ticket - Indian Express
Content:
Days after penalising Apollo Hospital for carrying out "unnecessary tests" on a terminally ill patient, the Delhi Consumer Commission has now slapped a penalty of Rs 1.5 lakh on Max Hospital on account of poor medical care that landed a 70-year-old man in ICU needlessly.

Dismissing the hospital's appeal against a consumer forum order, Commission president Justice J D Kapoor held that if a patient was to be admitted in ICU owing to lapses of doctors, the expenses could not be fleeced from him or his family. Had the doctors been vigilant and careful, the ICU charges could have been avoided, the Commission said in its recent order.

The remarks from the consumer panel came as it heard the cross-appeals filed by Max Hospital, Pitampura, and Dr Dhanesh Agrahari.

While Max approached the Commission aggrieved by the forum's order asking it to pay Rs 75,000 to Agrahari for medical errors in treating his septuagenarian father, Agrahari sought a bigger compensation. The earlier order, he claimed, did not take into account the money he was forced to spend for ICU treatment.

Agrahari's father was admitted to Max in May 2005 for knee replacement surgery and the hospital charged him Rs 3 lakh for the treatment. The operation was carried out successfully on May 19, the complaint says, but the patient developed complications the following day.

As per the complaint, he developed 'Hyponatraemia', resulting in irritability and sudden rise in blood pressure, as the doctors failed to take prompt corrective measures. The patient turned violent and was out of his senses, Agrahari complained.

The septuagenarian was admitted in ICU after his condition deteriorated further. Agrahari claimed his father was in ICU for three days and could be saved only because he and his wife are both medical practitioners.

But Max denied any negligence and contended that best medical care was provided to the patient, and that the patient's problem existed before he was admitted in the hospital. The hospital also claimed that the doctors took utmost care in treating Agrahari senior.

The Commission found substance in the earlier order as the consumer forum had relied on opinion of independent medical experts on the line of treatment. Justice Kapoor observed that doctors treating the patient should have been on high alert. They "could have anticipated that the patient can develop Hyponataemia in post-operative period because of (advanced) age and had been feeling drowsiness and restlessness since long," the judge noted.

The Commission raised the compensation to Rs 1.5 lakh, including Rs 50,000 Agrahari paid for ICU expenditure.

Before this order, the Commission had imposed a penalty of Rs 1 lakh on Apollo Hospital for keeping a patient admitted "unnecessarily" for 10 days. "The hospital prolonged the treatment to raise bills upon him," the Commission had ruled.

Heading: Congress MLA in trouble over Muslim graveyard in Shahdara - Indian Express
Content:
Daughter's efforts in the constituency, Valmiki vote will steer me to victory, says Nand Lal Bagari

MCD heavyweights Arti Mehra and Subash Arya might have failed to muster a ticket for the Assembly elections, but the father of an MCD councillor, Nand Lal Bagari has been lucky. Bagari, the father of MCD councillor, Sushila, has been given a ticket despite tall claims by BJP's chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra and Delhi BJP president Dr Harshvardhan that neither the councillors nor their family members would be given tickets.

Bagari was selected from Sultanpur Majra in Outer Delhi. Bagari's daughter Sushila is a sitting BJP councillor from the same area.

Bagari has an interesting explanation on the relaxation of rules claiming Sushila who is married is no longer a part of 'his' family. "Hindu reeti-riwaaz ke chalte pehle phere par ladki babul ki hoti hai par satwein phere tak laado parai ho jati hai," (According to Hindu rituals, upon marriage the daughter no longer belongs to her parents).

Ironically enough, Bagari says the development work done by his daughter Sushila, an MCD councillor from the area, would make him win the elections. "There is a sizeable population of the Valmiki community here, which will support me. My daughter has also done a lot of work in the area and therefore our family has a positive image," he said.

This is the second time Bagari has been fighting the Assembly elections. In 1993, as a member of the Janata Dal, he had stood from Sultanpur Majra but lost to Congress candidate Jai Kishan.

In 1996, he joined the BJP and two years later, he had been offered a ticket to fight the councillor's elections. "There was some problem so the party asked me to withdraw my nomination to which I readily agreed," he said. Since then, he had not been offered ticket. Bagari is a property dealer in the area.

Daughter Sushila had won the last MCD elections with a narrow margin of 2,400 votes.

"We will win the elections this time with a margin of 15,000 votes," he said. Meanwhile, Delhi BJP president Harshvardhan tried to skirt the issue with a vague answer. "We have given tickets only to suitable candidates," he said.

Heading: Goel storm in party ticket cup yields result as seats held back - Indian Express
Content:
Residents allege there is already a cemetry in the area and another will only lead to problems as the area is Hindu-dominated

A long-standing dispute over the Ramlila Maidan in Govardhan Bihari Colony might deprive standing MLA Dr Narendra Nath of a large chunk of votes of the majority community. As Nath eyes a hattrick in Shahdara this time, residents of the colony are yet to come to terms with what they consider Nath's role in converting their playground into a 'qabristan'.

In the colony, Khasra 559 has been a bone of contention for long. Residents found a few years ago, the ground where the children of the locality played and Ramlila performances took place, was slated to be converted into a graveyard. They allege the local MLA had been offering support to the move. An irate RWA filed a PIL in 2005 and has resolved to see the Congress MLA's exit.

The colony, a BJP stronghold, now has reasons to campaign against Nath. "How can the authorities even plan to build a Muslim cemetery in a colony which has a dominant Hindu population? We have been cheated," said Trilok Gupta, general secretary of the RWA.

"We have managed to lay our hands on the official papers which sanctioned the construction of a qabristan on the plot and also Rs 14.5 lakh for constructing the boundary wall. We have filed a PIL in the High Court and the construction has been stalled," he said.

Members of the RWA were shocked to see the official drawing of the area which allotted the plot for the qabristan and soon sprang into action.

"There is already a qabristan adjacent to the colony and there is no need for another one. This is nothing but petty vote-bank politics," said Nirmal Jain, municipal councillor

of the area.

"Though there is a negligible Muslim population in the locality, the MLA might be looking at winning over Muslim votes from neighbouring areas like Seemapuri, a part of which has been included in the Shahdara constituency this year," said the BJP representative.

"But if the High Court decides in favour of the residents and this plot is handed over to the MCD, I will ensure it is developed into a park," Jain said.

However, Nath denied all allegations and maintained, "Building a graveyard in the colony is an absurd proposition. There was an allotment for a graveyard but that does not mean the playground will be developed as one. At least as long as I am here as the people's representative, no one can hurt religious sentiments of the people."

But the promises are taken with a pinch of salt.

"If Dr Nath really means it, why did he not give us in writing, along with the Waqf Board's consent, that such a thing would not happen. We would have taken the case back immewdiately," said Ram Bhoon Sharma, a resident.

Heading: My way or highway: VK gets his way as BJP outs list of 57 - Indian Express
Content:
After losing the war, with BJP ignoring his chief ministerial ambitions, Vijay Goel on Saturday seemed to be losing even the battle of one-upmanship to Vijay Kumar Malhotra when state unit of the party met on Saturday to discuss Assembly election candidates.

Result: the former Union minister left in a huff midway through the meeting. But the sign of rebellion had its effect later in the evening, as the party decided to stall naming candidates for four constituencies.

Senior BJP leaders, meanwhile, tried to play down the incident, calling it merely a "difference of opinion".

Fuming, Goel left the Pandit Pant Marg office saying, "I am leaving the meeting in protest." He headed straight for his residence in Bengali Market and later, after discussing the situation with senior leaders over telephone, left for 11-Ashoka Road to register his protest. Insiders say he made his opposition very evident to senior leaders at the party office. "The final nod to 57 names decided by the party's Delhi election committee was delayed as Goel wanted changes," a BJP insider said. "But V K Malhotra remained adamant and senior leaders had a tough time managing tempers."

Since losing out to Malhotra in the race for the chief ministerial candidature, Goel had made his displeasure evident by skipping several party meetings. His dispute is mainly on Sadar Bazar and Chandni Chowk seats.

In Chandni Chowk the party wants to field Delhi trader's association president Praveen Khadelwal, while Goel is backing youth leader Praveen Jain. Khandelwal is backed by Malhotra. In Sadar Bazar, the party is projecting former councillor Satish Jain while Goel's man Jai Prakash has been cold-shouldered. "Goel has been fighting Lok Sabha elections from Chandni Chowk," a senior party leader said. "He contends he would not get support from MLAs of the area when he faces Lok Sabha polls in another six months."

Goel is also canvassing for Virender Babbar, a local trader, for the Matia Mahal seat. BJP had chosen Talat Sultana for the seat; she was in Lok Janshakti Party till recently.

Goel also wanted his candidates in Vikaspuri, Kalkaji, Okhla, Burari and Kirari. In Vikaspuri, Goel is opposing Vani Tripathi's candidature; instead, he wants local leader Ashish Sood, erstwhile general secretary of Delhi BJP youth wing. In Okhla, he was backing Mohammad Irfan, national president of the party's minority wing. The party has picked Surender Biduri for the seat.

Heading: Run parents run! - Indian Express
Content:
It's official now. BJP's chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra will fight from Greater Kailash in South Delhi, and Saket MLA Vijay Jolly will take on Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit from New Delhi constituency in the Assembly elections on November 29.

The party central leadership released names of candidates from 57 seats, including four from allies Akali Dal, on Saturday evening. After former Union minister Vijay Goel staged a protest (see report below), the BJP top brass withheld the decision on candidates from Chandni Chowk and Matia Mahal constituencies. The party had floated Praveen Khandelwal and Talat Sultana's names from Chandni Chowk and Matia Mahal, respectively.

Goel was opposed to both candidates.

Besides these two, a decision on 11 other seats have also been delayed. These include Vikaspuri, where the party had pitched Vani Tripathi, who is facing protests from local BJP workers. The other seats are: Patparganj, Laxmi Nagar, Seelampur, Mustfabad, Burari, Nangloi Jat, Sadar Bazar, Matiala, Najafgarh and Trilokpuri.   

Today's decision has brought the divisions between Malhotra and Goel camps to the fore.

Malhotra, meanwhile, had his say in rest of the seats. Sources said it was Malhotra's decision to not give tickets to sitting MCD councillors. Result: no councillor, including Mayor Arti Mehra, has managed a berth.

Only two women have managed tickets: Anita Arya from Patel Nagar and Kalpana Jain from Gandhi Nagar. No Muslim candidate has made it to the first list.    Adarsh Nagar, Shahdhara, Jungpura and Rajouri Garden seats have been given to Akali Dal.

Parvesh Verma, son of former CM late Sahib Singh, also did not figure in the list. The party had been projecting Verma from Mundka. Verma, eyeing the Lok Sabha elections, did not want to contest the Assembly polls. The party has nominated Manoj Shokeen from Mundka; Shokeen was initially proposed from Nangloi Jat.  

Top leaders such as Dr Harsh Vardhan, Jagdish Mukhi and Harsharan Balli have retained their seats. Other reigning MLAs have also been given their seats. Ram Bhaj, whose constituency Sarojini Nagar had been divided after delimitation, has been adjusted in Malviya Nagar. Despite protests on few seats from the party workers the leadership has stuck to names that had been doing the rounds; these include Yogesh Attrey from Mangolpuri and Chand Ram from Bawana.  

Party leader Jagdish Mukhi, meanwhile, said: "We first want to see who the Congress is fielding in these areas before declaring our own candidates."

Heading: IGI security breach: 3 CISF personnel suspended - Indian Express
Content:
In this nursery admission season, parents have plenty of choice without ringing up the schools: more websites, interactive blogs, and even a book to get all the information they seek

The confusion among parents over nursery admissions has now translated into business opportunities for some. A handbook for Delhiites seeking nursery admissions for their children was published this Diwali by Ashok and Sujata Gupta, a couple who launched a blog and ran a helpline last year for harried parents.

The electronic book — 'Parents Handbook Nursery Admissions in Delhi' — is selling on ebay for Rs 249 and Gupta claims it has all the information a parent might need about admission in some of the top-ranked schools in the city.

While there are at least four blogs and online community portals, at last count, on nursery admissions this time around, Gupta's book is possibly a first to tackle the issue that has had parents going around in circles every session of late. "I thought, 'why not use my experience and help other parents'?" the IT professional says. "It starts with simplifying the Department of Education's rules.

"You can say it is good business opportunity — we are putting in a lot of effort, and running a website costs money."

With admissions about to begin, parents are now increasingly flocking to blogs and portals to keep track of deadlines and eligibility criteria.

After a Supreme Court interim order accorded full autonomy to schools — institutions are now only required to incorporate some Education department guidelines — most private schools have charted their own schedules. What adds to parents' worries is the lack of information. As one parent says, newspapers often carry notices but these are easy to miss.

Modern School, for instance, has announced it will issue forms only for four-and-a-half hours on November 15. The news has been discussed widely on the forum of the site nurseryadmissions.com, with parents asking for help and tips.

Rajan Arora, the moderator and founder of the website, says traffic has increased by "leaps and bounds" since he and wife Puja launched the website last year as a discussion forum for harried parents.

"After all," as Shilpa Gupta, a parent, says, "where does one get information from?"

On Net, hitting bull's eye Arora says the site has some 3,500 members and more than 100 new one join every day. According to the website alexa.com, which tracks and measures page views of sites across the world, nurseryadmissions.com is hugely popular and traffic is on a constant northward curve since mid-September.

"We think schools should come out with a common admissions system to ease worries of parents," Arora says. Jaspreet Sahni, a parent and contributor to the portal, says, "You will see chaos now, and kilometres-long lines for forms." He says related websites and blogs makes it easier for the likes him as there are so many parents looking for and giving out information.

Sahni says he became a member 20 days ago after a friend told him about the site: "Now I spend two or three hours every day on it — there is so much information. We should thank the authorities that they have got us together. It is due to their lack of proactive attitude that we have become so involved."

Arora says such sites help parents share information without having to waste hours calling individual schools to enquire about forms or, worse still, going there. In terms of opportunity cost, just gathering information would cost a couple at least a month's salary, he says.

Heading: Retreating into the Sufi’s shadow - Indian Express
Content:
Three Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel, including an inspector, have been suspended from service with immediate effect, in the follow up to the security breach at the Delhi airport last week, when two-three private workers had reportedly entered the prohibited zone.

Sources said the decision came after senior CISF officers conducted an inquiry into the matter. Inspector P R Meena and two other constables on duty that day have been suspended. This was confirmed by CISF Public Relations Officer Rohit Katiyar.

CISF officers, however, didn't reveal the names of the two suspended constables.

On October 25, a Toyota Qualis carrying staff members of Sahara press, a private firm, just drove inside the restricted area without any requisite licenses or pass, and no one questioned them. The incident occurred around 1.25 am.
