Heading: Panel rejects district forum’s order, accepts PSEB appeal - Indian Express
Content:
The councillors of the Municipal Corporation have deferred the proposal to sanction additional funds for development work in Industrial Area. The Municipal Corporation had sanctioned around Rs 30 crore for various projects, including widening of roads and streetlights, but the recent proposal of the Administration, part of the ongoing House Meet, did not go down well with the councillors.

The Administration had demanded Rs 45 lakh from the MC to shift lines and other allied structures acting as barriers to widen internal roads in Block A, B, C and D of the Industrial Area, Phase I. This was part of the agenda of the House Meet. The Mayor asked the House to think over the issue and take a decision. He argued that since the MC was already paying around Rs 30 crore for the area, the Administration should not demand additional funds.

Sanctioning of funds for development of the Industrial Area has always been an issue of contention in the House. The councillors have held divided opinions on whether the money should be sanctioned or not. While a section of councillors had stated that funds should be sanctioned by the Administration itself as the same would be a burden on the MC funds and development work in other areas could suffer, others had opined that the corporation should give the funds so that the development work does not stop. This time, however, the councillors were united in opinion and decided not to sanction the amount.

Another issue was the fact that the MC is not given a share out of the conversion fees charged from the traders in Industrial Area. The civic body has demanded that the Administration should pay some amount or make the MC the nodal agency to collect the funds.

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra said: "The Administration sent the conversion fees collected to the consolidated fund of the Central government. This money should have been used for the development of Industrial Area. While we are paying enough money for development, the Administration wants additional funds to shift lines. The issue would be taken up in the co-ordination committee meeting with the Administration."

Recently, the Administration had demanded Rs 1.42 crore from the MC to shift cables from the site for the multi-storey parking in Sector 17. This included 24 per cent departmental charges and road cut charges. It was after the councillors as well as Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Bansal argued in the House against these charges that the amount reduced.

Heading: Airtel to pay Rs 5,000 compensation for deficiency in service - Indian Express
Content:
Dismissing an order of the Amritsar District Consumer Forum, the UT State Commission accepted the appeal of the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) against an order where it was directed to refund an electricity bill of Rs 19,106 to the complainant. The appeal was accepted as the PSEB had rightly charged the amount, the Commission stated.

An electric connection was released to Ajmer Singh for operating an agricultural tubewell in the area of village Sultanwind in District Amritsar. He had been paying the consumption charges regularly till free supply of electricity was allowed to all the categories of agricultural tubewell connections.

Since, it was a free electricity case, the meter installed at Singh's premises became 'dead' and the reading was never recorded by any official of the appellant.

It was next averred that he received a bill of Rs 3,571 in January 2002 which was not withdrawn and he was compelled to deposit the same under threat of disconnection. Singh claimed that an employee of the office of the opposite party (PSEB in this case) visited his premises and threatened to disconnect the electricity supply. The official stated that an amount of Rs 11, 470 was due, Singh said. He paid Rs 19,106 in all, under the threat of disconnection.

The Amritsar District Forum had later directed PSEB to refund Rs 19,106 with interest. The PSEB was also directed not to charge any amount for consumption of electricity for tubewell connections until the policy of free electricity was either withdrawn or altered.

The UT State Commission, however, found that the respondent had a electric connection meant for commercial purposes. PSEB appealed to the Commission that the respondent had a connection which was not entitled to free supply of electricity like the tubewell connection.

While dismissing the complaint and accepting the appeal of the PSEB, the Commission ruled that there was no evidence that the complainant was using the electric connection for agricultural purposes and not commercially. It also stated that the District Forum had wrongly refunded the amount.

Heading: Cn & heard - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum directed Bharti Airtel to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for harassing a complainant and has also asked the Centurian Bank of Punjab (now HDFC) to cancel the lien on the bank account of the complainant for a telephone connection she disowned in 2003. The company was found to be guilty of deficiency in service after they failed to inform the bank that the connection has been disconnected.

The complainant, Romila Aggarwal, took a post-paid mobile connection in 2002 from Bharti Airtel. The last billing cycle of the telecom company was in February, 2003.

The complainant, thereafter, requested the company to disconnect the mobile connection and cancel the lien marked on her Savings account. For this, she deposited an HDFC Bank cheque amounting to Rs 716 to clear the pending dues.

It was alleged that the company disconnected the mobile connection, but did not cancel the lien marked on the saving bank account despite her repeated requests. Faced with this situation, a legal notice was also served, but to no avail.

In its reply, Bharti Airtel admitted that as per the records maintained by them, the connection was closed on January 30, 2003. It was pleaded that the complaint was filed after a lapse of over five years, raising a dispute of lien with the Centurion Bank of Punjab. According to records, no lien was reflected in the customer account, replied the telecom company.

Finding no merit in the contention of the company, the forum ruled that after the disconnection, it was necessary for the telecom company to write to the bank for releasing the aforesaid amount and cancelling the lien, which they did not.

"The Centurion Bank of Punjab confirmed on the application of the complainant that the lien of the Bank exists on Rs 2,000 as a security lying in the bank account of the complainant," said Jagroop Singh Mahal, president of the forum.

Heading: Rajasansi airport blips off airlines’ radar - Indian Express
Content:
Smart one

Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria isn't fidgety about taking on the councillors any more. His hesitance, visible during the first few meetings, seems to have vanished. In a meeting before Diwali, he expressed his displeasure at the practice of councillors giving gifts to the Municipal Corporation employees. A seemingly peeved councillor quipped he would tell the employees that while they all agreed on giving gifts, the Commissioner opposed the same. To this the Commissioner replied, "On one hand, you keep cribbing about the working of the officials and on the other, want to give them gifts. The employees are mine first and yours later. I am more concerned about them."

Fond memories

Aneet Dulat, Chief Regional Manager, IRCTC, often gets nostalgic about his student days. In a recent interaction he said that while studying at Panjab University, he and the incumbent Urban Employment and Poverty Alleviation Minister Kumari Shelja became close friends. But their bond owed itself to the excellent gastronomical skills of Dulat's mother.

"We used to go to my place riding our bicycles and have paranthas cooked by my mother which she was really fond of. Now whenever we come across each other, she always reminds me of my mother's delicacies."

Rumour has it

Ever since the 'cash-at-judge's-door' scandal, speculation is rife about the transfer of a few High Court judges. These rumours haven't confined themselves to the advocate chambers. It has reached the other side of the bench as well. "Why are you seeking a long adjournment; don't worry, I am not going to get transferred," a High Court Judge assured an advocate. Before retiring in his rest room, the Judge also gave the same assurance to his Court employees.

Apple of the eye

Manjit Brar, UT's IT Secretary, is a diehard fan of Apple Products. He owns the entire range of the US-based computer company associated with inventor/entrepreneur Steve Jobs. He possessed an I- phone way before it was even heard of in India. His office has a stylish Macintosh computer and his laptop is a sleek Apple Macbook. In fact, every accessory, including the mouse, is an Apple make. Those visiting his office, notice his predilections for Steve Job's products. Any observation to this effect is causally shrugged, "Once you start using Apple's product, you just can't work on anything else. Everything else is a cheap travesty of what Apple originally made." We couldn't agree with you more sir, but if you could appeal to Mr Jobs to price his product a bit more reasonably.

Party time

Last week, Akali Dal president Sukhbir Badal threw a party for journalists at Taj Hotel. The invitations that were sent requested the journalists to bring along his or her better half. Badal himself was accompanied by his wife. Maybe he expected that if they come along with their wives, many of the scribes will restrain from showing their tipsy behaviour. That didn't exactly happen though! While the party overall was well managed and tastefully arranged, a couple of 'invitees' guzzled down a drink too many. Unable to walk straight, a particular group stumbled and fell in a heap. Being a gracious host, Mr Badal just looked, smiled and ignored.

Heading: SGPC wants to talk, end all dispute - Indian Express
Content:
Airport's international status in jeopardy as Singapore Airlines latest to call off operations

If the dip in Indo-Pak trade through the Attari border land route was not enough, there's more bad news for the region. Singapore Airlines has called off its direct Amritsar-Singapore flight, started four years back amid much fanfare. A few domestic airlines have already announced that they may call off their operations to cut costs, leading to speculation regarding the status of

Rajasansi as an international airport. The airport is already facing trouble due to lack of sufficient infrastructure and facilities.

If Singapore Airlines takes away its thrice-a-week flight on November 4, as announced, Rajasansi would have little reason to be called an international terminus, as Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and some other airlines have already reduced the frequency of their flights. Pulling off this major flight would also prove detrimental to tourism, as the direct flights attracted a sizeable Punjabi diaspora to the holy city to pay obeisance at the Golden Temple.

Singapore Airlines spokesperson Gunjan Chanana, when contacted, said that the company has decided to suspend the flight for the time being and the passengers booked in advance would be adjusted in their Delhi-Singapore flight. She said that their staff had also been informed to call off the operations and they would be shifted to other stations.

Shivinder Singh Sandhu, a social activist and head of Confederation of Indian Industry's Amritsar chapter, said it was an unfortunate development. "We had taken a delegation of businessmen to the Airport Authority of India (AAI) recently. They said they are doing their best to urge various airlines to continue with their operations. But there are certain inherent troubles, including rationalising of airport charges taken from airlines. This is a major factor for airlines to call off operations," he said, adding that they have called a meeting of the CII on November 16 to take stock of the situation.

Sandhu added that their studies reveal that there are major variations when it comes to airport fee paid by international and domestic operators. "To decongest Delhi airport and to give a fillip to the business and trade to this region, it is necessary that the fee is rationalised to attract operators. Apart from this, the district administration has also been paying scant regard to various problems of the airport, including disposal of waste, controlling touts and extra land required for the airport," said Sandhu, adding that though the Singapore Airlines flight was going full, its business class occupancy was virtually nil.

AAI director, Amritsar, Arun Talwar said they have spent over Rs 120 crore on the modernisation of the airport in the past one decade and work was on for further improvement. He, however, maintained that it was their endeavour that more airlines start their operations from here.

When asked about the variation in airport fee for international and domestic flights, he said they have already moved a proposal with higher authorities.

Sidhu writes to Prime Minister

BJP MP Navjot Singh Sidhu on Sunday wrote a letter to Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh, drawing his attention to Singapore Airlines withdrawing flights from Amritsar. He said Jet Airways and TransAero have also decided to withdraw flights, because of which the holy city's connectivity to the far-East, Australia and New Zealand as well as to US, Canada and Europe will be impaired and cargo movements affected.

"The airport was emerging as a major hub for operations and NRI and pilgrim traffic was made convenient. Major houses, including Radisson, Marriot and Holiday Inn, planned to set up hotels here that would have given an immense economic boost to the area. But landing charges at Amritsar are much higher than those in Delhi. For instance, Singapore Airlines is charged Rs 1,54,536 per landing at Amritsar, while they shell out Rs 75,163 if they land in Delhi," said Sidhu in his letter to the PM.

Heading: Finance ministers' meet to focus on Centre-state fiscal relations - Indian Express
Content:
Guruta-Gaddi Aftermath z Moots all-Takht meet on Nanakshahi Calendar

The clash over dates for celebrating the recent Guruta-Gaddi Diwas has spurred the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee to hold talks with warring factions and end all dispute "once and for all".

The Sikh religious body wants the Akal Takht to initiate dialogues with the other Takhts, especially Takht Hazur Sahib (Nanded) and Takht Patna Sahib (Bihar) for ending the friction, the main issue being the Nanakshahi Calendar. The "peace talks", as per SGPC chief Avtar Singh Makkar, will be held in Mumbai and a date will be set soon.

The two Takhts, which are outside Punjab, have not recognised the Nanakshahi Calendar and are celebrating various gurpurbs and other important events in Sikh history on separate dates as per the Bikrami Calendar.

"I have spoken to Hazur Sahib Jathedar Kulwant Singh and other office-bearers of the organising committee. Talks should be initiated and if the other Takhts want separate dates from us for various events, it should be decided once and for all," SGPC chief Avtar Singh Makkar told The Indian Express.

Regarding the "ill-treatment" meted out to the SGPC delegation in Nanded, he said it was an unsavoury situation. He said some local members of Hazur Sahib Guruta Diwas Celebrations Committee tried to break decorum on stage during an event, leading to verbal spats and scuffles. He said following the incident, he thought it fit to walk away from the function on Friday.

Though a large contingent of the SGPC left the celebrations midway, Makkar prefers to downplay the entire issue. "We did not want any disturbance as situations like these only bring disgrace to the whole community. If there are issues, they can be sorted out by dialogue and discussion," said Makkar, adding that Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Gurbachan Singh, who had also returned from Nanded, had taken up the matter with the Hazur Sahib Committee. "We want no clash between the Takhts. The three Takhts in Punjab have already accepted and implemented the Nanakshahi Calendar and if the two other Takhts are not ready to adopt the Sikh calendar, they could decide their own programmes separately," said Makkar.

Makkar also denied having received any threats. "It is just that the opposing group of the Takht Hazur Sahib management committee, comprising Laddoo Singh Mahajan and deputy mayor S.S. Gill, is at war with P.S. Pasricha, chairman of the Hazur Sahib Committee. When we were given the stage on October 30, all our functions went off very well. It was just at the end of the programme that Laddoo Singh voiced his discontent. He vented his ire on us when in reality he was opposing Pasricha,"

Makkar added.

The SGPC chief clarified, "We were at Hazur Sahib on the invitation of the Giani Kulwant Singh, the Jathedar of Takht Hazur Sahib, and all due respect was accorded to us. Even after this mild showdown, Laddoo Singh called me up and requested for a meeting to resolve the issue regarding the Nanakshahi Calendar. The bottomline is that we need to resolve all matters and the Khalsa Panth needs to stand on a common platform and work for the betterment of the religion."

Will not broach worship practices at Hazur Sahib, says Makkar

LUDHIANA: Interestingly, the SGPC is not ready to touch the "real issues" regarding the worship practices followed at Hazur Sahib and will stick only on resolving the controversies regarding the Nanakshai Calendar.

The SGPC and the Takht Sri Hazur Sahib standoff is legendary considering the fact that the practices adopted at Hazur Sahib are not accepted by the SGPC. While the Sikh intelligentsia prefers to call this standoff nothing more than attempts to capture supremacy, this rivalry stems from the fact that the Hazur Sahib has legitimised the controversial Dasam Granth, which the SGPC does not allow. Moreover, each year the Hazur Sahib Committee sacrifices a lamb and washes the artillery belonging to Guru Gobind Singh with its blood. Commenting on this, Makkar says, "At present we will only be talking about the opposing views on the Nanakshahi Calender. These are the practices that Hazur Sahib follows along with local traditions and we will not broach this issue now."

Heading: No relief for kin of Sikh soldier killed in ’84 - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre-state fiscal relations will be discussed in the one-day empowered committee meeting of state finance ministers, jointly being hosted by the Punjab and Haryana governments here.

This empowered committee meeting is an ongoing process and is held every 45 to 60 days at various places in the country. The last meeting took place in Kerala and in Jammu and Kashmir before that.

Some 12 finance ministers are expected to participate in the meeting tomorrow. While some ministers arrived today, the others are expected to arrive early morning.

"The issue of distribution of taxes is likely to be discussed once again on the finance ministers' forum, as 70 per cent is taken away by the Union government and states are left with only 30 per cent share," said an official.

He added that it will be viewed that states should have a share of at least 50 per cent of taxes in the tax distribution. Also, as far as Central-sponsored schemes are concerned, most of the states do not benefit as they do not get the funds due to stringent conditions. The Union government should give the money straight to the state governments and give them the autonomy to decide how to spend it and where to spend it, he said.

The matter regarding revision of pay for government employees by the Sixth Pay Commission is also likely to be taken up. The states are demanding that the Central government should bear the arrears of salary of the employees itself.

Also, the switchover from VAT to GST system from April 2010 will be discussed again, besides the economic meltdown.

Heading: ‘Scrap additional stamp duty’ - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-Four years and still waiting. The family of Naik Nidhan Singh, who was brutally killed at the hands of a violent mob in 1984, is yet to get the status of riot-affected, let alone any benefits provided to the riot victims by the state or Central governments.

Naik Nidhan Singh of 21 Punjab Regiment was killed at a railway station in remote Bihar by a violent mob that went berserk, killing Sikhs in the aftermath of then prime minister Indira Gandhi's assassination in November 1984.

His son Manjit Singh, now a farmer in this village, feels the wait has been long enough. He and his other family members now no longer hope for any relief, especially after numerous applications in various government departments yielded no results.

Manjit Singh recalls, "My father was going back to his regiment in Ramgarh Cantonment after a 20-day leave, when he was killed at Barkunda railway station at the hands of rioters on November 1. I was five years old then and my brother Baljit was 11. We have managed to build a life for ourselves as farmers without any help from the government. All our 60-year-old mother gets is the Army pension of our father."

The family got no relief, even after the Centre declared a compensation package for all those killed in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots all over the country. In fact, the family has not even got the "Red Card" issued to riot-affected families by the Punjab government.

When told that the Army authorities had for the first time admitted that their soldiers were killed during the 1984 riots and that it was identifying the families of those killed for grant of compensation, Manjit Singh laughed it off. "If they have taken 24 years to admit the fact that soldiers were killed during the 1984 riots, how much more time would they take to grant the compensation. Not in my lifetime, it seems."

The Centre promises to give a compensation of Rs 3.5 lakh, jobs for the next of kin of those killed, monthly pension for the widow from the state government and a lumpsum payment of Rs 2 lakh as rehabilitation grant for the family.

The Army has recently admitted that 34 Army personnel, including one ex-serviceman, were killed during the 1984 riots. Like Naik Nidhan Singh's family, there are many other such families in Punjab who are yet to get any benefits and are awaiting the grant of compensation, including the riot-affected status.

Heading: Sangat darshan reduced to Akali darshan: Khaira - Indian Express
Content:
Senior BJP Leader and Punjab state chief of BJP Investor Cell, Sukhminderpal Singh Grewal, today termed the additional 3 per cent stamp duty imposed by the previous Congress government on 39 Class II, 31 Class III municipalities and 29 nagar panchayats of the state Punjab as unconstitutional.

Grewal has written a letter to CM Parkash Singh Badal demanding immediate corrective action to grant relief to people, who, he said, were facing problems

Heading: Himachal confidential - Indian Express
Content:
Congress MLA from Bholath, Sukhpal Singh Khaira, in a letter to Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, said that it is a matter of great regret that he has neither been informed nor invited for the proposed sangat darshan programme being held in his constituency on November 5.

He said the programme should be called 'Akali Darshan' and not 'Sangat Darshan' if the local MLA was not invited only because he belongs to the opposition.

He has written that being an elected representative of the people he deserves to be a part of the programme.

"I am surprised that a politician of your stature, having an experience of 50 years in public life should indulge in such partisan and parochial approach," he has written in the letter. He has also alleged that over 200 Congress leaders and workers of his constituency, including himself, have been falsely implicated in criminal cases during the past over 18 months of the SAD-BJP rule.

"A well-planned campaign has been launched to target Congress cadre at the behest of Bibi Jagir Kaur, whom I defeated," reads the letter.

Heading: BJP assured state employees’ support - Indian Express
Content:
What's cooking?

The guests who came in to wish the Chief Minister on diwali this year were in for a special treat. Breaking away from the tradition of serving laddos, hot jalebis and crisp pakoras were dished out for all the guests. Many wondered if this was an impact of having a woman as the head of the state tourism department.

No 'jootha' for IAS officers

After the government appointed non-IAS or state cadre officers for posts of heads of department, PSUs, commissioner of Shimla Municipal Corporation and deputy commissioners, in some districts, the IAS officers have refused to accept these posts. According to them the dignity of the posts has been lowered by posting state cadre officers. In best of his wits one of the IAS officers said, "hum jootha nahin khayenge."

Who is better?

After Dr Pankaj Khullar retired in October from the post of Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF), the government gave the additional charge to Vinay Tando,a even though IFS officer A K Gupta approached the CAT claiming his seniority over Tandon. Though Tandon stands a greater chance of being appointed by the government, the question remains whether it is a war between seniority and choice.

Solidarity with Assamese

Director of Indian Institute of Advanced Studies, Shimla, Professor Peter Ronald DeSouza chose a peculiar way to express his solidarity with the victims of blasts in Assam last week. During one of the workshops at the IIAS he sported an Assamese gamocha around his neck and said, "Today I feel the pain of people who lost their loved ones in blasts. This gamocha represents that I am as much a part of Assam as I am of any other place."

Heading: Special scheme for solid waste management in villages - Indian Express
Content:
"Three lakh employees of the state will support Bhartiya Janta Party (BJP) in the forthcoming Lok Sabha Elections," claimed Gopal Dass Verma, Chairman of the Himachal Pradesh All Employees Joint Action Committee. In a press statement issued today, Verma said the grant of 10 per cent interim relief to the state employees is commendable.

Appreciating Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal's gestures of giving benefits of Rs 700 crore to the state employees, pensioners and labourers, Verma announced the state will also be fill up 2,200 vacant posts soon.

The Chief Minister has assured as soon as the Punjab Pay Commission report is implemented by the Punjab government, Himachal Pradesh will release the pay scales on the same pattern, he added.

Heading: Condition of roads Dhumal’s top priority - Indian Express
Content:
After receiving a positive response from Gram Panchayats under the Total Sanitation Campaign, Himachal Pradesh has initiated a special scheme for solid waste management to maintain hygienic living condition in villages.

A special Incentive Fund of Rs 40 crore has been set up by the state government for giving a grant to those panchayats that evolve a system for management of solid waste and its scientific disposal. Government would reward double the money spent by Panchayats annually.

At present there is no system for management of solid waste in rural areas and suburbs. Due to weak financial position of panchayats villages are not able to handle such problems. By implementing the special incentive additional resources can be mobilised to undertake such activities independently.

The idea was suggested by the third State Finance Commission in its recommendations. The commission recommended the Gram Panchayats could avail the incentive against the net fresh additional resource mobilisation by these bodies and Rs 10 crore would be spent annually.

Director of Panchayti Raj, R N Batta said, "The incentive shall be equally distributed under a two-pronged strategy for additional resource mobilisation and raising resources to undertake the statutory function of sanitation, liquid and solid waste management and lighting of village streets and other public places."

Under the new incentive scheme, the Gram Panchayats would be expected to generate new resources of revenue by either a fresh levy or by way of increase in the existing rates of various taxes, fees or levies being imposed by the Gram Panchayat under Section 100 to 106 of the Himachal Pradesh Panchayati Raj Act, 1994.

A report on the finances of Gram Panchayats in Himachal Pradesh for the year 2005-06 revealed that the income from the tax revenue (tax, fees, fines, rent) of Gram Panchayats in the state constitute 8.5 per cent of the total receipt of a Panchayat and 97 per cent of the Gram Panchayat did not spend on providing civic amenities like sanitation and street lighting due to lack of funds.

They are reluctant to impose taxes due to which these bodies are largely dependent on the state government grant for developmental works.

Heading: Process of shifting women care hospital gets rolling - Indian Express
Content:
Inter-state road connectivity remained the top agenda when Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal met Parkash Singh Badal and Bhupinder Singh Hooda in Chandigarh today. Dhumal discussed the repair and maintenance of Pinjore-Baddi road, where 18 kilometres of the stretch lies in Haryana, and construction of Kurali-Siswan-Baddi road. They also discussed problems accruing due bad condition of roads.

In a statement Dhumal said the Chief Minister of Punjab has assured construction of Kurali-Siswan-Baddi road by June 2009, for which necessary directions have been given to the officers concerned. Completion of this road would benefit the industrial units of both the states.

Talking to Hooda, Dhumal emphasised for need of timely repair of Pinjore-Baddi road as the stretch from Pinjore to Madhwala falls in Haryana. Hooda assured Dhumal to carry out repair of this road within 30 days.

Problems of industrialists and locals of Nalagarh-Baddi-Barotiwala area were also taken up.

Dhumal also assured Badal and Hooda to give priority to the construction and repair of the roads in border areas of Himachal.

Urging both the CMs to take timely action in a phased manner on common issues concerning all three states, he emphasised on bilateral talks among the northern states for better coordination.

Dhumal was in Chandigarh to attend the 18th Panchnad lecture on " National Integration" organised by Chandigarh based Panchnad Research Institute held on Saturday.

Heading: INLD-BJP did nothing for power sector: Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
Kamla Nehru State Hospital for Women and Child Care would be shifted from its present location to the vacant premises of Government Dental College for better coordination with IGMC Hospital. The present location, near Himland, is about five kilometers away from the IGMC Hospital.

A lot of inconvenience was caused when patients were referred to other medical departments at IGMC Hospital, in case of emergency. Some patients also lost their lives on way. The new premises is within the complex of IGMC where all specialists are available.

Senior officials of the health department, including Principal Secretary (Health) Deepak Sanan, Director Health Services, Dr Sulakshana Puri, Senior Medical Superintendent of IGMC Dr S S Minhas and Principal Dr Surender Kashyap conducted a survey of the Dental College building where a part of the women care hospital is to be shifted. The government is planning to shift the departments of women and child related diseases and OPDs to the building.

The decision for shifting the labour and operative units is still under consideration and would be executed in a phased manner.

A proposal of shifting the Directorate of Health to the present premises of Kamla Nehru hospital is also consideration. The state's only women and child specialty hospital has 135 beds; 29 in special wards.

Shifting of the hospital is part of the health sector reforms being introduced in medical care and medical education of Himachal Pradesh. For formulating a strategy for restructuring medical care in the entire state the government is likely to hire expert services of consultants for better functioning within the existing set.

Heading: CM, minister differ over choice of environment body chief - Indian Express
Content:
Referring to the NDA rally held on Saturday at Sonepat, CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda said that the people of Haryana had proved that the INLD-BJP alliance had no mass base in the state.

Addressing the gathering after laying the foundation stone of a water works at Sampla in Rohtak, Hooda said that this alliance was for selfish gains and the people associated with this alliance did not have any interest in the development of the state. He charged the INLD-BJP alliance, that ruled the state for about 10 years, with ignoring the development of the power sector.

Sampla would soon be developed like Gurgaon and the proposal for construction of railway overbridge had also been sent for approval, he said. A sum of Rs 10.30 crore has been sanctioned for the construction of the water works and the construction work would finish by the month of June next year. With the construction of this water works, every resident of Sampla would get 135 litres of water per day, Hooda claimed.

He also laid the foundation stone of a community health centre, to be constructed at cost of Rs 514.5 lakh. He also paid tribute to Sir Chottu Ram at his memorial.

Heading: Congress rally in Tosham on Nov 15 - Indian Express
Content:
Simmering differences between Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Minister of state for Tourism and Forests Kiran Choudhry have come to the fore over the appointment of the chairman of the Haryana Environment Impact Assessment Authority (HEIAA).

By recommending the name of retired IAS officer K S Bhoria to the Central government for the post of HEIAA chairman, the Hooda government has given a thumbs down to the Choudhry' choice, who reportedly wanted another retired IAS officer, H C Disodia, to be appointed to the post, according to sources.

The Centre is likely to go by the recommendation of the Chief Minister of the state, said a senior official. While Bhoria retired as Secretary (Finance) on October 31; Disodia, considered close to Kiran Choudhry, had retired as Secretary (Forest and Environment) a couple of months ago.

When contacted, Bhoria said he was not aware if the name of any other officer too had been floating for the post of the chairman. He said now that his name had been cleared by the Hooda government, it should not take much time, but it was upto the Central government to decide when to give the green signal.

The post of HEIAA chairman has been vacant since Promilla Issar quit the post after being appointed member of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT). Issar retired as Haryana Chief Secretary earlier this year. With the post remaining vacant, hundreds of major projects in the state needing environmental clearance have stayed on hold.

The three-member HEIAA, constituted by the Centre in consultation with the Haryana government, was to give clearance to the construction projects on the basis of their processes and pollution levels up to a certain level. It was with the purpose of checking pollution and protecting environment in the wake of a number of mega projects in the state that the HEIAA had been constituted in April. Besides the chairman, HEIAA has one member and a member secretary.

The HEIAA, however, was different from the state pollution control board, which checks projects only for pollution levels. The job of the HEIAA is to study the impact of any project on the surroundings and suggest a pollution management plan for reducing the ill-effects on the environment.

P K Gupta, member secretary, HEIAA, and secretary, forest and environment, said more than 150 cases, mostly construction projects, have already been admitted by the HEIAA for clearance. These would only get clearance when a chairman is appointed, he said.

Heading: Mobile vans to attend to electricity complaints - Indian Express
Content:
A rally would be organised on November 15 at Tosham to commemorate the 62nd birth anniversary of former agriculture minister, Surinder Singh. While addressing party workers at her Vijay Nagar residence in Bhiwani today, Minister of state for Forests and Tourism, Kiran Choudhry, said that Union Minister Pranav Mukherjee and Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda would unveil the statue of the late Surinder Singh at the premises of newly-constructed Surinder Singh Memorial ITI at Tosham.

She said Surinder Singh was very popular amongst the people of the state and he had always worked for the welfare of the masses like his father Bansi Lal. She urged the people to participate in this rally in large numbers and asked the party workers to contact and personally invite each household of Haryana to the rally. She said that prominent national and state-level politicians would participate in the rally.

Heading: Gurgaon shunning crackers: air pollution down by 15 pc this Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
In a step that could go a long way in providing doorstep service to consumers, the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam has taken a decision to provide a mobile van at each district headquarter by the end of this month. The vans would attend to complaints regarding power supply round-the-clock.

A spokesman of the nigam said here today that it had been planned to provide a fully-equipped mobile van to Panchkula during the first week of November. Ambala, Yamuna Nagar, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Kaithal, Panipat, Sonipat, Rohtak, Jind and Jhajjar districts would also get the vans by the end of November. The control of the vans would be taken care of by the executive engineer concerned, he said

Instructions had also been given to field officers to immediately set up Bijli Suvidha Kendras (BSKs) at each district headquarter with a common telephone number for all the BSKs.The Nigam had earmarked Rs 4 crore for setting up BSKs during the current fiscal, the spokesman added.

Initially, electricity complaints would be registered at these kendras and the staff of the areas concerned would attend to the complaints. "The nigam will also explore possibility of converting some of the BSKs into large call centres for handling complaints pertaining to outages and commercial matters too," he further said.

Heading: Providing Platform - Indian Express
Content:
Setting an example in shunning the practice of bursting crackers on Diwali, Gurgaon has recorded a marked decrease of about 15 per cent in the air pollution level in comparison with last year.

While officials claim increasing awareness about environment is the reason, local residents say it is because of escalating prices and the general slow-down of economy that have contributed towards people not spending money on crackers. Whatever the reason be, the decrease has shown that the practice of bursting firecrackers has seen a marked shift.

Sources said that the pollution-level was checked at various places in the city on the occasion of Diwali. The suspended particulate matter (SPM) was 832 microgram per metrecube as compared to last year's 978. The level of RSPM was also down to 520 mg/mc this year from 621 last year. Similarly, the level of sulphur dioxide (SO2) on Diwali day was 36 and nitrogen oxide (NOX) was 67 microgram per metercube. Last year, on the occasion of Diwali on November 9, SO2 level was 49 and NO2 level was 77.

Deputy Commissioner Deepti Umashankar said it is an encouraging sign and claimed that the sound pollution level was also decrease.

As per the figures available, noise pollution level was also checked at Mehrouli-Gurgaon road, Bus Stand, Sector 4 and 14. It was found to be lesser by 5 to 7 per cent as compared to last year.

Heading: Cambridge University Press opens its seventh office in Pune - Indian Express
Content:
In the computer age where cartoon characters and animations are fast gaining the popularity as the prime entertainers, there are a few organisations that are helping age-old methods of entertainment not only sustain but also flourish and gain momentum. Maharashtra Cultural Centre (MCC), with a motive to promote long and effective theatrical scripts has organised Deerghanka competition on January 2, 3 and 4, 2009 at Sudarshan Rangamanch.

"Deerghankas are plays that are lengthier than usual 40-minute plays and smaller than the long three hour plays. The average duration for a Deerghanka lasts between 60 to 90 minutes and its composition is different from a regular play. What makes the Deerghanka different from a short play and a regular play is the ease with which it can be presented concentrating more on the technical aspects like script and presentation rather than concentrating on time limits," says Shubhangi Damle, coordinator, MCC.

Open for all, the competition includes prizes worth Rs 50,000 in categories such as acting, writing, music, light effects and set design. This is also the only competition in Maharashtra to promote Deerghanka. "In today's fast paced world, where people are running away from good scripts due to time constraints, competitions like this need to be organised to encourage them to write effective and challenging scripts. The advantage of Deerghanka is that once successful they can be extended and made into a full length play," says Damle.

In its fifth year, the competition has been the place to showcase countless plays some of which have made a mark in the commercial theatre as well. "To name a few, plays like Loose control, Final draft and Davedar that have been successful even commercially have been the winners of Deerghanka competition at Sudarshan Rangmanch. Manomilan, a similar Deerghanka has also been extended into a commercial play and presented by well known actor Ashok Saraf," adds Damle.

What makes this competition different from others is the extended support given by the organisers. "Besides the prizes, the winners also get a chance to showcase their play at our festivals. In addition, we also sponsor first five shows for the winners. The participants are guided by experts in the field like Neena Kulkarni, Tushar Dalvi, Pradeep Mulye, Shrirang Godbole and so on," says she.

Heading: ‘AFK bullets may have gone to the hands of criminals’ - Indian Express
Content:
Pune has for long been called the 'Oxford of the east', we hope that in the future it will be known as the 'Cambridge of the east', said Christopher Boughton, Managing Director of Asia Pacific, Cambridge University Press at the inauguration of its seventh India office in Pune. The office is located at Kasba Peth.

Speaking on the occasion Boughton said, "We chose Pune as our destination because Pune is known as the educational hub of the nation. Also, with so many schools, colleges and business schools cropping up in the city, we felt the need for a quality store, which offers books written by world-renowned authors. Pune will also supply books to the rest of the Maharashtra region."

Tony Lund, regional finance director, Asia Pacific said, "We are also in talks with major educational institutes in the city to increase the readership. The range of books we have published covers a diverse array of fields. It is important to ensure that people in the city are well acquainted with our publication."

The office houses a bookstore too, which offers nearly 2,500 books and over 200 journals in addition to the course materials for schools following the Cambridge university pattern of syllabus. Mark O'Neil, executive director for Australia and New Zealand said, "The Cambridge pattern follows a student development and integrated learning approach. The emphasis in this pattern is not on mugging up the course work but understanding and logically reasoning the various subjects such that it caters to the overall development of the student."

Boughton also explained why the university has never set its campus offshore but has instead made its press and its books available throughout the world, "We want the students to come and experience the student life at Cambridge, as a result we do not have any offshore campus anywhere in the world."

Heading: Three dead in three separate accidents - Indian Express
Content:
Thirty-one-year-old Bholenath Bhegde, a worker with case plant of Ammunition Factory, Khadki, who was arrested last week for smuggling out bullets from the factory premises and selling it to 30-year-old Santosh Pawar has made certain revelations during interrogation by the police.

Police said that the stolen bullets might have been supplied to a retired teacher from Pandharpur and three criminals in Pimpri-Chinchwad. The police have arrested Sachin Dangat (33) and Rohidas Dangat (23), residents of Dehu Road on the basis of information provided by the duo. While Bhegde is a resident of Range Hills, Pawar resides in Parvati. "The four suspects will be produced in court on Monday," said police inspector Rajendra Bahirat.

The police had recovered 20 live cartridges of 0.9 mm and 0.38 mm worth Rs 4,000 from Bhegde. He was trying to sell them to Pawar for Rs 50 apiece, who in turn, wanted to sell it to others for Rs 100.

Heading: Sakaal and HDFC start ABIL tourney with a win - Indian Express
Content:
Three people died in three separate accidents in the city on Friday and Saturday.

In the first incident, a 38-year-old man Nandlal Tripathi lost his life when an unidentified four-wheeler rammed into him from behind killing him on the spot. The accident occurred at 5.30 pm on Friday when he was cycling to work as a security guard at the site of Samarth Developers, on the Pashan-Sus Road. Tripathi, a native of Madhya Pradesh was staying at Nimhan Chal in Pashan. His uncle Sheshmani Tripathi has filed a complaint with the Chatuhshrunghi police. No arrests have been made so far.

In the second accident, a speeding truck, laden with sand, knocked down a cyclist on late Friday night near Dehu Phata. The driver sped away. The identity of the cyclist has still not been ascertained. The unidentified driver has been booked for death due to rash driving by the Vishrantwadi police.

The third accident occurred on the Mumbai-Banglore highway near Tanaji Nagar, when a tanker carrying milk rammed into a Maruti Omni carrying six people. Driver Mehmad Irfan Patel (26) had given the indicator to turn left but the tanker driven by Anil Ranvare (36) rammed into the car. Patel's aunt Najma Khan who was seated in the backseat succumbed to her injuries. The driver of the tanker has been arrested and has been booked for causing death due to reckless driving.

Heading: AstraZeneca, Cognizant announce five-year deal - Indian Express
Content:
Sakaal Media Group defeated Infosys to kick-start the ABIL corporate cricket challenge on Saturday at Deccan Gymkhana ground. Cybage lost to HDFC in the second match of the day. Sakaal defeated Infosys by 6 wickets in their first match of this corporate tourney with one over to spare and Cybage lost to HDFC by 15 runs in the following match. Infosys and HDFC won the toss and elected to bat first.

The series was inaugurated by Kashinath Dere, chief groundsman, Deccan Gymkhana ground, who has won the best groundsman award for three consecutive years awarded by the MCA.

Brief Scores:

Match 1- Infosys V/s Sakal

* Sakaal Media Group: 145/4 (Sunandan Lele – 62, Sandeep Salunke – 27, Sanket Karkare – 2/25)

* Infosys – 141/7 (Sandeep Abhyankar – 52/39, Sanket Karkare – 37/27, Sandeep Salunke – 2/18)

Match 2- Cybage V/s HDFC

* HDFC – 143/5 (Nirmal Harshey – 61, Avinash Jadhav – 37, Manish Katasthane – 25, Pratik Pandit – 3/24)

Cognizant, a provider of consulting, technology and business process outsourcing services, today announced a five-year agreement with AstraZeneca to provide application maintenance services to AstraZeneca's global enterprise in the business-critical areas of research, clinical development, and sales and marketing. The agreement will further expand Cognizant's long-standing relationship with the pharmaceutical major. Under the expanded agreement, Cognizant will work with AstraZeneca's Global Shared Services organization and implement end–to-end application maintenance services. As part of this agreement, Cognizant will adopt an "Outcome" or "Effect-based" model to provide these services by leveraging its global delivery network, talent pool and best practices. This will ensure a predictable service model, reduce the overall cost of IT ownership, and deliver year-over-year efficiency improvements. The selection of Cognizant will allow us to leverage their global operations to meet the needs of our business and increase our focus on our core business — to make the most meaningful difference to patient health through great medicines," said Richard Williams, Global CIO at AstraZeneca.

"We are pleased to have been selected by AstraZeneca's global shared services organization to provide application-related services," said Francisco D'Souza, president and CEO of Cognizant. "We look forward to helping AstraZeneca identify and deploy operational improvements in its applications process ."

Heading: 4 SIMI men at Khadki ammo unit  under watch - Indian Express
Content:
The actress spills the beans on reality shows

Q* What is the format of your new reality show Jalwa 1 2 Ka 4?

The show involves singing, acting and dancing. A theme will be given to the contestants and they'll have to create an act around it.

Q* Will the scripts for the acts be created by the contestants?

We'll obviously have some help from scriptwriters, but we'll have to do a lot of work ourselves.

Q* Do you think that increasingly the reality shows are scripted?

My first reality show was Nach Baliye. Back then we were all so new to the idea. We had no idea what to do, so everything was fresh. But by the end, we'd figured out what works and what doesn't. It's the same now. People see what worked before and they go ahead and try out those same formulae. But I wouldn't blame the contestants entirely. It also depends on the questions that they're asked on the show by the hosts or the judges. If a certain kind of question is asked, everyone will react the same way, so it looks scripted.

Q* Do you think that's why there's an audience for such shows?

If a person is revealing their innermost thoughts on the screen, then of course people want to see it. It's natural. As for whether these people can control themselves on screen, it's very difficult. They come on the show thinking that they can master their emotions, but trust me, it's very difficult. The first day of rehearsals and they're bawling their hearts out. And that baring of emotions is something that everyone, unwittingly or otherwise, is very attracted to.

You're also starring in another show. Tell us about that.

I have a cameo on Meet Mila De O Rabba. It's a very spicy cameo. But I won't reveal more than that. You have to watch the show to find out more.

Q* And how about a music album?

Making a music album is hard work and I haven't gotten down to creating a new one. But as soon as I get a good idea, I'll start working on it.

Q* Any chances of seeing you with your husband Varun Badola on screen?

Not in the near future.

Heading: BJP steers clear of blast accused, ABVP offers help - Indian Express
Content:
Days after one of its employees was caught selling bullets smuggled out of the heavily-guarded Ammunition Factory, Khadki (AFK), it has now come to light that the nation's premier arms production unit has not only been battling regular thefts, but also tracking the movements of four employees suspected to be associated with the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI).

Even as security has been further tightened in and around the factory, officials said it was an arduous task keeping a constant watch on the four suspects and that the management was finding it difficult to get rid of them, given the lengthy government rules for removal of an employee from service.

Factory officials said the Intelligence Bureau and the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) had cautioned about them. "The first intimation from the intelligence agencies came about four months back when they asked us to keep a watch on one of the employees. In the last four months, IB has asked us to monitor the movements of four employees," said senior AFK officials.

After the IB tip-off, factory officials had been keeping the four, who stay in and around Khadki where the factory is located on a 90-acre land, under constant surveillance.

After the tip-off, the four were immediately transferred from sensitive departments to non-production departments or administrative duty, said a senior official. "Secondly, we made our internal checks more rigorous." Despite the "rigorous" checks, thefts of ammunition has been continuing, the latest being reported last week.

Of the four SIMI suspects, two have been working with the factory for 10-15 years and the other two for five years. All of them were said to be skilled workers. The city police and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) were also trailing the four suspects. "A shocking aspect that has emerged is that these suspects are drawing support (in their nefarious activities) from their families," said factory sources.

Last week, a worker identified as 31-year-old Bholenath Bhegde, a resident of Range Hills, was caught selling bullets to a man identified as Santosh Pawar. Officials now reveal that at least five workers had been caught in the past six months trying to smuggle out bullets in tiffin boxes.

"All of them have been placed under suspension and investigations have been started against them." The bullets were reportedly meant for terrorists and gangsters.

When contacted, factory senior general manager, confirming that four SIMI suspects were under watch, said the security chief had all the details. Security chief Col S N Sabnis said they keep receiving intelligence inputs on daily, weekly and monthly basis. "It is true we have been asked to keep a watch on certain employees. Their names have also been provided to us..."

Col Sabnis refused to comment further, citing security reasons.

Factfile: Khadki ammo factory

* Ammunition Factory, Khadki, is considered the premier unit among the ammunition factories in the country

* It was set up in 1869

* It has 5,500 employees

* It produces 19 kinds of ammunition

* The ammunition is provided to the Army, Navy, Air Force and Police

* It is said to be among the few profit-making arms units

* It produces one million units a day

* The daily production is to the tune of Rs 1.5 crore

Heading: Today, buses start run for Pimpri-Chinchwad BRTS plan - Indian Express
Content:
While the city unit of the BJP is distancing itself from the Malegaon blast accused, saying no form of terrorism can be condoned, the party's student outfit has said it will provide legal aid to the accused Sadhvi Pragya Singh and Sameer Kulkarni, as they were former ABVP members.

The local ABVP unit also feels that Shiv Sena chief Bal Thackeray had done the right thing by saying that Hindus should come forward to support the accused. "We support Bal Thackeray's statement. Both of them are former ABVP members and because of that we will provide them with legal aid. In any case, the Anti Terrorism Squad is only investigating the issue now and we do not know yet if they are guilty or not," said Dhananjay Kulkarni, senior ABVP leader.

The local BJP leadership, on the other hand, is non-committal. "The BJP's line on the national level has always been that terrorism cannot be looked at from a religious point of view. No form of terrorism, whether by Hindus or Muslims, can be condoned. The investigation into the case is still on. However, if what the ATS is saying is true, we must introspect on why some members of a traditionally peaceful religion have taken such extreme measures," said Vikas Mathkari, senior BJP leader in the city.

The Hindu Mahasabha had announced last week that it would offer legal support for the Malegaon blast accused. Now, following Thackeray's editorial in Saamna expressing displeasure at the Hindu community for not supporting the accused, other parties have come forward and said that legal support would be possible for the blast accused. This includes the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, which has said that it supports Thackeray's statement. Prakash Dhamdere, spokesperson for MNS said, "If Bihar leaders can come together over a single episode (killing of a Bihar youth in bus he was trying to take over with a gun in Mumbai), why can't leaders come together for the Malegaon blast accused?"

With at least three of the Malegaon blast accused hailing from Pune, Thackeray's editorial in Saamna urging all Hindu-based parties to support the accused may assume significance. However, parties including the Shiv Sena do not have any concrete plans on how to go about it. "The Sena pramukh's statement is our final stand. Although the accused are Pune-based, they are at not in the city now. If they approach us for help we will support them," said a local Sena leader.

Heading: Bicycle-friendly plan set rolling, civic body, Dutch NGO take lead - Indian Express
Content:
Care being taken to avoid Pune BRTS mistakes

The Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation is trying to ensure that its Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) is not besieged by the same problems that the BRTS in Pune city had run into. The Pune BRTS, started in 2006 on the Hadapsar-Katraj-Swargate route, had come under a lot of criticism.

Starting Monday, PMPML will use four CNG buses for a pilot run for Pimpri-Chinchwad BRTS on the Nigdi-Dapodi route, as reported by The Indian Express on October 20. After studying the response of the pilot run, PMPML will float tenders for buses on the BRTS routes.

The work on the BRTS is on at Nigdi-Dapodi, Telco Road, Alandi-Dehu, Hinjewadi to Talawde, Pune-Alandi and Nashik highway stretch in Pimpri-Chinchwad. Various feeder routes have also been planned for commuters to reach the bus-stops on the main roads.

The proposed BRTS routes will comprise eight lanes and will have a bus lane 3.5-metre wide on both sides of the divider, which will have a width of three metre. For other vehicles, an eight-metre-wide road will be provided on either side of the divider. Footpaths, not built for the Pune BRTS, will be constructed on either side and would have a width of 5.5 metre.

Keeping needs of cyclists in mind, a 2.5-metre-wide cycle track has also been proposed on all BRTS routes.

PCMC will construct parking facilities for people using private vehicles to reach bus-stops. The parking lots will also generate revenue for the BRTS services. Bus-stops will have features like real-time display of bus schedules.

Pune BRTS came under flak for a large number of accidents, caused mainly due to lack of foot overbridges. This required people to cross the road, which resulted in accidents. The rate of accidents also increased due to non-BRTS vehicles plying on BRTS routes.

But this will not be the case with Pimpri-Chinchwad, as foot overbridges and subways will be built along the BRTS stretch.

Heading: Inviting Trends - Indian Express
Content:
Efforts are on to bring bicycles back on the roads with a bang. Giving shape to the plan to give the the 'City of Cycles' tag to Pune is the Pune Municipal Corporation.

The civic body is roping in Netherlands-based Interface for Cycling Expertise (I-ce). It has signed an agreement with I-ce to carry out the Bicycle Partnership Programme till 2010. A training and awareness programme would begin shortly.

"I-ce has selected Pune over other cities for the programme that ensures inclusion of cycling in the urban development and transport policies," a civic official said. Experts from I-ce would begin the promotional campaign through public awareness and training of civic officials and finance it.

PMC would construct a 117-km cycle track along the Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS). It is ready in many parts of the city, officials said.

I-ce is an international NGO for low-cost mobility and integrated cycling planning and the programme aims at supporting 30 to 50 cities in Africa, Asia and Latin America. The partnership, under coordination of I-ce, has secured a subsidy from the Dutch Ministry for Foreign Affairs.

The city recognises the need for a more comprehensive vision for its urban transport system and the programme is meant to deliver expertise in response to the demand.

Under the programme, parties agree on a multi-stakeholder approach, involving civil society organisations, universities and partners from the public and private sector.

The partnership will focus on planning and design of cycling and pedestrian pathways and facilities, capacity building for planners, engineers and other key stakeholders.

"The responsibilities of I-ce will be to make available international expertise including funding for professional coaching of city officers and providing peer-to-peer reviewing of plans and designs," as per the agreement.

It will conduct workshops and interactive training sessions on issues like strategic planning for cycling, design approaches and issues related to involvement of stakeholders.

PMC will be responsible for organising and providing logistics for meetings and workshops with the international experts. PMC also has to provide local staff, cross-sector coordination, regular funding for implementation activities, ensure stakeholder involvement, share relevant data for assessment of impact of cycling facilities and relevant information among others. It has to prepare reports on a half-yearly basis on the progress made.

Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi, keen on promoting the idea, has declared every Tuesday the s 'cycling day' at the civic headquarters.

The PMC is also planning a 'hire and ride' bicycle programme as seen in Paris. PMC efforts had received boost with the Global Environment Facility (GEF) of the UN approving the proposal for developing cycle tracks on (BRTS) routes.

Heading: Small talk - Indian Express
Content:
Catching up with designer Anshu Arora and new husband and partner Jason Cheriyan

Five years ago, Delhi designer Anshu Arora Sen was creating a sensation with her quirky, lovable designs and a unique aesthetic. But then she moved south to Bangalore to remarry, she married fellow designer Jason Cheriyan, and disappeared from the fashion circuit for a while. Anshu Arora, as she is called now, is back with her label, Small Shop, and she held her first show at the Delhi Fashion Week after five years (though she did Lakme Fashion week in 2005 and Singapore Fashion Week in 2006). "It's been so long," smiles Arora sheepishly. "I admit I was nervous."

It turns out she need not have worried. Their Spring-Summer collection, a non-fussy range of casual ensembles in cheery neon shades like orange and lime green, were low on embellishment and high on draping. The clothes, born out of a series of sketches done by Cheriyan, emphasised on living the eco-friendly way. "Jason had done these sketches which spoke of alternative forms of energy. Much of it was fantastical—things like chlorophyll energy and pumpkin dwellings done for our daughter, but later it developed into a lovely storyboard," says Arora.

The reaction, says Arora, has allayed her concerns. "We have quite a few offers. Even our kids' line was appreciated by buyers from Saudi Arabia," says Arora, with a nod.

Of course, Arora and Cheriyan have made their presence felt in Bangalore. They have their own store in the city and retail out of Evoluzione in Chennai and Aza and Ogaan in Delhi. They have got into home furnishings, and have branched into kids wear.

"We want to look beyond India now, at markets overseas, so we thought showing at a fashion week would be a good option," she says, having sold out of Selfridges and Saks Fifth Avenue earlier in her career.

Jason and Anshu, as the two are now known, are wisely keeping the economic meltdown in mind. Arora says they ensure that the consumer gets his money's worth. "As a designer I need to go in for multiple products, rather than stick to ensembles alone," she explains. Accordingly, there is a gamut of kitschy shoes, ear-muffs, headphones and attractive jewellery that now form part of her stable. "Buying should be an experience. That's what our focus is on now," she says.
