Heading: Singh appointed intl skating judge - Indian Express
Content:
Pune's Amonara, comprising JK Bhosale, MP Kulkarni, PD Joshi and Swadi, with some consistent play ensured themselves for a place in the final of the Team of Four Dulicate Swiss League in the Tata Open Bridge championships, hosted by Tata Sports Club at Catholic Gymkhana here on Sunday.

They take on the Doctors (Rajul Dalal, Ashok Bhavnani, Yogesh Shah, Chetan Shah, Audrey Purshotam and S. Vijyakar) for the coveted honours.

Amonara, who were placed second with 127 imps behind leaders Manayawar (149) in the qualifying stage, first eliminated Mangos by a solitary point margin (40-39) in the quarters and then fought back after early hiccups to down Carotina Oil 62-60 in the semifinals. In fact, Amonara trailed 9-37 midway before rallying in the second session to outplay their rivals by notching up 53 points to Carotina's 23 to clinch the tie. The Doctors on the other hand, got the better of Deepak Podar 58-57 in the quarters and then defeated fancied Tolani Shipping 70-46 to make the final.

The following had qualify for the quarterfinals: 1. Manayawar (149); 2. Amonara (127); 3. Soumitra (124); 4. Doctors (123); 5. DepakPoddar (122); 6. Carotina Oil 120); 7. Mango (116) and 8. Tolani Shipping (114).

Heading: Songs for all Seasons - Indian Express
Content:
Indian men are least likely to be fashion clones. As predictions from the fash frat are individualistic and often antagonistic

This winter, don't cringe at the thought of stepping out in the regular turtle neck in the usual browns and greys, as designer Raghavendra Rathore feels its time to cut down on the flamboyance bit this season. "The general mood around the world is not a very bright one with this financial crisis hitting the young and the ambitious especially," says Rathore, who showcased a collection, which was mostly about classic cuts and silhouettes, at the Chivas Fashion Tour that came to the city last weekend. However, if fellow designer Varun Behl is to be believed, embroidery is timeless and is least likely to go out of men's fashion, even this winter. So while Behl, who showcased a vibrant traditional collection high on embroidery at Chivas, roots for 'bright colours', Rathore thinks it's time to cut down on threadwork and bet on the classics – beige, ivory and black. Fashion forecasts in our part of the world, evidently, are eclipsed in the face of strong individual style statements.

Rajesh Pratap Singh is all for the 'ubiquitous' bandhgala for men this season. And the flourishing wedding fashion in the country, too have mixed stories to tell. "Green would dominate the colour palette for trousseau. And solid colours it will be this time, no fussy embroideries," adds Rathore. Behl again finds wedding sherwanis without the customary bling not suited to an Indian wedding.

Heading: Just for Fun - Indian Express
Content:
Benefit to IT firms willing to invest in the state

The state government has decided to provide government land on concessional rates to IT companies willing to invest in the state, Principal Secretary, Industry, S S Channi said while addressing newspersons this afternoon.

He said the government has chunks of land in Ropar, Mohali and Kapurthala, which would be offered at a discounted price. Till now, the scaling land prices, especially in the periphery of Chandigarh, had been a dissuading factor for the investors.

After meeting representatives of top IT firms in New Delhi recently, the state government officials will now head for Bangalore and Karnataka on November 6.

Infotech MD R K Verma said several software giants, including Infosys, Wipro and TCS, have evinced interest in Punjab. The state government has set a target of 600 acres of land in one year for IT, Verma said.

The Punjab government, which had recently accorded its approval for uninterrupted power supply to IT sector, will be doing this at no additional cost, Channi said. He added that dedicated power supply in several other states comes at an additional cost.

He said the state has an advantage since many of the tier-I IT cites have been clogged. Verma said in the past five years, software exports from Punjab have grown by 27 per cent. "The target export projection has been estimated at 52 per cent in the next 10 years, with an estimated employment potential of 1.9 lakh jobs," he said.

The visiting delegation from Punjab will meet officials of Infosys, Wipro, Dell, Satyam and Mphasis. They will also be engaged in one-to-one meets for better understanding of the practices in the sector.

Heading: Dance Works - Indian Express
Content:
India gets its first film critic duo, thanks to a Hollywood review show

If nomenclature of television shows is ever recognised as a discipline worth studying, Sony Pix's latest film review show will surely prove to be a discussion generator. What is the logic behind naming an "intelligent movie review show", Chicks on Flicks one may ask. Is it reverse snobbery or something deeper? "The title is catchy, so we decided to use it," is the answer of Sunder Aaron, business head of the channel who was in the city to promote the show earlier this week. Fool-proof logic this, but the presenters of the show, television presenter, Neha Sareen, and theatre actor Ira Dubey, weren't buying. "Initially we had problems with the title of the show, but the Aaron assured us that we wouldn't be presented as stereotypes," says Sareen.

On book, the show exudes promise. It claims to be the first full-length Hollywood review show in India. "It is important to identify and acknowledge the English-movie-watching culture in this country," says Dubey. It also breaks stereotypes when it comes to shows of such genre. Generally we associate serious film reviews with portly, distinguished-looking, middle-aged men (read Roger Ebert), not attractive young women. "Both Neha and Ira have a deep understanding of Hollywood films. They have studied cinema and have prepared diligently for the show," states Aaron.

The first episode focuses on the latest Hollywood biggie, the James Bond film, Quantum of Solace. "We had a great time discussing the film and sharing our views on it," gushes Sareen. The duo also got the opportunity to interview the director, the lead actors and technicians of the film. "These take their work so seriously. Their passion for cinema is evident," says Dubey.

However, after the James Bond special episode, the show will settle down as a review show. "We will review new English releases every week in addition to DVD releases," says Sareen.

Chicks on Flicks debuts on Sony PIX Friday, November 7, 7.30 pm.

Heading: Delhi all set for polls, but where are voter I-cards? - Indian Express
Content:
When the International Dance Festival 2008 organised by German choreographer Pina Bausch kicks off this month, it will feature just one Indian dancer. Arushi Mudgal (in the picture), 22, daughter of vocalist Madhup Mudgal, will be the first Indian to feature in this prestigious festival's roster. A sociology student, Mudgal switched to a correspondence course in her final year to focus on dance. "I practise almost every waking hour," says Mudgal.

She grew up in the rich cultural atmosphere of Gandharva Mahavidyala, the institute founded by her grandfather Pt Vinay Chandra Maudgalya in 1939. The piece that Bausch wants Mudgal to perform is her self-choreographed Bageshri, a series of pure dance movements that have no literal meaning or narration. "It is a very strenuous piece that requires minute attention to detail as well as stamina and energy," she says, before adding that it was her first choreographed piece, so it's all the more special.

Her performance in the German festival on November 16 will be followed by several performances in India and will culminate with her first visit to Pakistan in December. "Apart from the chance to take Indian culture abroad, foreign performances are also rewarding because all the tickets fly off months before the show. It's a wonderful experience," she says, stressing that Indian traditional culture will always find some admirers among the youth.

Heading: No change in the list of candidates, says V K Malhotra - Indian Express
Content:
ASSEMBLY ELECTIONS: D-Day less than a month away but distribution of EPICs yet to pick up pace

Posters are out, slogans are ready and internal bickering within the political parties over tickets allotments is at its peak. Surely, the Capital is in the election mode. But the voters, for whom this entire stage is being set, are yet to receive their electors' photo identity cards (EPICs).

The final voter lists were published nearly two weeks ago. While the Assembly elections are less than a month away, the electoral office of Delhi is yet to distribute the 84 lakh EPICs prepared for the polls.

Election officials cited breaking down of machines during the printing of these identity cards as one of the reasons behind the delay. Chief Electoral Officer Satbir Silas Bedi, however, said the distribution work was delayed due to the festival season. "Most of our employees were on leave, which led to the delay. We have begun the distribution work in some parts already, but things will pick up pace by Monday," said Bedi. The contract for the printing has been given to a private firm.

"All cards are being printed simultaneously. The staff are finding it tough and the machines are giving way," said an election officer, adding that the distribution of cards had begun only in the North district.

Though Delhi's voting population is expected to be around 1.07 crore, according to Bedi, the department has managed to make EPICs of about 79 per cent of voters. The Election Commission has recommended a list of alternative documents for the rest. "There are options like driver's licence and passport, but we are yet to take a final decision on documents," said Bedi.

According to the process laid down by the electoral office, block officers will carry out door-to-door distribution of these cards and voters will be required to sign a receipt. "In case there are errors despite corrections in the draft rolls, voters can fill Form No. 8 and 1-A and give them to the block officer," Bedi said.

The residents, meanwhile, complained of confusion and a lack of planning on part of the authorities during the entire exercise over the last three months. "First our photos were jumbled up and then there was a spelling mistake in my name. They were supposed to start distribution of the cards on Saturday, but we haven't heard from any election officer yet," said B S Sethi, a resident of Rajinder Nagar.

According to BJP MLA Puran Chand Yogi of Patel Nagar, the electoral rolls published for the area had nearly 900 names missing. "They are delaying the distribution of cards. How will we get the mistakes corrected in such a short time," he said.

Delhi Congress chief J P Aggarwal said: "We have alerted our block units and are waiting for them to begin the work. Party units will ensure that the cards are distributed effectively."

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Suresh Marwah - Indian Express
Content:
BJP chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra is struggling with unhappy party workers. A day after the announcement of the list of candidates for 59 Assembly constituencies, more than 500 party workers from Sangam Vihar and Uttam Nagar constituencies gathered outside Malhotra's official residence on Bishamber Dass Marg on Sunday.

The workers alleged the party had sold seats to H L C Gupta and Krishan Gahlot in Sangam Vihar and Uttam Nagar areas. "It is a conspiracy against the party. These candidates are not going to win. It seems some member in the party wants it to lose the elections from these constituencies," said party general secretary of the unauthorised colonies,

Yashpal Bali.

On internal protest
Despite the protest, Malhotra says the decision has been taken by the party and the list which is out is final. "There is going to be no change in the existing list. It has been approved by the party high command," Vijay Kumar Malhotra told Newsline.

On women candidates
"There is going to be some new announcement in the list of women candidates. We shall be giving seats to at least four-five women candidates," said Malhotra. "I am aware of the announcement made by the party to give one seat to women in all seven parliamentary constituencies. But we want the party to win. In case we do not have a strong woman leader, we will not let the party suffer a setback," he says. "We shall also ensure a good and healthy political atmosphere within the party," added Malhotra.

On campaigning
The party shall start its campaigning officially from Tuesday. "We will have all the top party members campaigning for us. From Narendra Modi, to Sushma Swaraj, L K Advani to Arun Jaitley — everybody will be campaigning in the coming month," said Malhotra. Malhotra also informed the party shall not be hiring any television or film actor to campaign for them. "We have people like Hema Malini, Navjot Singh Sidhu and Smriti Irani to campaign for us," added Malhotra.

On Vijay Jolly against the Chief Minister
Malhotra is confident that Vijay Jolly is the perfect candidate against the Chief Minister.
"It was the decision of the party. He is a popular leader in Delhi and has done good work. Besides, Jolly is good speaker and is very persuasive," says Malhotra who feels that Jolly will give tough competition to Sheila Dikshit in the New Delhi Assembly seat.

On MCD and development plans for the Capital
Malhotra feels if BJP comes to power, the Capital will develop further. There will be better coordination between the MCD and the state government. "I am aware of the various developmental projects approved by the MCD that are stuck with the Congress in the Assembly.
I can assure the people of Delhi that if the BJP comes to power the pace of developmental work in the city will pick up pace," he says.

Heading: Sheila a good speaker, but that’s not enough to win: Jolly - Indian Express
Content:
Suresh Marwah

Retired govt officer
Constituency: Kasturba Nagar
Area: South Extension

A resident of a colony of South Delhi, Suresh Marwah, 64, feels Delhi lags behind by more than 100 years when compared to the other metropolitan cities of the world. "We pay more tax than any other nation, but whenever I visit foreign countries, I feel we are way behind than," says Marwah.

On petty crime
"Petty crimes like chain-snatching, robbery and eve-teasing are a routine affair for South Extension. Nothing has been done to make our area a safer place to live in," he says.

On Sonia Vihar water
For the past five years, every summer whenever there is a water crisis, the government assures us that we will soon have water from the Sonia Vihar water plant. But now we are tired of the false promises," says Marwah.
Marwah feels with the present system of functioning of the government, there is going to be no water from Sonia Vihar for another 10 years.

On price rise
"In the past five years, the government has done nothing to check rising prices. For people like me who have retired from service and have a limited income, life is going to get even more difficult. The government has taken no positive measures for making life better for senior citizens," says Marwah.

Heading: She’s Got the Look - Indian Express
Content:
After Vijay Singh Mankotia, a former minister and BSP's state convenor, quit the party and two other key figures followed suit, the Bahujan Samaj Party is in for another jolt in Himachal Pradesh.

Tej Singh Thakur, convenor of BSP's youth wing, has written to AICC general secretary and MP Rahul Gandhi, offering to join the Congress ahead of the upcoming Lok Sabha elections.

Thakur said his entire unit, which was formed in the state before the 2007 Assembly elections, has decided to desert the BSP and "strengthen the hands of Rahul Gandhi to fight communal and casteist forces in the country".

The announcement by youth wing leaders comes close on the heels of PCC chief Kaul Singh Thakur's remarks to see that the BSP is completely wiped out from the state before the next elections.

In fact, most of the activists in the BSP's youth wing are originally from the Congress and now want to return to the party fold. Tej Singh also levelled charges against unnamed Congress leaders, who, he alleged, did not allow the younger leaders to grow.

"The BSP youth wing, which comprises hardcore Congressmen since student days, has got suffocated and frustrated due to suppression by a section of senior Congress leaders," the BSP youth leader said.

Heading: Assembly figures - Indian Express
Content:
Despite a slow beginning, actor Sonam Kapoor is well on her way to becoming a style icon

At the Elle Breast Cancer Awareness do in Mumbai a fortnight ago, actor Sonam Kapoor made an appearance in an abbreviated baby pink Christian Dior gown, looking every bit the prima donna she's aiming to become. Cut to Kunal Rawal's show at the Lakme Fashion Week and the bubbly actor turned up in a chic purple houndstooth dress by Marc Jacobs, her hair permed ever so slightly to add a carelessly stylish touch. Ever since her debut last year, the 5' 9" beauty has featured on almost all the covers of leading fashion magazines, walked the ramp for designers like Tarun Tahiliani and Anamika Khanna (for whom she is now the brand ambassador), and has been impeccably turned out in Lanvin and Stella Mc Cartney for significant social outings.

While industry insiders are betting on Kapoor to be the next trendsetter in Bollywood, those who know the actor well are hardly surprised. Designer Anuradha Vakil, for instance, still cannot get over her first meeting with the actor during the making of Saawariya. "She would listen to me attentively and then ask such technically sound questions about cuts, silhouettes and drapes, that I was quite floored," says the Ahmedabad-based designer, who had done the costumes for the movie, and has been designing for Kapoor's personal wardrobe ever since.

Kapoor believes her mother has a lot to do with her sense of style. "When we were kids, mom (Sunita Kapoor) used to be a full-fledged designer, supplying to stores like Glitterati and Ensemble in Mumbai. I would watch models like Nayonika and Aishwarya, before she became Miss World, come in for fittings and discuss outfits and international designers. I saw the kaarigars at their embroidery stations for hours

together. I think that's how my interest in garments grew," she says from London, where she is currently on a vacation.

Stylist Anaita Shroff Adajania says that Kapoor has developed a distinct fashion sensibility for herself. "I won't call her a style icon yet, but she has an individual flair and she wears her clothes with confidence," says Adajania. Vakil adds that Kapoor's dedication to fitness helps. "Sonam has a phenomenal body, so she looks good in almost anything," she says. Designers like Tahiliani talk of how the actor's innocence works to her advantage. "Sonam has freshness and spontaneity that's refreshing, a flawless dusky skin, long black hair and the most endearing giggle. She's very conscious of being curvaceous. Once she starts celebrating that, she will be way ahead of the curve," he says.

It's a concern, that Kapoor admits, plagues her. "I would be lying if I said I am naturally thin. I work really hard on my body, but I feel I am too curvaceous. So I am careful to dress in a way that leaves something to imagination, rather than accentuating my assets. That's not my style at all," she says. India's answer to Brigette Bardot, perhaps?

Kapoor's Top Five Designers
1. Anamika Khanna
2. Sabyasachi and Tarun Tahiliani
3. Anuradha Vakil
4. John Galliano
5. Karl Lagerfeld

Heading: Two Noida doctors booked for attempt to murder - Indian Express
Content:
The last mega traffic Lok Adalat of the year 2008 was not only an occasion for residents of the Capital to wriggle out of possible tricky situations they could land into due to their pending traffic challans, but also earned the distinction of the first such event organised at the newly-created Dwarka court complex.

Dwarka courts became functional on October 8, as the fifth district court complex with the jurisdiction of south-west areas and the Lok Adalat was the first occasion when any such activity was organised under its auspices.

The event was inaugurated by the executive chairman of the Delhi Legal Service Authority (DLSA), Justice Mukul Mudgal of Delhi High Court, around 9.45 am at the Dwarka courts complex in the presence of Asha Menon, member secretary DLSA and district judge (south-west) I S Mehta.

Apart from Dwarka, Lok Adalats were held the four other district courts complexes — Tis Hazari, Patiala House, Rohini and Karkardooma.

The event witnessed as many as 11,403 challans getting disposed of with nominal penalties ranging from Rs 30 to Rs 100. The Delhi Police collected over Rs 5.19 lakh towards settlement.

The DLSA, in association with the Delhi Police, had constituted special courts with a magistrate as a presiding officer for compounding the disputes. Among the venues, Karkardooma courts received the maximum number of challans, 3003, while Dwarka remained at the bottom of the list.

According to New Delhi Bar Association president Santosh Mishra, it was the remoteness of the Dwarka courts and lapses in promoting the event that dampened the spirit and failed to draw more people there.

As per an official, only 405 traffic challans got settled at Lok Adalats in Dwarka whereas Tis Hazari received 2794 challans.

While 2681 challans were compounded at Patiala House courts, 2520 challans were settled at Rohini courts. "As a whole, the event was successful and less number of challans itself shows the achievements of the previously held lok adalats," said the official.

Heading: Directorate of Education asks schools to give out nursery forms from Dec 15 to 31 - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida police have booked two doctors of a private nursing home here on charges of attempt to murder. Two security guards employed at the nursing home have also been booked under various sections of the IPC in the same case.

The police said one Mahipal Singh Raghav, a resident of Sector-52, got his son, who had viral fever, admitted in the Noida Medical Centre on October 31. When he went to visit his son later, he found the room he had been allotted was unclean and the doctors were not paying any attention to his son.

When Raghav complained about the negligence to the chairman of the nursing home, Dr Naveen Chaudhary, he refused to take any action, the police said. Later, Dr Chaudhary, along with his friend, Dr Rajpal Awana, and two security guards, allegedly beat up Raghav. Raghav was rushed to Prakash Hospital in Sector-20. While security guards, Dinesh Chaudhary and Dharampal Yadav, have been arrested, the doctors are absconding.

Heading: Missing since October 30, Youth found murdered - Indian Express
Content:
A circular was issued by the Directorate of Education dated October 27 asking schools to use the standardised registration forms and to issue them from December 15 to 31. It has also outlined the schedule that schools must adhere to during the nursery admissions process. The attempt to regularise the chaotic nursery admissions process leaves much to be desired, some parents said.

In case the school wants to adopt its own schedule, they are required to notify the DoE by December 14, failing which they will have to follow the authority's schedule, the circular said. Some parents said their problems would have been solved somewhat had all schools distributed forms between December 15 and December 31. Chairman of National Progressive Schools Conference S L Jain said schools can adopt their own schedules. However, the NPSC schools have been advised to issue forms starting December 1. There are about 110 schools under NPSC.

Many private schools in Delhi will start issuing forms starting from Monday including Bal Bharti Pusa Road and DPS Mathura Road.

Heading: Write Angle - Indian Express
Content:
The body of a 20-year-old BBA student was found in a drain in Haiderpur Village in Samaipur Badli on Sunday morning. The police said the youth was reported missing on October 30.

Officers said Om Prakash had gone out for a morning stroll on October 30 and didn't return. His relatives registered a missing complaint with the Samaipur Badli police the same night, after searching for him the whole day. The police then registered a kidnapping case the next day.

Prakash's body was noticed by some bystanders around 8 this morning. "We took the body to Babu Jagjivan Ram Hospital. We then called in Prakash's family for identification, who confirmed his identity. There were some external injury marks on his body and a case of murder has been registered," a senior police officer said.

The police said Prakash's family and neighbours staged a protest outside the Samaipur Badli police station after the discovery of his body. They demanded the suspension of the SHO for inaction in the matter and blocked the Ring Road till about 3 pm. Outer Delhi DCP Atul Katiyar reached the spot and had to assure the people that an inquiry would be conducted and the erring officers would be suspended.

When contacted, DCP Katiyar told Newsline: "An additional deputy commissioner of police will inquire into the matter. Any action against the investigating officer or any other officer will be taken after the inquiry report is submitted."

Prakash lived with his parents and four sisters in Samaipur Badli village. His father is a conductor with the DTC. He was a final year BBA student at Bharatiya Vidya Peet.

Heading: Out of the box - Indian Express
Content:
An exhibition brings together 50 years of Prodosh Das Gupta's art

1943. Kolkata was Calcutta and the Howrah Bridge was still under construction. Indian art was still to find a place in the global art map, but in Kolkata a small group of artists were making an attempt to internationalise Indian art. The members included amid others, Prodosh Das Gupta (in the picture), a young graduate from Calcutta University who studied sculpture at The Royal Academy of Arts, London, but came back to India to pursue art. He passed away in 1994, but more than a decade hence Kumar Gallery is celebrating his work and paying tribute to him through a retrospective. Comprising over 80 works, including sculptures and drawings, the exhibition that will open today is accompanied with a book that documents 50 years of his art. "This was much needed. He is one of the finest artists and there is hardly any material available on him," states Virendra Kumar Jain, founder director, Kumar Gallery, who has spent the last few years shortlisting important artworks of Gupta from the gallery collection, and approaching private collectors to lend their work for the retrospective. "We wanted to include his significant works," he adds.

Prodosh Das Gupta's sons Prabuddha and Pradeep are well known photographers. As he flips through the pages of the book, looking at photographs of Prodosh Das Gupta's work taken by his son Pradeep, Jain points out that the text comes from those who closely followed Prodosh's art and each of them deal with different aspects of his work. While Keshav Malik describes his persona and gives a glimpse into his influences, Aruna Bhowmick gives a detailed analysis of particular works, from First Born (1946) to Suryamukhi (1978). They compare his work to international masters like Leonardo da Vinci and Brancusi. And even though the essays may be bereft of innumerable anecdotes, Prodosh's writings, where he describes his own work and the process of conceptualisation, give a deeper insight into his work and thinking. "He is one of the few artists who can actually describe each of his work," notes Jain. That the exhibition comes less than a month after Prodosh's companion in the Calcutta Group, Paritosh Sen, passed away is meanwhile mere coincidence.

The exhibition at Kumar Gallery, Sunder Nagar, will go on till November 15. Contact: 24358875

Heading: Delhi underground - Indian Express
Content:
The Gul & Tulsian Show

CNBC Awaaz
Saturday, 9:30 pm
Rating***

What's it about? As the global economy suffers one of the worst meltdowns in history, the faces of shocked investors at Dalal Street plaster every magazine and newspaper. We all know what these faces look like. They look a lot like us— discussing stocks with friends while taking cigarette breaks, passing by on pavements, or in between jumping in and out of crowded local trains. Everybody is worried about their money. Will the market recover from this blow? Will we ever see our money again? These are question on everybody's lips. And in such a time, CNBC Awaaz has identified the need of the hour and responded with The Gul & Tulsian Show— a talk-show that promises to give investors, traders and players the right advice to guide them towards risk-free investments.

Who's in it? The CNBC team brings together Gul Teckchandani, Chief Investment Officer of Sun F&C Asset Management Company, a big player in the mutual fund industry, and S P Tulsian, of sptulsian.com and editor of Premium Investments. The two financial experts debate it out at a coffee table along with the anchor and a guest.

What's hot? Virtually every sector has taken a beating this time around and investors are worried about whether or not the government or somebody else can bail them out. Teckchandani and Tulsian are clued into the latest bulls and bears and they also seem well in tune with the ethos of the common investor on the street. The two analysts discuss the problem at large giving investors the bigger picture as well as analyse sectoral trends. Listening to them one could know what a Merrill Lynch or a Morgan Stanley is really thinking. They also put things in context, at times citing moments of similar crisis in the past and the lessons learnt.

What's not? As theories are propagated and suggestions made, the cacophony sometimes descends into the din one imagines inside the stock-exchange or the your everyday commute. There is also an over-abundance of market-jargon and name-throwing assuming the common viewer to be well-versed in such matters. A show on the stock-market is no more a niche or special interest programme, and some lucidity in the discussions would be helpful.

Should you be watching it? In times like these, everybody's a self-proclaimed investment guru. But it's important to get the 'low-down' straight from the horse's mouth. And this duo is one of the best in the stable. The show is certainly worth it.

Heading: Talking point with Rajeshwari Sachdeva - Indian Express
Content:
Hindutva calling
At a time when Raj Thackeray is pointing a finger of suspicion at migrants from Bihar and UP, a small group of these same migrants, settled in Govardhan Bihari Colony in the Capital, are fighting for Hindutva, a la Thackeray. With the slogan 'Rambhakta ne thana hai, Ram setu ko bachana hai' painted on his shop, Jai Narayan Gupta, national president of the 'Hindu Raksha Parishad', hands out pamphlets propagating staunch 'Hindu' principles. Curiously, he and many other residents of the colony, who also run small shops, have been quietly pushing for Hindutva, not just by handing out pamphlets but also by taking time off from their daily routine to explain how, as a 'Hindu', one should let the Hindu population grow manifold!

Cast out
Youth For Equality (YFE), best known for their anti-reservation gimmicks, are back to hog the limelight by being "different". While all of JNU is up in arms against the Supreme Court stay order on students' union elections, YFE has maintained a distance, saying it supports the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines. But their stance has not fooled any one, as it is common knowledge in JNU circles that YFE is backing the court decision only because they would benefit the most if the Lyngdoh guidelines were implemented. Recent reports also say they have been barred from all meetings of JNU and have become the general outcasts, ironically enough.

Tip-off blues
Amid high drama, the Ghaziabad police rushed to Loni after receiving a tip-off that a bomb had been planted in a briefcase in the main market. The Loni market area was cordoned off and shopkeepers whisked away from danger. Residents of the locality were terrified on hearing this news. The bomb disposal squad had also been rushed in. But this drama had a comical end. Instead of a bomb, there were bricks and stones in the briefcase and children who were trying to have a look at the bomb burst out laughing. Embarrassed, the police refrained from commenting on the whole episode.

Poll antics
As anger and resentment continues to simmer among party workers of the Congress in Delhi over election tickets, party workers could not resist fighting during a function commemorating the death anniversary of Indira Gandhi on October 31. If allegations of sycophancy and money exchanging hands were not enough, a certain section of dissidents raised a banner against the lack of representation for Poorvanchalis (from Uttarakhand, UP and Bihar) in the list of possible candidates for the forthcoming elections, after the (usually sombre) commemoration function. The matter was raised in a party meeting on Friday, following which a section of workers from North District gave in their papers in protest. Party chief J P Aggarwal dismissed the entire episode as "immature" and said such protests were valid only if the list was final, which it was not.

Beasts of burden
The setting up of the new district courts was a move welcomed by one and all, even if the court staff grudged one particular administrative decision. With the courts getting shuffled, they were required to carry court records to the new courts and they did not mind the work. What bothered them was a directive restraining them from carrying the cabinets that contained these records. Reason? The cabinets could damage the newly laid tiles in the complex. As a result, the files had to be carried on their own, much to the frustration of the staff.

Court in a hurry
The penultimate day before the courts were distributed district-wise, was replete with moments never witnessed before in the highly disciplined courtroom situations. During a hearing, as soon as the judge finished dictating the order, court staff moved to pull the wire from his computer screen, also connected with the judicial officer's monitor. The judge, in a state of surprise, was then told by the staff they needed to shift everything to the new courtroom and very little time was left, requiring everyone to speed up.

Change of focus
Maybe because of the Assam blasts or the "Hindu" terrorists allegedly involved in the Malegaon blasts, the clamour for a judicial inquiry into the Batla House encounter has died down. While the Samajwadi Party continues to sing the same tune, three Congress leaders, including a Union Cabinet minister, who were supportive of the Batla House inquiry, keeping their vote banks in mind, have suddenly backed off. It is not that the Union Minister or his experienced colleagues have had a change of heart but the minister was summoned to the PMO and shown the evidence the police had on the Batla House encounter. Sure enough, from that day, the minister is now focussed on western India.

Aid de camp
BJP general secretary Arun Jaitely, like all politicians, has his share of enemies. But in the run-up to the Delhi elections, Jaitely was caught unprepared when his friends-turned-foes started targeting even his Man Friday, Om Prakash Sharma. Apparently a CD is doing the rounds showing photographs of the shops owned by Sharma in malls. Sharma, who is a BJP contender for the Vishwas Nagar seat, is a businessman and he invested money earned from the mithai shop he owns near Hanuman Mandir in Jamuna Bazaar wisely. While Sharma is going around the town explaining his legitimate income and shops, Jaitely has an additional task of not only defending himself but even his aide from these barbs.

Heading: Another Metro accident: 3-yr-old girl gets 17 stitches on her head - Indian Express
Content:
Clowning around
Bonding is big on the sets of Woh Rehne Waali Mehlon Ki. The cast and crew are one big, happy family and pulling pranks is just another way in which they have fun together. Recently Karan Grover, Manoje Bidvaai and Dharam Taneja distributed chocolates to everyone on the sets claiming that they were celebrating the adoption of a child by Sajnee Srivastav. Everyone trooped off to Sajnee's makeup room to congratulate her and totally confused the poor girl. The prank was revealed when she asked people why they were congratulating her and when she finally stepped out of her room, the whole set burst out laughing.

Happy hugging
IN an effort to spread cheer among the city's unsung heroes, the participants of Zee TV's Chota Packet Bada Dhamaka went around town giving hugs to those who serve us daily and yet go unnoticed. Those on the list included BMC sweepers, government doctors, traffic cops and school teachers. The kids were welcomed with open arms wherever they went and some of them even performed at the heroes' request.

Second chance
BHANU Pratap Singh has got a new lease of life on Indian Idol 4. The long-haired guy, who was put down by his two female partners for not singing well enough, almost had a nervous breakdown when he was rejected. The judges decided to give him a second chance and he made it to Mumbai. Now that Bhanu has got the golden ticket, he is leaving no stone unturned to make his presence felt. His confidence is soaring and his singing has taken everyone by surprise. In fact, the dark horse has won the sought after Silver Coin awarded to the best performance of the day on the occasion of Diwali.

Friends forever
AJAY Devgan and director Rohit Shetty were present on the sets of Voice of India for the Dosti special episode on Freaky Friday, the day of elimination, to promote their new movie Golmaal Returns. It was decided that neither the judges nor the audience will decide who will be eliminated, and it will be the contestants who will vote one of them out. But the friendship won the day as Zaakir, Ritisha and Saptaparna voted themselves out, instead of their friends. But the spirit of competition was alive too. The boys, Vipul, Mallar and Ravi said, "We are all friends but we are in a competition and we are here to compete with each other."

Heading: Power clash: tribunal to hear NDMC plea against regulatory body today - Indian Express
Content:
Khushboo was taking a walk with her cousin when an iron bar from an under-construction pillar fell on them near Moolchand flyover

Barely two weeks after an under-construction Delhi Metro bridge collapsed near Lakshmi Nagar, claiming two lives, another accident was reported from a Metro construction site on Saturday night that left two persons injured.

Bhawna (18) was taking a stroll with her three-year-old cousin, Khushboo, when an iron bar from one of the under-construction pillars fell on them. The accident took place near Moolchand flyover in South Delhi around 8.30 pm.

A bystander called the police, who rushed the girls to the All Indian Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). Khushboo sustained injuries on her head and had to be given 17 stitches. Bhawna (18) escaped with minor injuries. Khushboo lives in a village in Himachal Pradesh and had come to Delhi to spend Diwali with Bhawna's family.

Meena Ram, Khushboo's uncle, alleged that workers of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) tried to destroy the evidence of an accident and assaulted him when he objected to it.

"The DMRC employees were washing the bloodstains before any investigation could start. When I protested, they started beating me up," he said.

DMRC spokesperson Anuj Dayal, however, refuted the allegations and said it was actually the other way round. "It was the relatives of the victims who beat up our workers and two engineers, which led to a scuffle between the two parties. We have already filed an FIR with the police in this regard," said Dayal.

He claimed that there was "no evidence of negligence". The DMRC chief engineer met the family to offer medical compensation. Dayal said an inquiry had been ordered.

This is the sixth such incident this year to take place at a Metro construction site.

Heading: VP Singh’s granddaughter injured in road accident - Indian Express
Content:
The New Delhi Municipal Corporation (NDMC) will appear before the Appellate Tribunal of Electricity (ATE) on Monday against the Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission's decision to place 15 per cent of the civic body's electricity quota in the unallocated category.

The NDMC had approached the DERC earlier this year, requesting its power supply be allocated through three power stations instead of one.

"Earlier, our entire quota of electricity was being supplied through the Badarpur Thermal power station (BTPS). If any problem cropped up in the BTPS, our entire supply would get affected. Naturally, we were concerned about our reliability," said a senior NDMC official.

In an order dated March 7, the DERC agreed to let the civic body source its supply from three different power stations. The regulatory body, however, added a rider: the NDMC would have to agree to put 15 per cent of its allocated share under the unallocated quota.

"After investigation, we found the NDMC's actual consumption of electricity never exceeds 286-287 MW. This was also indicated by the data from the state load dispatch centre," a senior DERC official had told Newsline in May, a few days before the NDMC moved the Supreme Court. The SC rejected the plea for an interim stay on the DERC order that sought to cap 53 MW of its quota. "The SC said the matter would be decided by the tribunal," a DERC official said. Sources within the DERC have confirmed its main grouse was that the NDMC was selling its surplus power at a high cost. The DERC has alleged that NDMC was selling the surplus power at a profit of Rs 450 crore.

The NDMC, on its part, has maintained it wanted to use the profits to build infrastructure. This, too, did not go down well with the DERC. "Profits generated in the power sector should be used within the sector and not to build roads and bridges," a senior official of the power department said.

With NDMC's surplus power of 53 MW capped, the municipal body can still use the surplus power as and when the need arises, as can any other power distribution company. The NDMC, however, will have to approach the Delhi government before using the surplus power. The NDMC views this as a raw deal and will argue its case before the ATE with a bid to overturn the DERC's March 7 order.

Heading: At Lok Adalat, vehicle owners find challans that never reached them - Indian Express
Content:
SUV driver booked, he was on the wrong lane, say police

Former Prime Minister VP Singh's teenaged granddaughter was injured when a speeding SUV collided head-on with the car she was driving. The SUV was allegedly on the wrong lane. Aditi Singh (18) has been admitted to the Apollo Hospital where her condition is stated to be stable. The accident occurred around 9 pm on Saturday in New Delhi area.

From her 1, Teen Murti Lines residence, Aditi was going towards South Delhi in her white Alto. As she reached Golf Link Road, a Ford Endeavour rammed into her car. Aditi's chest hit the steering. "She could not save herself as she did not have response time and also due to the reflection of the headlights of another car on the road," said a senior police officer.

The SUV belongs to a businessman and it was being driven by his son, Harbir Chaddha (22). He was coming from Safdarjung Enclave. It was Chaddha who called the police and ambulance after the incident and Aditi was rushed to the hospital.

There was also a speedy action from the police after they heard the victim was the former PM's granddaughter. The Tughlaq Road police have impounded both the cars and registered a case.

Chaddha is doing his graduation from correspondence. He has been booked under Sections 279 (rash driving) and 337 (causing hurt) of the IPC. He was arrested but got bail later. His father runs a liquor business. Chaddha was reportedly accompanied by a friend in the car at the time of the accident.

Aditi, the daughter of VP Singh's son Abhay Singh, is an undergraduate too.

Heading: ‘Only artistic interactions between the countries can promote peace’ - Indian Express
Content:
It may have been touted as an opportunity for people to settle their outstanding traffic challans in an easy, less complicated manner. But the mega traffic Lok Adalat organised on Sunday proved to be "shocking" for some people, after they were handed over challans for violations that they had no idea they had committed.

Mohd Ataullah, an autorickshaw driver, was looking to settle a challan for jumping a red light last month, after a ticket for Rs 100 was mailed to him. When he enquired about his challan and sought a receipt from the counter, he was told he had three unpaid challans pending against him. He protested and said he had received only one challan but had to settle all of them. "This has happened to me before. When I enquired about any pending challans at the traffic department, I was informed by an official that there was none. At the Lok Adalat in September, however, I was told I had committed two violations," Ataullah said.

He said people should be informed through the proper channels and in the right mode about their offences.

Prakash Chawla, who turned up to settle the challan for a violation, too, was told there were three challans pending against him. "Lok Adalats are a wonderful opportunity for one and all to clear up pending challans. But the lackadaisical attitude of the police is clear from the fact that they never bother to inform us about the pending challans. We get to know about them for the first time when we want to settle the ones mailed to us," he said.

Heading: Buddha, Paswan escape ‘Maoist’ assassination bid - Indian Express
Content:
If the horrific events surrounding the Partition of India in 1947 prompted its documentation, or creativity in any way, it was mostly with the written word at the time. Not much visual art is known to have come out of the event. Neither India, nor Pakistan and, subsequently, Bangladesh, have registered noteworthy work in the visual art medium documenting 1947.

Visiting artist Salima Hashmi says it is probably for the simple reason that the event was too big and equally earth shattering for the painter to lift his brush or the filmmaker to compose his frame.

Hashmi, a renowned painter who is, incidentally, poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz's daughter, feels this vacuum needs to be filled with some significant work. She was in the Capital to speak at the closing seminar of the year-long event, 'Partition: The Long Shadow', convened by Zubaan Books and Heinrich Boll Foundation at the India Habitat Centre.

"I asked my father often why he wrote only one poem on Partition. All he could reply was that the event was too big to cope with. There isn't any good film either, except for Garm Hawa. No civilisation in the world has documented gory events well. Perhaps it is a human tendency to brush painful thoughts away from the mind," says Hashmi who has taught at the National College of Art, Lahore, for over three decades and also served as its principal.

With Faiz and Alys (who was a journalist and human rights activist) as parents, being jailed is inheritance for her. A human rights and peace activist, she was jailed last year when Pervez Musharraf imposed Emergency. "Around 50 of us were in a meeting at the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan. The police came and asked me to follow them, to which I refused. They lifted my chair and took me to the police van," she recalls amid peals of laughter. "Jail jaana to humaara khandaani kaam hai (being jailed is family practice)," she adds.

Perhaps these nerves of steel propelled her to articulate the idea of promoting peace through visual art at the seminar on

Saturday.

"Only artistic interactions amongst different sections of the subcontinent can promote peace. They will have to dispute the state's agenda and subvert it through communication," she observes.

But to achieve that tall order, shouldn't art renounce its elitist status and be taken out of the drawing rooms of the rich?

"The media has to play a role here. It has to instil curiosity in the minds of the grassroot people," she says. Pakistani artists like Farida Batool, for instance, have attempted that. Batool took young artists on the streets of Karachi and helped them paint the walls with mehndi, something which is easily available to the common man. "Today, video installations are a very vociferous medium. They capture so much in one frame. That will address terror, which is the single largest concern of the subcontinent," she feels.

Hashmi is thankful to the Indian art market for welcoming Pakistani artists to India generously. "When I came to India for work in 1986, people questioned if there was any art in Pakistan at all. Today, you see so many Pakistani artists displaying their works here. This has become possible only through dialogue," she says.

Dialogue between the two nations saw the light of day in Musharraf's regime. What difference does Hashmi feel between his regime and the current vis-à-vis art in Pakistan? "The atmosphere now is certainly more open but the government still doesn't have a policy on art, nor a minister for art and culture. They are so consumed with immediate issues like economy and terror. But people are addressing different facets of terror and peace in Pakistan, for instance issues arising out of mindless violence. I am hoping some young filmmakers will wake up soon," she says.

Hashmi, an author of two acclaimed books on art, is now a facilitator and mentor for young Pakistani artists. Her two art galleries in Islamabad and Lahore display works of the upcoming artists who according to her, "do impressive work, but still don't sell well".

Heading: Jindal factory off to a start in Salboni - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Union ministers Ramvilas Paswan and Jitin Prasada escaped an assassination attempt on Sunday afternoon after suspected Maoists triggered a landmine explosion on a village road in Salboni, West Midnapore, almost immediately after their vehicles had passed.

Six policemen were injured, two of them critically, after the explosion rattled an electricity pole and caused a high-tension wire to snap and fall on the last vehicle in the convoy.

The twin impact of the blast and the falling wire severely damaged the vehicle. Four policemen have been shifted to Kolkata.

Bhattacharjee and the two central ministers for steel were returning to Kolkata after the foundation stone-laying ceremony of the Sajjan Jindal-promoted JSW Bengal Steel plant. They had left the site at around 2.30 pm, and come about five kilometers in 15 minutes on the road to Kharagpur when the landmine was triggered. There are patches of sal forests and paddy fields along the road, with scattered habitation. The mine had been planted in a bush by the road at Barua Olaichanditala village.

Rajesh Singh, SP, West Midnapore, said the blast damaged the police vehicle bringing up the rear of the convoy carrying, besides Bhattacharjee, Paswan and Prasada, several other ministers and senior officers. "The landmine was not very powerful," Singh said. "The Maoists triggered it from about a kilometre away using a battery and wires laid in paddy fields."

Maoists have used landmines in West Midnapore before. This, however, was the first time that Bhattacharjee, a strong votary of industrialization, has been directly targeted. Later, at a function organized by the zilla parishad, the Chief Minister expressed concern over the incident, and ordered an investigation.

The CPM state committee secretary, Biman Bose, appeared to equate the Maoists with Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress: "Those who are opposed to development of the state have done this. They are the fruits of the same tree. Some have driven out the Tatas, some are exploding landmines," Bose said in Kolkata. Dipak Sarkar, West Midnapore CPM district secretary, said, "Locals had gathered to welcome industry in this backward area. Exremist groups organised the attack to create panic."

Police are now searching nearby villages for local contacts of the Maoists, police sources in West Midnapore said.

Heading: Twelve German auto majors abandon state - Indian Express
Content:
A few weeks after Tata Motors pulled out of Singur, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee inaugurated the largest steel plant in the country in West Midnapore's Salboni on Sunday.

Following the ceremony, Bhattacharjee announced that a power plant and a cement factory will also come up along with the steel plant.

"The social and economic condition of the residents of Salboni will change after this Rs 35,000-crore project is executed. The plant, with a capacity of 10 million tonnes, will generate employment for 25,000 people. Local villagers will get preference over others." He added that the process of land acquisition has been smooth in Shalboni.

The plant by JSW Bengal Steel will be completed by 2020.

Chairman Sajjan Jindal said: "The project will be executed in three phases. Production of steel will commence from 2012.

Initially, the plant will have a capacity of 3 million tonnes."

"The company has decided to arrange for the training of those who had given up their land for the plant. Everyone will get permanent employment after completion of training," said Jindal.

He added, "Four year ago, Omprakash Gindal, my father had expressed his desire to Buddhadeb to set up a steel plant in West Bengal."

As Salboni is primarily a drought-prone area, the company will bring water from river Rupnarayan through a pipeline.

A total 75 lakh gallon per day will be required for the plant, said the chief minister.

JSW Bengal Steel is promoted by the Jindal Group, which holds 89 per cent of equity capital, the remaining 11 per cent is owned by the state government. About 4,500 acres was acquired by the company, of which, 4,000 was vested with the government. The state government had leased out 4,000 acres to the company for a period of 99 years.

For the 4,000 acres, the company had borne the expense of Rs 78 crore.

It had purchased the remaining 469 acres from the villagers with the rate of Rs 3 lakh per acre.

While most of the 4,500-acre land is barren, on some parts of the land single crops were cultivated.

Who should be in the firing line?

* Kuldeep Singh, IG (Western Zone)

* Parveen Kumar, DIG (Midnapore Range)

* Rajesh Singh, SP (West Midnapore district)-Responsible for overall security arrangements

* A K Maliwal, IG -In-charge of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's security.

* Strict vigil was supposed to be maintained along the entire 25-km stretch from Kharagpur to Salboni — a Maoist-affected area. Scanning of roads and adjoining areas for explosives were supposed to be conducted.

* Questions being raised why 1,300 police personnel on duty were not able to detect the bomb placed so close to the road at Barua Olaichanditala village

* Sailendranath Biswas, OC (Salboni police station)-Responsible for security arrangements in the area where the incident took place

Cabinet to soon clear Nayachar chemical plant: Paswan

Union Chemicals and Fertilisers and Steel Minister Ramvilas Paswan said the Cabinet will soon clear the proposal for setting up a chemical hub in Nayachar.

He announced this at the foundation laying ceremony of the steel plant in Salboni on Sunday. The minister said his department has already cleared the proposal of setting up chemical hubs in West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat. "The department has forwarded the proposal to a high-power committee. After clearance from the committee, the proposal will be placed before the Cabinet for final approval," he added.

Regarding the fertiliser factories at Haldia and Durgapur, which have been closed for a long period, Paswan said the department has decided to re-open them based on the private partnership model. "The Centre will publish an advertisement in this connection very shortly," he added.

Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee requested Paswan to formulate a national policy on iron ore for the interest of the country.

Maoist explosions

* October 22, 2008: Three killed in a blast at Belpahari

* May 11, 2008: Six BSF jawans killed in Konkrajhar forest

* February 2006: Two policemen killed in Belpahari

* October 2004: Six jawans killed in Bankisole, West Midnapore's Lalgarh area.

* February 2004: Seven policemen and a driver killed in Konkrajhar forest

* 2004: Bandoan OC Nilmadhob Das killed in Maoist attack

* 2005: Barikul OC killed in Maoist blast

Heading: Two deaths in districts, toll rises to 25 - Indian Express
Content:
With the pullout of the Tata Motors, the state has lost the investment of at least 12 German automobile companies and 59 automotive companies.

This is what the records of Indo-German Chamber of Commerce reveal, a fact also confirmed by Subrata Gupta, Managing Director, West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC).

"Apart from Nano, the state has lost over Rs 500 crore of automobile and automotive investment. These companies could have made the state a large automobile hub," said Gupta.

The recurring controversies over the issuance of the trade licence to the German major Metro Cash & Carry have not helped either.

A German delegation of 65 investors which came to India recently, refused to visit Kolkata, citing political instability as a reason. They went to Pune, Mumbai and Bangalore — so while Bengal has only 25 German companies, the city of Pune ended up with 250.

German auto component giant Bosch Wagon that designed and will manufacture 60 per cent of the auto components for Tata Motor's cheapest car Nano, has cancelled its plan to set up plant in the state.

"We had planned a plant in Singur for manufacturing braking systems, starters and generators at the insistence of our customers Tata Motors. Since the Tatas has moved to Sanand (Gujrat), we will also set up a plant there," said Rana Mathew, spokesperson, Bosch Ltd (Bangalore).

The Indian part of Bosch Wagon will be supplying the fuel injection system, starter motor, alternator, glow-park, generators and braking system to Tata Motor's Nano project at Sanand.

Bosch will also supply its latest gasoline engine parts and security systems to Nano from its Naganathapura plant in Karnataka. "Many prospective foreign delegations are understandably reluctant to travel when they read reports on industries being pulled out from West Bengal," said BG Mukherjee, regional director, Indo-German Chamber of Commerce. According to him, corporates are not bullish any more about fresh investments here unless they have a compelling reason.

"The political instability is being discussed by global CEOs and international venture capital and private equity funds. It's suffering from a brand dilution syndrome due to political ill-will and instability. Many potential investors have been moving away to peaceful pastures," added Mukherjee.

As of now, there are around eight German projects in the pipeline. Among the upcoming projects, is a German bakery.

According to an official of the company, it is looking at two spots ¿ in Rajarhat and Kasba industrial estate. Besides, there are seven companies, including a cable manufacturing company that intends to set up its plant on the eastern fringes of the city, four engineering companies, one brewery and a chemical factory.

Heading: Neighbour shoots at 14-year-old kite runner - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 25 people have succumbed to vector-borne diseases in the state during the last one month. Two more deaths were reported in the districts on Sunday, taking the toll to 25.

Mithu Pal (19), a resident of Diamond Harbour in South 24 Parganas, was suffering from fever for the past few days. She died on Sunday. "The girl was suffering from fever for the last few days. As I am yet to receive the medical report, I cannot confirm the cause of the death," said District Magistrate Sanghamitra Ghosh.

In the other incident, Uttam Saha of Murshidabad district died at the Behrampore Sadar Hospital on Saturday evening. District magistrate Pervez Ahmed Siddiqui confirmed the report. "According to the doctors, he died of a vector-borne disease. We are taking preventive measures to prevent further deaths," he said.

Pradesh Congress supporters, meanwhile, protested near Bhowanipore against the outbreak of vector-borne diseases in Kolkata and burnt an effigy of Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya.

Bhattacharya, however, remains unperturbed. "We have done what we can. We are trying our level best to check the spread of vector-borne diseases. The residents have to be more careful," he said.

Other than Kolkata, several districts including North and South 24 Parganas, Howrah, Hooghly, Bankura, East and West Midnapore have been hit by vector-borne diseases.

Heading: Singur turns battlefield again - Indian Express
Content:
A Sunday morning's kite-flying turned into a nasty experience for 14-year-old Enayat Hussain, when he was shot at by a local while trying to retrieve his kite. He suffered an injury on his right hand.

Hussain, a resident of 20 Palm Avenue, and his friends were at Rifle Range Road when a severed kite drifted into the residence of Deboprasad Guha at 15C Rifle Range Road.

Hussain began scaling the wall to retrieve the kite when Guha, a first floor resident, spotted him.

He became infuriated and asked them to leave, but the boys insisted that he return their kite, police said.

Guha then produced an airgun and in a bid to scare them, fired, but Hussain was hit.

Hearing his cries, locals collected in front of Guha's building and began berating him. A brick was lobbed at his house, breaking a window pane. But police brought the situation under control and arrested Guha.

A senior officer said Guha's reason for firing was that the boys had verbally abused him during the altercation.

Hussain, who studies in Class VIII at Surendranath Chakraborty Institute, was taken to the Chittaranjan National Medical College and provided treatment. "We only wanted to get our kite back. We are really shocked by his (Guha's) reaction. At that time I thought it was a real gun," Hussain told the media at the hospital.

Police said Guha would be produced in court on Monday.

Heading: Assam blasts: efforts on to make rail stations safer - Indian Express
Content:
20 injured in clashes between Save Nano Committee and Trinamool, Mamta convoy held up

Nano is gone, and now Mamata Banerjee finds herself at the receiving end of the ongoing agitation in Singur by the CPM-backed Save Nano Committee.

On Sunday, her convoy, on way to yet another rally at Singur, was stopped for nearly an hour at Maitypara near Dankuni. The official car of Leader of Opposition Partha Chatterjee was vandalised.

The clashes left at least 20 people injured while a goods vehicle and a police jeep, five motorbikes and over 50 cycles were gutted.

The trouble began early in the morning.

In a bid to renew her agitation in support of her demand to return land to unwilling farmers, Banerjee had called for a rally in Singur. The Save Nano Committee had announced that they would not allow the Trinamool leader to enter Singur. Roadblocks were set up at Ratanpur on National Highway 2 —about 5 kilometres from the site of the Tata's erstwhile small car factory.

The Trinamool supporters also began to gather at the same spot. A huge police contingent was present there, but they remained silent spectators as nearly 4,000-strong Trinamool supporters first clashed with 200-odd Save Nano Committee supporters and then the police. The mob burnt two vehicles, over 50 cycles and five motorbikes. The police had to resort to lathichage and tear gas to bring the situation under control. Trinamool leaders claimed that over 20 supporters of the party were injured.

Banerjee had a tough time reaching Singur. Her convoy had to come to a stop at Maitypara after the CPM men deflated tyres of two trucks to block the road.

The official car of Chatterjee, meanwhile, was intercepted and vandalised at Ghanashyampur, about two kilometres ahead of Ratanpur. There too, the police had to use four rounds of tear gas shells to separate the clashing groups, said IG (Law and Order) Raj Kanojia said. Four of the injured had two each from the rival factions. Chatterjee alleged that he had been manhandled by CPM workers in presence of 200 senior police officers. The police, however, denied the allegation.

The Superintendent of Police, Hooghly, Rajiv Mishra, said eight policemen were seriously injured in Trinamool brickbatting over the day. An office of the suppliers of materials for the Nano project at Ratanpur was burnt.

The Trinamool rally was held at Khaserchak, where Banerjee called for a state-wide agitation against Sunday's incidents. "We have shown what we can do. We are not afraid of the CPM," she announced. The protest will be held in Kolkata on Monday.

Heading: Travel agents resort to ‘Gandhigiri’ - Indian Express
Content:
In the backdrop of the recent bomb blasts in Assam, the Indian Railways has chalked out elaborate security arrangements for station premises to make them safer for the commuters.

Six stations under the Eastern Railways located in Kolkata will be the first ones to be fitted with the latest security installations. To begin with, the implements will be introduced at Sealdah, Bidhannagar, Dum Dum, Ballygunge, Kolkata and Majherhat. A minimum of Rs 5 crore has been earmarked for each station.

The Sealdah station alone will be fitted with 300 cameras — fixed, moving and zoom lens — which will monitor the movement of people entering and leaving the station premises. An alarm system will be in place to warn the authorities when there is overcrowding at a particular spot on the platform.

For the first time ever, the station premises and parking lots will be under the surveillance of vehicle scanners to keep a check on vehicles entering the station premises. "This will help in eliminating the chances of miscreants leaving behind vehicles stacked with explosives in parking lots," said a senior railway security official.

A bomb detection and disposal squad will be deployed at each station and more sniffer dogs will be brought in. Barbed fencing will also be erected around the station premises.

The project will be implemented on a build-own-operate-transfer (BOOT) system and is set to get underway by early next year.

According to the authorities, the main hurdle to the implementation of the project is the hawkers and vendors dotting the platform.

"Unless the unauthorised vendors are removed from the platforms, it will be difficult to put the system in place," said a senior railway official. Till date, the railway authorities' decision to evict vendors has met with stiff resistance from hawker unions.

Heading: State sitting on proposal to buy explosive detection machine - Indian Express
Content:
The decision of most airlines to stop giving commission to travel agents, slated to come into effect from Monday, is now on hold after the Travel Agents Federation of India secured a stay order from the Calcutta High Court.

Of the 16 airlines that were supposed to implement the decision from November 1, the big names include Lufthansa, Singapore Airlines, Jet Airways, Kingfisher, Jet Lite and Air India.

Others including British Airways, Thai Airways and Emirates have not yet arrived at any decision. They have, however, allowed agents to charge a transaction fee of Rs 350 and Rs 500 on economy and business class tickets in the domestic sector over and above the ticket price from tomorrow.

Passengers travelling overseas would be charged a maximum of Rs 2,500 for each economy class ticket, Rs 5,000 for business class and Rs 10,000 for first class depending on the distance to be flown. "We have our first hearing on November 3 and till then there is a status quo on the decision following a court order," said Anil Punjabi, chairman, eastern region, Travel Agents Federation of India.

The federation has, in the meantime, decided against agitation. It has taken recourse to 'Gandhigiri' or peaceful protest.

"Airline officials have been adamant and have stuck to their decision. But we have decided to tread the path of peace," said Punjabi.

Heading: Stringent visa rules lead to a dip in Bangladeshi tourists - Indian Express
Content:
Had the state government not been dilly-dallying for two years over a proposal to buy a state-of-the-art explosive detection machine, the explosion at Salboni targeting Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's convoy could have been averted, say experts.

A proposal to the state home department, to procure ground-probing radars, was made by the then additional director general of police, Rajat Majumdar.

This machine can detect improvised explosive devices burried upto four feet in the ground. The metal detectors that the West Bengal police use now can identify IEDs planted upto not more than 3 inches.

"Hand held metal detectors that the state police use now are of no use in case of IEDs planted deep into the ground. The detectors cannot detect explosives burried more than 3 inches deep," said Majumdar.

Majumdar, who had been associated with counter Maoist movements for a long time, claimed that he had given a proposal to the state home department to procure the ground-probing radars.

"These machines can detect IEDs and explosives burried upto 4 feet. They can be mounted on vehicles and roads can be checked just before a VIP or police patrol traverses through," Majumdar said.

The soil in the West Midnapore region, where the Maoists are very active, are high in ferrous content. This often gives faulty indications to metal detectors.

Majumdar claimed that the ground-probing radar could have also negated this hindrance. "The machine could have helped avert Sunday's explosion," Majumdar said.

Two years ago, a demonstration of the Rs 40 lakh machine, was given in front of the then chief secretary Prasad Ranjan Roy at the Alipur Police Line Ground. "A formal proposal to procure the machines was made to the home department. But for some unknown reason these machines were not bought," said Majumdar. The state police department preferred to stay with the old hand held metal detectors.

According to sources, the machines were not procured due to the high price. "The state government delayed the decision as the experts thought that the machines were very costly," said the source. Prasad Ranjan Ray was, however, not available for any comment.

Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti did not want to comment on the issue. ADG modernisation, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, said that he was not aware of any such proposal. "Actually I have joined recently. I will have to look into the old files," said Chatterjee.

Heading: Kolkata confidential - Indian Express
Content:
Charan Chandra Nath (name changed) has been doing the rounds of the visa office for an extension for his stay in India that expired on October 18.

Having come to the city for his father's surgery at R N Tagore International Institute of Cardiac Sciences the doctors have asked him to stay back for another month for the check-ups.

Since then he has been hanging around the visa office. "I gave them all my official documents including the letters from the doctors at the hospital but they refused to listen. At first they threw me out and then they took away all the papers. But they have refused to say whether they will extend the visa," said Nath, a resident of Chittagong.

"My father is in bad condition and I cannot take him back like this and neither can I leave him alone to die here," he added.

According to Nath, there are many like him who have been queuing up outside the visa office in Kolkata but are being turned down by the officials.

Following the arrest of Bangladeshi criminal Subrata Bayen alias Fateh Ali, the situation has further worsened for those who bank on these yearly visits to the city.

The reason for the decline, especially medical tourists, range from a dip in the number of visas being issued to stringent regulation and custom checking and the five-hour wait at the border for those travelling by the much-famed Maitreyee Express.

Basab Talukdar, DC Security Control, said the security has been beefed up following the arrest of Bayen.

"We get regular information of the foreigners including Bangladeshis' who put at various hotels across the city," said Talukdar.

Officials of the Resident Passport Office, Bangladesh and Pakistan admitted that the number of visas being issued to Bangladeshi tourists has decreased. Since July 2007, the visas given out were being put in different categories and there has been an effort to increase visas while cutting down tourist visas.

"Earlier, we would operate five buses but now we have only four buses. In the period between January and July this year, the number of tourists have dropped by 7,000," said a private tour bus operator.

"Before we would ask our passengers to book a week in advance. These days you can buy tickets on the day you travel," he added.

Tuni Sherinakther of Chittagong, who was in the city for a holiday, said: "Three years ago, I did not face as much problem as I did while coming this year. Getting a visa was the biggest problem that I faced. This coupled with the restrictions imposed by the Bangladesh government made it worse. I came with one-and-half-lakh taka, which was not sufficient for a fifteen-day holiday," she said.

For Palash Kumar Chandra of Chattogram Foreign Exchange, what has hit him the hardest is the government's decision to limit the maximum dollars that can be brought into the country. "By road a person can bring only $150 and $500 by air. It's ironical that tourists want to bring dollars into the country but the officers are stopping them at the borders," he said.

Sudder Street, known for its string of Bangladeshi restaurants, serving "halal" meat and special "Dhakai" food has now more Bengali customers than Bangladeshi. "We get more locals than Bangladeshis. There was a time when there were enough Bangladeshi tourists to fill the hall. These days it is the locals who visit here," said the proprietor of Sukriti hotel on Sudder Street.

Heading: Md Sporting play safe, settle for a draw - Indian Express
Content:
Big brother is watching

The purpose behind the installation of spy cameras inside Writers' was to enhance the security of the state government's headquarters. But now makes the police top brass jittery. Reason: now that their job has been taken over by cameras, the security personnel seem to have lowered their guards. Instructions have been issued to the cops that no slackness will be tolerated and vigilance will be maintained on them too — probably through the very same cameras!

An axe to grind

The state government is attributing last week's transfer of Ashok Banerjee, Assistant Commissioner, Writers' Buildings, to illness. But the grapevine has it that the transfer of the top cop was a sequel to the October 28 clashes between the CPM-affiliated Coordination Committee of State Government Employees and the other employees unions affiliated with the Opposition. Banerjee was apparently regarded as a complete failure, since he failed to do much about the clashes that have almost become a daily feature at the Writers' Building.

Is anybody listening?

In order to inculcate traffic safety awareness among its citizens, the Kolkata police have put up large digital boards with slogans on them. But last week, one of the boards developed a glitch. Result? The citizens received advice of a rather contradictory nature with the board boldly displaying, 'Obey no traffic rules'.

Foot in the mouth

The recent spate of malaria has often caught the Member, Mayor-in-Council, health, Subodh Dey, off his guard. Last week, during a gruelling media conference, when reporters claimed one Jhunuri Sahani had died of malaria, KMC officials present insisted that she had died from illness that stemmed from her addiction to alcohol. But they promptly had to backtrack when the reporters told them that Jhunuri was a sixty-year-old woman and a teetotaller. Throughout the verbal skirmish, Dey sat mum.

Sting in the tale

As the city reels under the impact of vector disease menace that has already claimed 18 lives, Chief Municipal Health Officer Deb Dwaipayan Chattopadhya has become a butt of jokes among the citizens. An SMS doing the rounds currently reads: "To kill mosquitoes, use DDT. And to kill men, there is DDC (the officer's initials)".

'Fished' off

Former Pakistan human rights minister Hamid Ansar Burney's desire to taste Bengali cuisine during his day-long visit to the city remained somewhat unfulfilled. After a rigorous schedule that involved meeting with various officials and Pakistani nationals looking for a way home, Burney and his son Fahad were famished. Late in the afternoon, they settled down to a lunch ordered from a prominent Bengali restaurant, only to find that the main dishes were all fish, something they're not fond of at all. In fact, there were three types of fish, but Burney refused to try any and managed with rice, dal and vegetables. His son only picked at fish for the sake of politeness. Both, however, did tuck into the rosogullas with relish.

Heading: Whiz kid Sayantan eager to go the Anand way - Indian Express
Content:
Depleted East Bengal put pressure in second half, but fail to convert their chances

On match eve, Mohammedan Sporting coach Sabbir Ali said his team would play to win. Today, after the goalless draw against East Bengal in the I-League match at Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK), he made a U-turn, and said: "Our first objective is to get out of the relegation zone. I'm happy with the way my boys played."

He rather should have rued the lost opportunity. East Bengal took the field sans four frontline players. Surkumar Singh was out, suspended. Goalkeeper Subrata Paul, centreback M Suresh and midfielder Mehtab Hossain missed the game owing to injury. Yusif Yakubu, apparently unwell, sought to be taken off in the 21st minute. Yet, Md Sporting could not muster the courage to go all out for a victory.

They had their chances though, some of them pretty close. A lovely inter-play between Sovan Chakrabarty and Mike Okoro in the 22nd minute saw the former set it up nicely for Theodore Sunday, who was off target from eight yards. Theo had another one-to-one with East Bengal goalie Abhra Mondal in the 53rd minute. But his final touch was weak that allowed Suley Musah to go round his goalkeeper and clear it off the line.

The first half was exciting with attacks and counter-attacks. Md Sporting impressed with their passing game. Especially, Okoro, with his languid elegance, was a joy to watch. East Bengal tried to hit on the break. In the 35th minute, East Bengal were awarded a freekick as Madhab Das tripped Sunil Chhetri just outside the box. Renedy Singh's curler was acrobatically saved by Md Sporting custodian Tharangachan Tungshang. The latter was very impressive under the bar and earned the Man of the Match award. The youngster showed promise.
