The black-and-white brigade lost the plot after the breather. Suddenly, errors started to creep in and apart from Anit Ghosh, the defence started to look vulnerable. Ali's tactics to play a waiting game in the second half allowed East Bengal gain an upper hand. In the 48th minute, the red-and-golds had a very strong appeal for a penalty when substitute Praveen Kumar's shot hit Ghosh's hand inside the box. Referee PK Bose negated the appeal and gave corner instead. Chhetri had a clear sight of the goal from that corner but hit over the crossbar.

In the 71st minute, a Rahim Nabi centre from the right once again found Chhetri inside the box. This time the header was on target but Tungshang was up to the task. Seven minutes later, Kumar wasted another from close range. Little wonder that East Bengal coach Stanley Rozario was a little upset after the match.

After six rounds, East Bengal are placed sixth in the league standings with eight points, while Md Sporting moved to 10th spot with six points.

Heading: Palate Poopers - Indian Express
Content:
Bengal Peerless to financially support champion duo

Just days after Viswanathan Anand made India proud by yet again bagging the world's best tag in Bonn, Kolkata young guns Sayantan Das and Diptayan Ghosh returned to the city today after conquering the world in the junior circuit last week.

Young Sayantan won the prestigious Under-12 title in the World Youth Chess Championship in Vietnam last week, while Diptayan finished a creditable fourth in the Under-10 world category, apart from bagging the gold in the Asian Youth Chess Championship.

"I am a great fan of Anand. I want to play like Anand someday," gushed young turk Sayantan after arriving in the city this morning even as shutterbugs and reporters hounded the duo. Officials of the Alekhine Chess Club and the All India Chess Federation (AICF) welcomed the two players upon their arrival and they were escorted to Gorky Sadan, where a gala felicitation function was held to honour Sayantan and Diptayan. Fittingly, the venue is where the two chess whiz kids grew up picking up the strings under the watchful eyes of the instructors of the Goodricke National Chess Academy (GNCA).

Sayantan and Diptayan came up with their stellar performances in Vietnam just two days after Anand saw off the challenge from Kramnik to reign supreme in Bonn in the matchplay format. Unfortunately for the two Kolkata masters, their exploits have been overshadowed to an extent by Anand's world champion effort.

Sayantan, who impressed with his world championship title win in the Under-12 circuit, recalled the Vietnam experience, which lasted two weeks. "The main reason why I won is simply the preparation factor. I was very well prepared for this event, that's why I was confident of making it to the top three standings there, and thankfully, I topped," Sayantan said. "It was after losing to Ian Darwin of the US — my only defeat there — that I took it upon myself to bring home the title. In the 10th round, I knew that I was right on track."

Sayantan, who was accompanied on the trip to Vietnam by his coach and guardian International Master Saptarshi Ray, has now set his eyes on earning the International Master norm.

Interestingly, much of Sayantan's homework was done from Kolkata by his advisor Niladri Bhattacharya, who coordinated with Saptarshi over the internet and passed on valuable suggestions to the kid en route to the title win.

The organisers of today's felicitation programme handed over a cheque worth Rs 50,000 to Sayantan and silver salvers to both. Diptayan, meanwhile, has already been gifted with a laptop by the organisers of the Youth Chess Championship in Vietnam.

The GNCA has been organising an annual school chess event in the city which has grown quite popular in no time. And its products are grandmasters Surya Sekhar Ganguly, Sandipan Chanda, Neelotpal Das, and then women grandmasters Nisha Mohota, Mary Ann Gomes. Then there are international master Sankar Roy, Arghyadip Das, Saptarshi Roy and many others.

Grandmaster Sandipan Chanda, who hails from the same city, expressed his joy over Sayantan and Diptayan's achievements in Vietnam. "From now on, I will help them in whichever way possible, whenever I am free. I couldn't receive any gold medal in any world event as a kid, but they did it. They should continue the hard work and should get to play in different world events," Chanda said.

In a heartening development, Bengal Peerless Group's chairman KS Bagchi promised in the course of the felicitation programme that his organisation would be funding the two boys' expenses from now on.

Heading: Rumour of MNS member’s arrival in city sparks protest - Indian Express
Content:
Now, not every inmate of the kitchen has the spunk of a certain chicken tikka. That it grows out of the sheeks and kadais to grace pizzas and lasagnas. Talk lists some disastrous marriages of lip-smacking goodies

Maggi Massacre

Picture life without Maggi. No midnight snacking in hostels, no fun sleepovers, no comfort binging post-break up, simply no food on a rainy day when Mum's sick. Life without the two-minute feast is worse than sitting through Ram Gopal Verma's Aag agree Maggi maniacs. But what happened when Maggi decided to go for a makeover, once going sweet and sour, once all chocolatey and once chatpata? "Sweet & Sour was almost scared me away from Maggi, but Chatpata surely killed it. I mean, how much ever I loved Maggi, it couldn't get used to it tasting like bhel, very soggy bhel at that," laughs Tanusree Nandan, a lawyer based in the city. And if you could eat a tandoori chicken flavoured black forest (yes, you're reading right) then you could have a shot at the chocolate version too!

Preposterous Paan

If there was ever anything as tempting as a sip from Dad's glass of whisky as a kid, it would be a bit of a paan torn from one corner. And among the best things about growing up, the liberty to chew on an extravagantly stuffed mitha paan, figures among the top few. But that is not license enough to mess around with the contents. "I had a chocolate paan, which has a spoon of chocolate sauce instead of gulkand in it outside the Priya shopping mall in Delhi. It was terrible," says Ankit Saraf, a student based in Delhi. Chocolate and paan are not meant for each other at all it seems. "I had a paan dipped in white chocolate and then frozen in a posh Salt Lake eatery. I wondered if there were worse ways to spoil a good meal," says Rituparna Bandyopadhyay, a media professional. Add to that the notorious paan flavoured Centre Fresh and some other chewing gums, paan had quite a few bad taste-fellows.

Mishti Mayhem

What do you get when you marry two of the greatest desserts of the world? If chocogolla, a hybrid of chocolate and rosogolla is anything to go by, then the result is nothing less than a disaster. It makes little sense to overwhelm syrupy rosogollas with rich chocolate sauce, but try and explain that to the pioneering sweet shop of the city which came up with this turkey. "I thought it was a good idea until I had my first chocogolla. Needless to say I haven't had one ever since," says Riya Sengupta, an employee of Star India. Yet, that didn't deter people from meddling with other iconic Bengali sweets like sandesh. "I remember this South Kolkata sweetshop came up with something called carrot sandesh. It tasted awful as it looked," says Anirban Ghosh, a student of Mass Communications with St Xavier's College. Even the humble mishti doi wasn't spared. Synthetic cousins like "chocolate mishti doi" and "pineapple mishti doi" were imposed on her. "The pineapple mishti doi tastes very funny. It's neither pineapple-y nor is it anything like mishti doi," says Patralika Chatterjee, a housewife from Park Circus.

Drinks that drowned

Can one really blame soft drinks giants? All colas taste the same. So what they do for variety? They try and play around with the way the colas look of course. Which is why you have had your friendly neighbourhood panwalla handing you bottles of what looked like kerosene and suspicious-looking pale yellow liquid. Now some scientist in the Cola lab in Florida must have thought that it is a great idea to make a drink look like, lets say it, pee, but we were certainly not buying. Then there was vanilla Coke. "It was like tasting sweetened vanilla essence," fumes Chitralekha Chatterjee, an airhostess with a private airline. Then of course there were weird experiments with health drinks. "Have you ever tried butterscotch Complan. It's so tasteless that it's not funny," says Madhurima Mukherjee, a teacher with the Cambridge School. The synthetic-y flavour of Rasna Khus Khus has invited a lot of flak too. "It is like having talcum powder dissolved in water," says Sushmit Chowdhury, an employee of a software firm.

Dosa Disasters

Now one thing we must realize, the South Indian delicacy dosa, is not crepe. It may look like it, it may have the same basic ingredients but there is one basic difference between the two. As a savoury snack, dosa doesn't lend itself well to dessert recipes. So it's not really a good idea to stuff your dosa with chocolates, strawberries or pineapple. "I once tasted pineapple dosa in an eatery in Central Kolkata, and I hated it," says Pranaadhika Dev Burman, who is associated with a popular city-based NGO. Another no-no, mixing dosa with meat. "In a five-star hotel in Delhi they presented a special kind of dosa which had meat fillings. I didn't like the  taste of it, maybe because the fact that we think of dosa as a vegetarian snack," says Sonal Gupta, a student with XLRI, Jamshedpur.

Chipped Chips

Now it's useless to start on the importance of potato chips and popcorn in our lives, because we simply can't live without them. And film producers would probably go bankrupt without them, but that's not reason enough to feel especially kind to some like the chatkila nimboo something from a chips company. Or the chocolate popcorn for that matter. "It actually tastes funny. I'm sure there are better ways to enjoy chocolate or popcorn," says Gargi Banerjee, a media professional based in Delhi.

Heading: DSP begins investigation in dowry death case - Indian Express
Content:
The Ludhiana railway station stood witness to vociferous sloganeering on Sunday as rumours were afloat that a representative of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) was to visit the city. The protest, which saw the raising of anti-Raj Thackeray slogans all morning, was called off later when the rumour turned out to be false.

The 50-odd persons who gathered at the railway station threatened that they would not let anybody from the MNS enter the city for their alleged bias against north Indians.

"We will not allow anybody from the MNS to enter the city unless they change their outlook towards north Indians. People from this part of the country are very angry with the happenings in Maharashtra. The role of Raj Thackeray is highly objectionable," said a protestor.

The protesters included A N Mishra, Vinod Mishra, Vipin Gupta and Shamsher Anand belonging to different organisations including Purvanchal Vikas Parishad, Jan Jagaran Parishad and Rashtriya Janta Dal among others.

Heading: People are turning towards Ayurveda - Indian Express
Content:
After the Division Number 7 police registered a dowry death case against the in-laws of a deceased woman on Saturday, the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Industrial Area, today started investigations into the matter.

The woman, identified as Poonam, had died on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday.

Division number 7 Station House Officer Harpal Singh said that DSP Harmohan Singh will, henceforth, investigate the matter.

Rajinder Kumar, the uncle of the deceased, had alleged that ever since the marriage of Poonam with Navjot Verma, a resident of Chuharpur road in Haibowal, nearly three years ago, she was subjected to dowry harassment.

In the last week of October, Kumar alleged, Poonam was beaten up by her in-laws for dowry that caused her to suffer a miscarriage.

Kumar had further alleged that when they brought Poonam home in Sanjay Gandhi colony, her in-laws came to their house on Friday night and beat her up again.

Consequently, she sustained injuries and when she was taken to a nearby private hospital, the doctors declared her "dead on arrival".

A case under Section 304-B (Dowry death) was registered against the in-laws of Poonam on the complaint of Rajinder Kumar.

Those booked in this case include the deceased's husband Navjot Verma, mother-in-law Prem Lata and brother-in-law Rakesh Kumar.

Police sources, meanwhile, stated that after the registration of the FIR, Poonam's in-laws had rejected the allegations as "false and baseless".

They, according to the police, counter-alleged that Poonam was "not medically fit". No arrest has been made in the case so far.

Heading: Budding city artiste to feature in TV serial - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Narinder Kumar Dhand recently took over as the District Ayurvedic and Unani Officer. In conversation with Sameer Kumar Sharma, he talks about the development plans for the ayurvedic department and the changing image of Ayurveda in the state

Q* With the government appointing regular district ayurvedic officers, we are witnessing a change in the image of the department. How far do you expect this to continue?

For most of my career as an Ayurvedic medical officer, there has never been proper supply of medicines, let alone proper building and infrastructure for the Ayurveda offices.

However, all this is gradually changing and the Health Minister Lakshmi Kanta Chawla has taken interest in the development of the Ayurvedic department in the state.

Q* There have been reports time and again that the Ayurvedic department staff members do not receive salaries on time. How is the situation now?

That is exactly what is going to change with the appointment of regular district ayurvedic officers in 14 districts.

Disburisng the salaries of staffers on time is our top priority.

We will ensure that all the employees receive their salaries on time.

Q* After the appointment of the AYUSH commissioner and the ayurvedic director, how does the department fare now?

It is true that states like Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have done really well when it comes to developing Ayurveda.

With Rakesh Sharma having taken over as the director and K B S Sidhu as Department of Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH) commissioner, we have been on the right track of development.

People are turning towards Ayurveda and it is high time that we upgrade our facilities in the state. The department is shaping up well.

Q* What are the new developments taking place?

We are soon going to have an Ayurvedic Wing at the Civil Hospital as part of the under-one-roof scheme of the Centre, wherein treatments under Ayurveda and Homoeopathy will be provided.

While Rs 35 lakh has been sanctioned for the same, a special ayurvedic clinic is being set up in Khanna.

Q* What are the challenges that you are faced with at present?

I want all the nearly 50 ayurvedic pharmacies in the district to work towards achieving the standards of Goods Manufacturing Practices (GMP) in order that we have well-packaged good ayurvedic medicines available in the market.

The staffers working in dispensaries need to be regularised and I will ensure this happens soon.

Heading: Body parts frequently injured during routine exercise discussed - Indian Express
Content:
Riding high on talent, a 10-year-old budding artiste from the city is all set to make her mark in the entertainment industry. Jannatpreet Kaur, who earlier featured in Babbu Maan's "Hashar" will now be seen displaying her acting skills in a mega serial — "Meet Mila De Rabba" — to be telecasted on Sony TV channel.

Having completed shooting in Punjab for nearly 12 episodes of the Ravi Kaushal serial, an elated Jannat said, "I hope viewers appreciate my acting. The directors of the serial are Rajesh Seth and Rajiv Bhanot. I play the role of a younger sister of 'Geet', one of the main characters."

Jannat's career began early as she featured in the advertisement for Verka when she was just five years old. Having acted in 14 different plays, including Dhukjde Kaleere and Meinu katal na karayo mapeyo, the child actress has also worked in two albums — Bindo and Bhali-Bhali — with eminent writers like Shamsher Sandhu.

This Class V student from Sargodha National Public Senior Secondary School has already worked in the Hindi flick — Modern Devdas.

On that experience, Jannat recalls, "I played the role of a cousin of the heroine of the film while Abhay Deol was the lead actor in the film."

Jannat has an elder sister and her mother, Sonia Mussafir, is a homemaker.

Her father Malkiat Singh, a serviceman, says, "In Meet Mila De Rabba, Jannat was selected without any audition. Her coordinator, Jasbir Dhillon, has always encouraged her a lot."

Crediting Nirmal Rishi for having given her career a fillip with Hashar, Jannat said," Nirmal aunty is a blessing for me. She is the real motivator."

Asked about her favourite actress, Jannat responds with a beaming smile, "Katrina Kaif".

Having worked as a model for some readymade garments, Jannat's ultimate aim is clear: "To become a famous actress."

Heading: Govt to set up informal schools in all slums: Dhanda - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Anatomy, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH), today organised the 8th CME and 3rd annual meet of Anatomical Society of India (ASI) at Dumra auditorium.

The conference started with a session of research papers presented by delegates from all leading medical and dental colleges of northern India. The CME having four hours accreditation from Punjab Medical Council was also held.

The Head of Anatomy Department, Dr Poonam Singh extended a warm welcome to the delegates present on the occasion. The principal of DMCH, Dr Daljit Singh lauded the efforts of the Department of Anatomy in organizing this CME-cum-annual meet of ASI. The Secretary of DMCH Managing Society, Prem Kumar Gupta was the chief guest on the occasion while the guest of honour was Dr S Bhardwaj, vice-president, DNB.

A souvenir was released by the chief guest along with the dignitaries present on the occasion including the Vice-Principal, Dr Jagdeep Whig, and medical superintendents Dr Rajoo Singh Chhina and Dr Balbir Singh Shah.

In the scientific lectures held during the CME, Dr Jaspal Sandhu, head of the Sports Medicine and Physiotherapy Department, GNDU, Amritsar discussed the anatomical aspects of causes of low-back pain and the importance of segmental stability. Dr Mohd Yamin, Prof and Head of Orthopedics Department, spoke on the injuries related to knee joint.

Dr Sanjay Wadhwa, Prof and Head of Rehabilitation Medicine, PGIMER, Chandigarh, talked about anatomical aspects of rehabilitation of sports injury. He highlighted that a large number of people encountered injuries during daily exercises. He said that if there was inadequate management, the chances of re-injury increased.

Dr Harpreet Singh Gill, Head of Orthopedics, SPS Apollo Hospital, Ludhiana, discussed common shoulder injuries like dislocation and impingement syndrome in daily routine. He said that shoulder injuries were quite common as certain activities involved repetitive, propulsive and explosive movements of the joint.

Detailed panel discussions on "Know your body limits" were held where panelists discussed the importance of exercise, anatomical sites frequently injured in routine exercise. There was a deliberation on management and rehabilitation of common injuries and role of exercise in osteoporosis was also discussed both for prevention and treatment.

Heading: Rights body raps police for sitting on info sought under RTI - Indian Express
Content:
Harish Rai Dhanda, Chief Parliamentary Secretary for Local Government, Punjab, today said that under Sarb Sikhia Abhiyan programme for children of 6 to 14 years of age, new informal schools were being set up in all the slum areas/jhugi dwelling units in the state.

Dhanda was addressing a gathering after inaugurating a school at Chand Colony, Haibowal Khurd, here on Sunday. He also distributed kits consisting of books, note-books and pencils etc to the children on the occasion.

Dhanda said that under this programme, the government would ensure to bring all the deprived children and drop outs back to schools, which will be set up in their colonies. He said that one student with plus two or BA pass from the same locality was being deputed teach the students in the schools, which would have minimum of 20 children and would be run four hours daily.

He said that in these schools, the students would be given basic education for one or two years and later they would be shifted to the regular government schools to enable them continue their studies. He urged the parents to keep a watch on their children to ensure regular attendance in the schools.

Dhanda announced that a new room would be constructed for these children and uniforms would be given before the start of the winter season. Among others present on the occasion were Balkar Singh Sandhu, councilor, P.C. Garg, advocate, and Balbir Singh.

Heading: Malwa Sabhyacharak to focus on girl child during Lohri fest - Indian Express
Content:
The Universal Human Rights Organisation has condemned the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Ludhiana for not providing information even under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

In this connection, the organisation on Sunday held a meeting under the chairmanship of it's head Satnam Singh Dhaliwal. While chairing the meeting, Dhaliwal said that their orgnisation had sought information from the SSP Ludhiana, who is also the public information officer (PIO) of the Ludhiana police, regarding an FIR in a murder case registered in 2001.

Dhaliwal said that in May this year, the SSP office sent a reply to them that this information could not be provided as the papers regarding that case had been presented in the court. He said that the police suggested them to get the certified copies of that case from the concerned court. He said that then their organisation approached the Jalandhar zonal inspector general, who asked Ludhiana SSP to act on this application keeping in mind the opinion of the district attorney.

Dhaliwal said that when no reply was received from Ludhiana police chief, their organisation moved the Punjab State Information Commission, Chandigarh. He said that even now, they have not got the required information from the police. The organisation has demanded speedy disposal of applications under the RTI Act.

Heading: Soldiers killed in 1984 riots: ex-servicemen to approach court - Indian Express
Content:
At a meeting of the executive committee of Malwa Sabhyacharak Manch, Punjab, held under the chairmanship of Krishan Kumar Bawa at the local Circuit House, on Sunday, a number of decisions were taken regarding celebration of Lohri festival.

Giving details, Bawa said that this year the focus would be on girl child during the festival, in which many non-resident Indians (NRIs) would be participating. The festival will be held at the Punjabi Bhawan here on January 8 and 9.

"On the first day of the festival, there will a seminar on `Women empowerment through curbing the menace of female foeticide,'" said Bawa, adding that the meritorious girls from various schools would be honoured with merit certificates. Also on the first day, various folk artistes from India and abroad would enthrall the audience by singing songs.

"This year, we are inviting the NRI parliamentarians from across the world that have made Punjab proud by getting elected to coveted positions," said Bawa, adding that Gurmit Singh Gill, president of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur International Manch, and Mandip Singh Hans, were coming especially from the USA and Harbant Singh Deol, from Canada to take part in the festival.

Heading: Sanjay Bhatia ton helps G&B XI win - Indian Express
Content:
Ex-servicemen in Punjab have decided to approach the judiciary against the Congress for allegedly hiding the names of armymen who were killed in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The decision was taken after the Army recently admitted for the first time that 34 soldiers were killed in the aftermath of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984.

Col Partap Singh Phoolka (retd), president of the ex-servicemen wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal and who has been leading the campaign, said over 200 Sikh soldiers were killed in the riots in northern India.

"The Congress was aware of the fact but tried to hide it. The then Congress government did not allow the Army to reveal the names," he said.

He further added that the government had hatched a conspiracy to hush up matter by labeling the soldiers as deserters. He said he would take up the matter with the authorities.

Heading: LDA houses already crumbling - Indian Express
Content:
Onir is ready to look at the funny side of relationships

His first two movies were pretty intense — My Brother Nikhil in 2005 and Bas Ek Pal a year later. Filmmaker Onir, 39, is now moving away from serious movies to have some fun. He experiments with comedy in Sorry Bhai, starring Shabana Azmi, Boman Irani, Sanjay Suri and Chitrangada Singh, who is back on screen after three years. "The idea is to explore different nuances of filmmaking," says Onir.

The romantic comedy, which will be released on November 28, is about a middle-class family from Mumbai going to Mauritius for their elder son's marriage. "Boman and Shabana share amazing chemistry on screen. I loved their performance in Honeymoon Travels Pvt Ltd and I am sure they will recreate the magic again," smiles Onir.

After wrapping up the promotion of Sorry Bhai, he wants to start his next venture, a yet untitled Indo-German collaboration that deals with the identity crisis of marginalised communities in India. And he also plans to direct the modern version of the 1980s classic Chashme Baddoor. "The original film dealt with the '80s. My script will be adapted for today's audience," he says. The fun run won't end soon.

Heading: Wait for Haj visa still on in Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
After a decade, probe confirms 60% houses under Vinamra, Vastu Khand Scheme dilapidated

It's now official: 60 per cent of the houses constructed under Vinamra and Vastu Khand Housing Scheme, Gomti Nagar, are in a dilapidated condition. This was revealed after a preliminary inquiry by a commission instituted by the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA).

After a physical survey done by the commission, LDA has now started photographing these damaged houses. Officials claim that almost 70 per cent documents related to these schemes are missing.

According to LDA officials, three years ago, an inquiry was set up to look into the matter under the then chief engineer but that probe was never completed.

A fresh inquiry was again instituted on September 19, 2008, under Joint Secretary Atal Kumar Rai.

The other two members of the committee include Chief Engineer R K Singh and Executive Engineer V K Goyal. "The houses under this scheme are in a bad condition. Files related to these houses are missing and we are carrying out photography of each of these houses," Rai said.

"The LDA engineers and contractors who are responsible for the poor quality construction of these houses have been identified. But the names of the same cannot be revealed at present because the probe is underway," said LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram.

The LDA had developed 1,303 houses of various categories in Vastu Khand and Vinamra Khand in 1998-99.

Sources said within few years after their construction, these houses were in a dilapidated condition. Walls and roofs of most of the houses had already collapsed.

Seeing the condition of these houses, allottees had refused to take possession and applied for refund. But by reducing the cost of houses, the LDA had managed to sell all the properties by 2005. But more than 80 per cent allottees have yet not taken their possession.

At present, there are less than 100 houses in which allottees are residing after demolishing the old structures and erecting new houses.

Neeraj Verma, resident of 3/727 Vastu Khand, said: "When my father had purchased this LIG house — 60 sq metre — 10 years ago, 65 per cent of it was missing. Doors and window grills were either misplaced or missing. I had to spend almost Rs 1 lakh to construct two new rooms and a kitchen here."

Heading: Imposter appears for re-examination at CSMMU, FIR lodged - Indian Express
Content:
Govt blames lack of coordination

The Mayawati government has blamed the lack of coordination between the Haj Committee of India and the Embassy of Saudi Arabia for the plight of the Haj pilgrims from the state.

The state government has apprised E Ahamed, Minister of State for External Affairs and the Consulate of Saudi Arabia about the matter. Addressing mediapersons on Sunday, Chief Secretary Atul Kumar Gupta said Chief Minister Mayawati was concerned about the situation.

Around 13,000 people from the state are to go for Haj by the Saudi Arabian airlines. The first batch of pilgrims was to leave on October 30, but the flight was cancelled as most people did not receive their passports or visa on time. By Sunday, 1,250 people who were to have left, are still waiting. Over 8,000 pilgrims and their families are staying at the Haj house, which has a capacity of barely 5,000 people. Angered over the delay, the Hajis have been organising road blockades for the last two days.

According to the Saudi Consulate office in Mumbai, the Chief Secretary said the problem occurred due to a staff reshuffle in the Embassy. "But if there was delay in sanctioning Visa, the Embassy should have informed the Haj Committee of India or the latter should have made its own inquiries," the Chief Secretary said. He pointed out that the Haj Committee of India makes all arrangements for Visa and makes travel plans for Hajis. Normally, the passport and visa arrives at least two days before a Haji has to travel.

Later, while speaking to mediapersons, Ahamed termed the allegations as "baseless and politically motivated". "The UP government is playing with the sentiments of Muslims. I have told the chief secretary that the Saudi Arab Consulate office was facing some problems with its computers. What can we do?"

Heading: Papers missing from Naini jail - Indian Express
Content:
The admission process at Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj Medical University (CSMMU) came under the scanner again when an imposter was caught appearing for dental hygienists re-examination on Sunday.

The re-examination was ordered after an admission scam was busted during the initial examinations in September. The entire process was cancelled and re-examination ordered for Sunday.

Manoj Kumar from Bihar was found appearing for the examination in place of Dinesh Kumar Sachan of Kanpur. Though they were suspicious, the invigilators initially allowed Manoj to take the examination.

Soon after the paper was over, Manoj was interrogated by the faculty members. After sometime, he admitted being a proxy candidate.

"His picture on the admit card was not matching. We still let him sit for the examination, as it would have disturbed other candidates," said Dr Abbas Mahdi, controller of examination at CSMMU. Manoj had met Dinesh at a coaching institute in Delhi, he added.

Later, Manoj was handed over to the police. An FIR of fraud under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code was lodged against him at the Chowk police station. Sources in the police said Manoj had not revealed any links to a professional gang of "munnabhais".

Heading: Oil stolen from Indian Oil pipeline in Mirzapur - Indian Express
Content:
Documents pertaining to some important cases have gone missing from Naini Central Jail.

The stolen documents include the records of the murder of woman inmate Baby Mishra inside the jail a few years ago, said officials in the jail.

Among the missing documents is also paper pertaining to a woman Inspector, Vijay Laxmi — who is currently in Naini jail in connection with a custody death — the gate record book and other papers.

Jail superintendent Kedar Nath has begun an inquiry into the matter and a complaint has been lodged with the Naini police station.

The matter came to light during the search of a file over the weekend.

Consequently, all officials were questioned and issued a warning.

Admitting that some documents are indeed missing, Nath, however, refused to provide details.

In his letter to the police, the superintendent expressed his apprehensions regarding the involvement of some jail officials, said one of the jail officials.

A complaint has been lodged, but no FIR has been filed yet, said the inspector of the Naini police station.

Heading: Lucknownama - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Oil Corporation has detected a breach in its pipeline in Mirzapur district, which has been used to steal a massive quantity of oil.

An FIR against unidentified persons has been lodged at the Pandari police station by the Indian Oil official A P Pandey. No one has been arrested. The company officials and police suspect the involvement of an engineer or technical person in the theft.

The incident came to light on Saturday, when the officials of Indian Oil detected a major leakage between Allahabad and Mirzapur. The breach, at Toswa village in the outskirts of the district, had showed up in the computer sensor. "We immediately rushed to the spot and found a hole in the pipeline through which diesel seemed to have been stolen. There was no spillage near the spot, though oil flows at a very high pressure in the pipeline," said Pretinder Singh, Superintendent of Police, Mirzapur.

Company officials who accompanied the police suspected the hand of an engineer or technical person, Singh said. If an unskilled person had tried to drill the hole, the pressure in the pipeline would have sprayed the oil up to a height of nearly 30 feet.

"We suspect that drilling took place about four days ago and Indian Oil officials suspect that over two tankers of diesel have been stolen," he said. Over the last few days, villagers of Mirzapur had noticed a jeep standing near the spot. An inter-state gang could also be involved in the incident, Singh said.

The pipeline starts from the refinery in Barauni (Bihar) and ends at Mathura. It supplies petrol, diesel and kerosene to a large number of depots along the 750-km stretch.

Heading: Sadhvi gives no lead to Gujarat cops - Indian Express
Content:
Wrong number, all the way
You may be a senior Special Task Force officer and head a branch known for its expertise in electronic surveillance. But it does not mean that you have mastered your mobile phone. And why worry, when you have your subordinates at your service?
The officer in question still needs assistance whenever he has to add a new number to his phonebook or check a text message. And his juniors, have the added responsibility of helping out. But the worst time, of course, is when a case relates to surveillance or call details of cellphones.

With love, from Uttar Pradesh
An eye for an eye makes the whole world blind. Instead of retaliating to the ruckus in Maharashtra caused by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, the state government is out to woo the Marathis. As a token of their love and acceptance for all castes and cultures, including the Marathis, the department of culture have gone ahead and named it's newly-constructed auditorium of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi as Sant Gatge Ji Maharaj Prekshgrah Auditorium. According to the officials, the auditorium has been named after the saint from Maharashtra to show their love and respect for everyone, including the Marathis.

Give me more, says BJP leader
For long, a senior BJP leader has been annoyed with the party leadership. His conspicuous absence from all party programmes is being largely talked about. People close to him reveal the reason behind this annoyance. The veteran leader recommended the name of his protege and long-time associate — a member council — for the Lucknow Lok Sabha seat. The party leadership, however, is unable to digest this demand. In the past, while mending the career of this protege, this dynamic leader sacrificed power. He has categorically stated that he will not speak in the matter of ticket distribution. But of course, he can show his displeasure to the party leadership for not accommodating his one recommendation.

Monkey power in Lucknow
With Maya at the helm of affairs, criminals have stopped striking at will. Just when the administration could have claimed that "jungle raj" is over, creatures from the jungle have unleashed a reign of terror in Lucknow. On Friday, an eight-year-old girl took her four-year-old brother in her arms and jumped from the rooftop as over two-dozen monkeys reportedly attacked them. While the boy lost his life, the girl has been in a critical condition. Alarmingly, it is not the first time that the monkeys have created chaos. Reports suggest there have been at least six other instances where people were bitten by monkeys. Recently, some monkeys were in the news when they jumped over a duct in the ICU of Sanjay Gandhi Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences, injuring an attendant. Cases of simians striking at will were also reported from posh residential colonies like Butler Palace and Dalibagh.
Interestingly, in a newspaper office, monkey menace made news for different reasons. Just as the forest department and the police prefer to play passing the buck over such incidents, crime reporters and those covering forest, LMC and health are confused as to who should report the "event".

Heading: Kashi-Badrinath Shankaracharyas defend Sadhvi Pragya - Indian Express
Content:
Yogic powers at hand, she's a tough nut to crack: cops

Her impeccable mastery over yoga has made Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur a very hard nut to crack. Gujarat policemen, who interrogated the Sadhvi for her suspected role in Modasa blast recently, admitted this on Sunday.

The four-member team of Sabarkantha district police that had reached Mumbai on Friday for further investigations in the Modasa blast case, returned to Ahmedabad on Sunday morning. During its stay in Mumbai, the team interrogated all the five suspects of Malegaon blast, who were in custody of the Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) of Mumbai police. The Gujarat policemen wanted to probe if any one of them had any role in the Modasa blasts as well.

Deputy Superintendent of Police K K Mysorewala, who interrogated the Sadhvi for nearly two hours in Mumbai, said: "Pragya is a post-graduate and a very confident woman. Moreover, being a Sadhvi for several years, she has also mastered yoga and yogic meditation. While interrogating her in connection with the Modasa blast, I found her very composed and in total control of her mind and body. She refused completely to have played any role in the Modasa blast."

About other Malegaon blast suspects whom the Gujarat police team interrogated in Mumbai, Mysorewala said that none of them has visited Modasa. "As of now, we have no evidence against any of the Malegaon suspects to link them with the Modasa blast. But this does not mean that we have given them a clean chit. Our investigations are on and we may interrogate them again if needed," he added.

Involvement of the Sadhvi and other suspects of Malegaon blast in the Modasa blast was suspected because of their similar pattern, similar modus operandi and almost synchronised timings. Moreover, both the blasts occurred near mosques in minority-dominated areas. This made speculation rife.

The Gujarat policemen, investigating the Modasa blast that killed a 15-year-old boy and injured many, have until now questioned more than 500 people, including members of saffron outfits such as Vishwa Hindu Parishad, Bajrang Dal, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (AVBP). They are, however, yet to get a strong lead in the case.

Heading: Another outfit protests against arrest - Indian Express
Content:
The Shankaracharya of Badrinath, who visited Vadodara for a religious function on Sunday, came out in defence of Sadhvi Pragya, who has been arrested in connection with the Malegaon-Modasa blasts. In a ceremony for the ten-day long Ati Maha Rudra Yagna, two Shankaracharyas from Kashi-Badrinath visited the city.

Jagatguru Vasudevanand of Jyotirmath in Badrinath and Jagatguru Vidyanand, while addressing mediapersons, said, "Any person who is completely dedicated to dharma cannot do any adharma. She is an idol of peace and we would never give in to any such controversies."

While both the religious heads are in the state for the first time, one of the organisers of the Ati Maha Rudra Yagna Sewa Samiti and former BJP councillor, Pradeep Joshi, said: "This is for the first time that the yagna is being conducted in the state. Its purpose is to strengthen the stand on religion and understand the true meaning of Hindu dharma."

The yagna is being held on Old Padra Road.

He further said, "Attaining this spiritual stature is not something that can be achieved overnight. And Sadhvi Pragya's dignity cannot be questioned."

Heading: Pride of Gir finally in cage after ten-day chase by Forest Department - Indian Express
Content:
A new Hindu outfit — Vishwa Hindu Seva Samiti (VHSS) — has come forward in protest against Sadhvi Pragya's arrest by the Mumbai Anti-Terrosim Squad (ATS) in the Malegaon blast case.

At a press conference held in Surat on Sunday, the samiti members announced that they would take out a rally to protest the arrest and mobilise public support for her.

Coming in front of the media for the first time to oppose the arrest, the newly formed VHSS organised the briefing at Jay Ambe Temple in Rander. The samiti members, largely comprising of college students and service class youths, claimed that Sadhvi was innocent and was being wrongfully grilled.

Formed a month ago, the samiti is still in the process of being registered.

VHSS president Nirav Rana said: "We will not tolerate the insult on Hindu sants and sadhvis. We will start an agitation and perform programmes in Surat in the coming days. We want to give opportunity to all Hindu teenagers, including girls, to come and work for the protection of Hindu religion. People of our community are shocked and cannot even believe that a Hindu saint can in any way be involved in terrorist activities. The Mumbai ATS has done brain-mapping, polygraphic and even narco tests on Sadhvi Pragya, but have failed to find details about the attack. Somebody has to fight for her and we have taken the initiative."

Heading: Septuagenarian leads underprivileged children to light - Indian Express
Content:
The lions had strayed into human habitat in Gondal; will be rehabilitated in Sakkarbaug Zoo

The pride of lions that had strayed into human habitat in Gondal area of Rajkot from Gir, was finally captured by the Forest Department early on Sunday after a ten-day chase.

Ten days ago, a full-grown lioness and her three cubs (not full-grown) had come out of Dhari, the north side sanctuary area of Gir forest and reached Rajkot district, more than 150 kilometres from the sanctuary. Forest teams of Rajkot, Sasan and Dhari consisting of more than 60 personnel including veterinary doctors and senior officers had been after the lions ever since.

When contacted, Lalit Parmar, the Rajkot District Forest Officer who was part of this mission said: "This was the first such long operation in Gir forest. It was a terrific experience for all of us who followed the lions for 10 days and 10 nights non-stop through farms and grasslands."

He added: "On the night of October 30 (Thursday), we captured one 'Pathdo' (half grown) lion and then on Friday we tranquillised the lioness. On Saturday night, another half grown lion was captured and a few hours later, early on Sunday, we finally captured the fourth in a ring cage set up in the grassland. The entire forest staff had been camping in the grassland for the last four days and had installed seven ring cages at various places by cordoning off the entire grassland. It took us long to complete the operation, as the area was unknown to us and the topography was new. We are satisfied that neither the lions nor humans were hurt in the process."

All the four captured lions were sent to the Sakkarbaug Zoo on Sunday. According to Forest Department sources, the lioness and her cubs had strayed into human habitat on three occasions in the past. Every time, the forest staff had captured and taken them back to the forest. Fortunately, a radio collar was tied around the lioness' neck, which helped the foresters to locate her easily.

Heading: Thieves strike at Rajkot industrialist’s bungalow - Indian Express
Content:
A septuagenarian has been running coaching classes at Mangrol Port in Junagadh district that have no admission hassles, no donation and no fees either. Everyone in this port town in Saurashtra knows Muljibhai Gosiya (71).

For the last 40 years, Muljibhai has been single-handedly educating students from kindergarten to Class IX after school hours. He had himself studied only up to the Class VII, yet some of his former students are now doctors, merchants and community leaders. He holds free coaching classes everyday, even on Sunday and never keeps a single holiday throughout the year.

Muljibhai belongs to the fishermen community and has a family of seven. He is physically challenged and has to work as a painter or labourer to make both ends meet. Nevertheless, he runs coaching classes at his house at Sadhana Society on the outskirts of Mangrol town. He runs two batches — one from 8 am to 10 am and an other from 5 pm to 6 pm — in which around 70 students, mostly from the fishermen community are enrolled.

"Educating poor students has always been my first priority; coaching is my hobby. There is no holiday even on New Year or Diwali. There is no Sunday or a weekly off," he said.

Muljibhai had begun his mission to educate the downtrodden sections of society in the early sixties. His own community is economically, socially and educationally backward. Children from other communities have been his students as well. He said that he needs no finance for coaching the students. However, sometimes he receives donation, which he uses either for breakfast or for picnics.

Govind Gosiya, a fisherman leader and trader selling hardware, paints and fishing materials in a shop at Mangrol port, was Muljibhai's student. He said: "He changed my life. I had taken coaching from him for four years from 1964 to 1968. At that time, there was no electricity here. He had taught students with lamps at night."

Dhanji Bhai (45), a fisherman at Mangrol port, said that fishermen here know reading and writing, thanks to Muljibhai. "He is the man who imparted primary education to us and inspired us for a better life," he said.

Muljibhai's students come to him after school. He helps them in their studies, checks their homework, solves their problems and coaches them. In spite of his educational limitation, he has been teaching students up to Class IX. His mission has certainly brought about changes and educational awareness among the downtrodden in general and the fishermen in particular.

Heading: Water tops priority list for Pollution Control Board - Indian Express
Content:
Rs 22 lakh in cash and gold and silver ornaments worth Rs 4 lakh were stolen from the house; cops suspect Nepali guard's involvement in crime

In the second biggest housebreaking incident in the history of Rajkot city, cash and valuables worth Rs 26 lakh were stolen by unidentified thieves from the bungalow of a well-known industrialist of the city on Sunday. The theft took place when Dr Sailesh Makadia, owner of Radhe Group of Industries, and his entire family was enjoying festive holidays in Amreli.

Dr Makadia's four-storey house, bungalow number 125, Vrindawan Society in Kalawad Road area, had been locked since the last four days. The Rajkot police are suspecting involvement of Makadias' Nepali guard, Dipendra Neplai alies Kancho in the theft.

Dipendra had been working with Dr Makadia for the last one year.

However, when the family returned on Sunday, they found their house ransacked and the guard missing. All the locks of the doors were not even touched by the thieves, who entered the house through the elevator and reached for lockers installed in cupboards situated on the second and third floors of the bungalow.

According to Dr Makadia, cash to the tune of Rs 22 lakh and gold and silver ornaments worth Rs 4 lakh were missing from the lockers.

In the past few cases of theft in Rajkot, the police have observed that Nepali guards first conduct the theft and then escape to Nepal with the stolen booty. In this case as well, the police are suspecting Dipendra of fleeing to his native village.

The police have detained other Nepali workers and guards working in Dr Makadia's office for further inquiry.

Heading: Seven Pakistani fishermen arrested near Jakhau coast - Indian Express
Content:
In its Annual Action Plan for the year 2008-09, the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) has given the highest priority to pollution control in identified river stretches and lakes within the time frame of March 2009.

The river stretches include Ambika, Khari, Tapi, Amlakhadi, Kolak, Purna, Mahi, Mindhola, Dhadhar, Bhadar and Sabarmati, while the lakes are Kankaria, Sursagar and Ranmal.

For this, the GPCB is considering reviewing all the permissions granted to dispose trade effluents and sewage into the water bodies of the state. At the same time, the Common Effluent Treatment Plants are being upgraded through ongoing performance studies.

In addition to this, GPCB is also monitoring coastal waters surrounding the outfall of disposal pipelines with respect to the National Institute of Oceanography report. As per the report, all outfalls must be into the sea. A provision of water metres on bore well lines of all water intensive industrial units is also being looked into.

Another important measure that the GPCB is considering is the installation of two low- cost Sewage Treatment Plants (STP) with water cess fund, one in Visnagar in Mehsana and the other in Viramgam in Ahmedabad. Two other STPs are also being planned in Limbi in Surendranagar and Kalol in Panchmahals with support from Department of Environment and Forests.

Heading: Free education for kids from next academic session - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) seized a Pakistani fishing boat and apprehended seven Pakistani fishermen onboard from Indian waters near Jakhau coast in Bhuj district on Friday afternoon.

The motorised boat, named Al-Ahujja, had strayed more than 14 kilometres into Indian waters, officials said.

The ICG ship, Tarabai, intercepted Al-Ahujja some 40 nautical miles off the west of Jakhau coast and apprehended Abdul Rahim, Noor Hakim, Majid Alam, Naseer Hussain, Mohammed Yusuf, Madma Kasim and Mamad Usman, all residents of Karachi.

The ICG officials also seized more than a tonne of fresh fish from the boat. Wing Commander Satish Menon, Defence spokesperson, ICG, said: "All the seven Pakistani nationals were brought to Porbandar and handed over to the local police for further investigation."

The Porbandar police later transferred the case to Okha police station in Jamnagar district, as the said arrest was made from an area that comes under jurisdiction of the Okha police.

Earlier, the ICG had apprehended eight Pakistani nationals from an island near Jakhau on October 19 this year. A hired Pakistani motorboat had dropped the eight there.

A day before these arrests, the ICG had unearthed a liquor smuggling racket through the sea route and caught 12 foreign liquor laden fishing boats, some 20 miles off the Jakhau coast, on October 18 this year.

Heading: Alang ship-breaking industry hit by global recession - Indian Express
Content:
Policy's implementation cost of Rs 400 crore to be shared by Centre and state

From the next academic year (2009-2010), all children in the state between the age of six and 14 years will get free and compulsory education, as per the national law policy.

A senior officer from the State Education Department said, "We are waiting for the primary objectives and issues from the Central government. The policy will come into affect as soon as we get it."

State Education Minister Ramanlal Vora, however, told Newsline: "We already have a state policy of free and compulsory education for kids between six and 14 years of age, and it is being followed from a long time. We do not have details of the national policy at present. So before commenting on it, I need to check its contents. As of now, I cannot say when we can start work on it."

Maya Kodnani, Minister of State, Women and Child Welfare and Higher Education, said, "The state is already committed when it comes to education. Whether the Centre makes a policy or not, the state already has its own policy and we keep upgrading it from time to time."

"Through our various state policies, we are way ahead of national education policies. Moreover, everyone knows the way Gujarat is progressing in the education sector," she added.

The national policy's implementation will cost Rs 400 crore, which will be shared by the Centre and the state.

Heading: Gujarat govt justifies Nandy’s prosecution - Indian Express
Content:
Steep fall in scrap prices and strengthening of the US dollar against the rupee have badly impacted the already ailing ship breaking industry at Alang in Bhavnagar district.

According to ship-breakers, the industry is passing through its "worst recession", as the steel scrap market fell by almost 50 per cent in the last two months, while the dollar has become stronger against the rupee, hitting the industry hard.

These two factors have pushed the industry into "recession" despite the fact that a good number of ships arrived in Alang in the last two months.

"In the last two months, more than 30 ships in the range of 3,000 to 15,000 tonnes have arrived at Alang for dismantling," Bhavnagar-based international ship agent Mehul Mehta told PTI.

A leading ship breaker, Hareshsinh Parmar, said, "The international market of steel scrap was at USD 600 per tonne two months ago, which has now fallen to just 150 USD per tonne."

In the local market, cost of steel scrap has fallen from Rs 32,000 per tonne to Rs 16,500 per tonne.

"We used to sell steel plates at Rs 32,000 per tonne here. Now, we are selling at around Rs 16,500 per tonne. There has been a drastic fall in the market, making it extremely difficult to survive," Parmar said.

In September, ship prices were USD 750 per tonne. But at present, it is around USD 150 per tonne, Parmar added.

Another blow that hit the industry very hard has come from fluctuations in the international currency market.

"This makes a huge difference to us as we have to make the entire payment for buying ships in dollars only," Mehta added. According to the two, the industry will suffer a lot if the international and local scrap markets do not improve and exchange rates do not stabilise.

"Some improvement in the scrap market and stability in currency is what we are waiting for to run the industry, otherwise it is becoming increasingly unviable," Mehta said.

Heading: In debt, mini truck driver commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat government has justified the criminal prosecution of political analyst Ashis Nandy for writing an article in a national daily allegedly portraying the state in bad light and has pleaded the Delhi High Court not to interfere in the proceeding at this stage.

Filing a response on Nandy's petition seeking quashing of proceeding against him in Ahmedabad, the Narendra Modi government has said that the FIR registered against Nandy cannot be transferred to the national capital and the Delhi High Court should not interfere in the ongoing investigation.

"It is submitted that the FIR in this case prima facie discloses the offence under the Criminal Procedure Code and the court should not interfere and allow the investigation to be completed," the state government said in it's seven-page affidavit filed in the High Court.

"It has been held time and again by courts that the power of quashing criminal proceeding should be exercised sparingly with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases," it said, adding that the government had allowed the prosecution of Nandy after perusing the article published in a national daily in December last year.

The government was responding to the notice issued to it by the High Court on June 25 on Nandy's plea. An FIR was filed in Ahmedabad by an NGO, National Council for Civil Liberties, alleging that the article written after the last assembly elections projected the state in bad light and promoted communal disharmony between Hindus and Muslims.

Earlier, Nandy had approached the Supreme Court after the High Court refused to restrain the Gujarat Police from arresting him. The apex court on July 1 had restrained the police from arresting him.

Nandy's counsel had contended in the apex court that the FIR was registered out of malafide intention and was aimed at penalising and depriving him of expressing his sincere and bonafide views.

Heading: Mother sets herself, two minor sons afire - Indian Express
Content:
A 30-year-old mini truck driver from Bapunagar, Jagdish Makwana, allegedly committed suicide by consuming poison late on Saturday. Police said that the incident resulted after a private finance company confiscated the deceased's vehicle after he failed to pay back the loan. About two years ago, the company had financed an Eicher mini truck for Makwana.

Preliminary police investigations revealed that Makwana had not paid the loan instalments for the last six months. He owed nearly Rs 2.5 lakh to the company, police said. The recovery agents of the company finally confiscated the vehicle last week, the police added. "His family members have told us that Makwana was mentally disturbed, as the mini truck was the only source of his income. It seems he took the extreme step because of this reason," said Inspector K P Gajipura of Bapunagar police.

On Saturday night, Makwana, who stayed in Khodiyarnagar Ni Chali in Bapunagar, allegedly consumed poison near Satyam Flats in Bapunagar, while he was on his way home. One of his acquaintances saw Makwana lying on the roadside in a semi-conscious state and intimated his family members, police added.

Makwana was rushed to the V S Hospital, where he died during treatment. The Bapunagar police have sent his body for post-mortem examination and are waiting for the report to ascertain the actual cause of death. Meanwhile, a complaint of accidental death has been registered and investigations are on.

Heading: Deprived, sweepers seek permission for mass suicide - Indian Express
Content:
In a mass suicide attempt at Khimrana village of Jamnagar district on Sunday, three persons including two children and their mother died of serious burn injuries.

Twenty-seven-year-old Bhagwatiben Satwara committed suicide by setting herself and her two sons — Jaysukh (6) and Pankaj (5) — afire at her residence Chamunda Krupa in Khimrana village, situated some 16 kilometres from Jamnagar city on the Rajkot Highway.

According to Khimrana police records, Bhagwatiben's husband Shantilala Khimji Satwara (28), is a labourer in a brass work unit in

Jamnagar. Their marriage was seven years old.

On Sunday afternoon, due to some unknown reason, Bhagwatiben set herself and her sons afire. While Pankaj and Jaysukh died on the spot, Bhagwatiben breathed her last in the burns ward of G G Hospital in Jamnagar. The incident occurred around 11.30 am on Sunday. Shantilala informed the police at 3.15 pm. The police, fire brigade and 108 emergency services rushed to the spot. The reason behind the suicide is not yet confirmed, as the police are investigating the matter.

Heading: After tourism, city now turns to the hospitality industry - Indian Express
Content:
Sweepers from the Valmiki and Dalit community of Gandhinagar have written to the President of India, Pratibha Patil, requesting her to permit them to commit mass suicide.

Deprived of proper wages, housing, sanitation and other basic amenities, about 35 sweepers have signed the petition for mass self-immolation.

There are 164 manual scavengers in the city. Out of these, 94 are on record, whereas 70 nameless labourers have been working in the capital city since 1992. These workers earn Rs 30 per day and work for 8-10 hours instead of the promised four hours of work.

After repeated appeals to the state government, the workers started a campaign in August this year to protest against the injustice being done to them.

As many as 94 labourers have been involved in this campaign, but it has had little impact on the government.

The workers have been toiling hard for years to manage two meals a day and educate their children.

Heading: Four private security guards arrested in Reliance Petrol Pump loot case - Indian Express
Content:
After taking a decision on developing the city into a tourist hotspot, the state is now inching towards a fresh goal — turning it into a dynamic destination for holding meets.

With the recently concluded World Health Organisation (WHO) meet in Ahmedabad, Gujarat has taken one step ahead in attracting international-level conferences. Ahmedabad has hosted quite a few important corporate meetings in the past. This, perhaps, because of the economic activities happening in the city, as well as the state.

Tourism Minister Jay Narayan Vyas said: "While the WHO meet held recently in Ahmedabad was outside the capital for the first time, Gujarat is increasingly playing host to a number of conferences. This is an indicator of how our state is being perceived by corporate groups and that we are gaining importance in terms of being preferred as a destination for all kinds of activities."

Ahmedabad alone has seen an influx of demand for 'meeting locations' and is thereby increasing a number of related facilities. Vyas further said: "The three and four star hotels under construction will add a whopping figure of 3,500 rooms, to the already existing hospitality industry in Ahmedabad in a year's time. The figure is again an indication of the kind of demand that exists in the city. Gujarat will emerge as a prime location for conferences and meetings in a few years."

Heading: VMC to rehabilitate Vishwamitri crocodiles in Ajwa Sarovar - Indian Express
Content:
This is the first time that loot involving private security guards has occurred in the region, say cops

Four security guards, three from Uttar Pradesh and one from Madhya Pradesh, were nabbed by Vadodara district police on Sunday afternoon from the office of a private security agency based in Godhra.

On Wednesday, the four had looted the Reliance Petrol Pump on the Ahmedabad-Vadodara Expressway by robbing Rs 30,000 from the safe, after beating up two employees, Siraj Malik and Jitendra Lakdana.

Police officials say that this is for the first time that loot involving private security guards had occurred in the region.

According to Bhadarva Police Sub-Inspector, M.M. Puar, who is investigating the case, the police started questioning Maninder Singh Yadav, the guard of the Reliance Plaza restaurant attached to the petrol pump on the expressway. Yadav was present on the spot when the loot took place.

"Yadav's version of the loot had many loopholes. When we scanned the mobile phone records and observed his movement for the next 24 hours, we found he knew more than what he was telling us," said Puar.

On Saturday, Yadav was again detained for interrogation when he finally confessed that he had masterminded the loot along with the other three security guards, Umesh Kumar Dayal alias Chote Prabhu, Sompal Yadav alias Sanjay and Ramsevak Bhadoria alias Kallu from the Godhra-based security agency, Capsule Security Company.

"While Yadav kept a watch on the vehicles coming to the petrol pump, the other three took advantage of less traffic on the expressway, switched off the lights and attacked the employees," said Puar.

He added that Dayal, Sompal Yadav, Maninder Yadav are from the Mainpuri district of Uttar Pradesh, while Bhadoria is from Bhid district in Madhya Pradesh.

Heading: Defunct equipment ail SSG Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
With the commencement of the Vishwamitri dredging project, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has issued a notification for the rehabilitation of 50 crocodiles of the river in Ajwa Sarovar.

The announcement comes after the civic body had issued a stern notification to forest officials and NGOs against releasing stray crocodiles into Ajwa Sarovar just a month ago.

Though VMC plans to start the rehabilitation of the reptiles from November 13 along with crocodile rescue organisations, certain NGOs have voiced against the two-faced decision of the corporation.

"This was the first question that I raised during the meeting. One day they say that the Ajwa has surpassed the capacity to hold more crocodiles and the next day there is suddenly space for 50 of these reptiles. The decision is obviously crafted to suit their (VMC's) purpose, because the rescued crocodiles are those that stray away from the Vishwamitri belt itself and many of these reptiles enter the Vishwamitri from the Sarovar. So where is the question of rehabilitating additional reptiles in the Sarovar," said Ashok Pawar, president of city-based crocodile rescue team, Late Rohan Crocodile Charitable Trust, which will be a part of the VMC''s crocodile rehabilitation drive.

After notifying the ban on September 20, forest officials and NGOs were left with the option to rehabilitate the rescued crocodiles at Dev dam, Sukhi dam or at Karjan.

There are over 100 crocodiles in the Vishwamitri belt. While the VMC estimates that the dredging of the river will take over two years time, 50 crocodiles will be rehabilitated to Ajwa Sarovar and the remaining crocodiles will be enclosed at various points of the belt as the work progresses.

"The decision was made after taking in the opinions of the NGOs for maintaining the security of the crocodiles. As we start, over five to six crocodiles will be rehabilitated by the NGOs everyday," said city mayor Balkrishna Shukla.

Heading: Rajkot coach hits bull’s eye in cost-cutting bid - Indian Express
Content:
It was 10.30 in the night when six-year-old Sukhdev Rathwa had to be rushed to the SSG Hospital from Kawant with severe head injuries that he received from a leopard attack.

But coming under hospital's care did not bring much relief to the family. Despite registering the case, the doctors asked the family to get his CT Scan done from outside the hospital. For, the hospital's CT Scan machine had been lying defunct for the last three years.

The CT Scan was required to confirm the intensity of the injury and the family had to fork out more than Rs 1,500 to get it done from a private imaging centre.

For the boy's parents, who work as labourers in a farm in Kawant, the amount was astronomical, but they managed the huge expenditure somehow.

This is not an isolated case where the poor have had to shell out a huge amount for tests conducted outside the hospital.

Despite a poor economic background, people are sent to private clinics for various pathological tests.

According to information drawn from the hospital's emergency ward, most of the casualties reported are of road accidents.

"Over 70 per cent of the accident patients are told to get a CT scan or an MRI done. Almost every patient referred here either belongs to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category or is from the tribal or interior areas, hardly able to bare the expenses. One CT Scan costs anywhere between Rs 1,200 and 2,500," said a doctor. Unable to bear the expenses, many patients return without treatment.

Admitting that most of the machines are defunct, the medical administrator of the hospital said: "The machines donated to the hospital by the State government are over a decade old. Moreover, they were second hand machines. The machines are so badly damaged that there is no point in repairing them."

Hospital authorities confirm that the state government has signed a memorandum of understanding with private firms for replacement of the machines. However, not many are optimistic about it. Doctors themselves are sceptical about the lab reports that are forwarded to them by the hospital.

"The X-Ray plates do not have the clarity that is required for a proper diagnosis. I don't have complete trust on the pathological reports of the hospital. The lab argues that there is a huge staff crunch, I would rather rely on reports from outside the hospital," said a doctor on condition of anonymity.

Heading: 3 dowry cases reported in city in 24 hours - Indian Express
Content:
Now, archery students will not have to go to Kolkata and north-eastern states to order bows and other equipment

There's good news for archers in the state. In a bid to cut the cost of ordering archery equipment from other states, a coach from Rajkot has started making Indian traditional bows styled in the lines of International Recovery bows.

"Archery students have to go to Kolkata and north-eastern states to order bows and other equipment. There, they pay Rs 6,000-7000 for arrows and bows alone. But now, students do not have to go to these places. The equipment manufactured here costs Rs 6,000 with a kit bag and 15 other additional equipment which includes arrows and strings," said Deepak Joshi, the one-man manufacturer under the name of Sharp Archery.

Joshi also heads the Rajkot Archery Association as its secretary. For the first time, he managed to get Open State Archery Competition for juniors and seniors to the city.

"The state has a lot of potential for archery, but sports such as cricket have overshadowed its presence. I had been making archery equipment for the past two years, but now I have started getting customers," Joshi said.

The making of a set of bow and arrows along with the equipment takes around 15 days. Joshi, with his indigenously developed skills, makes 10-15 bows per year for the archery students. "I have used some of the methods used by our tribal friends from Madhya Pradesh and eastern Gujarat, but the demand is such that only 10-15 bows are sold. I want to manufacture recovery bows, but it requires an infrastructure," he said.

Joshi added that if the Sports Authority of Gujarat provides him the means to manufacture more equipment, he would like to start a showroom in the tribal districts of the state.

Archery Association of Gujarat (AAG) has extended full-fledged support to Joshi in his venture. "Now, Gujarati archers do not have to spend extra money in travelling, as the equipment is available in Rajkot. AAG has approved of the equipment," said Ketan Trivedi, member and coach of AAG.

Heading: 'N Indians adding to travel woes of Marathis' - Indian Express
Content:
At least three cases of domestic violence related to dowry were registered in various police stations in the city on Saturday.

All the three victims filed the complaints after being unable to withstand the pressure of their in-laws for dowry.

According to police officials at Jawaharnagar police station, Nehal Vaghela, a resident of Salatwada Bawan Chali in Harijan Vas, filed a complaint against her husband Mahesh Vaghela, mother-in-law Jyoti Vaghela, sisters-in-law Daksha, Beena and Jashi Vaghela, residents of Udera Gam Harijanvas, accusing them of torturing her for the last six months. On October 29, she escaped to her parents' house in Salatwada and later filed the complaint. She has charged her in-laws with physically and mentally torturing her every night when all the neighbours would go off to sleep.

Meanwhile, Punam Shah, a resident of Anandnagar under Karelibaugh police station, has charged her husband Vijay Shah, brother-in-law Kamlesh Shah and sister-in-law Anjali Shah with mentally torturing her for the past one-and-a-half years. Police officials could not confirm if there was demand for dowry. Punam has stated that she was always made to work much more than she could manage and when she refused to work her husband threatened her with divorce.

On the other hand, Raziya Sheikh, a resident of Mehboobpura-Imambada, filed a case against her husband Mazhar Sheikh, mother-in-law Bismillah Sheikh and brother-in-law Munawar Sheikh, accusing them of torturing her for the last two years because her family could not pay Rs 34,000 as dowry. Panigate police investigating the matter said Raziya was beaten up every night for not bringing dowry.

Heading: Normal life hit by Assam bandh against serial blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a fresh swipe against the North Indian population in the state, Shiv Sena on Monday alleged that their burgeoning population in the metropolis was adding to the travel woes of 'Marathi Manoos'

"It is an irony that the Marathi 'manoos' to whom Mumbai belongs, finds it hard to even enter the local train thanks to the North Indian commuters, who stand in the door blocking passage into the compartment. But broad-minded Maharashtrians tolerate all this," the Sena mouthpiece 'Saamana' said on Monday in an editorial comment.

The paper decried the hue and cry raised over the mob lynching of Dharam Dev in a local train recently and said, "This episode had nothing to do with Marathi-Bihari divide as was projected by some elements. In Mumbai's local trains hundreds of such incidents take place daily and even Marathi people too get beaten up."

The paper also condemned the reported attack on a Marathi woman IAS officer named Ashvini Thakre in Poorniya district of Bihar and said not a single Bihari leader spoke against it.

It also criticised the reported refusal of Bihar Chief Miniser Nitish Kumar to attend an NDA Kisan rally organised in Haryana because Shiv Sena too had been invited for the same.

No Shiv Sena leader actually attended the rally called by Omprakash Chautala. But Nitish Kumar chose to make a political stunt, the editorial said.

"These pseudo secularists are comfortable in the company of Imam of Jama Masjid or Muslim league. But they hate the nationalist Shiv Sena," it alleged.

"When Bihar was ravaged by the fury of Kosi in spate, help reached there from Mumbai. A medical team went to Bihar and one Dr Chandrakant Patil died there while discharging his duty towards the hapless Biharis," it added.

Heading: 80 kg RDX used in Assam serial blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Normal life was affected on Monday as a 11-hour Assam bandh was called by the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) protesting Thursday's serial blasts in the state.

Protestors' pelted stones on a bus early this morning at Makum in Tinsukia district but no passenger was injured, the sources said. They also damaged two goods trucks on national highway 37 near Sonapur while train movement was stalled at Moran, sources said.

In Moran, under Dibrugarh district, picketeers attempted to block the railway tracks to stop movement of trains, while, two goods trucks were damaged at Jugdal near Sonapur in Kamrup district, the sources said.

Meanwhile, markets, shops and banks kept their shutters down and educational institutions and offices remained closed.

All vehicles, including long distance and city buses, cars, auto-rickshaws kept off the roads, except the ones specially operated by the Greater Guwahati Bus Association to hospitals where the blast injured are admitted.

Flights and trains operated as usual, the sources said.

Attendance in the secretariat here and district deputy commissioners offices was thin as the people could not reach their work places due to absence of public transport.

Several picketeers were rounded up from across the state for attempting to enforce closure of markets, block roads and train tracks, the sources added.

AASU had earlier called a 24-hour bandh on Monday but changed it to an 11-hour one to avoid inconvenience to the injured and their family members.

Stating that all essential services were exempted from the purview of the bandh, AASU General Secretary Tapan Gogoi said the students' body had decided to reduce the bandh period in view of the inconvenience faced by the family members of those injured in commuting to the hospitals.

''Moreover, we have directed our members to guide and help all relatives going to the hospital and have also set up a special cell to help victims in all possible ways'', he said.

The AASU members have also been directed to ensure that there was no untoward incident and the bandh is imposed peacefully, he added.

The Greater Guwahati Bus Association has also decided to ply the buses from different parts of the city to the hospital where the injured are undergoing treatment.

Meanwhile, security has been beefed up in view of Monday's bandh and a strict vigil is being maintained in the vulnerable areas.

Heading: 'I have done my job', blast accused told Sadhvi: ATS - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 80 kg of deadly Research Development Explosive (RDX) was used in the October 30 serial blasts in Guwahati alone, officials said on Monday as investigators worked on sketches of the suspects.

Forensic officials claimed that nearly 80 kg of RDX was used in the three Maruti cars planted at the three blast sites in Guwahati. The blasts that took place in several parts of the state claimed over 80 lives.

"Such large quantity of RDX were never used to carry out explosions in Assam before as Ammonium Nitrate, with plasticers as propellants and Programmable Time Devices (PTD) were usually used to carry out a blast," said Padmapani, the Joint Director in the Forensic Science Laboratory in Guwahati.

Each of the cars were laden with 25 to 30 kgs of RDX to carry out the blasts and a total of 75 to 80 kgs was used to cause maximum damage, he said.

The officials said a maximum amount of explosives used for a single blast in the state was 10 kg at Dhemaji during the 2004 Independence Day which killed 13 people, including 10 school children.

Police have asked a Kolkata-based artist to prepare sketches of suspects involved in the blasts based on the eye-witnesses accounts.

The sketches are being prepared 'in an organised manner under police supervision' and it would take some time to complete them, police said.

Heading: Speaker overlooked breach of privilege by PM: CPM - Indian Express
Content:
Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur, arrested in connection with Malegaon blasts, allegedly had a long telephonic conversation with the absconding main accused in the case and told him why there had been lesser casualties in the incident, the prosecution told a court in Nashik.

The lawyer of Maharashtra Anti Terrorist Squad told chief judicial magistrate K D Boche, before whom Thakur and two others were produced amidst high drama, that during the long conversation between her and prime accused Ramji after the September 29 Malegaon blasts, Ramji told her "I have done my job."

Pragya asked Ramji whether police have seized her motorcycle used in Malegaon blasts and why less people had killed in the blasts, said the prosecution.

Ramji told Pragya that "I did not find proper parking place for the bike", claimed the prosecution.
