Heading: Drop in suburban prices: Mid-size projects blink first - Indian Express
Content:
No stay on termination notice, last episode to be aired on Thursday

The time has come to bid adieu to television's most enduring Saas-Bahu serial. Kyunki Saas Bhi Kahi Bahu Thi, Balaji Telefilms's staple, will be taken off the air; the final episode is on November 6.

The Bombay High Court sealed the soap's fate on Monday with vacation judge Justice J H Bhatia refusing to grant a stay to the termination notice served by STAR TV to the producers.

Star has decided to scrap the serial following a drop in its television rating points between July and September. Ekta Kapoor, head of Balaji Telefilms, had moved the court last week, seeking a stay to the termination notice.

Balaji's counsel Ram Jethmalani argued that the agreement stated that the show would run at least up to March 2009. He contended that STAR did not fulfil its obligation to promote the serial through advertising.

The agreement had been modified in August, allowing STAR to end the serial if its TRP should fall by 20 per cent since June 2008. But Jethmalani argued that when the contract was modified, the TRP was already 28 per cent down, so the benchmark TRP should be the one in August, and not that in June 2008. STAR's counsel Ravi Kadam, on the other hand, submitted that the agreement specified that the June TRP was the benchmark, and it had fallen over 20 per cent since then.

Kadam argued, "The programme has outlived its life." He added that the serial has to be taken off the air as the channel was losing viewers on the prime time slot to other channels.

Balaji gets Rs 27 lakh per episode. But STAR, Kadam said, would be a "bigger loser" if serial continued because the channel was losing out on advertising revenue.

Kadam said if at all STAR was at fault, the arbitration panel, to which the dispute will be referred soon, can award damages to Balaji eventually. Both parties have agreed to appoint arbitration panel if dispute arose.

Jethmalani denied that the serial was losing its pull. According to him, "A recent television audience measurement (TAM) report shows that the serial is in the top ten."

However, the judge agreed with STAR's stand, saying that prima facie Balaji could not be given any relief.

Kyunki... has been the forerunner among Saas-Bahu dramas on television for the last eight years.

Heading: Deonar dump ready for Rs 5000-cr makeover - Indian Express
Content:
Developers of mid-ranged projects in suburban locations across cities in India have become the first to blink in the tug-of-war between buyers and builders.

After stamp duty waivers and free parking slots failed to rope in buyers, builders in some suburban locations have started bring down their rates. According to a report released by Cushman and Wakefield on Monday, suburbs such as Andheri, Goregaon and Malad have seen a 4 per cent drop in property prices over the last three months after prices had remained stagnant for a while.

"Peripheral and suburban locations have taken a hit beyond doubt. Also the correction in values in the secondary sales market has impacted the overall value of residential properties in that location," said Aditi Vijayakar, director (residential services) for Cushman and Wakefield. She added that the trend of investors or others in the secondary sales market lowering their prices will further affect the overall property rates by the end of the year.

Besides the decrease in prices, the lull in the realty market may also mean more affordable housing projects being launched. The report states that poor sales in the festive season of Diwali and Dussera, the plunging stock markets, loans taken at higher rate of interests and liquidity crunch will all lead to developers focusing on middle income housing projects which commands a high demand since it is driven by end-users.

The report states that demand in the rental market is likely to remain stable for now as many prospective flat buyers have put off their decision to buy in anticipation of a further decrease in rates. Another market that will fairly remain unaffected by the slump would be properties in prime residential locations. However, the report notes that Pune's prime residential areas of Koregaon Park, Bundh Garden Road and Kharadi already seen a decrease of 5 per cent in the high-end segment.

Heading: Missing her favourite shampoo in jail, Susairaj moves court - Indian Express
Content:
A few months from now, the foul-smelling Deonar, where the country's largest and oldest dumping ground is located, will close its gates to the city's garbage. The reason for the partial closure for two years is that it is gearing up for a Rs 5,000-crore makeover. A waste-treatment plant, the biggest such project by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), is being set up there.

After the plant for scientific treatment of waste comes up, the 71-year-old dump will also earn the BMC carbon credits and help it generate electricity from methane released.

Around 4,000 tonnes garbage from the city is dumped there every day.

Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev said a consortium comprising United Phosphorus Limited, Kerala-based POABS and Germany-based MDSE, has been awarded the contract.

Deputy chief engineer (Projects, Solid Waste Management) Y M Chikhale said the proposal will soon be tabled before a Standing Committee. The project being sanctioned under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission has received environmental and civic clearance.

Chetan Zhaveri, project director and vice-president of BMC's consultants IL&FS Ecosmart Ltd, said the project was the first of its kind in the country. "The waste will be processed and the rejected inert will be scientifically disposed of in sanitary landfill," he said, adding it was also the largest integrated MSW facility on a public private partnership.

The closure of the dumping ground will take place in two phases: 65 hectares will be closed while the remaining 55 hectares will have a processing plant and sanitary landfill. Presently, of the 132 hectares, 120 hectares is covered by waste haphazardly dumped without treatment. In a process similar to that of Gorai dumping ground, waste on 65 hectares will be reformed and the land will be levelled. The site will be covered by layers of geo-textile and geo-membrane to avoid generation of leachates and then enclosed with soil and landscaping. There will be a collection and treatment plant for draining liquid from the landfill. A landfill gas generation project will capture methane to generate power.

In the remaining 55 hectares, a waste processing plant and sanitary landfill will come up. Mixed waste of 2,000 tonnes per day will be processed in the plant. The inert material that is non-recyclable will be disposed of in the landfill.

The project will also earn carbon credits issued by the Clean Development Mechanism, as methane will not be released into the atmosphere. Deonar is expected to generate 60 per cent effective carbon credits to the tune of 1,99,780 tonne/annum. Revenue can be generated by trading the credits.

Heading: Alert neighbours foil one-man bank robbery - Indian Express
Content:
Byculla Jail officials take days to provide what she needs, Kannada actress complains

Kannada film actress Maria Susairaj, accused in the Neeraj Grover murder case, has moved court. But it has nothing to do with the case. All she wanted was her favourite brand of shampoo and soap.

Susairaj moved an application on Monday seeking permission to get the cosmetics and toiletry she was accustomed to, which the jail authorities were unable to provide her.

Opposing the application, public prosecutor R V Kini said as per a recent state government circular, all jails had a canteen stocked with things of daily use like toiletry, which she can avail herself of, but not the high-priced brands she had sought.

The defence claimed that even when she requested for the available brands, the jail authorities provided the articles days after the request.

The court has now called for a report from the jail authorities on the matter.

Speaking to the media before she was taken away by the police, Susairaj said she was not interacting much with other inmates in Byculla jail. "I spend most of the time sketching, which I am good at. The sketches are of birds and animals. Some of them are of the jail itself," she said.

When asked who all were in her barrack, she said mostly women arrested in narcotics cases were her cell-mates.

A former inmate, Joy Tola, a Nigerian national out on bail, had also reached the court to meet Susairaj. She presented the actress with a prayer book and spoke highly of her. Tola said: "We used to offer prayers together when I was in custody. She is a nice girl."

On the letter said to have been written by Susairaj from Byculla jail to Emile Jerome, her boyfriend and co-accused in the case who is lodged at Arthur Road Jail, pleading for his forgiveness for giving a confessional statement naming him as the main accused, Susairaj's lawyer G S Kunnur said, "He did not wish to comment on it."

On the matter, Maria said, "I would not comment on the case as well as our (Emile's and her) relation."

She added, "I constantly read the Bible and things will surely turn out to be good."

Maria and Emile were arrested for allegedly killing Grover on May 7 and later chopping his body into several pieces before disposing of the body in a jungle near Manor in Thane district.

Court orders car to be returned to owner

The court on Monday allowed an application filed by one of the witnesses in the case, Kiran Shreyas, who had sought the return of his Santro car that was allegedly used by Jerome and Susairaj to dispose of Grover's body. The court directed the police to return the car to Shreyas as the prosecution said that all evidence it needed had been collected from the car.

On November 17, the court is likely to issue summons to mobile service providers Vodafone and Reliance following an application filed by Jerome asking the prosecution to declare the ownership of a mobile number mentioned in the chargesheet.

In the chargesheet, calls dialled from and received on Susairaj's mobile since the day of the murder have been mentioned but no details have been reportedly given. Emile had moved an application seeking details of these numbers.

Heading: 2 Bangladeshis held for circulating fake currency - Indian Express
Content:
A Chopper-Wielding robber almost managed to get away with the cash kept at the Bank of India's Bhandup branch on Monday afternoon, before some alert employees of a neighbouring company nabbed him as he was trying to escape.

The robber, Fauji Haji Mirza alias Shanu Ali Husain (26), was handed over to the Bhandup police.

Mirza had entered the bank's premises at L B S Marg in Bhandup and threatened three female officers and a peon with a knife and asked them to hand over the cash to him.

"At around 2.30, I was chatting with a couple of my colleagues outside our office when we heard muffled screams coming from inside the bank. Initially, we did not pay any heed. Later, when we heard the sound of glass-breaking and more screams, we rushed to the bank's entrance but found it locked," said Kshitij Basra, a technical application engineer with Hilti India Pvt Ltd, an MNC located close to the bank in Aniraj Tower.

Then Basra and his colleagues, Mahesh Shinde and Vinod Vardhan, rushed to the back entrance and knocked on the door. "An EPBAX repairman met and told us that a tall, robust man had shoved him aside and gone inside the bank. That's when we realised that something was seriously wrong. We then gathered people from other offices and collected bamboos and metal rods for safety," said Vardhan.

Meanwhile, a visibly shaken female employee of the bank came up to the door and told the trio to go away. "She then went away but came back again after we continued knocking. She repeated herself indicating that something was wrong inside. A few moments later a man similar to the one described by the EPBAX repairman came out of the door and all of us pounced on him," recalled Vardhan.

The group tied him up and called the police who arrived at the spot in about 15 minutes. "We immediately rushed inside to check on the women who were still sobbing. They said that the robber had held the knife to the peon's throat and broken the glass of the money cabinet. He then took the money and left. The women also bore some scratches on their body which indicated that the robber had manhandled them. But they were more traumatised than physically hurt," recounted Basra.

"We have registered a case of robbery on the complaint of Shaila Mohan, the bank official who was at the cash counter when Mirza began threatening. We will also be investigating whether the accused was involved in any previous cases," said Police Inspector N M Rode of the Bhandup police station.

Heading: Few conservancy workers eligible for house sop - Indian Express
Content:
One Indian held; trio went on shopping spree with their counterfeit Rs 500 notes, say police

Two illegal Bangladeshi immigrants and an Indian of Bangladeshi origin were arrested over the weekend by the officers of NM Joshi Marg police station for trying to circulate fake Rs 500 notes in the market. Ebrahim Sheikh (35) and Akbarali M Sheikh (30) were arrested from a slum at Reay Road station on Saturday and Abdul Jabbar Sheikh (33), who is an Indian of Bangladeshi descent, was arrested from a slum in Antop Hill on Sunday. Police have recovered fake Rs. 500 notes worth Rs 2,65,000 from the trio, and believe that Rs 35,000 worth of fake notes have already been distributed. The three have been remanded in police custody till November 11.

According to police, Akbarali's father had come to Mumbai after the 1971 war and lived as a beggar. He went back to Bangladesh after Akbarali's birth and used to shuttle between the countries. Being born in India, Akbarali was an Indian citizen. "Akbarali's father used to bring these fake notes with him to Mumbai and he also brought the other two men from Bangladesh to help his son circulate these notes," said DCP (Zone 3), A Deshdhratar.

"The men used to go shopping and pay with the fake Rs. 500 notes and thus put them into circulation. Alternatively they would go to construction sites and ask workers to get change for Rs 500 and to keep some of the money. The men used to earn 40 per cent of what they exchanged," he added. "This is a very dangerous trend and it can just add to inflation," said Deshdhratar.

When asked who could be involved in this circulation, Deshbratar said, "So far we don't know, but it is clear that such notes are not made in Bangladesh. It is only a point for circulating these notes, like Nepal." Refusing to pinpoint anyone without evidence, he said, "The third country in our region, which is also our enemy, is probably behind it. You need a lot of funds and expertise which certain intelligence and government agencies of that country must be providing."

Police have, meanwhile, sent a report of this case to the crime branch and to central agencies. The Bangladeshi immigrants will be deported after they have served their sentence. DCP Deshbratar, however, believes they might come back, "When I was in the FRRO and SB1, I saw many cases where even after deportation these immigrants came back, even if they would always be arrested. It seems they would rather be in jail here than back home."

Heading: Chhat Puja celebration: Police beef up security in city - Indian Express
Content:
The state government's gift of permanent houses to conservancy staff workers, who have completed 25 years in service, has failed to raise hopes of the thousands of workers who sweep the city's streets and dispose of the thousands of tonnes of garbage produced daily.

The BMC has only recently absorbed nearly 1200 labourers, who were on contract for more than 15 years. They will, however, not be liable to get the house until they complete 25 years in service. Another 6,000, who are currently on contract, will also not benefit.

Activist and general secretary of Kachra Vahatuk Shramik Sangh, Milind Ranade said they had requested the state government to provide permanent houses to all the conservancy staff workers, irrespective of service completion factor.

"Many workers do not complete the service of 25 years. There are others who have been on contract for around 20 years and have been recently taken as permanent employees. When will these workers complete 25 years so that they get a house?" he asked.

The 1200 contract workers have worked for 10-20 years and in recent years have been taken as civic employees. Elsewhere in the state, there are an estimated 90,000 conservancy workers, with less than 25 per cent of them on permanent basis. Most of the conservancy employees work on contract basis and therefore are not liable to benefit from the scheme. Of the estimated 24,000 conservancy workers in the city, only 3,000 have completed 25 years in service. The reason, say labourers, is that many die young owing to tuberculosis, respiratory disorders, skin problems or even cancer.

Officials from the Solid Waste Management department said as per the information provided to the state Urban Development Department (UDD), there are around 3,000 workers who have completed 25 years in service. The state government last week approved a resolution to make it mandatory for all municipal corporations and councils to provide permanent houses to conservancy workers who have completed over 25 years in service or to the close relatives of workers who die while in service.

According to the notification issued by the UDD, there would be reservation for 15 per cent of houses in existing projects such as Low Income Group housing, Integrated Housing and Slums Development Programme, Basic Services to the Urban Poor and surplus flats generated under the Slum Rehabilitation Scheme for conservancy workers' housing.

It also states that if the civic body decides to implement a mass housing project for such workers on its land or on land owned by state government, then the project will be granted a maximum Floor Space Index (FSI) of 4. If the same project is carried out through a private builder, he will be allowed 50 per cent of the total build up area as his incentive FSI.

The BMC has recently approved the Ashray project, which will provide staff service quarters to around 21,000 conservancy workers at a total cost of Rs 850 crore. The 350 sq ft carpet area tenements with a bedroom, balcony and a lift will cost Rs 5 lakh each.

Joint municipal commissioner (improvement) V Radha said the civic administration plans to construct the permanent houses on plots belonging to SWM department.

Heading: Nursing Council programme to train nurses in midwifery - Indian Express
Content:
With the Chhat Puja starting today, the Mumbai police have beefed up security arrangements in the city. All police officers except for those on station or court duties will be deployed in about 19 places in the city where the Puja will take place. Apart from this, as many as 19 companies of SRPF as well as RAF personnel will also be deployed to help the police in security arrangements at beaches. The police have also installed nine CCTV cameras— five on the way to Juhu Chowpatty and four on the beach— at various locations. Five pandals also have been constructed in Juhu Chowpatty. The police also have four watch towers on this route and a CCTV control room at the Santacruz Chowpatty police chowky.

The police are expecting at least four lakh devotees in Juhu chowpatty alone. Apart from Juhu chowpatty, devotees are expected to throng the beaches near Seven bungalows in Andheri like Sagar Kutir which is the largest of them. A large crowd is expected in Moragao Beach near Chandan Cinema also.

Despite a heavy crowd, the traffic will be normal on the roads to the beaches, said the police. Juhu Tara road will be fully operational though a big crowd is expected. Birla Lane next to the Tulip Star Hotel will be closed and cars except those of residents will not be allowed inside.

The same lane leading to Moragao beach will also be shut. VM Road from Vile Parle to Juhu Chowpatty is another road where many devotees are expected.The route to the beaches in Seven Bungalows will be mainly JP Road. However, according to the police, in case of congestion a diversion through PK Sawant Road will be employed. Quizzed why the traffic diversion was not felt, ACP Amarjit Singh said, "The devotees will mostly be pedestrians and will walk along the sides of the roads. People might come in rickshaws or cars also. We will arrange a separate parking lot for tempos, if they come."

Asked about the reason for installing CCTV cameras this year, Additional Commisioner of Police Archana Tyagi said, "Its' just an advancement of the security system that we have introduced last year." Quizzed on the interferance by any political parties, she said, "According to the High Court order in 2006, any political message cannot be relayed through the loud speakers. In fact, they can only relay religious songs and even entertaintment programmes are not allowed." Talking about certain organisations' plans to call Bhojpuri actor Manoj Tiwari she replied, "We can't stop him from coming to celebrate but we have not received any intimation or permission requests pertaining to this matter."

Heading: Civic officials, firemen to be taught to manage disaster - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to provide better medical services in rural areas, Indian Nursing Council (INC) - the parent body of the nursing councils in the country - along with Trained Nurses Association of India (TNAI) will soon introduce independent 'nurse practitioners' programme on midwifery in Maharashtra along with other states. Under this programme, trained nurses will take up on them normal deliveries in sub-centers and primary health care centers in the absence of doctors.

At the centenary conference of TNAI, it was announced that the programme will be formally inaugurated by the former president of India APJ Abdul Kalam in the city. Experts believe that the initiative will lower the alarming Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) and Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in rural areas.

"We are waiting for the INC to give State Nursing Council (SNC) a course module on midwifery so that we can start training nurses," said Anita Deodhar, state representative, TNAI.

"The major challenge before starting this midwifery programme was to protect the nurses under legal framework. The Government of India, under limited legal framework, has sanctioned these nurses to start practicing," said Arvind Kulkarni, president TNAI. The organization that plays an active role in policy decisions has over 2.5 lakh members on board.  

"Even though nurses are competent enough to conduct deliveries, now they will be trained so that they can deliver single-handedly, even in the absence of doctors. If not deliver, they should at least be capable enough of providing medical support to the mother till doctors arrive," added Kulkarni.

States like Gujarat, West Bengal, Kerala and Tamil Nadu have already initiated the midwifery practice since August 1. The two-day conference starting from Tuesday will, meanwhile, discuss about challenges and issues faced in the nursing sector. Currently there are only 10 lakh nurses to look after over 1 billion population in India. According to INC, for every 2,500 people, there should be five nurses. The ratio, however, is skewed and now for a population of 15,000, there is only one nurse. "In Maharashtra we are not just facing acute shortage of doctors, but also nurses. As compared to states like Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka or even Andhra Pradesh, number of seats and institutions offering nursing education is far less in Maharashtra," said Deodhar.

Deodhar points out that the reasons behind the acute shortage of nurses include lack of seats in postgraduate courses, no research facilities and lack of motivation. These, he feels, make nurses opt for jobs abroad. Only recently INC has recognized 13 specialty courses, where nurses can specialise.

Heading: She’s got the look - Indian Express
Content:
Hinduja Hospital and KEM Hospital will be joining hands with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) disaster management cell and the fire brigade for a unique exercise.

Keeping in mind rising number of road accidents, fire accidents and any such 'urban' catastrophe, these hospitals will be giving a week-long practical training to fire officers, civic hospital staff and officials from each ward office.

This emergency management exercise will start on November 3 and will end on November 9. The event will have a series of practical training, lectures and workshops focussing mainly on pre-hospital care, hospital disaster preparedness and advance trauma care for front line physicians.

"Unfortunately, we are living in a time when any kind of disaster can take place at any time. With terror attacks also increasing, people need to be prepared to deal with any kind of fire accidents and disasters. Disasters mean mass casualties, so we need to be prepared to manage the enormity of the situation. This is especially true for medical and fire personnel," said Dr Gustad Davar, medical director of Himduja hospital.

Dr Sanjay Oak, dean of KEM Hospital, also echoed his sentiments in the function. "We need trained personnel to deal with all kinds of emergencies. This event is basically to give hardcore training to doctors, nurses and fire officials who will be handling any emergency situation," said Oak.

As many as 25 doctors and 40 nurses from various civic hospitals, 20 personnel from the fire brigade, 24 engineers from each ward, 30 teachers and officers of the BMC's disaster management cell are expected to attend the event. "The idea is to train officials from various departments to give in-built support to stabilise a patient's condition during transportation to the nearest hospital after any kind of accidents. At times, essential time is lost when we transport a patient from the accident spot to the nearest hospital. Though we have essential first aid services, we need to enhance the emergency trauma situation," said Chief Fire Officer P D Kargupikkar.

According to Dr Davar, experts from New York Fire Brigade and hospitals are expected to attend the event to give training. The training programme will end with a large field drill session.

Heading: Godly Delights - Indian Express
Content:
Sonam Kapoor is well on her way to becoming a style icon

At the Elle Breast Cancer Awareness do in Mumbai a fortnight ago, actor Sonam Kapoor made an appearance in an abbreviated baby pink Christian Dior gown, looking every bit the prima donna she's aiming to become. Cut to Kunal Rawal's show at the Lakme Fashion Week and the bubbly actor turned up in a chic purple houndstooth by Marc Jacobs, her hair permed ever so slightly to add a careless touch. Ever since her debut last year, the 5' 9" beauty has featured on almost all the covers of leading fashion magazines, walked the ramp for designers like Tarun Tahiliani and Anamika Khanna (for whom she is now the brand ambassador), and has been impeccably turned out in Lanvin and Stella McCartney for significant social outings.

While industry insiders are betting on Kapoor to be the next trendsetter in Bollywood, those who know the actor well are hardly surprised. Designer Anuradha Vakil, for instance, still cannot get over her first meeting with the actor during the making of Saawariya. "She would listen to me attentively and then ask such technically sound questions about cuts, silhouettes and drapes, that I was quite floored," says the Ahmedabad-based designer, who had done the costumes for the movie, and has been designing for Kapoor's personal wardrobe ever since.

Kapoor believes her mother Sunita Kapoor has a lot to do with her sense of style. "When we were kids, mom used to be a full-fledged designer, supplying to stores like Glitterati and Ensemble in Mumbai. I would watch models like Nayanika and Aishwarya Rai, before she became Miss World, come in for fittings and discuss outfits and international designers. I saw the kaarigars at their embroidery stations for hours together. I think that's how my interest in garments grew," Sonam says from London, where she is currently on a vacation.

Stylist Anaita Shroff Adajania says Kapoor has developed a distinct fashion sensibility for herself. "I won't call her a style icon yet, but she has an individual flair and she wears her clothes with confidence," says Adajania. Vakil adds that Kapoor's dedication to fitness helps. "Sonam has a phenomenal body, so she looks good in almost anything," she says. Designers like Tahiliani talk of how the actor's innocence works to her advantage. "Sonam has freshness and spontaneity that's refreshing, a flawless dusky skin, long black hair and the most endearing giggle. She's very conscious of being curvaceous. Once she starts celebrating that, she will be way ahead of the curve," he says.

It's a concern, that Kapoor admits, plagues her. "I would be lying if I said I am naturally thin. I work really hard on my body, but I feel I am too curvaceous. So I am careful to dress in a way that leaves something to imagination, rather than accentuating my assets. That's not my style at all," she says.

Heading: It ain’t over yet - Indian Express
Content:
Beauties on wheels

The Cartier 'Travel with Style' Concours d'Elegance, at the Royal Western India Turf Club, Mahalaxmi, drew to a close on a 'champagne and restrained elegance' note on November 2 under the auspices of the master of ceremonies, sporting car legend Alain de Cadenet and Cartier International CEO Bernard Fornas. The Classic cars competition, the raison d'etre of the show, saw the 1939 Delhaye 135 MS owned by Maharaja Duleep Singhji of Jodhpur, being declared the Best of the Show by the judges Prince Michael of Kent, Imran Khan, Sir Michael Kadoorie, Nick Mason, Yasmin Le Bon, Peter Stevens, Gordon Murray, James Lindsay, Don McCullin CBE, Mark Stewart and Simon Kidston. Apart from the mandatory royalty present, one saw a smattering of select Indian celebrities like Yuvraj Singh, Nisha Jamvwal, Monica Vaziralli, Devika and Suresh Bhojwani, Simone Tata, Arjun Khanna, Adar and Natasha Poonawalla, Manav Gangwani, Shah Rukh Khan, who happened to be celebrating his 43rd birthday, and Jackie Shroff, who, incidentally, won the Ladies Prize for his 1937 roadster, a Jaguar SS 100.

Showstopper Sometimes utilitarian, sometimes flamboyant, but always breathtaking—the classic cars on display made for some serious eyecandy.

Dazzling act

The Maharashtra police department's Diwali bash though delayed was a dazzling show. Like every year, this event at the Andheri Sports Complex on Sunday had the film industry biggies grooving to hit numbers. Hrithik Roshan, Salman Khan, Govinda, Imran Khan, Jeetendra, Rakesh Roshan and Dharmendra were present at the star-studded evening. Though it was Shah Rukh Khan's birthday on Sunday, the superstar still made an appearance, albeit late. This won him wishes of Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, Home Minister R R Patil and Mumbai Police Commissioner Hasan Gaffoor.

Showstopper Sallu sporting a mauve shirt and a new hairstyle danced with Govinda to the title song of Partner.

Heading: How to eat out at home - Indian Express
Content:
With 350 children dying of Acute Encephalitis Syndrome (AES) in eastern Uttar Pradesh this year, a group of volunteers led by a doctor couple have taken a unique initiative to fight the disease.

Under the banner of Encephalitis Eradication Movement, Gorakhpur-based Dr RN Singh and his wife Dr Veena Singh are spreading awareness among the villagers for using sun rays to kill entero-viruses in drinking water.

The AES is mainly caused by waterborne entero-viruses and contaminated water supply remains a major threat in the region for the spread of the virus.

Experts from the US Centre for Disease Control (CDC), appreciated the simple and inexpensive technique of killing the virus during their recent visit to Gorakhpur.

After going through various studies conducted in other countries, Singh found that if water is kept for four hours under direct sunlight, it can kill entero-viruses.

Subsequently, he began a campaign to spread awareness about the method. He told the villagers to collect water in a bucket, cover it with clean white cloth and keep it in the sun for four hours.

"The masses here are so poor that a majority cannot afford fuel to boil water," Singh said. "But there is no shortage of sunlight. The villagers should be told to use sunlight for disinfecting drinking water."

Last month, the couple travelled across Gorakhpur and adjoining districts like Maharajganj and persuaded villagers to adopt the technique. It has already been used effectively in the villages of Samardhira and Ranipur in Maharajganj district and Sumersagar in Gorakhpur.

Dr Veena said: "Since a majority of the affected children belong to poor families, this method can offer them huge respite, if not 100 per cent protection."

The US experts have shown interest in supporting the cause, Singh said. He is now seeking help from various quarters to spread awareness about this technique.

"Since my reach is extremely limited, I am trying to get the support of CDC in conducting research and finding out the exact time needed to kill such viruses. I will also write to the Centre and the state government to include the method under the National Rural health Mission," he added.

Officials of the Health department said they were not aware of the technique.

"We have not heard that sun rays can kill entero-viruses. We have to consult experts about its efficacy before making any comment on it," said Dr VS Nigam, Joint Director, Communicable Diseases Wing of the department.

Heading: Last bite with Vidya Malvade - Indian Express
Content:
The best places and ways of sourcing foods, courtesy top-lining restaurants

Most of us have had to endure that gagging stench while passing a fisherwoman's cart; naturally assuming fish are meant to smell that way. So it was a bit of a surprise to discover that seafood isn't supposed to stink, it just does due to bacteria caused by poor storage and processing.

To ensure that his ingredients are fresh and do not start smelling, Taranath Kuckian, manager of

Trishna at Kalaghoda, has his shopper visit Crawford Market or Sassoon dock everyday at 6 am with all purchases delivered to their restaurant at 6.30 am. He emphasises, "We purchase our fish daily and clean, process (if required) and freeze the fish immediately."

One can see why the resulting dishes taste so good at Trishna, unarguably one of the best seafood eateries in the city, that only sources its seafood locally, even during the monsoon from Gujarat, Cochin or Kolkata.

Executive Chef of the Taj President, Ananda Solomon, though, oversees a much larger and trickier procurement operation—a large proportion of his ingredients including seafood has to be imported every morning after going through a maximum nine-hour flight. "I firmly believe in using fresh, natural and authentic ingredients available locally depending on the season," he states. However, often the quality of ingredients sourced locally is not good enough for his rigorous standards and that of his discerning customers.

He cites the example of the humble lettuce; it can be sourced from the Nashik-Pune region but he imports lettuce from France because it is still healthier, fresher and crisper than the local alternative.

"The main issue is the lack of adequate cooling facilities during transportation of the lettuce to

Mumbai," concurs Pallav Singhal, Executive Sous Chef of the Hyatt at Kalina, when quizzed about this particular plant.

He has even offered to assist suppliers in investing in refrigerated trucks to transport vegetables such as lettuce, but so far they have not considered this option economically viable.

Chef Singhal, though, is committed to sourcing locally when possible. For example, he uses lamb sourced from Jaipur for his Indian restaurant Soma while M Grill only uses lamb from New Zealand — the flavour of Indian lamb suits the dishes it is used in. Ideally, though, Chef Pallav would be delighted if the hotels and restaurants in Mumbai united to set standards of quality in food supply and distribution.

Nikhil Chib, owner/chef of Busaba, uses the 400 square-foot terrace on top of his restaurant to grow the exotic vegetables he needs — lemongrass, kaffir lime and sweet basil. Chib has an established network of suppliers in local markets, a fruit of his hard work in scouting Crawford Market and Sassoon Dock for quality suppliers.

He also suggests visiting Dadar market, and for pork particularly, one can get good quality in Dukkar Gali near Metro.

"The only way for suppliers to consistently provide exotic vegetables we need is through vertical integration — buying a plot of land and then growing, processing and transporting them myself," he says.

Which really isn't a bad idea, given the shocking price rises of vegetables recently.

Heading: Virar youth found hanging in resort had slash marks on wrists: police - Indian Express
Content:
I was in Panchgani two weeks ago for the housewarming party at a friend's bungalow. We were a huge gang of friends so we decided to do potluck. The boys went shopping for the ingredients and we all then took turns to cook our specialities. By the end of the day, we had mutton cutlets, palak paneer, fresh salad, jawar roti and a fruit salad on the buffet.

I contributed aloo parathas and bhurji, my specialities, to the meal. It's the biggest and most lavish meal I have ever treated myself to.

Heading: Water supply project for Navi Mumbai okayed - Indian Express
Content:
The police on Monday confirmed the body of 20-year-old Virar resident, which was found hanging in a beach resort near Arnala recently, had some slash marks on his hands.

Senior Police Inspector Pradeep Mane from the Virar police station said, "The manager of the Mohan Resort on Thursday morning informed us about the body of Shailendra Shukla which was found hanging from the ceiling with a bed sheet used as a noose. During examination of the body, we found slash marks on his wrists. We also recovered a small jack-knife from his trouser's pockets, which might have been used by Shukla to injure himself."

Mane added the enquiries indicate that Shukla probably slashed himself first in an attempt to kill self, and when that did not work out, he used a bed-sheet to hang himself. Shukla, a resident of Manvelpada in Virar, was a student of the Viva College and used to stay with his parents and a younger brother.

"Though we have not found any suicide note from the spot, we believe he might have taken this step due to some problems at home. Unless his family returns from their native place, we would not be able to question them about it," he said.

As per Mane, the police have also questioned the resort manager as Shukla used to go there often with friends. "He told us that Shukla had come alone to the resort on late Wednesday night and demanded a room.

When asked as to why he was alone, Shukla apparently told him that he had left his house after a quarrel with parents and now needed a place to spend the night. As the manager knew him from previous visits, he made a room available for him. The next day, the manager discovered Shukla's body hanging from the ceiling and he informed the police," Mane said.

The police are now waiting for Shukla's family to return so that they can be questioned about any trouble Shukla might have been facing at home or at his college, which may have compelled him to commit suicide.

Heading: POTA repeal, SC judgment bring relief, not release - Indian Express
Content:
The Ministry of Urban Development approved a water supply project estimated at Rs 230.52 crore to augment the water supply in Navi Mumbai, within the urban agglomeration around Greater Mumbai. The project is expected to benefit as many as 7.03 lakh residents of Navi Mumbai.

The project comprises augmentation of the 161-km distribution network, 4.9 km of transmission lines, consumer and bulk meters which would enable a continuous gravity-based distribution system and quality water supply to the entire city till 2041.

The 35 per cent cost of the project, which is Rs 80.68 lakh, would be borne by the Government of India. Current infrastructure in the satellite city of the financial capital extends to 80 pc of the city's area.

At present, the water source for the Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) is from Barvi dam, (100 mld from MIDC) and from Hetwane (52 mld from CIDCO), both relatively expensive sources of treated water.

NMMC has developed its own source at Morbe dam, with a capacity to supply 450 mld and was commissioned in 2006.

With the water project in pipeline, NMMC may discontinue taking water from MIDC and CIDCO. It will also lead to reduction of non-revenue water to 15% by 2010 with 24x7 water supply in a pilot area being extended to the entire system to provide 150 lpcd water throughout the city.

Heading: Kids’ fight ends in father’s suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Gateway, Zaveri blast accused set to be discharged under Act but will stay in jail

Based on a recent Supreme Court order, two alleged conspirators of the 2003 Gateway of India and Zaveri Bazaar bomb blast cases are likely to be discharged from the now-repealed Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA).

The two, Mohammed Ansari alias Usman Ladoowala and Mohammed Ansar Shaikh alias Hasan Batterywala, were arrested at Mumbra in Thane district and Kurla respectively and had been in custody since November 11, 2003.

On Monday, their defence lawyers informed the special POTA court about the apex court order and the prosecution gave its consent to withdraw POTA charges against the two.

The order was adjourned to Wednesday as the prosecution pointed out to special Judge M R Puranik that it would be a miscarriage of justice if the order stated that they were acquitted and not discharged. The court, halfway through the order, had stated that after framing of charges, the accused can be acquitted and not discharged.

The decision to withdraw the charges was based on the October 21 judgment of the apex court. Chief Justice K G Balkrishnan and Justice R V Raveendran had held that, "If the Central POTA Review Committee holds that review under section 2(3) of the Repealing Act, expresses the opinion that there is no prima facie case for proceeding against the accused, in cases in which cognisance has been taken by the Court, such cases shall be deemed to have been withdrawn".

Based on the judgment, the defence lawyers argued that the trial court will not examine the correctness or propriety of the opinion or exercise any supervisory jurisdiction in regard to such an opinion of the Review Committee. It had to just pass the discharge order, they stated.

Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said, "The decision to discharge them from POTA charges would be based on the apex court judgment. As regards evidence, we have enough against the two accused."

A total of six accused were arrested for alleged role in the twin blast on August 25, 2003 that killed 52 and injured over 100. Of the six, one is a woman. Another turned approver and is out on bail. The police claimed to have recovered 750 gm RDX from Batterywala's auto repair shop in Kurla and two detonators from Ladoowala's Mumbra residence.

As per sections of the POTA, in June 2005, the POTA Review Committee exonerated Ladoowala and Batterywala for lack of "admissible evidence". Based on the recommendations of the committee, the two moved an application before the POTA court which was rejected, observing that the decision of the POTA committee was not binding on the special court. The two then moved the Bombay High court, which also turned down their plea and thus they had moved the Supreme Court.

Clarifying that even if the accused are discharged under POTA they won't be freed, Nikam said, "The accused would then be tried for other charges by the same court and the evidence such as confessional statements and other circumstantial evidence can be used against the three other accused as well. However, while appreciating the evidence after the final arguments, the court would not consider the POTA charges for the two accused."

Heading: Fed up with corrupt officials? Call 2740012 - Indian Express
Content:
A routine quarrel between two toddlers turned out to be the cause of death of 33-year-old Mohammad Rafi, the father of one of the children, in Sohana late on Sunday.

Rafi hanged himself to death after he was reportedly beaten up by his neighbours when he complained about the "erratic behaviour" of their child.

Sohana Station House Officer, Mohinder Singh, said: "Around 6 pm on Sunday, Rafi's 3-year-old daughter was playing with the daughter of their neighbour, Amrik Lal, in Telian street, near the old Ram Lila ground. The kids had a fight and Rafi's daughter went crying to her house. She complained to her father that her friend had beaten her.

Irritated, Rafi went to the other girl's house to talk to her parents."

There he was assaulted by Lal and four others, Rafi's wife Shinder told the police.

"They threw my husband onto the street, publicly thrashed him and hurled abuses at him," she said.

On returning home, Rafi bolted himself inside a room.

"Around 9 pm, when our repeated knocks went unanswered, we broke the door down. We found him hanging from the ceiling with a dupatta," said Shinder.

Though no suicide note has been recovered, Shinder claimed Rafi was forced to take the drastic step as he was "ashamed of his humiliation in public".

Rafi was a driver by profession and had two daughters, aged three and two.

The body of the deceased, meanwhile, was handed over to the family after autopsy on Monday afternoon.

The viscera have been sent for chemical examination to establish the cause of death, said SHO Mohinder Singh.

The police have booked Lal, his son-in-law Billa, Billa's son Golu and two others for abetment to suicide under Section 306 of the IPC. However, no one has been arrested yet.

Heading: Panchkula gangrape: victim demands CBI probe - Indian Express
Content:
To mark the Vigilance Awareness Week, the Vigilance Wing of the UT Administration has introduced a special telephone number — 0172-2740012 — where residents can lodge their complaint against corrupt officials. The week is being observed from November 3 to 9.

UT Home Secretary-cum-Chief Vigilance Officer, Ram Niwas, said: "Such steps will help build confidence of the public in the police. The initiative will provide the public full access to the CVO and Administration."

The week commenced with all officials, including senior administration and police officers, taking an oath for continuously striving to bring about integrity and transparency in all the spheres.

The pledge was administered by Adviser to the UT Administrator, Pradip Mehra, at the UT Secretariat, Sector 9, today.

All the organisations falling under the purview of the Central Vigilance Commission will observe the week.

"Efforts will be made to raise awareness among the public about the services provided by various departments, the initiatives taken for improvement of procedures, the complaint-handling policy and the avenues available for redressal of grievances," said Ram Niwas.

Heading: Ghost of homework continues to haunt students - Indian Express
Content:
The 17-year-old girl, who was allegedly raped and tortured by five persons on September 17, lodged a complaint with the Police Headquarters, Sector 6, on Monday alleging police inaction and demanded a CBI inquiry into the case.

The victim could not meet the Haryana Deputy General of Police, Ranjiv Dalal, as he was away to Bhiwani in the wake of an alleged fake encounter by the police there.

The Panchkula police are yet to arrest two of the main accused in the case, Jatin and Chhavi.

One of the arrested youth, Aman Ahuja, was released on bail on Saturday while the bail application of Jitesh, arrested on September 26, will come up for hearing in the district court on Tuesday.

"The police have completely failed to get us justice. It was only after several requests that the sketches of the two accused were released. The police are taking the entire process very casually. Now, the Panchkula

Superintendent of Police Sandeep Khirwar has gone on leave for 15 days, further delaying our case," said the rape victim.

But the police claims to be on the trail of the accused. A police officer, on condition of anonymity, said: "We are trying to trace a girl named Tanu, who was involved in the making of a pornographic CD of the victim about a year ago. She may shed light on the whereabouts of Jatin and Chhavi."

Heading: Students’ body protests against Haryana government - Indian Express
Content:
Two years ago, the CBSE had issued directions to all affiliated schools that no homework shall be given to students of Class I and II

In spite of instructions from the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to exempt primary students from homework, schools in the city are still following the practice.

Almost two years ago, the CBSE had issued directions to all affiliated schools that no homework shall be given to students of Class I and II while alternative assignments will be introduced for students of Class III to V.

But it seems the local schools are yet to get the message. "We do give children a little homework but, at the same time, we make sure that they are not over-burdened. As far as the Board's guidelines are concerned, we are not aware that there is a complete ban on giving home assignments," said a teacher at St John's School.

"We never received any such directive. Giving homework is an age-old practice and I believe it is essential. Children should be given some work to do at home to help them keep up with their studies," says a teacher at Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 19.

Asked about the lax implementing the Board's instructions, Director Public Instructions (Schools) Samawartak Singh said: "The Education Department wants to bring these guidelines into effect but this cannot be done overnight. A lot of other factors have to be kept in mind before implementation."

The CBSE had given these recommendations so that students have enough time to develop life skills and adequate emotional rapport with the parents. "It is felt that at this age, learning should be as informal and joyous as possible so that there is time and scope for nourishing the mental health of students," the circular stated.

Heading: Diarrhoea grips Majri village, 403 cases in two days - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian National Students' Organisation (INSO) activists led by Haryana INSO president Vikas Rathee protested at Haryana Raj Bhawan in the city on Monday against the Haryana Police and the state government.

Rathee along with Chandigarh INSO president Sunil Kumar, DAV College students' union president Karambir Singh Dadri, student leader Aman Godara, DAV college leader Vikas were arrested by the police during the protest.

They were, however, released later. Students raised anti-government slogans and demanded Chief Minister Hooda's resignation for the alleged fake encounter in Bhiwani recently.

Heading: Blood banks struggle to cope as dengue takes over city - Indian Express
Content:
Leak in water-supply pipeline caused the epidemic, says Health Department, as Water Supply and Sanitation department denies claim

Almost every family in the sleepy hamlet of Majri, near Mohali, has been affected with diarrhoea. At least 403 villagers have complained of pain in the abdomen, vomiting, loose motions and mild fever on Sunday and Monday, said Mohali District Health Officer (DHO) Dr S P Surila.

Around 297 diarrhoea patients were reported on Sunday while 106 cases were detected till Monday evening. While seven of the critical cases were shifted to the PGI and GMSH-16 in Chandigarh, 50 others were admitted at a makeshift health centre set up at the community centre in the village. No casualty has been reported yet.

To tackle the epidemic, two medical specialists, a medical team and an ambulance have been stationed at the village.

"We are providing free treatment and medicines to the patients and spreading health awareness in the village," said Dr Surila. He added that 10 water samples were collected from different sources on Monday for tests.

Preliminary investigations by the District Health department revealed that a leak in the water supply pipeline to the village had caused the epidemic. The villagers who subsisted on water from handpumps were not affected while those who drank tap water had fallen ill.

Water supply to the village was suspended on Sunday. On Monday, the Water Supply and Sanitation department plugged the leak and restored supply.

Refuting the Health department's claim, Executive Engineer of the Water Supply and Sanitation department, Partap Singh, said: "We supply water to four villages — Majri, Fatehpur, Sialba and Khera — from the same two tubewells installed at Fatehpur. No where except Majri was this problem reported."

However, four teams have been deputed to plug any minor leaks in the connections. The engineer said he suspected the use of booster pumps may have contaminated the water.

DOCTOR'S ADVICE

* Drinking water should not contain any suspended particles

* Drinking water should be boiled/chlorinated before consumption

* Avoid eating overripe fruits and vegetables

Heading: First Chhat Puja at Sector 42 lake today - Indian Express
Content:
The high incidence of dengue cases in the region has taken a toll on the city's blood banks as they have been reeling under severe pressure for the last couple of months to cater to the platelet needs.

The demand for platelets have been higher this year compared to the past years, say blood bank authorities — both private and public who have been urging voluntary donors to donate blood. The Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Sector 32, says that demand for blood units has gone up by two to three times in the past few months.

Dr Savita, Head of Department of Blood Transfusion, GMCH, says high demand for platelets suggest the surge in the number of dengue cases compared to last two years.

"This year, we have seen more number of cases as compared to the last two years. With facilities like separation of blood into components like platelets extremely limited in the surrounding areas, the entire burden of demand shifts to Chandigarh."

The doctor adds, "We have been able to meet the demand of patients and provide blood units to nursing homes as well, but the authorities must focus their attention on improving the facilities for collection and preparation of blood."

A doctor at the PGI said: "The demand for units has definitely gone up since September and would last till November, when the cases gradually stop coming in the hospital wards. With no facilities of separating blood into components being available in the periphery areas, the burden on the city increases."

"We still receive demand of platelets from nearly two new patients a day. The management of dengue cases becomes very crucial as platelets have to be extracted from freshly donated blood," said Col R S Shah, director, Blood Bank Society, Sector 37.

Blood donation in numbers

The UT Health department so far claims that the city has reported over 40 cases of dengue this season while over 250 cases, detected in nearby towns and cities of Haryana and Punjab, have been reported in Chandigarh hospitals. At the end of October, the PGI still had 22 cases of dengue patients undergoing treatment.

Heading: Eight STA officials in the dock as UT Home Secy conducts ‘punctuality check’ - Indian Express
Content:
After the Sukhna Lake was declared a 'Silence Zone' and religious ceremonies and rituals were completely banned on the premises, the Chandigarh Administration today said Chhatt Puja, Ganesh Puja and other rituals could be performed at the new Sector 42 lake. A Chhatt Puja shall be performed at the Sector 42 lake on Tuesday.

In a press statement issued today, the Chandigarh Administration stated that two decks have specially been constructed at the lake for the purpose of holding religious ceremonies. Changing rooms and various other facilities have also been provided.

City-based architect, Vinod Joshi, who designed the lake said work was completed in a record time of 67 days. On the instructions of the Administration, the depth of the lake has been kept at three feet. However for safety reasons, the minimum water level is being maintained at two feet, so that people who wish to immerse flowers can do so conveniently.

"Besides religious ceremonies, the lake and its landscaped surroundings will cater to the needs of residents for walks and picnics as well. Various features, including small steps for senior citizens, bridges to enable people to cross the lake, a green environment, pathways, washrooms and changing rooms, have been provided at the lake," said Joshi.

Heading: Chaos reigns at Sector 38-D market - Indian Express
Content:
The State Transport Authority (STA) officials, plagued with the "reaching-office-late" syndrome were in for a shock on Monday when UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas reached the STA office at 9 am to check the punctuality of the staffers. As many as eight officials of the STA department, Sector 18, are in the dock for reporting late to office.

Niwas found the office empty and had to wait for the officers to arrive. Till 9.22 am, it was reported, only seven of the 17 officials reached office. Irked by the irresponsible attitude, Niwas ordered stern action against the eight erring employees.

"I have sought explanations, following which stern action shall be taken against them who did not reach office by 9.22 am," said Niwas.

The surprise visits did not cease at the STA office as Niwas also conducted visits to various construction sites under the Chandigarh Industrial and Tourism Corporation.

He reached the Park View Hotel in Sector 24, and took a round of the newly-constructed floors. While taking a look at the sample room constructed at the hotel, Niwas pulled up the contractor and concerned officials. He directed the contractor to give the final touches and show him the complete work once again, before the final inauguration of the hotel scheduled in December.

Niwas warned the contractor that he shall not be entitled to any payment, if the work is not in accordance with the required criteria and people's satisfaction.

On his visit to Hotel Mount View, Niwas inspected the construction of the newly-built Health Club which is scheduled to open on November 10.

Heading: I QUIT - Indian Express
Content:
After playing many roles, Mansi Joshi Roy now takes the director's seat

After actor Mansi Joshi Roy turned producer, she insisted on adding 'creative' as suffix to her new role. "I always believe that I'm a creative producer and not just a producer. I like designing my complete show, which I'm doing with Cinemascope," says Joshi.

Joshi Roy's prowess as a director comes to the fore with the new season of Cinemascope, which was launched by Zee Music on Sunday. The Bollywood-based show hosted by Roshni Chopra will take the viewers through new releases and their making, besides filling them in with all the gossip related to films. It will also package reviews, previews and the box-office outcome.

The small screen might experience a surfeit of such programmes but the newly-turned director claims that her show, replete with trivia, will stand out. "Apart from trivia, interviews with actors and behind-the-scene footage will be our USP," she says.

Though direction is very fulfilling, Joshi Roy doesn't want to take more assignments right now. After setting the template of Cinemascope and directing its initial episodes, her focus will shift to acting — which remains her abiding passion. Production will also take up her time.

She has launched a production house, called Magic Works, with husband Rohit Roy. Both of them are involved in the creative process while administration remains Joshi Roy's domain.

However the actor, who won hearts as Sudha in Saaya, has no plans of appearing on the small screen. "Not until I get something exciting," she says. Next summer, she will appear on the big screen in Alibaug. The year 2009 will also see the release of Pankh, which is co-produced by the Roys. "We are very happy to have made a non-mainstream film like Pankh," she says.

After mapping a successful journey in the world of entertainment, the actor — who has her roots in theatre — still longs to go back to stage. "I wish to do some plays sometime soon," says the daughter of Arvind Joshi, an eminent Gujarati theatre personality.

Heading: Live it up - Indian Express
Content:
Q* We hear you are out of Saat Phere?

Yes. I am quitting the show. I have been lucky to play Saloni, who had so many flavours to her. I played a child (a la Sridevi's role in Sadma), a banjaran and even turned negative. To get such a role at the beginning of your career is a blessing. But I have been working continuously for the last three years without a break. Now, I want to spend some time with my family, which is why I am leaving the show.

Q* Is it your decision or the producer's?

Of course it's my decision. I conveyed it to the producer and they respect my decision. However, they told me I cannot quit immediately. They want to work out how my character will exit.

Q* What is the track right now?

Nahar is not well and I am taking care of him.

Q* How has the journey been so far?

It's been great. Whatever I am today is because of the show. I feel proud to be associated with it. People have appreciated and accepted me, I think I have got more than what I asked for and I am grateful to God for that.

Q* There was a controversy about you quitting Ek Se Badhkar Ek because you were scared of competition.

I think reality shows are all about controversies. I had a old ligament tear which I ignored. But the heavy-duty dancing and rehearsals aggravated my pain, which is why I quit. Why should I be scared of competition? If I was, I wouldn't have participated.

Q* Are you exploring other shows now that you have quit Saat Phere?

Not right now. As I said, I want to spend time with my family, specially my husband. I was married a year-and-half ago and I didn't have enough time even for my wedding. If possible, I would like to conduct my marriage again.

Q* So, are you planning a long honeymoon?

Let's see. First I have to finish my commitment to the show, only after that can I decide.

Heading: Jt Director Agriculture accused of fake land registry - Indian Express
Content:
