Heading: MBBS seats at IGMC increased to 100 - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another instance of fraud charges against a government official, allegations of preparation of fake registry of land at village Makhan Windi, jointly owned by a family and their kin, have surfaced against Gurdev Singh, Joint Director Agriculture.

The complainants have also charged the police with sheltering the accused and his kin, by not initiating any action against them.

Addressing mediapersons, Jasbir Singh, one of the owners of the land, said that his relative Joginder Singh and his brother Gurmeet Singh jointly owned the land. Jasbir said Joginder Singh died in 1997. According to Jasbir, Joginder's widow, four sons and four daughters have 50 percent share in the land.

"The accused got a fake registry done in the name of his son in 1997, while Joginder Singh was still alive," alleged Jasbir Singh.

He claimed that no action has been taken against the accused, though several representations had been sent to various police officials in this regard.

When contacted, Gurdev Singh, Joint Director Agriculture, termed all the charges against him as baseless. He added that he had legally purchased the share owned by Kulwant Singh, a kin of Joginder Singh.

Gurdev Singh asserted that he had purchased the land, and had nothing to do with the share of the other persons.

"The charges are being leveled against me with malafide intention. The accused damaged the crop that my family cultivated on this land and we have submitted an application with the police in this regard," claimed Gurdev Singh.

The family, meanwhile, claims that the land registry is fake.

Heading: HC takes up contempt case - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant move, the state government today decided to increase MBBS seats at Shimla's Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC) from existing 65 to 100 and also create additional posts of teachers to meet the requirements of the Medical Council of India.

Himachal has two medical colleges, one at Shimla and other Rajendra Prasad Medical College at Tanda (Kangra), having 65 and 50 MBBS seats, respectively. The seats at IGMC were increased to 100 during the earlier Congress regime in 1993-94, but the Medical Council of India had refused to grant its approval.

A decision to increase seats at IGMC was taken at a meeting of the Cabinet, held here this evening. Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal presided over the meeting.

The Cabinet, at the initiative of the state's health department, approved a proposal to increase nine seats in post-graduate courses and sanctioned 45 posts of different categories of teaching faculties. An increase of 11 seats in post-graduate courses in five different departments of Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College and 12 posts of teachers to shoulder the additional teaching responsibility was also cleared.

In the power sector, the Cabinet agreed for setting up a captive thermal power plant, preferably based on biomass. The HP State Electricity Board will have the first right to purchase surplus power from the plant. The government will levy environment cess on such plants. The cess will be determined by the state government separately, said official sources.

In a move to strengthen the state's farm and horticulture sectors and to protect interests of the fruit growers, the Cabinet today decided to enhance support price for price of citrus fruits by 50 paise per kg under the market intervention scheme (MIS), to be applicable between November 20, 2008 and February 14, 2009.

Different categories of citrus fruits will have procurement of kinnows, malta and orange at a rate of Rs 5.85 and Rs 5.25 per kg for B and C grade fruits, respectively. Galgal will be procured at Rs 4.15 per kg from the growers.

The government also decided to reserve 5 per cent posts in Class III and IV services to provide relief to the dependents of employees who expired during active government service.

This will also help the dependents to get compassionate appointments in the departments and public sector undertakings.

The Cabinet also granted some relief to women seeking recruitment in the police by deciding to amend the recruitment procedure and physical efficiency test of women constables in the Himachal Police. The Cabinet approved one-time age relaxation to Homeguard volunteers from 28 years to 33 years for filling up the backlog vacancies reserved for Homeguards constable in the state police.

It also approved implementation of the group superannuation pension scheme for the employees of HIMUDA. Approval was given for one-time relaxation in recruitment and promotion rules for filling up 50 per cent of the posts of assistant professors by promotion in IGMC and Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College from amongst the joint roster of the GDO category.

It consented to revive the post of engineer-in-chief (quality and control) in the Department of Public Works for a period of two years. The government decided to make 15 newly-upgraded high schools functional and sanctioned 60 posts of various categories.

Other Cabinet decisions

* 40 teaching posts created at IGMC, 12 at Kangra medical college.

* Thermal power plant based on biomass approved.

* Govt to levy environment cess on thermal plants.

* Procurement price for citrus fruits raised by 50 paise.

* Norms relaxed for women in police recruitment.

Heading: Rana takes over as govt media panel chief - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab and Haryana High Court has fixed November 18 as the next of hearing in a contempt case against a local resident Jaswant Sarpal.

The case, filed as 'Court of Own Motion versus Jaswant Sarpal', was filed in August 2004. The contempt pertained to Sarpal's behaviour in the court. Sarpal had made derogatory remarks against the court and judges. Sarpal, who deposed before the High Court on October 30, said that he would face the proceedings and would hire lawyers to file an appropriate reply.

Heading: Directive on using Tricolour on VIPs’ cars - Indian Express
Content:
Rajender Rana, BJP's media incharge, today took over as chairman of the newly-formed media advisory committee of the government and stressed upon the need for using modern technologies in highlighting policy initiatives of the government. He spoke highly about the role of media in Himachal Pradesh and said efforts would be made to maintain full transparency about working of the government. "The government headed by Prem Kumar Dhumal has always tried to maintain cordial relations with the media. This effort will help the media in getting information on policies and programmes," he added.

This was the first time when the state government has appointed a chairman for the media advisory committee, which earlier was headed by the Chief Minister. Rana said the committee will advise the government on media-related issues.

Speaking to mediapersons, Rana said the BJP government, on return to power, had adopted the manifesto as a policy document and a large number of promises have already been fulfilled. He said the public relations department would be strengthened and new technologies will be used to give mass publicity to the policies and programmes of the government.

Meanwhile, hurt by the government's offer to make him member of the media advisory committee under Rajender Rana, Dr Ashok Kapahita, who was BJP media incharge during the December 2007 election, has declined the offer.

Kapahita said he had conveyed his decision to Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal on the day when the notification for the committee was issued without consulting him.

Kapahita had been the most visible face in the town's media circles and had managed the party campaign successfully. Insiders said Kapahita was upset at being placed under Rana, who is very junior to him in terms of his association with the party. Dhumal was the one who promoted Rana and had even favoured giving him a ticket from Hamirpur.

When contacted, Kapahita said, "I am a loyal party soldier and will continue to work tirelessly without expecting any reward. I will continue to discharge organisational functions whatever assigned me. I have no regrets in saying no to membership of the committee."

When Rana was asked about Kapahita's refusal, he said, "Dr sahib had some personal pre-occupations."

Heading: ‘Walk to work’ concept to tread into industrial policy - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has issued a directive to check the misuse of Tricolour by VIPs.

Till now, all the chief parliamentary secretaries, chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of corporations and boards, Advocate General and cabinet ministers flaunted Tricolour on their official and private vehicles. In a recent communiqué, the Deputy Secretary (Coordination), citing the provisions of the Flag Code of India 2002 issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs, said only state Chief Minister, cabinet ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chief Justice and judges of the state High Court were authorised to put the national flag on their official vehicles.

Sources said with this order, only those entitled to use the flag could put the national emblem on the number plate of their vehicles. There are 14 chief parliamentary secretaries and over 24 chairpersons and vice-chairpersons in the state."The recently-appointed chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of advisory boards of traders and industry were also given official cars with red light and national flags," said an official. A senior police official said, "A person can be booked if he is found violating the Flag Code."

Heading: Now, BSP youth wing eyes Congress - Indian Express
Content:
The state government will introduce the concept of 'walk to work' in its new industrial policy to give corporate players investing in Punjab the added advantage of next-door housing for employees.

The concept is also aimed at easing out the pressure on infrastructure and transport system that may sooner or later hamper everyday living. Principal Secretary, Industry, S S Channi said the idea was to bond housing with industry. "There is a plan is to incorporate a clause that prohibits the industry from selling the houses. The modalities are being worked out. It will be like official accommodation given to government officials who are suppose to vacate it once they move out."

The government also plans to put a cap on the selling price of the housing unit to make it affordable for the company. Channi said a private developer could be roped in for the project in case the industry was reluctant to

develop it.

Punjab's new industrial policy, a strategic roadmap for which was prepared by the United Nation's Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO), would be finalised shortly.

Punjab is also preparing its own SEZ Act, a draft of which is almost in place. A meeting with Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal to finalise the SEZ Act draft was scheduled for November 6, but has been now put off to November 19.

R K Verma, Managing Director of Punjab Infotech, said the 'walk to work' concept would save the time spent on road by company officials and improve employee efficiency. "We are viewing various options, including leasing out the housing set-up or its

outright sale."

Heading: Celeb watch - Indian Express
Content:
Despite a slow beginning, actor Sonam Kapoor is well on her way to becoming a style icon

At the Elle Breast Cancer Awareness do a fortnight ago, actor Sonam Kapoor made an appearance in an abbreviated baby pink Christian Dior gown, looking every bit the prima donna she's aiming to become. Cut to Kunal Rawal's show at the Lakme Fashion Week and the bubbly actor turned up in a chic purple houndstooth dress by Marc Jacobs, her hair permed ever so slightly to add a carelessly stylish touch. Ever since her debut last year, the 5' 9" beauty has featured on almost all the covers of leading fashion magazines, walked the ramp for designers like Tarun Tahiliani and Anamika Khanna (for whom she is now the brand ambassador), and has been impeccably turned out in Lanvin and Stella Mc Cartney for significant social outings.

While industry insiders are betting on Kapoor to be the next trendsetter in Bollywood, those who know the actor well are hardly surprised. Designer Anuradha Vakil, for instance, still cannot get over her first meeting with the actor during the making of Saawariya. "She would listen to me attentively and then ask such technically sound questions about cuts, silhouettes and drapes, that I was quite floored," says the Ahmedabad-based designer, who had done the costumes for the movie, and has been designing for Kapoor's personal wardrobe ever since.

Kapoor believes her mother has a lot to do with her sense of style. "When we were kids, mom (Sunita Kapoor) used to be a full-fledged designer, supplying to stores like Glitterati and Ensemble in Mumbai. I would watch models like Nayonika and Aishwarya, before she became Miss World, come in for fittings and discuss outfits and international designers. I saw the kaarigars at their embroidery stations for hours together. I think that's how my interest in garments grew," she says from London, where she is currently on a vacation.

Stylist Anaita Shroff Adajania says that Kapoor has developed a distinct fashion sensibility for herself. "I won't call her a style icon yet, but she has an individual flair and she wears her clothes with confidence," says Adajania. Vakil adds that Kapoor's dedication to fitness helps. "Sonam has a phenomenal body, so she looks good in almost anything," she says. Designers like Tahiliani talk of how the actor's innocence works to her advantage. "Sonam has freshness and spontaneity that's refreshing, a flawless dusky skin, long black hair and the most endearing giggle. She's very conscious of being curvaceous. Once she starts celebrating that, she will be way ahead of the curve," he says.

It's a concern, that Kapoor admits, plagues her. "I would be lying if I said I am naturally thin. I work really hard on my body, but I feel I am too curvaceous. So I am careful to dress in a way that leaves something to imagination, rather than accentuating my assets. That's not my style at all," she says. India's answer to Brigette Bardot, perhaps?

Heading: Culturally charged - Indian Express
Content:
Getting Knotty

MTV VJ and city's very own Ayushmann Khurrana tied the knot with his college sweetheart Tahira Kashyap this Saturday. The pair glowed like a million flashbulbs on their reception held at AKM Resorts on Sunday. The special occasion saw a bevy of special guests which also included actor Varun Badola, singer Dolly Guleria and those from the television industry bring in their best wishes for the couple. And as always dad Pandit Khurrana played perfect host.

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
Art, culture, music, books...there's space for the fine things of life at these informal gatherings in the city

In this walk of life, where time's in a hurry and there's room for only business, money, politics, there are people, who are looking for a getaway, one that's mentally stimulating, relaxing and gives a chance to know people who can enrich life and being. Precisely why endeavours are being made to get out of cocoons and share laughter, perspective, ideas, passions. Socializing is getting back in fashion and it's not only about a big do and Page 3 events.

Community service may not be that crowd-pulling an idea but, "we could always have a space where people can come and offer workshops, share their ideas and skills, watch films together or have poetry reading sessions," Sukhmani Kohli talks about Cafe Kaffee Kuchh. The idea is to open space for people to make food together and serve it, voluntarily. "We also want to open the space for people to come and just spend time reading books or starting interesting conversations with new friends. We want to open ourselves to people participating and contributions, monetary, physical work or with just their presence."

The group held its first meeting last Sunday at Children's Cultural Centre, Lajpat Rai Bhawan, Sector 15, Chandigarh. and will meet every week between 4 and 8 pm. A poetry reading group that has already booked the café as their meeting point and more are welcome. "It's nice to pause for a while, look around and savour the moment. It's like cycling as against going on a fast motor bike. When on the cycle, one tends to notice more, to absorb one's surroundings more. Slow motion is good sometimes…most times. "Go on, take your time. Digest your food, digest yourself. Have a chai," Sukhmani invites.

Coffee, cake and chatter; a perfect backdrop for a cozy meet, one that's also literary in spirit. The Chandigarh Ladies Book Club was Simran Grewal's idea to catch up with old friends, meet their new families and of course, get to pore over books. "I came back from abroad after many years and wanted to reconnect with friends from school and college and make it an activity that would also encourage reading, a personal passion. And so, some 15 of us decided to take it up seriously in March this year,'' Grewal loves the regular meets and decided it would be a simple affair. The venue is not a coffee bar, but the homes of the ladies and the menu does not exceed two items. It's the hostess, who usually zeroes in on the book to be read. "We give each other a month to read the book and then discuss it. This month, it's The White Tiger that we are glued to,'' Simran says they hope to read one autobiography, biography and a classic by this year end and feels the club is a fantastic way to catch up and share.

The need for informal gatherings, where like-minded people can discuss art, culture, music is what the city needs and it's a get-together that has to be encouraged, Diwan Manna, Chairman of the Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi, who is all set to have a monthly get-together either at the State Library or Museum and hopes to start a conversation with either an art or film show and then take it further.

A play, movie, concert, dance recital, always culminates with an informal chat, "it's an unsaid ritual among us friends, and is usually done over a cup of tea, either at the venue itself or the nearest home. The nuances of a theatre performance, what could be done better, the high and low of a music concert, the acting, cinematography of a film...it's a practice that has been going on since our repertory days and there's a sense of fulfillment in this gathering here that's hard to explain,'' smiles Kamal.

Now free from professional responsibility, Rajnish Wattas is itching to give shape to a plan that's really close to his heart — forming a discussion circle that will encompass people from all walks of life, who are curious and inclined to meet more people and have free-floating conversations, where politics and business are taboo topics. "We will begin this month, right now we are five of us friends and the circle will only widen. We hope to have a topic of discussion, be it about a book, a painting, music, piece of architecture. There is no agenda here, just a purely mutual sense of enriching our lives, widening our horizons and sharing some happy moments over high tea.''

Let the good times roll!

With input from Navdeep Sandhu

Heading: Farmers to protest for demands across state - Indian Express
Content:
A time to remember

Six veteran Rajput officers and their families had the time of their lives as they journeyed to Kolkata and Port Blair. Organised by Rajput officers Association Punjab and Chandigarh Chapter, the officers undertook this adventure from October 18 to 21. As part of this memorable trip, the officers interacted with serving and retired officers of the Rajput Regiment settled at Kolkata, enjoyed a gala evening organised by Mrs. & Lt. Gen V.K Singh and marked a wonderful reunion of veteran and serving Rajput officers courtesy Lt. Gen V.K.Singh PVSM, AVSM, YSM the Army Commander and Maj Gen A.M Verma SM, VSM Area Commander, both from Rajput Regiment. Banquet at the famous Bengal Club courtesy Maj Gen Arun Roy AVSM, YSM, a royal welcome at Port Blair at the newly constructed annex of Raj Niwas courtesy His excellency Lt. Gen Bhopinder Singh PVSM AVSM, Lt Governor Andaman and Nicobar, visits to Ross Island and Hovlock island, trip to Coral beaches, it sure was a fascinating treat. Encounters, up close and personal with bountiful treasures of nature, Rajput Veterans of Chandigarh Chapter have returned after a grand memorable odyssey. The Chandigarh Chapter of Rajput Association is organizing its 16 annual dinner meet on November 7 at Shivalik View, Chandigarh. Colonel of the regiment, Lt. Gen M.L. Naidu PVSM, AVSM, YSM and many senior serving and retired officers are expected.

Heading: Bail out Rajasansi: Majha leaders to CM - Indian Express
Content:
Alleging that the state government has failed to protect the interests of farmers, the Himachal Kisan Sabha (HKS) has decided to launch a statewide campaign from November 23 on issues including restoration of timber distribution rights, relief against monkey menace, increase in milk procurement price and proper availability of fertilisers.

In a meeting held over the past two days, which was attended by N.K. Shukla and Noorul Huda from the All India Centre, the HKS discussed that due to continuous attack on livelihood of peasants due to pressures of market forces, the agriculture sector in the state is in deep crisis. The experts observed that agriculture had become non- remunerative as the government has withdrawn its support to it in form of subsidies, increasing cost of production manifold.

President of HKS Tikender Singh Panwar said a mass-level protest would be staged across 36 blocks through rallies. "The government is answerable to people on various issues that were included in its party manifesto and so far the government has not done anything on it. The promises include increasing subsidies of seeds and fertilisers, system for marketing of vegetables and a strategy to tackle the menace of wild animals, especially monkeys," said Panwar.

The farmers affiliated to the Sabha have reported shortage of fertiliser. In a statement, general secretary of Kisan Sabha Onkar Shad said there has been a big loss to vegetable growers of the state due to continuous bad weather, but the government has not acted.

Heading: 'PTA teachers to be reinstated when Cong returns to power’ - Indian Express
Content:
MPs, ministers and MLAs of Majha region, led by MP Rattan Singh Ajnala and Information and Public Relations Minister Bikram Singh Majithia, today called on Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and requested him to write to Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh, Union Civil Aviation Minister, Praful Patel and Union Commerce Minister Kamal Nath to take immediate steps to ensure that ongoing international as well as domestic flights to Rajasansi Airport were not discontinued and its expansion work was completed at the earliest.

In a joint representation, they said the Union Civil Aviation Ministry should immediately bring down the landing charges for flights in Amritsar and make it lower than the Delhi airport.

They said the basic purpose of starting flights from Amritsar was to decongest Delhi airport, as 29 per cent of the international air traffic at Delhi was from Punjab. They said at present, Union Civil Aviation Ministry was charging Rs 1.54 lakh landing charges per flight from Singapore Airlines in Amritsar as compared to Rs 75,000 charged at Delhi airport.

Similarly, Jet Airways was shelling out Rs 94,000 as compared to Rs 69,000 paid in Delhi. They said nearly double landing charges in Amritsar were making flights from this airport unviable for the airlines.

The legislators said discontinuation of flights from Amritsar would hit the business, besides causing inconvenience to the pilgrims to Darbar Sahib and Vaishno Devi.

They also brought to the notice of the Chief Minister that Rs 140-crore expansion work of Rajasansi Airport was to be completed by October 31, but till date not even 40 per cent of it has been done, resulting in decrease in traffic to the Holy City airport.

Heading: Suicide after gang-rape: kin  of girl allege police inaction - Indian Express
Content:
All PTA teachers removed by the BJP government would be immediately re-instated and regularised when the Congress returns to power in 2013, announced former chief minister Virbhadra Singh, while talking to mediapersons here last evening. He said it was unfortunate that teachers appointed under PTA scheme had been removed without considering their credibility and qualification. He said Chief Minister P.K. Dhumal did this only because these teachers had been appointed by the Congress government. He said these teachers were appointed only in remote areas where no other teachers were willing to work.

Singh also expressed concern over the change of names of schemes introduced by his government. He said Rajiv Gandhi Post-Graduate Medical College at Paprola had been renamed as Dindayal Upadhyay College. He said similarly Rajiv Gandhi Kutir Avas Yojna had been named as Atal Bihari Avas Yojna.

Heading: ‘Ignored’ at state function, Mayor and others hit out at district administration - Indian Express
Content:
Complainants in a case of suicide by a girl, who was gang-raped in Bhindi Saidan village more than seven months ago, alleged that the police have failed to arrest two accused, as they enjoy political clout.

Kin of the girl today met Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla, who urged the IG (Border Range) Rajpal Meena to ensure that justice is done.

Mohan Singh, brother of the girl, said though Sahib Singh, one of the accused has been arrested, the police were yet to arrest his two accomplices, Lakha Singh and Billa Singh, who enjoy political backing.

"The cops are constantly pressurising us to reach a compromise within a month or face a fake case," said Fakir Singh, an uncle of the girl.

He alleged that Balwinder Singh, in charge of Lopoke police post, took an undertaking from them, ensuring a compromise within a month. But, the policeman had penned the undertaking himself, he said.

"This is jungle rule. We feel like leaving the village," said Bir Singh, another uncle of the girl.

Mohan said three youths had raped his 19-year-old sister, when she was returning home after an engagement ceremony along with him late in the evening. He said the accused, who belong to their village, waylaid her and beat him up when he objected. He added that his sister reached home with injuries on all over her body and was so upset that she committed suicide by consuming a poisonous substance.

An FIR was registered under sections 306 and 34 of the IPC on Mohan's complaint.

The IG said the matter was in his notice. "We are probing the case. Justice will be done," he said.

Heading: Log in here and get land at concessional rate - Indian Express
Content:
The Bathinda district administration today came under fire from Mayor Baljit Singh Beer Behman, Senior Deputy Mayor Tarsem Goel, Deputy Mayor Gurinderpal Kaur Mangat and a number of BMC councilors for the indifferent attitude shown to them during a function here today.

Social Security, Women and Child and Welfare Department minister Chaudhary Swarna Ram was the chief guest at the state level function organized to spread awareness about drug de-addiction. The drama unfolded before him. However, the Mayor, Senior Deputy Mayor and Deputy Mayor squarely blamed the district administration for the mess. The Mayor and others stated that the minister was not even told about their presence.

The agitating Mayor and other elected representatives were finally persuaded by officials of the Bathinda administration, including Deputy Commissioner Rahul Tewari, to attend the function, but not before they had spewed venom against the administration, while expressing their anguish to media.

Mayor Beer Behman, who is considered close to Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, threatened to take the district administration to task by bringing the matter to the CM's notice, and lodge a complaint with the administration. Senior Deputy Mayor and Deputy Mayor, who owe their allegiance to BJP, were equally upset with the developments and blamed the administration for it.

Beer Behman alleged that organizing officials did not recognize him as the Mayor, and asked him and others accompanying to him to sit somewhere else. None of the three were invited to light the ceremonial lamps for the function.

"I clearly told the officials that he is the Mayor, but they did not listen to me," said Deputy Mayor Gurinder Kaur Mangat. "We had to give our identification. The councilors were also humiliated, when the officials told them that they were not invited," Mangat added. She said the minister was not to be blamed for what had happened.

"There was total mismanagement on the part of the district administration. But the DC claimed that he was only an invitee, and was not involved with organising the function. He added that the district administration was not roped in to shoulder any organizing responsibility. I do not know, however, how much truth is there in what he says," said Senior Deputy Mayor Tarsem Goel.

Bathinda Deputy Commissioner Rahul Tewari said that it was a state level function organized by the Social Security, Women and Child Welfare Development Department. "The department officials decided who would sit where and who would speak," said Tewari, adding that district administration had a little role to play in the function.

Heading: Cycle sales drop, industry woos buyers with offers - Indian Express
Content:
Onir is ready to look at the funny side of relationships

His first two movies were pretty intense — My Brother Nikhil in 2005 and Bas Ek Pal a year later. Filmmaker Onir, 39, is now moving away from serious movies to have some fun. He experiments with comedy in Sorry Bhai, starring Shabana Azmi, Boman Irani, Sanjay Suri and Chitrangada Singh, who is back on screen after three years. "The idea is to explore different nuances of filmmaking," says Onir.

The romantic comedy, which will be released on November 28, is about a middle-class family from Mumbai going to Mauritius for their elder son's marriage. "Boman and Shabana share amazing chemistry on screen. I loved their performance in Honeymoon Travels Pvt Ltd and I am sure they will recreate the magic again," smiles Onir.

After wrapping up the promotion of Sorry Bhai, he wants to start his next venture, a yet untitled Indo-German collaboration that deals with the identity crisis of marginalised communities in India. And he also plans to direct the modern version of the 1980s classic Chashme Baddoor. "The original film dealt with the '80s. My script will be adapted for today's audience," he says. The fun run won't end soon.

Heading: Result not declared, PTU students harassed - Indian Express
Content:
The global meltdown has led to a reduction in the price of raw material used by the cycle industry. With this, major cycle industrialists of the region have come up with offers, decreasing the price of the basic model by Rs 50.

This is in stark contrast to the trend earlier this year. From January to September, there was a hike of Rs 370 in the price of bicycles. While these new offer are going to be introduced from November 1, a further fall is likely in the price of the basic model, as steel prices of domestic companies are expected to come down in the next few days.

About two months ago, the bicycle industry was crying for a reduction in prices of steel and other raw material. But now, when the prices of almost all the raw materials for the cycle parts have come down, sales have dropped drastically too. Buyers seem to be adopting a wait and watch policy, waiting for better offers.

In addition to slashing the price of bicycles, the industry has come up with offers for dealers, to enhance sales. Hero has offered its dealers a tyre at Rs 30 (its market price is Rs 70), along with the sale of every black bicycle. Atlas is offering a free chain along with the same model of bicycle. Avon has slashed the prices of its bicycle by Rs 30 approximately.

Agrees SK Rai, MD of Hero Cycles, "The global meltdown has gripped the domestic market as well. The customer will benefit from the slash in prices of steel, rubber, nickel, plastic etc."

Adds Onkar Singh Pahwa, MD of Avon Cycles, "Steel prices, which were in the range of Rs 45 a kg, have come down to Rs 26-27 a kg. But this variety is mostly used in building material. Our industry uses steel rods and steel strips. The prices of these goods have decreased marginally, but still we are passing on the benefit to the consumer. Accessories like bell, carrier, lock, stand etc have also become cheaper by about 10 per cent. Add the concession of Rs 30, and prices of bicycles will come down by Rs 50 approximately from November 1."

According to Charanjit Singh Vishvkarma, president of United Cycles Parts and Manufacturers Association, "Prices of some products like chain, wheel etc have also increased because scrap is being sold at throwaway prices. While making bicycles, 30-35% scrap is produced, for which we are not getting good prices now. The present rate of this scrap is Rs 17 a kg approximately. A month ago, the same scrap was being sold at Rs 30 a kg approximately."

Pahwa and Rai say that while dealers are either delaying the booking of orders, or are not ready to lift stocks, because they are expecting a further slash in prices. "Small scale industries are the worst hit by the fall in sales. We expect the market to pick up after two-three months. In the bicycle industry, a sudden increase and or fall in prices affects the business much," reasons Vishvkarma.

Heading: Little hearts need big help - Indian Express
Content:
The alleged non-declaration of result of the re-appear examination of many students of Punjab Technical University (PTU) has raised the hackles of their parents.

PTU authorities, however, said parents come to Punjab Technical University directly without checking with the institutes concerned. Randhir Verma, father of a B.Pharma student, alleged that his son had taken admission in MSc (Stem Cell and Tissue Engineering) in Panjab University (PU) on the basis of the confidential result provided by Punjab Technical University on September 1. "But now, Panjab University (PU) had refused to take the examination fee till the formal result card was provided," said Verma. He said he has been shuttling between Chandigarh and Jalandhar for two months, but to no avail.

Kulwant Singh alleged that the confidential result of his daughter was provided by Punjab Technical University in August, but till date her result has not been declared.

Punjab Technical University (PTU) Dean (Examination), Dr NP Singh said they had asked all the institutes to take the result from them, as the university doesn't deal directly with students. He said the result of many such students has already been sent to the institutes concerned.

Parents, on the other hand, said institutes had sent them to the university, and allege harassment.

Heading: Crater on Ridge creates panic - Indian Express
Content:
Surveys finds 250 cases of heart ailments among schoolkids; state health dept to sign a contract with PGI for treatment

Here'S heartbreaking news. A routine medical check-up by the state Health Department in about 12 government schools in Ropar and SAS Nagar revealed that many students were suffering from heart ailments.

So alarmed is the department by the results that they have decided to carry more such surveys in the state, for which a contract will be signed with PGI, Chandigarh, on November 5.

The survey found over 250 cases of various heart ailments among children, which are usually reported in adults. "The situation is worrisome," said Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla.

She said the preliminary inquiries in government school revealed that such cases would be in thousands if the figure was collected from throughout the state. The congenital malformations of heart, malnourishment, deformities in auricles and ventricles and severe anaemia and infections have been reported. "Such cases need special attention because most of them are related to diet and only immediate medical treatment can save the lives of children," said Chawla.

"We discussed the matter with PGI and they said they will take the responsibility of treating the children and the cost will be borne by the Health Department. We are paying PGI a lump some and more will be released as per requirements," said the minister, adding that funds would not come in the way, as she would seek special provisions in the next budget.

Dr Palwinder Singh, paediatrician at children's ward of Guru Nanak Hospital, said he was aware of the survey and over 60 per cent of the cases were due to congenital causes. "In most cases, disease was hereditary and in other due to severe infections, like rheumatic heart disease," he said, adding that the government must seriously think over the issue, as in certain cases children require surgery.

"District-wise teams will be formed to conduct surveys in all the government and aided schools," said Chawla, adding that if any poor child studying in a private school was found ailing, provision would be made to admit him in a government school to entitle him for treatment.

Heading: Civic body downplays malaria cases - Indian Express
Content:
MC says nothing serious, work on to plug hole

A six-feet-deep crater surfaced on the Ridge today, leading to panic among residents.

However, Shimla Municipal Corporation Mayor Narender Kataria said the deep hole had emerged on the Ridge as result of sinking of stones and debris around the sluice pipe used for draining dirty water from the storage tank beneath the Ridge. "It is not a serious thing and work has been started to close it," said the Mayor.

However, the technical staff of the MC denied that the crater had appeared due to sinking of soil and maintained that it had been purposely created since the construction of the Ridge many years ago to monitor the drain leading out of the water tank. They claimed that the hole was opened up today to carry out some repair work.

The heavy rains in September had also posed a threat to the Ridge as the land on the northwest hill side had sunk after being washed away and half of the Ridge towards Scandal Point was cordoned off for safety reasons at that time.

The Municipal Corporation has already approached the Asian Development Bank with a detailed proposal for long-term restoration of the Ridge and to prevent it from further sinking. The work is expected to involve an estimated cost of about Rs 3 crore.

Heading: After colleague dies, NRS nurses hold protest - Indian Express
Content:
Even though the state and the Central government officials repeatedly asked the local urban bodies to provide accurate figures of the reported cases of vector-borne diseases, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) health officials continue to suppress the data.

Reports submitted to Municipal Commissioner Alapan Bandyopadhya say that 25,109 malaria cases were reported in the city by October 29. A senior civic official, however, said that according to the reports received from 81 malaria clinics under the KMC, 25,667 cases of malaria were recorded in Kolkata by September 29.

Moreover, records of the main computer centre of KMC's health wing say that from October 5 to October 11, 2,142 blood samples were tested positive for malaria, of which 315 were detected with Falcifarum (malignant malaria).

"Anyone can gauge from the weekly reports we receive that there has been a considerable increase in the number of patients affected with vector-borne diseases," said a senior civic official.

Even though the figures of the state Health Department and the civic body never tally, no action has been taken action against those responsible for providing wrong figures. 

Bandyopadhaya, however, denies allegations of fudging the figures. "Reports of the Health Department and the KMC do not tally, as there is some confusion in ascertaining the area under the KMC jurisdiction. Sometimes we do not receive reports from private labs and cannot add them to the final report," he said.

Former director of School of Tropical Medicine, Amiya Hati said: "The KMC always collects passive data by which it can never get the correct figures. Consequently, the vector-borne diseases continue to spread because even one unregistered case holds the potential to affect ten more people."

Heading: Day after blast, Bengal DGP admits to security lapse - Indian Express
Content:
Protesting against the death of their colleague, a few nurses at the NRS Medical College and Hospital submitted a deputation to Medical Superintendent L K Ghosh on Monday, asking him to probe the reason behind her death.

Staff Nurse Kaveri Bhowmik was down with fever and admitted to the hospital on October 20. But she died two days later. While the death certificate says Bhowmik had suffered a stroke, fellow nurses claim she showed the symptoms of dengue or encephalitis. "Her platelet count was below normal. She was running temperature, vomiting blood and had convulsions. These are symptoms of dengue or encephalitis. But she was not administered treatment for these diseases," said nurse Parvati, convener of the Forum for Safety and Security of Nurses.

Members of the fourm claimed that Bhowmik was not given proper treatment, not even given a bed and was also not given proper attention by the head of the nursing staff.

"In our deputation, we have asked for 10 beds to be reserved for doctors and members of the nursing staff in the emergency ward. We have also sent a petition to the Shastha Bhavan to inquire why the head nurse was negligent towards Bhowmick. If a nurse can be treated in such a callous way, there is little hope for outsiders," said Parvati. Citing medical negligence by the hospital authorities, the nurses also demanded compensation for the victim's family.

Bhowmik, the nurses say, was the sole earning member of her family and had been a working as a nurse at the hospital for 13 years. Her sister Sraboni Sarkar alleged that Bhowmik's death had led her family to penury. The nurses also demanded a job for the deceased's brother to support the family.

Ghosh has agreed to conduct an inquiry and accepted the petition to reserve 10 beds in the hospital for its staff. "I have forwarded the petition to the Director of Medical Enquiry (DME)," he said.

Nurses, however, said they will approach the DME within seven days and take up the matter with him.

Heading: ‘Govt should have done more to save Nano project’ - Indian Express
Content:
The West Bengal government has admitted to a lapse in security of the chief minister which suspected Maoists used to target his convoy in Salboni on Sunday. And the man to admit this was none other than West Bengal Director General of Police AB Vohra.

Six policemen were injured in the blast that ripped through a police jeep minutes after the convoy carrying Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Union minister Ram Vilas Paswan passed the spot.

Police said six persons had been arrested. Three policemen — an inspector and two constables — who were responsible for manning the blast spot have been suspended for dereliction of duty.

Vohra, who rushed to the blast site on Monday morning, also talked to the district administration and pointed out the lapses in CM's security.

Later talking to reporters, he said: "The police failed to apprehend the attack."

After receiving a primary report from the DGP, Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti described Sunday's incident as "a serous lapse in security".

"No one responsible for the incident will be spared, no matter how big an officer one is," Chakrabarti said.

The CPM state secretary, Biman Bose, made it amply clear that the police and intelligence failure was the reason for Sunday's incident.

"The administration should have had information that such a thing was about to happen. The Maoists had over a half-kilometer-long wire attached to the bomb. It ran through open fields and along a canal bank. It is very difficult to accept that no one saw them," said Bose. Sources in the Chief Minister's secretariat said even Bhattacharjee himself was unhappy about the role of the district police. He has pointed out the lack of intelligence inputs.

Apart from the inquiry initiated by the DGP, Bhattacharjee has directed his Chief Security Officer, AK Maliwal, to file a separate report on the incident. "The superintendent of police of West Midnapore cannot deny his responsibility," said a senior official of the CM's secretariat.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Union Home minister Shivraj Patil, meanwhile, had a telephonic conversation with the Bhattacharjee on Monday. "Both asked about my well being and wanted to know the details of Sunday's incident," the chief minister told reporters.

Earlier in the day, both Vohra and Maliwal made a on the spot inquiry of Sunday's blast. The officers traversed through the paddy fields adjacent to the blast spot and went to the point from where the Maoists reportedly triggered the blast.

They tried to comprehend how the high tension wire, overhead the blast site, snapped with the blast. The police are also trying to trace the escape routes that the Maoists could have used.

Both the officers were present for more than two hours on the spot and later Vohra held a series of meetings with the district police officers.

Heading: Buddha apprehensive about economic meltdown - Indian Express
Content:
The Parliamentary State Secretary of Federal Ministry of Economic and Technology, Germany, Hartmut Schauerte, smacked the state for not being industry-friendly, as the Tata Motors' pull out has discouraged German investors to venture into the state.

"I understand that the government tried its level best to keep the Nano project in the state. But the government should have convinced the Opposition or used its power," Schauerte said.

Schauerte is in the city to inaugurate International Mining Machinery Exhibition (IMME) 2008

"An investment depends on three factors — the government, the society and the Opposition. If any of these tumbles upon, then the entire investment gets affected," Schauerte said.

According to him, the state should concentrate on small and medium enterprises.

Nearly seven German delegations are scheduled to visit the country till December, but not a single one is going to visit West Bengal.

Schauerte, however, said the state can still hope to attract more investments. "The agitation in Singur by the villagers implies that the society has started responding against people who are anti-development and it sends a positive signal to industrialists," Schauerte said.

Heading: ICC concerned about exporters hit by global crisis - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Monday expressed concerns over the effect of global meltdown on the economy.

Expressing apprehensions about the situation, Bhattacharjee said the crisis has not affected only the banking sector but also sectors like manufacturing, real estate and information technology.

"We are in the middle of an economic crisis and we do not know what is going to happen in the next few days," said the chief minister, who is a strong supporter of industrialisation in the state.

Bhattacharjee was speaking at the inauguration of 36th IAHS World Congress on Housing Science, hosted by Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, at a city hotel. Talking about housing projects in West Bengal, he said the state government would come up with townships at Dankuni in Hooghly, Domjur in Howrah and Baruipur. He added that the major realty players like Shapoorji & Pallonji and the DLF were developing townships in the state.

The chief minister also stressed on the problem of availability of land in urban areas. "Some companies like Lakshmi Mittal and Jindal Steel want to set up their central offices at Rajarhat. But prices are as high as Rs 7 crore per acre," Bhattacharjee added.

Addressing delegates at the three-day convention, he said that RK Pachauri, advisor to the state government, has suggested that arrangements for harvesting rain water and harnessing solar power be made in all housing complexes.

Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee, who was the chief guest on the occasion, said that by the end of the 10th Five Year Plan there will be a shortage 24.7 million dwelling units and this may go up to 26.53 million units by the end of the 11th Plan.

Addressing the crisis which the housing sector may face because of the urban explosion, state Minister for Housing and Urban Development Gautam Deb said that about 90,000 houses are required in the state and the government with all its agencies and joint venture companies has been able to come up with only 20,000 houses.

According to Deb, on an average, 47 per cent people in the world reside in urban areas and in India the percentage is 28 per cent. Within 10-15 years, however, the demand for houses in urban areas may increase by 40-42 per cent.

Heading: Rajasthan-Bengal Maitri Parishad inaugurated - Indian Express
Content:
The global financial crisis and falling demand in the US and European markets are adversely affecting exports from India. According to the Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC), from an average growth of 35 per cent between April and August, the growth in exports fell to 10 per cent in September. This has triggered sizeable lay-offs in labour-intensive export sector.

According to the ICC, the government needs to take immediate measures to prevent these job losses.

According to an ICC statement released in Kolkata on Monday, the financial sector crisis has exposed exporters to greater risks on the credit given to buyers. Insurance firms have hiked premium rates by 25 - 30 per cent for export credit insurance covers and have imposed a host of restrictions like maximum liability and credit limit in case of single buyers. The statement said that fearing losses, insurance firms have also stopped covering pre-shipment risks.

Suggesting ways to pull out exporters from the present crisis, the ICC said that all insurance companies, including Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Limited, should be advised to provide insurance covers at reasonable cost, to help exporters in concentrating on their businesses without worrying about the credit default of the buyers.

It added that currency has been extremely volatile in the last nine months throwing several exporters off balance. Exporters have booked long-term contracts to hedge their foreign exchange exposure, which has now resulted in huge losses, the ICC statement said. The chamber requested the government to allow moratorium to exporters, so that those who have booked their forward cover or hedged the currency, are saved from paying substantial differences to banks for the unexpected mounting losses.

Heading: Kolkata Port Trust acquires new dredger - Indian Express
Content:
With the inauguration of Rajasthan-Bengal Maitri Paishad on Monday, the CPM has strengthened its strategy of wooing the Rajasthani community in the city.

Despite CPM member Narayan Jain claiming the organisation to be a non-political one, the presence and involvement of leftists at the inauguration of the parishad was conspicuous.

"The parishad is an important step towards improving relations between Rajasthani and Bengali communities. Rajasthanis residing in Bengal are equally contributing in the development of West Bengal," said Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee.

The chief minister condemned the incidents of animosity between Biharis and Marathis and said that every Indian citizen has the right to live anywhere within the country.

"It is the cultural tradition of West Bengal that people of all communities live in harmony and such incidents are unthinkable in the state," Bhattacharjee added. Left Front chairman Biman Bose also lauded the formation of the parishad. The inauguration was attended by guests like MP Salim, MP Sudhanshu Seal, MP Prashanta Chatterjee, CPM party secretary of Rajasthan Basudev Acharia and CPM state committee member Robin Deb.

"The object behind the formation of this parishad is to strengthen relations, exchange and promote culture of both the states," said MP Hannan Mollah, convener of the parishad.

Rajasthan Bengal Maitri Paishad will not only help in promoting business activities between both the states, but also aims to promote tourism, socio-cultural activities, education and vocational training.

Mollah said, "We have seen people from other states facing problems in Maharashtra and Assam. Even people from West Bengal sometimes have to face problems in other states, as they are branded as Bangladeshis."

A similar gathering of the parishad is planned in Jaipur after the Assembly elections.

Heading: CPM cadres launch parallel inquiry - Indian Express
Content:
In order to tackle the dredging and draught problems, the Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) on Monday announced that it has acquired a state-of-the-art dredger — Dredger 16 — from the Sethu Samudram project to add to its fleet of five dredgers.

State Secretary for Commerce and Industry Sabyasachi Sen had earlier admitted that the decreasing river draught had made it difficult for ships to enter the Haldia port, adding that the government would appeal to the Centre for help.

The worsening silting situation at Haldia had made it imperative for the KoPT to acquire a new dredger. The dredger was commissioned on Monday. The KoPT has, meanwhile, announced that its another dredger, Dredger 14, which was sent to Vishakhapatnam for repairs would be ready to join the fleet by the end of November.

At present, the draught at Haldia is around 7.10 meters and 17 ships are anchored at the dock loading and unloading their cargo.

The Haldia dock has handled 25.293 million tonnes of cargo between April-October 31, 2008. The cargo is expected to touch 44 million tonnes by the end of this financial year. In 2007, between April and October, the dock had handled 25.168 million tonnes of cargo.

"In 2007-08 we handled 43.588 million tonnes of cargo, but the draught situation needs to improve further, hence the new dredger was required," said BK Sahu, Chief Public Relations Officer, KoPT.

He added that the Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS) along with the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways were working along with the trust in schemes like river survey and river training works.

"Dredging the river bed alone will not solve the problem. River training and dredging together will lead to a significant improvement in handling draught problem, as one needs to monitor the river to see where dredging is required and can be done," Sahu said.

Heading: Declare Todis proclaimed offenders, CBI asks court - Indian Express
Content:
Cops suspect three Maoists were involved, villagers say strangers on mobike were seen at the spot

The CPM cadres of Salboni virtually conducted a parallel inquiry on Monday to find out who triggered the landmine targetting the Chief Minister' convoy.

Officers from the Salboni police station had carried out a raid in the villages last night, said Jogen Roy, a resident of Kuturia village. But at 11 am, the CPM cadres showed up to inspect the paddy field from where the blast was triggered. Soon after, a group visited the villagers and questioned them in search of possible eyewitnesses. Dipak Sarkar, the CPM district committee secretary, said the party had instructed them to maintain a strong vigil in and around the villages of Salboni.

According to senior officers of Salboni police, preliminary investigations suggest that possibly three Maoists had carried out the blast. They had triggered the landmine from the paddy field, a carefully chosen location from which the VIP convoy was clearly visible. It is suspected that after the blast, the activists left. They walked through the village road to reach a dairy farm in Kuturia village. The villagers, however, say a red motorbike was waiting near Sidheswari dairy for at least 15 minutes around 2.30 pm — the time the blast occurred.

The spot is remote and only a few locals were present with their herds. A boy, Madan Bhuinya, said he had seen three youths who were around 30 years old, dressed in formal shirt and trousers. They also had sunglasses on. Their motorbike disappeared into the forest soon after.

The CPM cadres suspect two residents of Kuturia village had acted as a link to the Maoists. Local CPM leader Shyam Pande, however, said the Maoists are not active in this area. They are more active in Lalgarh, about 23 kilometres from Salboni. Police say if the trio escaped on motorbike, it would take them only 45 minutes to reach Lalgarh. The blast, they suspect, was carried out by the Lalgarh squad of the Maoists.

Heading: Mamata rallies against Singur violence - Indian Express
Content:
Fearing that Ashok Todi and his relatives — accused in the Rizwanur Rehman murder case — may skip the country, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has requested a court to announce them proclaimed offenders.

The court had issued arrest warrants against Ashok and Pradip Todi and their relative Anil Saraogi on October 27. The CBI was directed to produce them on November 3.

"It appears that the absconders are in hiding and we apprehend that they might transfer their properties in the name of some other person and leave the country," said Partha Tapaswi, senior public prosecutor for the CBI. The court will decide on the CBI appeal on November 10.

The petition by the Todis to stop the proceedings of the lower courts, meanwhile, was admitted by Murari Mohan Ghosh, chief judge of the city sessions court. But no stay order was passed. The CBI can still arrest the Todis, said Tapaswi.

Earlier, Partha Sarathi Ghosh, the agency official investigating the case, filed a report on the non-execution of the arrest warrant.

In its report, the CBI admitted that it was unable to arrest the three absconders despite the best efforts. "The agency raided the residence and offices of the Todis in Kolkata and other places but they could not be found. They are evading arrest," stated the report filed in the court of Bibhash Chatterjee on Monday.

After the court declares the absconders as proclaimed offenders, the CBI can issue a lookout notice with their photographs in the media. "The agency might also declare a reward for anyone who could help in arresting the Todis," a lawyer said. But if the accused still remain elusive, the agency can appeal to court to take over their property.

The interim bail for the three officers of Kolkata police — Ajay Kumar, Sukanti Chakraborty and Krishnendu Das — was extended till November 10. The officers appeared before the court around 11 am on Monday. A huge force was deployed in the court before the officers arrived.

Heading: CM’s security tightened - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee on Monday participated in a rally organised to protest against the violence caused by the CPM-backed Save Nano Committee in Singur on Sunday.

"The CPM cannot decide our venue of meeting. Had the people of Singur really wanted to prevent us from entering the area, we could have never reached there," said Banerjee.

The rally was attended by Trinamool leaders such as Sougata Ray, Shobhan Dev Chattopadhyay and Madan Mitra. Rizwanur Rehman's brother Rukbanur also attended the march.

Banerjee said not a single person in Singur was disappointed by the Tata pullout. "Only those who had dreamt of thrieving Tata's money are disappointed," she said. "We are not against industrialisation. Had we opposed industries, the state government would not have been able to inaugurate the steel plant at Salboni," said the Trinamool leader.

She challenged the government to make the agreement with Tatas public and said, "Tata Motors had preferred to leave the state than disclose the details of the agreement."

In Singur, members of the Krishi Jomi Jibon Raksha Committee staged a protest near the local police station. There was a minor tussle between the committee members and the police but the situation was brought under control.

Heading: Bengal keen on Chinese investment in automobile sector - Indian Express
Content:
After the chief minister narrowly escaped a blast triggered by suspected Maoists at Salboni in West Midnapore on Sunday, the Kolkata police have made unprecedented security arrangements for his movements in the city.

The police went into a tizzy soon after Sunday's incident. Following a meeting of senior police officers, a communiqué was sent to all the police stations of the city informing them about the tightened security of the chief minister.

The Kolkata police have decided that the streets and footpaths through which the chief minister's convoy passes will be thoroughly combed for bombs. Till now, the CM's security cover mainly involved an escort car that moved ahead of his convoy.

The officer in-charge or the additional officer in-charge of the police station concerned will have to be present in the area whenever the chief minister's convoy will pass through.

Keeping in mind the way the bomb was placed under a tree on Sunday, the police have also decided to trim the trees on the chief minister's route. The Kolkata Municipal Corporation will be asked to trim the trees lining Lover Lane and Khiderpore Road.

As Bhattacharjee is a frequent visitor to Nandan, his security at Nandan and Rabindra Sadan complex will also be stepped up. According to police sources, garbage bins in the area will be emptied regularly so that subversive groups cannot place explosives in them.

Heading: Brothers in Arms - Indian Express
Content:
Although the state had to bid adieu to Nano, the West Bengal government is still keen on setting up an automobile manufacturing hub in the state and is looking for Chinese investment in the sector.

"We are keen to develop an automobile manufacturing hub in West Bengal and for that purpose we welcome investment from China and other foreign countries," Sabyasachi Sen, Principal Secretary, state Department of Commerce and Industries, told a visiting Chinese delegation on Monday.

The delegation from the Hubei province of China was participating in a seminar organised by the Bharat Chamber of Commerce on the investment opportunities in West Bengal.

This is the first important visit by a government delegation from China after the inauguration of the Chinese consulate in the city two months ago.

Stressing on the state government's determination to set up the manufacturing hub, Sen said that such automobile clusters already exist in other parts of the country like Gurgaon, Pune and Chennai and that the government believed that eastern India needed one too.

"While there are automobile clusters in western, southern and northern parts of the country, we are yet to have it in eastern India. So, we have invited Chinese companies to look for investment opportunities in two-wheeler and four-wheeler segments," Sen said.

The seminar mainly focused on areas like petrochemical, engineering, leather, information technology and infrastructural sectors.

"With the gross domestic product of Hubei province reaching RMB 915 billion Yuan, we are looking forward to invest in West Bengal as we see opportunities galore here," said Li Xiansheng, Executive Governor of Hubei province and leader of the delegation. Apprising the delegation on the industrial growth of the state, S P Yadav, Executive Director, West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation Limited, said: "Last year, the state received an investment of Rs 4,000 crore and has 75 projects worth $ 990 million in the pipeline."

In 2006-07, West Bengal had recorded a net state domestic product of Rs 18,82,870 million with an industrial growth of 16.02 per cent and agricultural growth of 8 per cent. "From January 2008 to September 2008, the bilateral trade between India and China stood at $42 billion and is expected to touch $56 billion by the year end, touching the target of $60 billion much before the slated 2010," said Mao Siwei, Consul General of China in Kolkata.

Heading: Urban landscape - Indian Express
Content:
Director Onir's next film is about two brothers vying for the attention of the same woman

When the word first began to circulate across cyberworld in early 2005 about India's "first gay film", Onir was a name not many of us were familiar with. However, the young director from Kolkata had enough conviction to rope in the likes of Juhi Chawla and Karan Johar for his debut film, My Brother Nikhil. Today, My Brother Nikhil has a cult following and Onir is a filmmaker of considerable repute in the industry. Yet, he feels he has a lot to prove with his next film Sorry Bhai. "This film is very different from my earlier two films. Bas Ek Pal was a very dark film. Sorry Bhai belongs to a different genre. It's a romantic comedy, a genre which I feel is not very easy to handle," says Onir.

Sorry Bhai, which releases later this month has the director's favourite Sanjay Suri as a part of an ensemble cast which includes names like Shabana Azmi, Boman Irani, Sharman Joshi and Chitrangadha Singh. "It is about a guy who is irresistibly drawn to his brother's fiancee. It tackles the concept of forbidden love in a contemporary, progressive manner," says Onir. Very much like the way the gay relationship was treated in his debut film, My Brother Nihil. But wasn't he afraid of being tagged as a "gay filmmaker'? "Not at all. All I wanted to do was make a film about relationships," he says. As sensitive as his handling of the gay relationship in the film was, Onir was not spared criticism. "People felt I played it safe by not showing any kind of physical intimacy between my characters. But my focus was on their rapport and the emotional bond they shared. Had I shown two guys kissing on screen, the film would have been in news for all the wrong reasons. Even in Sorry Bhai I try and refrain from showing any sensational scene," he states.

Which brings us back to the film which is also being touted as Chitrangadha Singh's comeback film. "I keep asking her why did she agree to do my film when so many other directors were dying to work with her," he laughs. But he agrees that it was a pleasure to work with her. "She brings a different kind of sensibility to a film. She is very urban yet Indian," he says.

Heading: Saas, Bahu and Revolution - Indian Express
Content:
This Colombian writer paints dark, vivid portraits of metropolis and the life of immigrants

In retrospect, Santiago Gamboa (in the picture), Colombian writer and the new consul at the Embassy of Colombia in Delhi, feels he was born in Peru. Not that his country, made famous by writer Gabriel Garcia Marquez's chronicles of provincial towns and ramblings of Colonel Aurelia Buendia, did not offer outlandish literary imagination.

But, besides the magical realism of Marquez's novels, there was little scope of broaching the urban reality of everyday Colombia convulsed by paramilitary forces, drug lords and hit men. "At the age of 16, I had the desire to become a writer. Sometimes, I considered it my bad luck and wished I was born in Lima where urban literature flourished and I could write about big cities," says Gamboa, 42, who recently moved to Delhi. He is part of the group of young Colombian writers who are cranking out dark, realistic novels, a departure from Marquez.

For him, it is not just a question of giving an identity to Bogota, the capital of Colombia in literature, but also to talk about the problems that deal with social reality. His book The Ulysses Syndrome (2005) is a gripping tale of a young immigrant writer who washes dishes in an oriental kitchen, while his latest novel Hotel Pekín talks about Colombian Francisco Munévar who adopts an American identity to become the "star trainer" of an American assistance company. "When I was in Paris, it was difficult to find a street which had not appeared in (Marcel) Proust or (Honoré) Balzac's books," smiles Gamboa. "This propelled us more into giving a definite identity to the Bogota we grew up in," he adds.

He does not deny that coming from Colombia gives a sad advantage to writers. "Yes,it does, in a way, with the situation around us," shares Gamboa, who has also written about Paris from the vantage point of Madrid and Rome from the vantage point of Paris.

Will the move to Delhi influence his literary works? "There is a striking similarity between Bogota and Delhi and it may feature in my works," he replies.

Up next, Gamboa will be bringing out an anthology of stories by Colombian writers. Literary gatherings and discussions with Colombian writers in Delhi are also on the cards.

Heading: Sohal props up Punjab on Day One - Indian Express
Content:
In its thirteenth year, The Great Indian Rock gets a bunch of foreign bands and comes to Kolkata

Thirteen years ago, a festival called The Great Indian Rock began with bands from across the country competing at Delhi's open-air theatre Hamsadhwani. This season, with the name tweaked a little to The Fuel Great Indian Rock, the fest will have a new avatar as it transforms into a national concert tour, spanning seven cities — Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad and Shillong— with 21 Indian bands and three international acts. "The festival has always aimed at providing local bands a platform to write and perform good, original music. It is not a competition anymore, it is purely bands in concert," says Amit Saigal, founder of the festival.

After the fest kicked off at Mumbai's Andheri Sports Complex on Friday, it plays out in Delhi on November 1 and 2 with myriad subgenres of rock spelt out by bands such as Them Clones, Kryptos, Undying Inc and Frequency alongside the hard rock act put forth by the Swedish band Freak Kitchen (in the picture) and the Norwegian black metal bands Sahg and Satyricon. "The foreign bands and the Indian bands together will add to the festival since it's always good to mix things and see what comes out of it," says Saigal. "Well, to be honest there is nothing super happening in the western hemisphere. It is here that all the energy is happening," says Mattias Eklundh, vocalist and guitarist of Freak Kitchen, which also performed at the fest last year and have been so smitten by the country's rock and raga that in their upcoming album they have Indian classical musicians like flautist V Selvaganesh playing.

But it is a first for Sahg and most of the Indian bands. Saigal says all that mattered in choosing them was a good, original song. "It doesn't matter how fast you play, it is all about good song writing," he says. And with bands putting out their originals and pushing the envelope, this season seems to be bigger than ever.

Heading: Damage control: Consolation prize for Arindam - Indian Express
Content:
The first delivery was a bouncer from Pradeep Sangwan that he fended off deftly. Next ball, an inside edge rolled dangerously close to the the stumps. Then, sandwiched between two deliveries that were left alone, one ball touched a dead bat. And finally, off the last ball of the over, he tamely lobbed a catch to first slip. The Yuvraj Singh show started 10 minutes before lunch, and ended with two minutes still left for the interval — six balls, eight minutes, no score.

Yuvraj was the first of his team mates to arrive at the ground on Monday morning, and remained at the Roshanara Club with the last batch that saw the covers coming on, and the outfield being invaded by members. But the left-hander, playing his first match for Punjab in two years, couldn't remain for long enough in the middle of the crease, the spot he so desperately needed to occupy.

On his dismissal, Yuvraj trudged slowly towards the pavilion, and while he remained the 'main event' thereafter for autograph hunters, his colleague Sunny Sohal reveled in the attention of national selector Yashpal Sharma with his maiden century that helped the visitors recover from a precarious 92 for 3 to a healthy 237 for 5 when play ended early due to fading light. Uday Kaul and Ankur Kakkad remained united through the post-tea schedule for a sixth-wicket stand of 61 as Delhi lost their early initiative.

Sohal, coming in at number three after Ashish Nehra has sent Karan Goel's stumps flying, remained a nervous starter with the pitch offering ample justification for Delhi skipper Aakash Chopra's decision to field first. But once the sheen off the new ball was taken off, and the ball replaced twice inside 26 overs, the lone right-hander in the top-four latched on to anything pitched up. He prospered in the middle session, belting 10 boundaries for his half-century and nine more in his next 50 as the wicket eased up considerably under the afternoon sun.

Sizzling Nehra

The Delhi bowlers bowled well only in patches, but Nehra clearly stood out as someone belonging to a higher level of cricket. The lanky left-arm seamer started with an incisive spell with the new ball, and was probing throughout his other spells. The effort gave him scant rewards but generated ample admiration. His understudy, Sangwan, was a touch guilty of overdoing the short stuff but doled out a lion-hearted performance nonetheless. He provided vital breakthroughs in his second spell, removing Ravi Inder Singh and Yuvraj after a change of ends. Amit Bhandari bowled with zest but without any luck and together the pace attack asked questions, inducing seven outside edges that dropped frustratingly short of an extended slip cordon.

Seam-up Rajat Bhatia and leg-spinner Chetanya Nanda proved steady allies — the latter had Sohal for 110 at mid-on — but the lack of a specialist off-spinner against a team that has five left-handers didn't help Delhi's cause as the day wore on.

Brief scores: Punjab 237 for 5 in 85.2 overs (S Sohal 110, R Inder Singh 37, A Kakkar batting 30; P Sangwan 2/56, A Nehra 1/66) vs Delhi.

Heading: Cloud over PHL, Dec 4 hearing - Indian Express
Content:
After Ranji snub, CAB appoints the player as Rest of Bengal captain

Just a few days after he was omitted from the Bengal Ranji team, Arindam Das has been given the responsibility to lead the Rest of Bengal squad that will play a practice match against the first-choice XI at the Eden Gardens from November 4 to 6.

The CAB is organising this game to give match practice to the players after Bengal's Ranji Plate Group opener against Assam was postponed due to the blasts in Guwahati last week.

"I hope the boys will take this opportunity before they start their Ranji campaign," said Bengal coach Utpal Chatterjee.

Das' omission created some controversy with Manoj Tiwary hitting out at the selectors. CAB joint-secretary Arun Mitra, however, said the issue was a closed chapter.

Joint felicitation?

CAB is likely to felicitate Anil Kumble, along with Sourav Ganguly at a function in the first week of December. According to sources, the association top brass is mulling over this idea, though nothing has been finalised yet. Kumble, who retired from Test and first class cricket yesterday, had his best ODI figures at the Eden Gardens when he ran through the West Indies batting line-up in the 1993 Hero Cup final and returned with a career best 6 for 12. He also had a Bengal connection the day he took a Perfect Ten at Ferozeshah Kotla. He borrowed a pair of boots from Laxmi Ratan Shukla, an India team member then, during that innings after his own boots started to give some trouble.

Teams for the practice match: Team-1: Laxmi Ratan Shukla (captain), Rohan Banerjee, Anustup Majumder, Manoj Tiwary, Wriddhiman Saha, Soham Ghosh, Iresh Saxena, Sourashis Lahiri, Ranadeb Bose, Shib Shankar Paul, Ashok Dinda, Aranyadeb Sarkar.

Team-2: Arindam Das (captain), Sreevats Goswami, Ritam Kundu, Avik Chowdhury, Sourav Sarkar, S Nadeem, Dibyendu Chakraborty, Avik Mallick, Amitava Chakraborty, Ambarish Mitra, Priyankar Mukherjee, Prinan Dutta.

Team for under-22 CK Nayudu Trophy: Arindam Ghosh (captain), Sufian Khan, Debabrata Das, Amit Das, Md Aziz Ansari, Arnab Nandi, Nilkantha Das, Bunty Gwala, Pankaj Shaw, Aritra Chatterjee, Debopam Biswas, Shamshad Hassain, Stalin Ghosh, Ashrafuddin.

Heading: CBI registers 9 FIRs in food scam - Indian Express
Content:
After much delay, the Anti-Corruption wing of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered nine cases in connection with the multi-crore foodgrain scam.

The scam was related to the misuse of the foodgrain meant for the Below Poverty Line families during the Samajwadi Party rule between March 2004 and October 2005.

According to CBI sources, eight cases were lodged related to Ballia district involving eight chief development officers and four other PCS rank officers. The other case related to Lakhimpur Kheri in which 10 PCS rank officers and 90 others have been named.

The Ballia scam amounted to Rs 14 crore and Kheri to Rs 1.25 crore.

The state government had recommended a CBI probe into the scam related to Ballia, Gonda and Kheri districts on December 1, 2007. The agency, however, only took the case of Ballia and Kheri and conducted the preliminary inquiry before lodging the FIRs.

Earlier, the matter had been investigated by the Food Cell of the state police and was being probed by the CB-CID before the CBI took it up. The police had then registered 251 FIRs at several police stations of Ballia, Gonda and Kheri districts.

The cases related to the Ballia district were picked up from the earlier FIRs lodged with the six police stations. Similarly, an FIR lodged with the Sadar police station in Kheri by the state police, too, was included in the fresh CBI case registered on Monday.

List of accused

Ballia case: Chief Development Officers — Ram Murti, JB Singh, Hiramani, Hari Om, Ashwini Kumar Srivastava, Deenanath Patwa, Kedar Prasad Gupta and Tapendra Kumar.

Project Directors — Arjun Ram and RB Singh District Development Officers — Ram Kishun and Lal Bahadur

Kheri case: The CBI named 10 of the then SDMs and 90 others including district supply officers and supply inspectors posted in the district during 2004-2005.
