Heading: BJP’s Lok Sabha strategy: ignore rebellion in UP, welcome good governance in other states - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Police are hunting for four absconding constables accused of thrashing, molesting and making seven citizens of Nepal hostage, among them five women, in Gorakhpur on October 30. The absconding constables are Harendra, Shatrugan, Manoj Patel and Kameshwar.

Four persons, including constable Rajesh Pandey, were arrested the same day. The

Nepalese were Mannaya, Neema, Chameli, Budhimaya, Nanu Maya, Bhagyaman and Man Bahadur.

On October 30, Inspector General (Gorakhpur zone) Harish Chandra Kashyap received a call that some miscreants had held hostage a few Nepalese at Mallika Guesthouse near Gorakhpur Railway Station. A police team rushed to the hotel and rescued seven Nepalese from room number 209. 

Circle Officer of Gorakhpur, Vishwajeet Srivastava said the victims informed that they were held hostage by the policemen and the guesthouse owner. The Nepalese also accused the policemen of molesting the women. "Since the women did not complaint of rape, we did not send them for medical check-up," said Srivastava.

The Nepalese were going to Dubai via Gorakhpur and Mumbai for work. They told the police that on October 27, they had come to Gorakhpur from Nepal by road with one Gopal, who had arranged their ticket and visa for Dubai. When they reached Gorakhpur, one Rajesh Verma alias Raju met them and told them that he could arrange their stay at a guesthouse.

According to the police, when the Nepalese reached the guesthouse and retired into the room, four policemen barged in, beat them up and demanded Rs 25,000. "After the beating, the Nepalese decided to give money. They sent Gopal to their house to arrange the money," said Srivastava. Gopal did not return.

The police, meanwhile, conducted a raid at the guesthouse and released the victims. The police also arrested the guesthouse owner Rakesh Kumar Singh and manager Anil Sharma. Later, the police also arrested Raju and one constable Rajesh Pandey, who told the police about his four other accomplices — constables Harendra, Shatrugan, Manoj Patel and Kameshwar.

Senior Superintendent of Police ( Gorakhpur) R K Srivastava suspended the outpost in-charge Vinay Pathak and sent Inspector Cantt Mangla Prasad Tiwari to Lines.

The SSP said, "The Nepalese have been sent back to their country."

Heading: 40 days after HC order, FIR filed against Yogi - Indian Express
Content:
Forget rebellion in Uttar Pradesh, welcome good governance in other states—- this is the mantra, the Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) will follow in the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections.

The party is losing its already weak support among Other Backward Castes (OBC) in the state. Caste leaders like Kalyan Singh, Om Prakash Singh and Vinay Katiyar are not seen in party meetings and speculations are rife about the differences emerging within the party among various caste groups.

The BJP, therefore, has decided to ignore these leaders and shift its focus to cash on the issue of 'good governance' in BJP-led states namely Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Uttarakhand. "We are trying to increase the Lok Sabha seats in other states, rather than wasting energy on cajoling the rebel leaders in UP, which may provide at most a few more seats," said a senior party leader.

He explained that due to strong presence of regional parties like the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and the Samajwadi Party (SP), UP has almost lost its credentials of being the 'seat of power'.

The party will, therefore, focus on other states where it has performed well and a little effort can secure handsome gains. "We will be satisfied with whatever we gain in UP. We will be glad if our LS seat tally in the state increases to 15 from nine at present."

This perhaps explains why no senior party leader is talking about the rebellion in the party. "There is no rebellion, all decisions are taken by consensus," said Kalraj Mishra, the party election in- charge of Uttar Pradesh, after holding the first meeting of leaders in Lucknow on Saturday. Incidentally, all the aforementioned OBC leaders were absent in the meeting. Mishra, however, said they were on a statewide tour to garner support for the party.

Sources also said to counter the SP and the BSP, the party is trying to tie up with small but powerful parties in different regions of the state. A truck with Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) is almost final in western UP. The BJP is considering giving seats of Baghpat, Muzaffarnagar, Mathura, Bijnor and Nagina to the RLD. So far, the BJP has only two MPs, Kalyan Singh and Ashok Pradhan, in western UP and the new alliance is expected to bring gains to the party.

Speculations are also rife that the party national president Rajnath Singh will contest from Ghaziabad seat. Of late, Singh was seen taking part in several programmes in Ghaziabad. In two rallies, his sons also participated.

In poorvachal (eastern UP) BJP is negotiating with Sanjay Chauhan of Janvadi Party and Om Prakash Rajbhar of the Bhartiya Samaj Party to gain OBC votes.

On October 31, Rajbhar had held a Pal sammelan to show his strength, where Rajnath was the chief guest. Sources said the party is first negotiating for a couple of Lok Sabha seats with these small outfits, later they can be given bigger roles in the state Assembly. " Due to its upper caste image, the BJP cannot forge an alliance with these caste groups, therefore a tie up on seats with these parties will be done," sources confirmed.

The party has already secured the support of Gorakhnath math, which was earlier headed by Adwait Nath and now by Yogi Aditya Nath. "For the last two times, Yogi is contesting the LS elections from BJP because when he fought under the banner of his outfit Hindu Vahini, he lost his deposit, but won when he contested from the BJP," said a party leader.

Heading: 15-yr-old ‘raped’, ‘murdered’ in Banda - Indian Express
Content:
The Gorakhpur police late on Sunday evening registered cases of murder, robbery and spreading communal violence against BJP parliamentarian Yogi Aditya Nath, MLC Y D Singh, MLA Radha Mohan Das Agrawal and city Mayor Anju Chaudhury.

The police action came following a directive by the Allahabad High Court. Hearing a writ petition on September 26, the HC had directed the Gorakhpur chief judicial magistrate to get an FIR lodged against the MP and his associates within 24 hours for allegedly inciting communal violence.

The violence had erupted on January 27, 2007 in Gorakhpur and spread to nearly a dozen districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, claiming six lives and causing heavy loss of public and private properties.

After receiving a copy of the HC order on October 16, Chief Judicial Magistrate Ajay Kumar Tripathi directed the Cantt police to lodge an FIR against Aditya Nath within 24 hours and inform the court accordingly. But the FIR was not filed till November 1.

The Indian Express had reported in its issue of November 2 that the Gorakhpur Police had defied the HC order. The same day, the police filed an FIR against the MP and his aides.

Yogi a symbol of Hindu nationalism, says BJP

The Bharatiya Janta Party has strongly opposed the case lodged against the Gorakhpur MP, Yogi Aditya Nath. State BJP president Ramapati Ram Tripathi said this was a conspiracy of the communalist forces against the party.

Claiming that Aditynath is the successor of the Goraksh peeth and a symbol of Hindu nationalism, Tripathi said the BJP stands by him and will support him. Filing of the FIR is an appeasement tactic for which both the state and the Centre are allying with the communalist forces, he added.

Heading: UP cricket body pays Rs 1 cr to keep the show going - Indian Express
Content:
A minor was allegedly raped and subsequently killed by her schoolmate on her way home from school in Banda district.

In his complaint to the Jaspura police on Sunday night, the girl's father, a resident of Gadariya village, wrote that Om Narain (18) had raped his 15-year-old daughter on Saturday and had forced her to consume poison. She was admitted to a Kanpur hospital, where she died on Sunday evening. The youth is yet to be arrested.

Superintendent of Police (SP) Banda, Ashutosh Kumar, however, said preliminary investigation has revealed the girl was having an affair with Om Narain. The girl was a student of class VIII at Baijnath Vidyalaya in the village. The boy was a student of Class X.

Additional Superintendent of Police, Banda, Saligram said: "She was caught in a compromising position with the youth that day and was later beaten up by her mother. Upset over the issue, she committed suicide."

A case of rape and murder has, however, been registered, the ASP said. The police are waiting for the postmortem report. "If the report confirms rape, the accused will be chargesheeted," the ASP said.

Heading: Service files of all LDA employees under scanner - Indian Express
Content:
With the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) paying Rs 1 crore to the state government, the uncertainty over the One-day cricket match between India and England slated to be held in Kanpur on November 20 ended on Monday.

"The show has to go on," said Prem Dhar Pathak, secretary (sports administration), UPCA, adding that the cheque has been handed over to Kanpur District Magistrate, Anil Kumar Sagar.

But the UPCA is not entirely pleased with the deal. Pathak alleged that the sum of Rs 1 crore is 34 times higher than what it had to pay for hosting an Indo-

Pakistan ODI last year. "We want to host the match at Green Park stadium at all costs and the state government was unrelentingly forcing us to deposit the exorbitant amount," said Pathak.

With Rajiv Shukla secretary, UPCA, not in India, the matter could not be resolved despite several rounds of talks. It is learnt that with the match date approaching, Shukla, who is also the chairman of BCCI's finance committee, had asked UPCA office-bearers in Kanpur to deposit the amount.

It is to be noted that the UPCA, an offshoot of cash-rich BCCI, and the state government were at loggerhead over the ground fees, which was fixed by the latter as Rs 1 crore as against Rs 3 lakh paid last year for an Indo-Pak match at the same venue. While the state government offered its own reasons for the fee hike, the UPCA, a private limited company, demanded a concession as offered to other sports associations.

Now, the money has been deposited under protest and the UPCA still hopes to get some part of the amount back. "We are still negotiating with the state Government is still on and we are keeping our fingers crossed," said Pathak.

"With only 16 days left for the match we have to urgently look into renovation, whitewash, paintings of advertisements within and outside the stadium," said Pathak, adding that the UPCA also plans to install two additional manual scoreboards in the stadium.

Regional Sports Officer (Kanpur) Bula Ganguly said preparations for the match would be conducted on a war footing now.

This is not the first time that the UPCA and the state Sports Department have been at loggerheads over a similar issue.

Heading: Soon, mandi rates will be available on cellphone - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) employees are in for a tough time in the coming days. The authority has started verification of educational as well as caste category certificates submitted by the employees at the time of their appointment.

Earlier, the LDA had also asked its employees to disclose their assets.

"Personal service files of all the employees are under scanner as there were complaints that some employees had submitted fake certificates to get the job," LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram said.

"After going through the service files of the staff members, I found that the required documents of almost 25 per cent of the employees were missing. It was also found that some of the employees who were recruited on class-IV positions are working on class-III posts," LDA Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra said.

"There are over 3,500 employees in the LDA. It has been found that some employees have submitted copies of marksheets instead of the required certificates. After a probe if it is found that the documents of an employee are fake, FIR will be lodged against that person," said Joint Secretary (Establishment) Atal Kumar Rai.

Another hurdle the LDA employees are facing is that they have been asked to disclose theirs and their family members' assets by November 20, otherwise their salary of this month will be withheld.

Asked the reason for seeking property details from the employees, Meshram said: "It is mandatory for all government employees to disclose their assets every January. But for several years now, the LDA employees have been giving teh rule a go-by."

Rai, however, said: "The decision to check the assets was taken after receiving information that few of the employees have purchased properties more than their salary allows."

As per the order, the employees have to disclose details of all non-movable assets worth over Rs 500 which they had purchased in the last five years.

They also have to give details of the source of earning through which these assets were purchased.

"A similar order was issued by the then LDA secretary on May 30, 1984, but almost 90 per cent of the employees had defied that order," said an official.

Heading: Mystery death in Nishatganj school - Indian Express
Content:
After a month of successful trial, the Uttar Pradesh government is ready for the "soft launch" of its scheme to provide mandi rates to the state's farmers on Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) phones.

According to the scheme "Mandi on Mobile" — a brainchild of the Mandi Parishad — the farmer can dial a BSNL number — 0522-1255534 — and ask for the rate of any vegetable, grain, pulse or fruit in any mandi across the state. The farmer is required to simply name the product and the district and he will be told the tehsil-wise rates.

To provide the service, the BSNL has tied up with a private company — On Mobile — a channel partner of BSNL which is also offering various other services.

The Parishad will also start distributing 710 mobile phones each month to the farmers.

The distribution will continue till most farmers across 71 districts have access to cellphones and the service. "After ironing out certain technical glitches from the software, we will conduct a soft launch of this project by the end of this month," said Rajesh Kumar, Director, Mandi Parishad.

"Once it takes off in a full-fledged manner, a proper launch will be done by Chief Minister Mayawati," he said.

There are 108 items — ranging from grains, pulses, fruits and vegetables, the rates of which can be had through this service, said Kumar.  

The salient feature of this project is that unlike other customer care centres where the caller is required to press different numbers for different queries, this software functions solely on voice command.

The information, too, is provided immediately.

"We assumed that the voice ommand system will be more user-friendly for the farmers,"said Kumar. 

The servers installed at Mandi Parishad and at the BSNL office will be connected to each other.

"The Mandi Parishad will keep updating its price list and the moment we get a call, our server will connect to the server there to provide the latest rates," said Deputy General Manager Mobiles Mahendra Srivastava.

Heading: Cleaning drive at Sangam ahead of Magh Mela - Indian Express
Content:
A 15-year-old student died on Monday, when he was practising for a forthcoming sports event in his school in Nishatganj. While the principal denied any sporting event being held in the school, other students claimed that two trainers had come to provide instructions.

Ratnesh Mishra was a student of Class VIII in Government Inter College. Fellow students claimed that he was practising for Tuesday's trials. "At 11 am, he said he was feeling dizzy and suddenly collapsed," said Vikramaditya Gautam, Mishra's classmate.

"We immediately informed the principal, who took him to the Devraj Hospital," said Jaiprakash, friend of Ratnesh. But the hospital refused to admit Ratnesh, saying his condition was critical. He was then taken to the Civil Hospital, where the doctors declared him dead on arrival.

Principal V K Dubey said, "No such event was taking place in the school. Ratnesh was coming to the class after the lunch break and due to some weakness he fainted."

A police officer said actual cause of the death could not be known since relatives of the deceased did not allow a postmortem. "No one is responsible for my son's death," said Ratnesh's father Uday Mishra.

Heading: Killing entero-virus with sun rays, Gorakhpur docs draw US applause - Indian Express
Content:
With barely two months to go for the month-long Magh Mela, the district administration has geared up to undertake a cleaning drive at Sangam on Monday.

District Magistrate Rajeev Agarwal and his team — including Mela Adhikari Jitendra Kumar — has roped in some social organisations for cleaning the river.

The drive was launched at several ghats including Sangam, Daraganj, Arail and Jhunsi. Municipal Commissioner M L Pandey, Additional District Magistrate S K Pandey, Additional

District Magistrate (City) Pradeep Kumar and several officers led the drive at the Sangam.

Agarwal made a strong appeal to the people to stop dumping garbage in the river. They have also imposed a ban on the use of polythene in the

Sangam area.

The quantum of filth and polythene that was fished out from the river pushed the administration to call for a meeting of the locals at Sangam and discussed how to keep the area clean.

Witnessing the direct flow of sewage from Moori drain into Ganga at Daraganj, Agarwal ordered the municipal commissioner to stop it immediately. The sewage, he said, must be treated before it is discharged into the river.

The local priests and residents assured the administration that they would form a group, which will monitor the drive regularly.

Spot checks on

The district administration has prepared a whopping budget of Rs 1,490.25 lakh for the mela, commencing from January 14. The proposed budget was sent to the state government for approval. The power department has demanded a maximum budget of Rs 397 lakh for the electrification of the mela area.

This year, the mela administration has acquired 1,500 acres at the Sangam for the devotees, saints and religious organisations. The area will comprise 7,500 public conveniences, 30 big toilets, 12 primary health care centers besides three big hospitals.

Besides, keeping in mind the ongoing terror attacks, the police are planing tight security arrangements in the area.  

Disaster management experts will also be roped in to work on the plan of inflow and exit of the pilgrims and putting up security measures at the bathing ghats.

Heading: It Ain’t Over Yet - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra police department's Diwali bash though delayed was a dazzling show. Like every year, this event at the Andheri Sports Complex on Sunday had the film industry biggies grooving to hit numbers. Hrithik Roshan, Salman Khan, Govinda, Imran Khan, Jeetendra, Rakesh Roshan and Dharmendra were present at the star-studded evening. Though it was Shah Rukh Khan's birthday on Sunday, the superstar still made an appearance, albeit late. This won him wishes of Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, Home Minister R R Patil and Mumbai Police Commissioner Hasan Gaffoor.

Showstopper Sallu sporting a mauve shirt and a new hairstyle danced with Govinda to the title song of Partner.

Heading: Dazzling act - Indian Express
Content:
Dressed in a bright green sari with golden motifs, a dozen bangles adorning her hands, and bridal make-up, Eesha Koppikhar seems to have gotten into the skin of a stereotypical Rajshri heroine. And why not? Koppikhar's forthcoming film Ek Vivaah.. Aisa Bhi, which releases this weekend, after all, is a Rajshri film. Talking about the film and her character, Koppikhar says, "It's a film about true love. My character, Chandni, who belongs to a middle-class family in Bhopal, falls in love with Prem (Sonu Sood) who belongs to an affluent family." The Rajshri twist obviously comes when Chandni's father dies and the responsibility of her siblings falls on her, stalling the couple's marriage plans. And that's not all: while Prem sticks by Chandni through thick and thin, the wait goes on for 12 long years.

"The crew spent over a month in Bhopal and shot at exotic locations like Gauhar Mahal and Bharat Bhavan. The city is a mix of colours, and the mannerisms of the locals further inspired our characters," says Koppikhar, who last film Hello failed at the box office. While her career has been on a slump for a long time, she is working hard at changing it all. With Jahnu Baruah's Har Pall with Preity Zinta, Shiney Ahuja and Dino Morea, and Manoj Tiwari's Hello Darling, Koppikhar is hopeful. But before that she says, "Rajshri is a coveted banner and I am sure of the film's success."

Heading: BJP, Akali spar over poll symbol: Will it be lotus - Indian Express
Content:
The run up to the Assembly elections gathered further heat with Congress president Sonia Gandhi stepping in late Monday evening and directing for a 'reconsideration' of candidates finalised so far for 53 seats by the state unit.

According to sources, Gandhi was reportedly "worried" over the choice of candidates for at least six constituencies finalised by the election screening committee. These six were reportedly considered "weak" to take on top BJP leaders such as chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra, Dr Harsh Vardhan and Jagdish Mukhi among others.

Gandhi, sources said, has asked Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary Ashok Gehlot to re-draw the list. DPCC chief J P Aggarwal, a key figure in the selection of candidates, was not invited for the meeting, Congress insiders said. This assumes importance in the wake of Aggarwal and Dikshit being at loggerheads over the choice of 17 candidates yet to be finalised by the party's state unit.

Meanwhile, names of retired IPS officer Amod Kanth, Minister of State for Urban Development Ajay Maken, and Alka Lamba are now doing the rounds to beef up Congress's chances in three of these seats.

Maken is reportedly being pitted against Malhotra in Greater Kailash — also in the fray, sources say, is present MLA Subhash Chopra who was earlier fielded for Kalkaji. Insiders said the party is also considering replacing chosen candidate Dipika Khullar by either Arvinder Singh Lovely or Dr A K Walia against Harsh Vardhan in Krishna Nagar.

While the state Congress had earlier decided to pitch former MCD councillor Jeetinder Kochar against Malhotra, with Maken's name now doing the rounds, the political scene is expected to gather heat as Maken would be a contender for the chief minister's position if the Congress returns to power. With Vijay Jolly expected to contest against Sheila Dikshit from New Delhi constituency, Amod Kanth's name was discussed in today's meeting to replace Tek Chand Sharma in Sangam Vihar to cash in on the Bihari migrant vote in the unauthorised colony now up for regularisation, sources said.

In Janakpuri, the state Congress unit had recommended Deepak Arora, known to be a close associate of former MP Rajesh Khanna. But he is now considered a weak candidate against BJP's Jagdish Mukhi. No decision has yet been taken but former MCD councillor Sanjay Puri's name is also doing the rounds.

In Hari Nagar, BJP MLA Harsharan Singh Balli's stronghold, the party is considering the names of either former NSUI president Alka Lamba or former Congress MLA O P Wadhwa.

Heading: Calling the Shots - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP and their political partner in Delhi Assembly elections Shiromani Akali Dal have locked horns over which symbol to use. While Akalis want to fight on the strength of their own symbol, tarazu or a balance, the BJP wants them to fight with their symbol, lotus. The issue, vexing both parties since the alliance was forged, remained unsolved even after a meeting between Akali Dal members and BJP's chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra.

Akali Dal also wants to issue its own manifesto for the Assembly elections. This is yet another unresolved issue. The Akali Dal will be fighting elections from Adarsh Nagar, Shahdara, Jungpura and Rajouri Garden.

"It is natural for every party to make its presence felt in areas it is contesting. We're discussing the issue with the BJP leadership at present," said Delhi State president of Akali Dal, Manjeet Singh GK.

Ironically, the Akali Dal has been struggling unsuccessfully since 1998 to fight the elections in its own symbol. The party also has been striving to get its own manifesto out.

"We want to raise the issue of the 1984 refugees and the minimal compensation paid to them. We also want Delhi to have signage in Gurumukhi," Manjeet Singh GK added.

In 2003 too, Akali Dal had fought elections from Adarsh Nagar and Shahdara but lost on both. Malhotra, meanwhile, said the BJP would be working in tandem with the Akali Dal in the elections.

"We will leave no stone unturned to ensure victory of Akali Dal candidates in Delhi," said Vijay Kumar Malhotra. Punjab Chief Minister Prakash Singh Badal will also arrive in the Capital for campaigning on November 8.

Meanwhile, the BJP is yet to decide the fate of 13 seats held back by the BJP election committee. A three-member committee comprising Thavar Chand Gehlot, Delhi BJP president Harsh Vardhan and BJP chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra will be deciding on them.

Heading: Case of ‘missing’ Prabhakar - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood rarely sees an actress turning director. Nandita Das does it with Firaaq

Big, bad, glamorous Bollywood was never her home — and it did not seem to matter much. Nandita Das was courted by the Other filmmakers — by Deepa Mehta and Nagesh Kukunoor, Mrinal Sen and Adoor Gopalakrishnan. And now at the fag end of 2008, she is a frequent flier, flitting from Toronto to London to Pusan to New York to Dubai, with a film in her check-in luggage — Firaaq. Her debut directorial venture, Firaaq is about a day in the life of people exactly a month after the 2002 Gujarat riots, when rage and pain have been seemingly quelled, but not quite. During a stopover in Delhi, Das says, "It is a work of fiction, based on a thousand true stories."

And in an industry where actresses seldom turn filmmakers, how did the movie happen? "I think it had to do with waking up to newspapers filled with stories of violence. It probably even went back to growing up in a liberal, secular environment and gradually finding oneself in the midst of prejudices," says the daughter of artist Jatin Das. "I didn't start off by wanting to direct and looking for stories; instead the many stories inside me almost compelled me to direct," says the actor-filmmaker-social activist, who has often had a cause rather than a blockbuster up her handloom sleeve.

And for the cast, she has got the veterans of art-house cinema, Naseeruddin Shah, Deepti Naval and Paresh Rawal, along with Sanjay Suri, Tisca Chopra and Shahana Goswami. "The little boy Samad, who plays a lost child looking for his father, has been quite a find," she says. But, no, Das did not cast herself. "I didn't want to add to my already challenging task of direction. People also suggested that I do a Hitchcock or Subhash Ghai and appear in a cameo, but in Firaaq there is no moment when one can afford to get distracted and come out of the story and its characters to see the director. I am glad I didn't act in Firaaq," she smiles.

Before the film releases in India in January 2009, it will be shown at the Kolkata Film Festival and then at the Kerala International Film Festival, and Das is candid about the benefits of the whole festival rigmarole: "A film like this doesn't have a big marketing budget and getting some buzz is important for its promotion. The festivals give it some attention."

And once it is released in India, does she fear a tsunami of controversy to follow, since it deals with the riots and their aftermath? "It doesn't point fingers at someone or preach, giving simplistic answers to complex problems. It is about the fierce and delicate emotions that people go through in times of fear and violence," says Das, "And I believe there are stories that need to be told and heard, even though there may not be too many telling it or wanting to hear it. And there is a collective need to understand violence."

Das is game to direct another movie, but now, euphoric and jetlagged, she just wants to catch up on sleep and read some books before taking a flight out to another festival.

Heading: Late fightback saves Tripura - Indian Express
Content:
Every one of Delhi's support staff was present at the Roshanara ground when the defending champions opened their Ranji Trophy campaign on Monday — except bowling coach Manoj Prabhakar.

The former India all-rounder's grouse is that he hasn't been given an appointment letter, setting out the terms and conditions.

Though he took over as Delhi's bowling coach last season, DDCA did not give him any formal appointment order then. Prabhakar was available last year but he hasn't joined the team since the Mohammad Nissar Trophy in September.

Though the DDCA insists Prabhakar has been 'retained' as the bowling coach this season and that he has been duly informed about it, officials are clueless about his absence at the training sessions. Prabhakar himself spelt out his terms clearly.

"Yes, I had very clearly told them (DDCA officials) that I would need a proper appointment letter with the terms and conditions. But I haven"t heard from them so far. If they send me the letter tonight, I am ready to be there at the ground tomorrow morning," he said.

Other reasons

But insiders say that Prabhakar, unhappy after being sidelined last season, has fallen out with main coach Vijay Dahiya —the main reason for his insisting on a contract letter. But DDCA have refused to toe Prabhakar's line so far. "Prabhakar hasn't come up to me to discuss his problems. I have no idea why he hasn"t joined the team yet, though I requested him to join as the bowling coach on the same terms and conditions as last year," sports secretary Sunil Dev told Sportline.

"We still hope that the matter would be resolved and he would join the team as soon as possible," Dev added.

DDCA vice-president and chairman of selectors Chetan Chauhan, however, admitted that Prabhakar had spoken to him about a written contract of service before re-starting work with the team.

"I had informed the president that Prabhakar wanted a letter if we wanted him to join the team. But I don't know what happened after that. It's unfortunate if he's not able to join the team."

Heading: Yadav, Raut get top billing among Indian athletes - Indian Express
Content:
Abhijit Dey digs in after Rakesh Kumar and Suvra Karmakar deal early blows

Choosing to bat first on a typical sub-continental track is a sensible decision to make; and Tripura's debutant skipper too made the obvious choice and then looked up towards his batsmen to provide a solid platform-a thumb rule of Ranji Trophy games often decided through first innings lead.

Instead openers Rajib Saha and Sourav Dubey acted like saving the game from Ball One as the scorecard read a paltry 69 for 1 at lunch, and trickled towards 206 for 7 — the score could have been worse, and Tripura were indeed left to save their day.

For Services pacers Rakesh Kumar and Hari Prasad, there weren't too many things happening in the shortened two hours of first session — play started late due to moisture in the pitch—apart from a streak of leg-before appeals that didn't interest the umpires.

But then the batsmen never looked to have settled down; Rajib Saha's 58-run knock-the highest for the day—came off 190 balls and he looked like playing the new ball throughout his stay —poking at deliveries outside his reach and failing to read the spinners keeping the Services bowlers interested. Saha's first runs in front of the wicket came through a boundary that beat mid-on, taking him to his half-century.

Left-arm spinner Suvra Karmakar was the first to convert the interest when he snared Dubey at point and later his arm-ball rattled Timir Chanda's stumps in the thirty-ninth over.

Left-arm pacer Kumar, after missing Rajib Saha's blade on numerous occasions, finally got one with a gentle away-swinger that landed into Sunil Tomar's palms at first slip. After the untidy, but useful innings'close, the floodgates opened for the visitors.

As the sun stared directly overhead, another arm ball from Karmarkar trapped former Tripura skipper Rajesh Banik in front in his next over. Doing justice to the innovative field placing, Kumar contrived with Yashpal Singh at second slip to send Subhal Chowdhury for a duck. Tripura's deep batting order began to look shallow after batting mainstay Nishit Shetty hit on the full straight to Madhushudan Reddy at covers off Kumar after a tailored 34 that included five boundaries.

Tripura were paying the price for going for the shots, albeit at a wrong time. The prolonged post-lunch session reaped the heaviest harvest for Services, made easy by skipper Saha's illogical attempt to go past mid-off with his side tottering on 152 for six as Kumar had his fourth victim off another innocuous delivery.

The lost logic, however, returned through Abhijit Dey's flicks and drives in a dramatic turnaround of the day. The tall right-hander, along with Rajib Dutta avoided further damage putting on unbeaten 54 runs for the eighth wicket. He kept leaving everything outside off-stump until he found them good enough to drive. With the new ball taken in the 86th over, his strokeplay matched the gloss.

If Dey was better than most of his team mates in his unbeaten 73-ball 32, including seven hits to the fence by the end of the day, Dutta had already tackled 68 deliveries for his 22. But the challenge begins again on Day Two, as much as the need to extend their fightback in search of that respectable first innings score.

Brief scores: Tripura 206 for 7 in 91 overs (Rajib Saha 58, Nishit Shetty 34, Abhijit Dey batting 33; Rakesh Kumar 4/68, Suvra Karmakar 3/43) vs Services.

Heading: Core of Big Apple - Indian Express
Content:
Ram Singh Yadav and Kavita Raut, the top finishers among the Indian entrants last year will return to defend their titles in the Airtel Delhi Half Marathon on November 9, The Elite Indian men and women athletes list has the approval of the Athletics Federation of India.

Services athlete Yadav, the Indian winner for the last two years, clocked 66.09 while emerging the fastest Indian athlete in 2007, a timing that fetched him the 16th position overall. He was followed home one second later by Deep Chand, who clocked 66.10 for overall 17th position. Deep Chand too is among the AFI list, while the other fancied names are Surender Singh, Shivadan Singh, K C Ramu, and Raj Kumar.

Among the women athletes, last year's winner Kavita Raut leads the list. Kavita, a 5000 and 10,000m track runner from Nashik, surprised the rest of the field last year by clocking 78.34 to finish 15 th overall.

The Indians, while having a shot at the overall prize fund, are also in line for monetary benefits from the separate prize fund for Indian athletes. The top prize for Indian finishers, men and women is US $4,000 and goes down till the 10th place finisher.

Men: Surender Singh, Shivadan Singh, K.C.Ramu, Ram Singh Yadav, Raj Kumar, Deep Chand, Bining, BS Lone; Women: Preeja Sreedharan, Pampa Chanda, Reena Das, Kavitha Raut, Leelamma Alphonso, Bhagwati, Indresh Dhiraj

Heading: Mumbai Local - Indian Express
Content:
It is probably the best view of New York that one can have sitting in New Delhi. The photo exhibition "Landmarks of New York", with 80 black-and-white images, offers a slice of Big Apple, whose character seems to be mutating post 9/11. There are the sloping roofs of the 17th century Browne House (which became a museum later); the neo-classical Grand Central Terminal built in 1903 and the 57-storey Woolworth Building, one of the oldest skyscrapers.

The photographs on display at the Open Palm Court Gallery at the India Habitat Centre have been culled from more than 1,100 pictures of landmarks in the five boroughs of New York taken between 1965 and 2005. "The exhibition traces how New York started off as a small town and became a teeming metropolis. The 19th century buildings are neoclassical in design, and planned by some of the most famous architects," says Michael P Macy, counselor for cultural affairs. The buildings date from 1640 to 1967 and have been documented by 43 photographers. Some of the images give quirky insights, like the photograph of the Central Park designed in 1857 as a response to the outbreak of cholera, or that of the famous Flatiron building, a wedge-shaped skyscraper crowding the Manhattan skyline. Other landmarks on display are the famous Carnegie Hall and the decadent Four Seasons. "You cannot help but be affected by the energy of New York. And every building there looks different," says Larry Schwartz, counselor for public affairs, a tad nostalgic.

The exhibition is on till November 7

Heading: Agents of Change - Indian Express
Content: Harsha V Dehejia is a Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada, but when the 70-year-old is not in his white coat or in North America, he walks the footpaths of Mumbai, and takes photographs. "To walk Mumbai's footpaths is to live a million lives and be a part of myriad journeys," says Dehejia, who was born and raised in the maximum city, and has come out with the book Mumbai Footpaths (Vera Books). From a "Homeopathic Mobile Clinic" at Flora Fountain to a red Ganesha at Babulnath to the dabbawallahs at Churchgate to the boys dancing in the rains by their tin-roofed homes at Byculla, Mumbai moves in these images.

Heading: HC: build on Yamuna bed at own risk - Indian Express
Content:
Aravind Adiga left William Morris for David Godwin. We speak to Delhi's literary agents on what they want and how much they want

In far simpler times, "literary" was followed by "criticism" rather than "agent". And then a young woman called Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize — and we got familiar with the legend of Rahel, Estha and David Godwin. It was a Cinderella story — of how Godwin, awed by Roy's manuscript, booked a flight to India, signed her up and got her a million-dollar advance. The literary agent as godfather dawned on the scene and everyone with ink stain on their forefinger wanted one. Godwin was recently in the news after he snapped up this year's Man Booker Prize winner Aravind Adiga as a client, even as the media reported a fracas between Adiga and his former literary agent. Adiga said he was unhappy with the way he was represented by Jay Mandel of William Morris, the world's biggest literary talent agency.

A literary agent is slowly becoming a norm in Delhi, and writers are increasingly looking for one who would change their fate of Rs 25,000 advance. The Capital's busy ones are Red Ink by Anuj Bahri that has been in the business since October 2006, and Osian's — The Literary Agency that is 17 months old. Both of them get 15-20 per cent of the book deal between the author and the publisher.

Foreign agents are also in the game. A first-time author, who does not wish to be named, got so disillusioned with the quality of paperbacks and the quantity of advances coming out of Indian publishers that he promptly e-mailed his manuscript to an agency in New York. He says the agent takes 10 per cent of the profits, and adds that one has to pay more greenbacks to get the book edited. An initial critique of the manuscript alone costs about $100.

Renuka Chatterjee, senior vice-president of Osian's — The Literary Agency, who has a list of 21 writers, says the first part of being an agent is pretty much the same as being an editor in a publishing house. "An agent is the author's first reader. We do the first editing of the work. Once the manuscript is ready to submit, then we send it to various publishers. Rights are sold territory-wise, so we would send it to four-five publishers in India, and to publishers in the UK, US and countries in Europe and elsewhere. The decision of which publisher to give it to in a particular territory, depends on whether the advance and royalties they are offering are fair. So unless an author trusts you to do your best for him or her, it's not going to work," she says. Bahri and Chatterjee each receives over 100 manuscripts every month. Chatterjee, however, rues that 99 per cent of unsolicited work that she gets cannot be published. "But there is still that 1 per cent that might turn out to be brilliant, which is why none of us can afford to ignore the slush pile," she says.

Chatterjee's most recent success story is Karan Bajaj's Keep off the Grass (HarperCollins), that has sold over 18,000 copies since June, and is now going into its fourth reprint in less than six months.

Many first-time authors these days make their way to Bahri Sons at Khan Market to meet Anuj Bahri, CEO of Red Ink. It handles over 40 authors in Delhi and beyond, including Canadian writer Shauna Singh Baldwin. "The building of an agency is a very slow process. It can take an agent 5-6 years to build a good list of writers and a sound reputation," says Bahri, who adds that he hasn't had acrimonious relations with his writers.

It is not just money, says writer Advaita Kala. "I think it is really important to be with an agent who cares about you and just doesn't view you as a business proposition. Writing can be lonely and a lot of times the kind of advice you need is hard to come by," says Kala whose romantic comedy Almost Single was published by HarperCollins in mid-2007. Once the foreign press got wind of the favourable reviews it received in India, Kala got noticed and had agents coming her way. Her New York-based agent finally got her book auctioned and Bantam Dell won the bid. They are now introducing Kala this February in their fiction programme called Bantam Discovery.

So getting a pen pal, dear writer, is not a bad idea.

Heading: In Noida, woman journalist robbed, molested by ‘saviour’ - Indian Express
Content:
"Massive" construction work for 2010 Commonwealth Games on the Yamuna banks will continue at the peril of the builders. These words form the thrust of a Delhi High Court judgment on the legality of the ongoing construction activity on the riverbed.

Monday's order also said the court has set up a five-member expert panel led by Nobel laureate and environmentalist R K Pachauri to monitor construction work on the riverbed.

The judgment is addressed to the Centre, Delhi government, Delhi Metro, DDA, and any private party with stakes in the project.

"We were told that construction at a massive scale was being carried out. We have made it amply clear that those raising constructions and creating third party interests despite the pendency of the writ petitions (in High Court), were doing so at their own peril," a Division Bench of Justices A K Sikri and Rekha Sharma said.

In her separate judgment, Justice Sharma did not mince words in criticising the Ministry of Environment and Forests, the DDA and NEERI for hastily supporting construction activity with little attention to ecological balance of the river.

"Their hands appeared to be tainted," she observed.

Both judges found suspicious the contradictory role played by NEERI, which, in its 2005 report, spoke against "heavy capital investment" and advocated "horticultural operations" in the Yamuna bank, only to change its tone this year. An affidavit by NEERI recommended release of "vast chunk of land for urban activities".

The court said the government should provide the expert committee all information within three weeks to start functioning; the committee is to submit a report in court within four months. The court subsequently would pass "appropriate directions" on the findings.

The decision comes on petitions filed by environmentalists who pleaded in court that the construction was on the riverbed and would, in time, "destroy the river and pose severe threat to the city as well".

The government, DDA and DMRC contended in court that the construction had started after "extensive deliberations" to develop the river, after getting the required environmental clearances from concerned authorities.

The construction in question includes the Delhi Metro depot (called Yamuna Depot), the Metro Mall and the Games Village.

The builders claimed any prohibition of construction for the Games would affect "national pride", as also India's reputation — a contention that environment activists placed secondary to saving the Yamuna.

Heading: Senior citizens robbed: Ex-rail officer killed, wife in hospital - Indian Express
Content:
A woman journalist was robbed by a gang and then molested by another man in a car, who helped her chase down the robbers to retrieve her items, while returning home in Noida late Saturday evening.

The incident took place around 10 pm, when the journalist (name withheld) working with a national daily was returning home (in Sector 55) from office. The victim has lodged a complaint at the Sector 58 police station.

The victim said she was waiting for an autorickshaw when an eight-seater share tempo (registration UP16320) stopped. "There were three boys in it, and as I asked the driver whether he was going towards Sector 55, one of them held my arm and snatched away my mobile phone and wallet and drove off."

Determined not to give up, the victim flagged down a Maruti car passing by and told the man what had just happened. According to her complaint, the man asked her to hop in and gave a chase. They caught up with the tempo and retrieved her belongings after a brief fight, she complained.

According to the victim, the man in the car then offered to drop her home. But instead, he drove towards a different direction. "When I asked him to stop, he started molesting me," the victim said in the complaint. The car was in motion all this while, and as it slowed down after hitting a ditch the victim jumped off, the complaint says.

"Shopkeepers in the area heard my screams and came to help; the man sped off at this point," she has complained. The victim said she could not note the car's registration number in the haste. In August, a radio taxi driver had allegedly tried to abduct three women reporters in Noida.

Heading: Mishap or ‘hate crime’? Days after 11 bikes burnt, no FIR - Indian Express
Content:
An 80-year-old retired railway engineer was murdered and his 72-year-old wife stabbed brutally by robbers who struck at their house in Southeast Delhi's Sukhdev Vihar area on Mathura Road late Sunday night.

The police said Madan Mohan Lal Gulati died on the spot; wife Indu Gulati, a retired teacher, was admitted to AIIMS with multiple stab wounds. She underwent operation on Monday morning and her condition is now said to be stable.

Police said tenants of the house — 81, Sukhdev Vihar — rang up the police around 1.30 am. Missing from the house is Rs 20,000 cash and jewellery (value yet to be deduced), the police said.

Police said the assailants seemed to have surveyed the house well in advance: they apparently scaled the main wall from the trees outside and broke open at least three doors to gain entry to the elderly couple's room (see box). They made their way out through the rear door, the police said.

"Madan Mohan's body has been sent for postmortem; it had several stab marks all over," a police officer said. "He had suffered injuries on head, stomach and neck. Besides stab marks, injuries caused by a hard weapon are also noticeable."

The officer said the couple's children live in the US. "Their son Vivek and daughter Namrata are both software engineers. They are settled there for the past few years."

Police officials said the two have been informed and are expected to arrive by Tuesday.

Gagan Gulati, the victim's nephew who reached the house on Monday morning, said the Gulatis were staying in the house for the last 30 years. He said their tenant, Abhay Dongre, informed police about the incident.

DCP (Southeast) Ajay Chaudhary said, "We have registered a case of robbery, murder and attempt to murder at the New Friends Colony police station. Further investigations are on." He said the police are yet to zero in on anyone and have detained a few persons for questioning. "We have lifted fingerprints, glass pieces and shoe marks from the entrance wall they had scaled. We are working on them (evidence)."

The police said they found two shoes and noticed bloodstains at rear end of the house from where the assailants had escaped. A domestic help has also been detained.

Cops: Assailants had surveyed house in advance

According to police sources, the assailants seemed to have surveyed the house well in advance and knew the ins and outs. After scaling the main wall, they broke open the main door, then smashed the sliding door's lock before breaking open the lobby door. "They then entered the room where the couple was sleeping," the sources said.

Sources said the assailants attacked the couple after they retaliated and yelled.

"The murder was cruel — the police used buckets of water to wash off the blood," an officer said. "Their tenant Abhay Dongre told us during questioning that he heard screams from downstairs and tried to go down but was stopped by his wife."

He then made the police call.

Heading: Schools want to break free, but govt tough on official line - Indian Express
Content:
Late Diwali night, a few residents of a small village in South Delhi faced a peculiar problem. Eleven two-wheelers parked at a lot in Katwaria Sarai in Hauz Khas went up in flames, leaving their owners stunned.

More shocking, they say, is the fact that no FIR has been registered even six days after the incident occurred late October 28 night. The police contend the two-wheelers — eight 150-cc motorcycles and three scooters — went up in flames due to the firecrackers. But more than one local told Newsline that they saw the fire at 2 am, and there was no firecrackers going at the time.

Five of the charred vehicles are still at the spot; they have not been moved to a police station as no case has been registered. Five bike-owners are yet to return from their hometowns after Diwali, the police said.

Most of the bike owners are students from Bihar and eastern UP settled in the area.

"I don't know who did it but it is not an accident," one victim, "scared" to give his name fearing reprisal from locals, said. "There are some people in this area from the dominant group who want to see us gone. I think they did it. We cannot complain against them because we live on rent and any complaint against our landlords will result in either assault or eviction."

Another victim, Manish Abrol, said he did not know anything about the incident as he had gone home in the Diwali holidays. "I learnt about it when I got back later," Abrol said.

A local resident, Robin Singh, said he was woken up on Diwali night around 2 am and saw the bikes on fire. "I tried to move the other bikes parked nearby," Singh said. "Then, with some of the others, I went to the terrace and threw water. The police arrived at 11 am the next day and concluded that firecrackers triggered the fire.

"But it was 2 in the night, and I heard no firecrackers when I got up."

A senior officer at Hauz Khas police station, however, called it an accident. "No FIR has been registered because their owners did not approach us with a complaint," the officer said.

The officer, however, could not explain why a case under Section 336 (act endangering life or personal safety of others) was not registered; or even a case of accident or negligence.

Heading: Sukhdev Vihar: locals say no police presence in area - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate of Education's advice that schools follow a standardised approach to nursery admissions has not gone down well with several umbrella bodies of private schools which believe the Supreme Court has given them enough power to frame individual admission criteria.

On October 27, the Directorate of Education (DoE) had asked schools to distribute a standardised registration form, all between December 15 and 31 and to complete the submission procedure by January 7, 2009. Education Secretary Rina Ray has said schools are expected to follow the new timeline in "good faith and fairness".

"These markers were framed after a talk with school authorities. Let them now show good spirit," Ray said. She also said schools which have already started giving out forms may be asked to re-issue them again.

However, an interim order from the Supreme Court gives autonomy to private, recognised schools to put together their own admission procedure and schedule. President S K Bhattacharya of the Action Committee — a body that represents 1,900 unaided private schools — said he will soon convene a meeting to discuss the new guidelines. Bhattacharya said: "We shall protest if the recent order contradicts that of the apex court's. Regularisation may not always be good for healthy education." He also said the government's claim that the guidelines have come up after consultation with schools is ambiguous. "Many schools have already started issuing forms. How can they do it if they knew what the government was going to do?" he asked.

The circular has also said that schools which wish to follow their own schedules will have to notify the DoE by December 14, failing which they will have to fall in line with the diktat.

Education Secretary Ray has set up a system by which parents can notify the directorate if they are unhappy with individual timelines. Complaints can be sent to www.edudel.nic.in, Ray said.

Sanskriti School in South Delhi has postponed giving out forms — which was to happen from November 10 — after the circular.

Parents are happy the DoE has taken efforts to bring some method into the admission chaos, with most complaining they usually spend hours trying to track which school is doing what and when. Mother Jaspreet Sahni said: "Schools do whatever they like. But now we can hope for a common schedule."

According to the circular, an admission committee — represented by the Parent Teacher Association, the school's principal, the headmaster of the primary section — will be formed to oversee admissions. The district deputy director will also man a monitoring cell in each district to check on schools regularly. He will ensure the admission process is transparent and that parents are not hassled much.

Inputs from Adeeba Iqbal Zaidi

Q* What? Where?

DPS, Mathura Road and DPS International, RK Puram have begun giving out nursery admission forms. All branches of Bal Bharati School have also begun the admission process. The forms for Bal Bharati in Pusa Road and in GRH Marg are available online as well as at the Pusa Road campus.

Heading: Yamuna more important than development, says High Court - Indian Express
Content:
After residents came to know about the incident this morning, they gathered around the Gulatis' house and complained about the lack of police presence in their area.

Residents also alleged criminal cases are a routine affair in their locality and despite repeated complaints to the police, no strict action has been taken by them.

Rajeev Goyal, a resident of Sukhdev Vihar, said: "Some assailants had broken into our house a few weeks ago and made off with cash and other essential belongings. We have complained so often to the police about lack of security but no action has been taken."

Goyal said his house was vulnerable because it falls on the Mathura road, which is said to be crime-prone. "Residents who live further away from the road, inside the colony, have managed to avoid such incidents by locking the entrance gates during the night and other ways but our houses fall on the main road, due to which we can't even do that," he said.

Another family whose backyard falls on the main road also spoke of a recent robbery at their home. "We stay on the ground floor. On May 3, some assailants jumped into our house from the backyard and broke into the house. As all my family members were sleeping in one room, none came to know and when we woke up the next morning, cash and jewellery worth lakhs of rupees was missing," Uma Sharma, a resident, said.

Her husband, Surender Sharma runs a painting and framing business in South Delhi.

Uma said: "We have spoken to the police many times. They came to our house till three days after the incident and since then there has been no development. Realising that the police will not provide any security, we hired private guards at our home for security."

Kanta, who lives at 78, Sukhdev Vihar, said, 'Sometime ago, robbers struck our house and made off with jewellery worth lakhs of rupees."

SC Sareen, president, residents' welfare association, admitted there was a lack of security in their colony. He said: "There is no doubt that the police presence in our colony is inefficient. Another reason for more crime in this area is that some flats are constructed with their fronts or backyards falling on the main road, which makes them vulnerable."

When asked about the security of senior citizens in the area, the Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southeast District) VA Gupta, who was present at the spot, said, "Our men do interact with senior citizens in the area and take full precautions to prevent crime."

Gupta said security deployment in the area needed to be changed. "As per the crime pattern in the area, we will reschedule our security deployment to avoid such incidents. In this case, we are working on various leads and are hopeful about cracking the case soon."

Heading: Nithari murders: CBI defends former director, SP - Indian Express
Content:
"It is fear and anxiety that makes me pen these lines," begins Justice Rekha Sharma in a crisp four-page verdict that says the river is "gasping for breath".

Supplementing a formal 45-page judgment from Justice A K Sikri, is the four page judgment from his "sister Justice Rekha Sharma", who says the entire project of building on the Yamuna riverbed is a "sad story of men fiddling with major issues and resultantly playing havoc". "This judgment," she observes, "relates to a river which once flowed majestically but is now gasping for breath. If this continues, time is not far off when this gift of Gods will die an unnatural death buried under layers of silt."

She pits the oft-mooted contention of "development" with the environmentalists' cry of "save the river", and concludes that Yamuna is more important of the two. "The significance and importance of the Commonwealth Games is not lost on anyone (but) the impact of building on the Yamuna, its environment, ecology and the long-term damage is, as the petitioners (environmentalists) say, pregnant with disaster," the judge notes. "If no urgent measures are taken, the Yamuna may exist only in books." Justice Sharma also notes: "No doubt is left that the site in question is on the river bed."

In his separate judgment, Justice Sikri considers the issue a "disputed question" that needs to be looked into by an expert committee.

But Justice Sharma goes a step further to add that even if the construction is not on the riverbed, "urbanisation and colossal construction underway may yet adversely affect the environment, the river and the ecology". She also lashes out at the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute for unexpectedly changing its stand to favour urbanization. Justice Sharma concludes with a parting shot that neither the government, DDA or the NEERI have been "fair" to the river.

Heading: Maharashtra Sadan vandalised - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday strongly defended former director Vijay Shankar before the Supreme Court and said he was in no way involved in the alleged murder of Jatin Sarkar, key complainant and father of a victim in the Nithari killings.

Terming the allegations as "mischievous", Solicitor General Goolam E Vahanvati submitted before a bench of justices P Sathasivam and G S Singhvi that allegations that the former CBI chief and the SP, S J M Gilani, murdered Sarkar were motivated. He said even the West Bengal Police, which registered a case following Sarkar's death, had given a clean chit to Shankar and Gilani.

The CBI was responding to a petition filed by Bandana Sarkar, Sarkar's wife, through counsel B P Singh Dhakrey, alleging that her husband was killed at the instance of Shankar and Gilani, who wanted to shield Moninder Singh Pandher, the key accused in the Nithari serial murders.

Sarkar's body was found floating in a pond in West Bengal's Murshidabad district on September 1, 2007. His 20-year-old daughter, Pinki Sarkar, was one of the 40-odd victims raped and murdered in Nithari.

'Nithari accused Koli ate breasts of female victims' Surender Koli, prime accused in the Nithari serial killings, allegedly chopped off the breasts of his female victims, whom he raped and murdered, and ate, the CBI on Monday claimed before the Supreme Court. In an affidavit filed before the apex court, the CBI submitted that Koli murdered and sexually abused 12 women and children and disposed off their bodies by dismembering them in the most horrific fashion, between February 2005 and October 2006. The CBI said, on February 5, 2005 Koli lured one of his victims, Rimpa, to House D-5 and then strangled her the with her own chunni. "He carried the dead body to the bathroom on the first floor, decapitated the body with a knife, threw out the head, clothes and chappals into the rear gallery and body parts into a drain. He then cut the breasts and flesh from the dead body, cooked it and ate it," the CBI said in the affidavit.

Heading: 3 killed, 40 hurt as DTC bus collides with tempo - Indian Express
Content:
Around 20 activists of the little-known outfit Rasthriyavadi Sena vandalised the premises of the Maharashtra Sadan on Monday afternoon, allegedly in retaliation to comments made by Raj Thackeray against North Indians.

Sena chief Jai Bhagwan Goel, who has worked with Shiv Sena for 26 years and split from the party in May this year because of ideological differences, said: "Raj Thackeray and Bal Thackeray have targeted North Indians and many lives have been lost. Today, there was only loss of property but the lives that have gone will never come back. This is a strong warning to Thackeray, and if he doesn't mend his ways, he will have to pay for it. We will take the agitation forward. There are a number of Marathis in Delhi and in Parliament and even we can harm them."

Suresh Sharma, the national organisation secretary, and Amardeep and Raja, both party workers, were arrested from the spot. "When we reached the spot we found extensive damage had been done to property. Three members were arrested on charges of rioting under Section 146," DCP Delhi Anand Mohan said.

Workers at the Sadan, however, said the miscreants were mostly hired strength and not party members. "They entered the premises forcibly and started damaging the reception area. We have lost property worth Rs 1.5 lakh but thankfully no one was injured," Jyoti Dennyson, manager of the Sadan, said. "There were dharnas in front of the Sadan last Sunday too but the police had intervened. There have been dharnas outside the Sadan ever since Thackeray's attack on North Indians but this time it went out of control and the agitators entered the premises," Dennyson said.

Heading: Four killed in road accidents in last 24 hours - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons, among them two minors, were killed and 40 others injured when a tempo and DTC bus had a head-on collision in the Kanjhawala area of Outer Delhi.

The police said the driver of the tempo was speeding and did not see the bus coming from the opposite direction on the two-way road, which doesn't have a divider. He died in the accident.

Victims and eyewitnesses said it was a bit dark and foggy at the time, due to which Tara Chand (40) could not judge the width of the road and failed to see the bus. "He could not control the tempo and collided with the bus head-on at about 70 km per hour," Hari Ram, an eyewitnesses, said.

The incident took place around 6 am in Jaunti village. The DTC bus, Mudrika Gramin Sewa, was heading towards Azadpur with some 40 passengers in it. The tempo, carrying about 50 labourers, was heading towards Jhajjar in Haryana. Most received minor and major injuries.

"We are working in a brick unit in Khairpur in Jhajjar and travel from Badayun in UP in the tempo everyday. The contractor hired the tempo for us," Shripal, a labourer, said.

The tempo had onboard both male and female labourers and their kids. All the victims were rushed to various hospitals. Tara Chand, Ashu, a three-month-old girl, and Vishal, a six-month-old boy, died in the hospital.

"I and my wife work in the same unit for the same contractor. We also brought our daughter Ashu with us to take care of her at work and now we have lost her. My wife is also in hospital," Shripal said.

Fourteen victims have been admitted in Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, 18 are in Maharishi Valmiki Hospital, 5 in Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, two in the Trauma Centre and one is admitted in Ambedkar Hospital. All of them have received injuries at their hands and chest, and some are said to be critical.

The Outer District police have registered a case under sections 279 (rash driving) and 304 A (causing death sue to rash and negligent driving). "Since driver is dead we will call the owner of the tempo and ask him as to how he sent so many people in a tempo," Atul Katiyar, DCP Outer District, said.

The DTC passengers didn't sustain much injuries in the incident.

Heading: ‘Noida farmers can claim 5% of land’ - Indian Express
Content:
Four fatal accidents, including two involving Blueline buses, were reported from across the Capital in the last 24 hours.

In the first incident, a truck rammed two two-wheelers, which resulted in the death of a 2-year-old boy and left four others injured. The police said the truck first rammed a scooter, on which one Hemant Kumar was travelling, before hitting a motorcycle on which one Yogender Singh was travelling with his family. The incident was reported around 9.30 pm from near Khajuri Chowk. Yogender Singh (26), his wife Sangeeta (24), their son Nakul (2) and daughter Jyoti (3) were going home. All the victims were rushed to the Trauma Centre, where Nakul was declared dead on arrival. The other victims are said to be in a stable condition. Residents told the police the truck driver was swerving while driving and officers suspect he was in an inebriated condition. The driver is absconding.

The second incident was reported from Khajuri Khas around 1 am today. A Blueline bus, plying on route no. 254, crashed into a cycle, killing one person and injuring another. The police said Radhey Shyam (24) died on the spot, while Jitender (12), who was rushed to a nearby hospital, was discharged after first aid. Officers said the bus driver managed to flee the spot.

The third incident was reported from Sangam Vihar on this afternoon. A 10-year-old school girl was crushed while she was trying to cross the road after school to go home to Sangam Vihar. The police said the incident was reported around 2.45 pm. Punam was crossing Rasiya Marg when a truck hit her. She died on the spot. Her father, Sunil Gupta, and other relatives protested outside the Sangam Vihar police station after the accident. She was a Class V student of the Government School in Tughlakabad, officers said.

Elsewhere, a Blueline bus hit a motorcycle and killed the 58-year-old pillion rider. The police said the accident was reported from Noida Mor in Sarai Kale Khan. Officers said Ranjana Manchanda was going back to her Jal Vihar residence with her husband Baldev Manchanda. The Blueline bus, plying on route no. 473, hit the bike and Ranjana came under its rear wheels. The couple was rushed to a nearby hospital, where Ranjana was declared dead on arrival. The driver, Mahender, has been arrested for causing death due to negligence.

Heading: Democrats in city ‘cautiously optimistic’ on eve of US elections - Indian Express
Content:
In their 155th board meeting, the Noida Development Authority and the Greater Noida Authority have decide to give farmers the option to claim five per cent of the land meant for settlement.

Both authorities have also decided that compensation rates for land acquired in 2006-07 — Rs 850 per square metre — will be given to all farmers.

The villages that will benefit from the new compensation rates include Shorkha, Zahidabad, Behlolpur, Arthala Khanjapur, Gadhi Chowkhandi, Raipur Khadar, Rohillapura and Jhatta.

Mohinder singh, CEO of Noida Authority, said fresh tender have been invited from builders for the Noida Sports City. "The bid was scheduled to be closed today but we realised we have not incorporated building of a road from the expressway to the Sports City. Therefore, fresh applications will be invited and the closing date for submitting tenders is now December 5," Singh said.

The boards have also decide that institutional areas could accommodate corporate offices like clinics, dispensaries, banks, auditoriums and post-offices. Another major decision of the board comes in the area of education. "Earlier, educational institutions had to have a charitable trust to establish any institute. Now, private companies can establish their schools or colleges without having charitable trusts," Singh said.

A new housing scheme for the Below Poverty Line population has also been announced. "Five-hundred flats of 35 sq m each will be constructed under the Kanshi Ram Urban Residential Scheme for the poor," Singh said.

Heading: Last-minute dash: Denied tickets, aspirants make a beeline for rival offices - Indian Express
Content:
Shelli Koffman was trying to connect to the wi-fi network at Choko La in Khan Market last evening. She had found a Democrat, who hadn't cast her vote and wanted to download a form for her.

As I expressed surprise, she said, "She's from California. Democrats are really strong there, so she thought her vote wouldn't really make a huge difference." Although the voter seemed incredibly certain about Barack Obama winning the election, Koffman and her compatriots at Democrats Abroad-India were being cautiously optimistic about the most crucial elections America has witnessed in recent times.

Rashmi Jaipal, a cross-cultural psychologist from Bloomfield College in New Jersey, and Sarah Figge, an editor with the United Nations Development Programme, joined Koffman as they prepared for the Election Day programme, which will be held at Choko La's Basant Lok outlet on Wednesday from 7 am. The organisation is coordinating with its members to set up an "Election Watch" across metropolitan cities in the country, and in Delhi, the Democrats are going to have a night-out at Capitol at the Ashok Hotel.

"We're not pre-empting a victory. It's going to be a time to sit back and reflect on the work done all these months," Koffman said, even as all four of us at the table, including me, said a silent prayer for an Obama victory.

To break the silence, we talk about the campaign and the possible reasons why America might still vote for McCain. "I know some people back home who're voting for McCain because he's got Palin by his side. This show that the Republican gender politics have worked to an extent," Figge, who initially voted for Clinton in the global primary, said. Obama's decision to have Senator Joe Biden as his running mate, however, convinced her to support him.

What about the Bradley effect? "This election has gone beyond race. What is on everybody's mind now is the economic crisis and the conservatives are not comfortable with 'spreading the wealth' but Americans need to understand that we are on the threshold of a completely new crisis and hence, need a new beginning," Jaipal said.

Heading: Change in SP’s Jamia Nagar candidate sparks unrest in ranks - Indian Express
Content:
Four former Congress members feature in the BJP list, many flock to BSP

With elections closing in and political parties making formal announcements of their lists of candidates, aspirants who were denied tickets have started scouting around for opportunities in parties that were enemy camp not so long ago.

While at least four former members of the Congress, figure in the list announced by the Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday, many have also started tapping the Bahujan Samaj Party as a viable option.

At least 300 workers, a councillor and some former councillors of the Congress from the Chhattarpur constituency are set to join the BSP on Friday.

Kanwar Singh Tanwar, general secretary of the party's state unit, will be contesting elections from the constituency. Speaking to Newsline, he said, "The neglect of people from this constituency and also areas where these workers and councillors come from has fuelled the move." He, however, refused to divulge names of councillors who will be joining the party. "We do not want other parties to start wooing them now," he said.

Insiders say the BSP has been looking at roping in experienced candidates denied tickets by the Congress and the BJP.

Speaking to Newsline on condition of anonymity, a senior leader of the party's state unit said, "Being new to the political scene in Delhi, it is important for us to have experienced campaigners. We are on the lookout for probable candidates from other parties who have a strong base but have been denied tickets." The leader added party "higher-ups" were in the loop and every move was being discussed with them.

Former Congress MLA from Badarpur, Ram Singh Netaji, joined BSP on Sunday and said the decision was a response to the party's "anti-poor policies". Netaji had won the election from the seat in 1998 but lost out to Ramvir Singh Bidhuri of the Nationalist Congress Party in 2003. Bidhuri, on the other hand, had joined the Congress in September and has been given the ticket from Badarpur by the party. Netaji's decision to move to the BSP is being termed as a last-minute option by party workers.

Netaji is being termed a strong candidate from the seat, considering that anti-incumbency will work against the Congress this time. He had lost out to Bidhuri by a margin of only 436 votes in the last elections.

The four members of the Congress who have been given tickets by the Bharatiya Janata Party include Chaudhary Bhim Singh, the nephew of former Delhi Assembly speaker Chaudhary Prem Singh. While Prem Singh was seeking a ticket for his son from the Deoli seat, Bhim Singh has been given priority and will be fighting from there.

Another former Congressman who figures on the list is Khem Chand. Chand will be contesting from Badarpur.

He was a member of the Delhi Congress executive committee in 1993-94. Another former Congressman, Sher Singh Dagar, a member of the Delhi Congress Farmers' cell in 1993-94, has been given the go-ahead by the BJP for the Mehrauli constituency. Similarly, ex-NSUI member Anil Jha figures in the BJP list. He will be fighting from the Kirari assembly seat.

Heading: Plan to streamline transport in Gurgaon - Indian Express
Content:
The Samajwadi Party on Monday announced its list of candidates for 33 seats for the upcoming Delhi Assembly elections amid protests over its candidate from Okhla, which includes the 'sensitive' Jamia Nagar area.

The Left parties also appeared divided over the seat. Both the CPI and the CPM have been claiming ownership over the candidate, Raza Haider.

In the case of the Samajwadi Party, the candidate from Okhla constituency has been changed in the present list and workers of the previous shouted slogans opposing the decision outside the party office. Wasim Ghazi has replaced Amanat-ullah Khan. Insiders say top leaders in the party took the decision to field a stronger candidate from Jamia Nagar area.

Gauri Shankar Sharma, the spokesperson of the party's Delhi unit, said, "It is an important seat considering the visits of senior party leaders in the area after the encounter."

Ghazi had been at the forefront of protests against Delhi police after two alleged Indian Mujahideen terrorists were killed in the September encounter and the death of Inspector M C Sharma in the shootout. He had also led protests against media coverage of the Jamia Nagar encounter.

Party workers say Amanat-ullah Khan had also been a strong candidate from the area and had organised party workers ahead of senior party leader Amar Singh's visit to the area.

Singh had termed the encounter fake and demanded a free probe.

The Left parties also had a tough time deciding on their candidate from Okhla.

Raza Haider, chairman of the Urdu Editors Guild, had been declared the CPI candidate from the constituency and the CPI (M) was expected to leave the seat to him.

However, spokespersons of both parties have been claiming Haider would fight for their respective parties.

Haider, meanwhile, has said he will represent the Left Front and is "least interested" in which party he fights for.

The four Left parties in the fray are yet to finalise seats which they will be contesting and who they will support in seats they do not contest.

Heading: The Curtain Goes Up - Indian Express
Content:
Looking at the choked roads across Gurgaon, the Urban Mass Transit Company (UMTC) has recently submitted an inception report on Integrated Mobility Plan for Gurgaon-Manesar Urban Complex to the state government and the Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) here.

The present mode of transport, according to the report, is mainly dependent on bus and private vehicles. However, owing to limited accessibility and congestion, there has been a rapid increase in private vehicles and other modes like shared autorickshaws in the city.

Though the new 14.5-km Metro line, which would connect Ambedkar Nagar in South Delhi to Sushant Lok here and would be completed by 2010, would help reduce vehicular traffic to some extent, new developmental projects in the city would only add more traffic in the near future, especially on NH-8.

The report also highlights the inadequate transport facilities for non-motorised traffic in the old city.

"The facility, if at all it exists, is in a pitiable state making the system ineffective," reads the report.

The mobility plan which would be developed in layers highlights the vision of the transport system, short-term, medium-term and long-term measures to be implemented to improve it.

It would finalise it on the basis of how the final plan elements are aligned and after public opinion is sought. The short-term improvements include junction improvement like traffic lights and traffic control devices; restriction on parking on the roads; improving pedestrian facilities and stricter enforcement of traffic rules.

The medium-term improvements include widening of existing roads; construction of flyovers, over-bridges; augmentation of transport services, amongst others.

The long-term proposals include development plans required to meet the travel demand keeping in view Master Plan 2021.
