The primary data collection includes survey of road network inventory; intersection vehicular volume count; parking surveys; speed and delay surveys, of others. The UMTC has taken into consideration the demography of the area and the issues and concerns of all project stakeholders.

Heading: Joint venture - Indian Express
Content:
Q* We hear you are out of Saat Phere?

Yes. I am quitting the show. I have been lucky to play Saloni, who had so many flavours to her. I played a child (a la Sridevi's role in Sadma), a banjaran and even turned negative. To get such a role at the beginning of your career is a blessing. But I have been working continuously for the last three years without a break. Now, I want to spend some time with my family, which is why I am leaving the show.

Q* Is it your decision or the producer's?

Of course it's my decision. I conveyed it to the producer and they respect my decision. However, they told me I cannot quit immediately. They want to work out how my character will exit.

Q* What is the track right now?

Nahar is not well and I am taking care of him.

Q* How has the journey been so far?

It's been great. Whatever I am today is because of the show. I feel proud to be associated with it. People have appreciated and accepted me, I think I have got more than what I asked for and I am grateful to God for that.

Q* There was a controversy about you quitting Ek Se Badhkar Ek because you were scared of competition.

I think reality shows are all about controversies. I had a old ligament tear which I ignored. But the heavy-duty dancing and rehearsals aggravated my pain, which is why I quit. Why should I be scared of competition? If I was, I wouldn't have participated.

Q* Are you exploring other shows now that you have quit Saat Phere?

Not right now. As I said, I want to spend time with my family, specially my husband. I was married a year-and-half ago and I didn't have enough time even for my wedding. If possible, I would like to conduct my marriage again.

Q* So, are you planning a long honeymoon?

Let's see. First I have to finish my commitment to the show, only after that can I decide.

Heading: Cong man with saffron heart: NSUI leader punished for supporting sadhvi - Indian Express
Content:
In their first ever public appearance, cast of Raaz - The Mystery Continues attended the Halloween party in Mumbai on Friday. Keeping in spirit of the celebration, Emraan Hashmi and Adhyayan Suman, along with director Mohit Suri, unveiled the Raaz promos. Other guests included Tarana Raj Kapoor and Nina Manuel. The famous serial-kisser realised that he has an equally besotted male fan following when a masked guy began to haunt him and refused to budge unless he had his photograph clicked with the actor. Disarmingly, Emraan obliged.

Bummer It was a Halloween party but none of the stars, dressed in casual tees, looked the part.

Heading: Raj has an island of support in Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
Rana had launched Vishwa Hindu Seva Samiti; his mother is the state INTUC vice-president

Nirav Rana, who announced the new Hindu outfit, the Vishwa Hindu Seva Samiti (VHSS) in support of Sadhvi Pragya, here on Sunday, has turned out to be major embarrassment for the Congress.

Nirav is the acting vice-president of the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) — the students' wing of the Congress in Surat. Besides, Urmilla Rana, his mother, an ex-Congress councillor, is the vice-president of the Gujarat unit of the Indian National Trade Union Congress.

Nirav had organised a press conference on Rander Road over sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur's arrest by the Mumbai ATS for her alleged role in the Malegaon blast. Nirav also declared full support of the VHSS members to the sadhvi.

His mother also said his son was right in his actions. "My son took a decision and expressed his feelings. We are Hindus and so we should fight to protect ourselves. Sadhvi Pragya is innocent. Various tests like brain mapping and polygraphy among others were conducted on her but nothing came out of them. She should be released," she said.

The news of the press conference spread like wild fire in the city on Sunday afternoon. The city NSUI members were shocked to learn about Nirav's role in organising the event.

NSUI Gujarat president Indra Vijaysinh Gohil suspended Nirav for six years following this event, after taking permission from senior NSUI authorities.

Gohil said: "Nirav Rana has acted against the NSUI ideology. He can only air his views on students' issues and not on other topics. He cannot join another organisation or Samiti. Pragya was an active leader of the Akhil Bharitya Vidhyarti Parishad (ABVP) and Rana cannot lend support to her as they are our rivals. Terrorists have no religion and the issue of sadhvi Pragya's involvement is under investigation."

Surat NSUI general secretary Anup Rajput said: "We have received many complaints against Nirav in the past about his anti-NSUI ideology. Several complaints were registered against him in different police stations in Surat."

He said a person who is committed to the NSUI cannot take the president's post in any other organisation and if he/she wants to do so, they have to take due permission from the higher authorities. "We are satisfied with the decision taken by our higher authorities. This move will make NSUI members more alert and not let them get involved in other activities," he said.

Rana could not be contacted following his suspension from the NSUI.

Embarrassed, Surat city Congress president Sunil Bhukhanwala further said: "The statements of Urmilla and her son Nirav are against secularism. I have reported to Congress state general secretary Girish Rana about the statements. Both should be expelled from the party. Urmilla and her son are frontline office bearers of INTUC and NSUI and they should not give statements in support of sadhvi Pragya Singh."

Heading: Family feud: Irked by their leader’s arrest, VHP protests against BJP govt - Indian Express
Content:
Newly-formed AGMM seeks better rights for Marathi people, backs MNS chief

BJP councillors of different regional roots might unite in Surat following the Bihari —Marathi Manoos controversy triggered in Maharashtra by Raj Thackeray. But in Vadodara, which has sizeable Marathi speaking population, the opposite is happening.

The recently formed Akhil Gujarat Maratha Mahasangh (AGMM) is giving a call in favour of Raj Thackeray, while seeking better rights for the Marathi speaking population of the city and Gujarat.

Headed by Shreeram Shinde, the AGMM, which was formed on August 10, 2008, intends to take out a rally in support for the rights of the Marathi speaking population.

Incidentally, Shinde, who is well associated with the Baroda royals, is known for organising such events and associations. Besides, he is also the administrator of the Devsthan Trust formed by Baroda scion Ranjitsinh Gaekwad.

He said: "I do not support the violent acts of Raj Thackeray, but if the north Indians have reached a stage where they are making conspiracies to kill him, then as a Marathi, we will not tolerate such nuisance."

Incidentally, after the Raj Thackeray incident, the AGMM has suddenly awakened to the identity crisis that Marathis seem to perceive outside Maharashtra. Along with supporting Raj Thackeray, the group also has taken up the issue of being left out from the rights and reservations that Marathis should get in Gujarat.

"We are also a linguistic minority community here and are bound to enjoy certain rights and reservations as OBCs. Though the benefit is taken by the other linguistic minority groups, we Marathis are left out in Gujarat."

With anonymous SMSes doing the rounds across the city among the Marathis on community strengthening the support to Raj Thackeray, the AGMM has taken up the demand for linguistic minority reservation with Human Resource Development Minister Arjun Singh and Linguistic Minority Commission Chairman Suresh Keswani. "Most Marathis in the city are not financially well-off and we will fight for our rights so that we are equally considered for all reservations," he said.

With Marathi integrity as their agenda, the AGMM has also raised the issue of alleged undermining of Hindutva sentiments. The group raised the issue of raising a nation-wide ban on companies packaging their products with pictures of gods and goddesses.

"We talk highly of Hindu religion on one hand and on the other let our gods and goddesses lie in dust and in the gutters," said Shinde, adding that he has taken up the matter in a letter to Congress chief Sonia Gandhi.

Heading: Narmada branch canal develops off-season breach near Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
Widening the rift between the ruling BJP and the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) over the arrest of VHP Ahmedabad city general secretary Ashwin Patel, several parishad leaders and workers protested in the Ghatlodia area on Monday.

Many were detained and later released by the police. The Gandhinagar police had arrested Ashwin Patel on October 27 under charges of sedition and forgery. At present, he is in police remand.

A thin group of around 50 VHP workers held a demonstration at the Maharana Pratap Chowk in Ghatlodia to protest Patel's arrest. They also shouted slogans against Chief Minister Narendra Modi, calling him 'Miyan Modi.'

Ranchhod Bharwad, Manish Sharma, Dilip Trivedi and Harshad Gilitwala were some of the leaders who were present at the protest programme.

Bharwad told media persons: "Right now, there is a competition between the different state governments to prove themselves secular and the Gujarat government has also joined the competition. The VHP workers are being wrongly implicated in criminal cases."

Bharwad said that if sending SMS is a crime, then he would send lakhs of such SMSes.

The VHP workers were carrying a number of banners against the state government, one of which also made a reference to a minority community youth from Delhi who had sent a threatening email to Narendra Modi and whom Modi had pardoned off and offered sweets.

The banners accused Modi of giving discriminatory treatment to the VHP workers.

The protesting VHP workers also issued a pamphlet 'Godhrakand na Sakshi Parishad Shaher Mahamantri Shri Ashwin Patel ne Mukt Karo' (Release Ashwin Patel, the witness to the Godhra Carnage and VHP City General Secretary).

Before the demonstration, the Ghatlodia police who were deployed at the spot to check any untoward incident, had removed the tent put up by the VHP workers for the demonstration.

Ghatlodia Inspector R C Mehta said: "We detained some VHP workers who were protesting at the spot and later released them. No untoward incident happened during the protest."

Zadaphia detained for protesting Ashwin Patel's arrest former BJP leader Gordhan Zadaphia who now heads the Mahagujarat Janata Party, comprising BJP rebels, was also detained for holding a sit-in protest following the arrest of VHP leader Ashwin Patel.

Zadafia and over 300 of his supporters had organised a sit-in protest on Monday at the Income Tax circle on the busy Ashram Road defying police permission.

Zadafia said: "The government is anti-Hindu and the arrest of Ashwin Patel has exposed its real face. We will support the VHP on the issue. Our workers will organise similar sit-in-protests in all districts across the state and will court arrests tomorrow."

Heading: Fire breaks out at three places, property worth crores destroyed - Indian Express
Content:
Release of excess water into main canal led to problem, says SSNNL chairman

Barely four months have passed since the Mehsana Canal breach of June 11. Yet another canal breach was reported in Vadodara district near Nimeta village in the Vadodara branch canal of the Narmada due to a drainage work being carried out by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM).

Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) chairman N V Patel has, meanwhile, said that the breach probably occurred due to the release of excess water into the Narmada Main Canal.

"The drainage works carried under JNNURM using the trench technique might have created the breach," said Patel.

The breach on the Vadodara branch canal occurred around 1:30 am on Monday morning. According to one of the villagers from Nimeta, the water from the canal rushed into his field, submerging an overwhelming portion of his newly planted bajra crop. "When I came to the fields in the morning, a large portion of my field was under water," said Pradeep Solanki, a villager from Nimeta.

By afternoon, the breach was fixed, but the VMC city engineers were unavailable for comment. The drainage system is supposed to bring the water from the Ajwa Reservoir to the water scarce prone areas of the city.

Heading: Illegal Bangladeshi migrant nabbed from Ahmedabad - Indian Express
Content:
One person was injured and property worth several crores were gutted in a major fire that broke out in the premises of a textile-processing unit in Piplaj village near Narol on Monday morning. No casualties were, however, reported.

The incident took place in one of the units in the premises of Rinku Process Ltd around 10.30 am. Vatva police along with personnel of Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services (AFES) rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control.

According to the Deputy Chief Fire Officer, Rajesh Bhatt, a short-circuit in the processing unit premises was the reason behind the mishap. Vatva police said that the processing unit was closed during the five-day Diwali break and had opened on Laabh Pacham on Monday. A worker in the unit, Malak Prashad (40), who sustained burn injuries in the incident, is presently under medical treatment. The police said he is out of danger.

Even before the AFES personnel could extinguish the Piplaj fire completely, another fire broke out in Revadibazaar area in Kalupur. While five shops adjacent to the market area were gutted completely in the fire, no casualties or injuries were reported. A sudden commotion was caused in the area that teems with activity around that time. An AFES team, however, took control of the situation.

The third incident of fire on Monday was reported in Niharika Society near Himmatlal Park, in Ambawadi. Fire department personnel immediately rushed to the site and controlled the situation. No injuries were reported, said police.

Heading: Power of news to fertilise farmers’ land - Indian Express
Content:
His parents had also stayed in the city illegally and had procured ration and election cards

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch detained an alleged illegal Bangladeshi migrant from the slums of the Shah-e-Alam area on Sunday.

The detained person has been identified as Shakayat alias Shaukat alias Biko Shaikh (30), a native of Babupur village of Nodail district in Bangladesh.

Shaikh was allegedly residing in Nawab Nagar na Chhapra in Shah-e-Alam for the past seven months along with his family. After his detention, Shaikh's family members have gone underground and further investigations are on to find them out.

According to the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch, Shaikh was detained near the Chandola Lake during a patrol carried out to find out such illegal Bangladeshis living in the area.

Shaikh has confessed to have lived in the area for the past seven months along with his wife Nasima and two-year-old son, Tanvir. Shaikh has reportedly confessed that previously also he had lived in Ahmedabad for five to six years before returning to Bangladesh. He came to Ahmedabad again seven months ago with his wife and son after crossing the Bangladesh border illegally by paying Rs1,000 per person to an agent called Ajad.

The police said that Shaikh has also confessed that his parents who are now dead, had stayed with him in Ahmedabad and had illegally procured a ration card and election cards.

Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch officers have now initiated procedures to send Shaikh back to Bangladesh and to find out his wife who has gone underground along with her son.

Heading: A landfill site: victim of AMC’s ‘stink operation’ - Indian Express
Content:
Newsline report forces admn to allot 6,700 tonnes fertiliser to agitating farmers

The Junagadh administration has allotted 6,700 tonnes of fertilisers to the farmers of the district after The Indian Express reported unrest due to a shortfall in fertilisers in the district.

The consignment arrived at the railway station and the distribution has been started with immediate effect.

Junagadh had received adequate monsoon rains and there was enough water for irrigation. That is why the winter crop cultivation has been going on in full swing throughout the district and there has been a high demand for fertiliser for a fortnight now.

The unavailability of fertilisers due to a huge gap between demand and supply, however, led to an unrest and the irked farmers started an agitatation.

Following the farmers' stir, cooperatives and farmer leaders immediately approached authorities at IFFCO and GUJCOMASOL for a solution.

Ranchhodbhai Thesiya, Director, APMC yard, Junagadh and Chairman of the Majewadi Group Cooperative Service Society, said: "The immediate allotment of 6,700 tonnes of fertilisers has met the shortage in Junagadh district, and the situation will soon come to normal."

According to Thesiya, during the current winter crop season, the fertiliser requirement is 10,000 metric tones.

Considering the seriousness of the issue and the demand, concerned authorities have also allotted 1,800 tonnes of fertilisers reserved for Rajkot district, as the demand for fertilisers has not risen there.

"Thesiya added: "The IFFCO director and Congress MLA from Dhoraji, Vithal Radadiya and GUJCOMASOL director Natubhai have helped us in the right way to supply this stock of fertilisers."

Meanwhile, farmers at Supasi village set up roadblocks on the Junagadh-Veraval Highway on Sunday to protest against the shortage in fertiliser supply.

They gathered in large numbers in front of a fertiliser depot run by GUJCOMASOL on the outskirts of the village. But without adequate stocks, the farmers lost their temper and started stopping vehicles passing through either side of the highway. The stir stopped traffic for four hours.

Concerned officials and local Congress leaders immediately rushed to the spot to cool down tempers.

Their timely mediation helped to bring the situation under control. "Following the assurance given by the officials to immediately provide adequate stocks of fertilisers , the farmers stopped their agitation and disbursed," said an official.

Heading: NMCE launches futures trading in cotton - Indian Express
Content:
'The enormous dumping of solid wastes has led to an increase in the number of flies and plague-causing rodents. These flies, which carry pathogenic organisms, cause diseases such as dysentery and diarrhoea. It is estimated that about 70,000 flies can live in one cubic foot of garbage. Just imagine the potential of Gyaspur-Pirana'
Reckless dumping of solid waste has turned Gyaspur-Pirana site into a breeding ground of diseases

The 84 hectare Gyaspur-Pirana landfill site near the Narol Industrial Estate is a classic example of the callous indifference of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC). The aesthetic aspect apart, the site has become a breeding ground for major diseases for the surrounding population.

Environmental scientist D J Mohan, who works for the Environment Bureau of Investigation, a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), said: "The enormous dumping of solid wastes has led to an increase in the number of flies and plague-causing rodents. These flies, which carry pathogenic organisms, cause diseases such as dysentery and diarrhoea. It is estimated that about 70,000 flies can live in one cubic foot of garbage. Just imagine the potential of Gyaspur-Pirana."

Another major problem is the ground water pollution caused by the seepage of toxic materials in the neighbouring areas. The site has been in use since the last many decades and registers an estimated daily dumping of 2,200 tonnes of municipal solid waste.

Mohan said: "The AMC must not allow anyone to dig bore-wells within at least two kms from the landfill site. The existing bore-wells must also be periodically checked for water quality."

Although the AMC has signed a formal contract with Solid Waste To Electricity Company (SELCO) to burn 'organic' waste for electricity generation, the major hurdle seems to be the segregation of non-biodegradable waste like plastics, leather and electronic disposals at the landfill site.

Prashant Pandya, Deputy Director, Solid Waste Management at the AMC said: "The segregation must be done at the source, for which we are launching a Project, 'Wealth out of Waste – WoW' in tie up with Reliance Fibre."

He said the project aims to segregate garbage at the point of generation and pack it in bags of blue and white colour, adding that it will be launched as a pilot project in Dudheshwar and Mennagar wards for 3 months soon.

The landfill site is also a regular hunting ground for the city's rag pickers. Hundreds converge on the site every morning to collect plastics from the garbage heaps. The rag pickers are the most prone to health problems that invariably also endanger their families.

Leela, a rag picker who has been coming to the Gyaspur-Pirana site for the last 20 years said: " We get between Rs 50 and 60 per day by selling the garbage. It's our only source of income."

When asked about the rag pickers flocking the landfill site, Pandya said, "We have a staff crunch, but still our Sanitary Inspectors are instructed to take strict action against the rag pickers whenever they catch hold of them."

Heading: ‘Salute the soldier’ honours defence personnel - Indian Express
Content:
National Multi-Commodity Exchange of India Ltd. (NMCE), the country's first online de-mutualised, multi-commodity exchange, on Monday, announced the launch of futures trading in cotton at a function in Surendranagar.

The announcement was made by Anil Mishra, Chief Executive Officer, NMCE and the launch ceremony was inaugurated by B C Khatua, Chairman, Forward Market Commission under the Ministry of Commerce.

Cotton is a very important commercial crop of India. With annual cotton production of 32.2 million bales, India is the world's third largest cotton producer. But the world cotton market is one of the most volatile commodity markets. Indian cotton production also fluctuates between years as it is highly dependent on monsoon and pest attacks, which leads to high fluctuation in prices. As a result, cotton producers, merchants and stockists are exposed to high risk on their production, purchase and stocks.

Similarly, exporters and spinners are exposed to heavy risks from adverse price increase on their overseas or domestic sale commitments of fibre or yarn for delivery at a later date.

Khatua said: "Since NMCE has designed this contract after extensive deliberations with cotton growers, ginners, traders, brokers, exporters and experts, I believe that the contract will be found useful by all types of market players and maximum stakeholders, both big and small."

Kailash Gupta, Managing Director, NMCE, said: "NMCE has started trading in Kalyan Kapas: V-797 and it is expected that during the current cotton season, it will have reasonable liquidity in Surendranagar-based cotton contracts. We believe that an active cotton contract will bring both producers and consumers to the exchange due to its efficient pricing."

The margins for the cotton contracts will be 5 per cent and the delivery samples will be certified by NMCE approved surveyors. The deliveries will be tendered in multiples of 4,000 kg, with the delivery centre located at Surendranagar.

Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Director, NMCE, said: "Our main aim in choosing Kalyan Kapas: V-797 cotton futures is to provide a hedging facility for price volatility in cotton trading. The analysis carried out by NMCE has found that contracts in these varieties act as a good hedge for price volatilities."

Cotton is cultivated in almost all parts of the country, but nine states namely Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka account for more than 95 percent of the output.

Cotton sustains India's cotton textile industry, which in turn accounts for nearly 20 per cent of the total national industrial production and provides employment to over 15 million people.

The function was attended by large number of cotton farmers, ginners, traders, brokers, senior directors of regional commodity exchanges and opinion leaders.

Heading: Vaidya’s body donated to Sassoon Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Trishakti will observe Nov 1 every year as 'Salute the Soldier' day

In a unique tribute to the retired and serving armed forces personnel, Trishakti Foundation, a city-based non-government organisation, founded by a group of ex-servicemen in 1989, had organised a 'Salute the soldier' programme at Pancard Clubs in Baner on Saturday.

A host of individuals who have had illustrious careers in the forces and other fields were felicitated at the function. Some of those felicitated were Lt Gen (Retd) N S Cheema, Air Marshal (Retd) Prakash Pingale, and Commodore K O Thakre.

Southern Command chief of staff Lt Gen R K Chhabra, Additional DGP (CID-Maharashtra) S P S Yadav and former Indian hockey star Dhanraj Pillay, who were the guests of honour, were also felicitated during the

programme.

"Several nations dedicate a particular day to remember their soldiers — particularly those who lost their lives in the line of duty — apart from serving and retired personnel. Henceforth, Trishakti will commemorate November 1 every year as 'Salute the Soldier' day," said founder member, Trishakti, Col (Retd) SDK Patil.

Speaking on the occasion, Dhanraj Pillay said, "We should start thinking beyond mere regional considerations and work together as Indians — that is our collective identity. The sacrifices made by members of the armed forces to protect the unity and integrity of the country must never be forgotten."

Heading: Whirpool wins at ‘Mindscape 2008’ - Indian Express
Content:
Noted educationist and the man behind 'school for failures', PG Vaidya's body was donated to Sassoon General Hospital on Monday. He passed away in the early hours of Saturday after a massive heart attack.

Sitting member of the Pune Municipal Corporation's school board and chairman of Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Balkumar Sahitya Sammelan, he was a former senate member of the University of Pune.

Vaidya was also the founder chairman of Pune district and Maharashtra state mathematics board, life member and secretary of 'Education Technology', member of International Mathematics Olympiad and had taken initiative in starting computer curriculum for classes VIII to XII students.

Vaidya was one of the founders of 'napasanchi shala' (school for failures) to encourage students who failed in their exams. He taught Mathematics and Science at the Apte School for 30 years and was the principal of the school from 1962 to 1992. He also taught Mathematics for 15 years at the Apte junior college.

He co-authored and independently wrote more than 50 books on education, scientific stories, imaginative mathematics and also textbooks for standards VIII to XII. Vaidya was also the winner of Maharashtra Sahitya Parishad award.

He was 75 and survived by his wife Vasundhara, son Rahul and daughter Ashwini

Heading: AFMC comes second in 10th Raid De Himalaya Rally, 2008 - Indian Express
Content:
Whirlpool, for the second consecutive year emerged as the winner of 'Mindscape 2008', a two-day event organised by ASM Group of Institutes at the Institute of Business Management and Research campus, recently.

'Mindscape 2008' was the fifth edition of the event with major participants like Tata Motors, Siemens (Nashik), Mahindra and Mahindra, Behr India, Kirloskar Pneumatic and Whirpool.

'Mindscape' is an industry-level case study competition wherein industry teams have to resolve live case studies. Presentations of these case resolutions are evaluated by independent juries.

The two-day event turned out as a rich experience for management students, faculties and the industry participants as well. This year the event had participation from Thermax and Maharashtra Scooters.

Thermax and Tata Motors bagged the runners up trophies. M S Unnikrishnan, managing director, Thermax Ltd was the chief guest of the award ceremony. During his speech after distributing the prizes, he emphasised the need for renewed grit and preparation.

J A Kulkarni, S P Marathe, Pavan Patil and Vibhuti Aggarwal of ASM Group of Institutes were instrumental in the organisation of 'Mindscape 2008'.

Heading: Shop looted in Dighi - Indian Express
Content:
Displaying another facet of excellence in the desolate reaches of the Himalayas, the Armed Forces Medical College's two-member team came second in the 10th Raid De Himalaya Rally, 2008, an annual event open to cars, SUVs and motorcycles. The team had Lt Col V Bhatti as the driver and Col Soumen Basu as the navigator.

As many top-ranked national rallying teams participated in the event, the Indian Army was represented by nine teams with three each in every category — T1, T2 and Adventure (Reliability). The team of Army Medical Corps from Armed Forces Medical College competed with 59 teams in the adventure group.

The event was organised by the Himachal Pradesh Department of Youth Services and Sports. It was flagged off from Hotel Peterhoff in Shimla.

The Raid covered 2,050 km through the rugged terrains of Himalayas — Shimla, Sangla, Manali, Kaza, Keylong, Sarchu, Leh, Kargil, Jhanskar valley and finally finishing at Leh.

The rally was in TSD (time, speed, and distance) format where the competitors tried to stick to the given speed in a worked out timeframe. A precision of 100th of a second considering the slope, terrain, traffic and track had to be attained.

The Army Medical Corps team drove a Maruti Gypsy of 2004 vintage. According to Lt Col V Bhatti, the team had to compete with company teams including team Mahindra & Mahindra, team Maruti and team Godwin.

AFMC Director and Commandant Lt Gen S K Kaul complimented the team members for their endurance, commitment, focus and willpower that took them from the 20th position at the end of the first day to the second position at the conclusion of the rally.

Heading: Suresh Jethwani elected Sindhu Seva Dal president - Indian Express
Content: Three men, in broad daylight looted a sweet shop in Dighi on Sunday. Ganaram Chowdhary, who owns 'Mamta Sweets, 'lodged a complaint with the Vishrantwadi police station. The police said that around 4 pm, three youths arrived in a car, entered the store and began pelting stones. They robbed Rs 3,000 and also broke glass panels in the shop causing damages worth Rs 2,000. The three accused — identified by the police as one Bobby Mose and his two accomplices — are absconding.

Heading: Speeding sensation - Indian Express
Content: Suresh jethwani has been elected as the president of Sindhu Seva Dal for the year 2008-2010. Outgoing president Udho Murjani handed over the charge at a function recently. The other office bearers elected include Mohan Chugh - vice president, Vijay Daswani - secretary, Paramanand Bathija - joint secretary, Sachin Talreja -treasurer and Deepak Wadhwani, Anil Pherwani, Peter Dhalwani, Moti Milani, Ashok Waswani, Haresh Paryani - all committee members.

Heading: Of flora & fauna - Indian Express
Content:
For Rubber Ripperz, biking is all about accelerating to new dimensions with pace and technology

An assemblage of bikes zoom past on the roads, arresting attention in the most spectacular way. For the onlookers it is the profligacy that many of the bike groups flaunt, but for the keen observers it's an interesting revelation. What bonds these 29 group of youngsters together is their chase for speed and the fondness for the same bike exploring their passion through rides, pace and stunts. The city biker group, Rubber Ripperz rides no other than Bajaj Pulsar 200cc or 220cc. Formed through the social networking site, orkut a year ago the group have been speeding to popularity.

Nitin Bansal one of the initial members who has been into biking since last five years, says, "The group turned out gradually but we do not allow bikers without the 200 or 220 cc bikes to be a part of the rides. The outings happen often, and we go to places likes Diveagar, Mahabaleshwar, Panchgani and so on." As another member Varun Narula says, "We were once spotted by the Bajaj team while we were on a trip and they were shooting for their 135 cc Discovery advertisement near Lonavala. It was an exciting moment to be appreciated by them as we exhibited some of our stunts on their bikes."

Ranging from age group 18 to 28 most of them are students who have been into bikes and speed since their school days. Adding on the road chase the group adds, "The most basic thing that motivates us is the sense of freedom. This has been out of choice and also the total control over the machine makes it ecstatic enough. It is addictive with a sense of thrill and satisfaction. It is also the shrieks and waves that we draw from the little kids and people as we pass through the villages. We love the attention. The bikes are special because they are a pioneer in a lot of technologies as well as with an overwhelming velocity."

Having been featured in the Bike magazine earlier the Rubber Ripperzs now plan to make it to Chennai on wheels, riding at the Chennai Race Track. And as they accelerate the bikers claim to have crossed the maximum speed the bike maintains. Adds Arzin Dalal, "Each one of us have crossed the 135 kmph speed limit. I have driven at a speed of 145 kmph. And then there are stunts that we are gaining proficiency in, including the christ, wheelie, stoppie, 360, burnout, donut and skitching. That makes it invariable to wear a helmet including other precautions. We also strictly follow the traffic rules and thankfully till date only the bikes have been injured."

Heading: Act Two - Indian Express
Content:
Ecofest — a film festival has been organised to use filmmaking as an effective medium to address issues related to environment

There are a few who use the handy cams and mobile phone cameras for purposes beyond shooting functions and family videos. Foliage outdoors, with a motive to create awareness amongst the masses about environment protection and wildlife conservation, has organised a two-day short film festival named — Ecofest.

"We have been conducting over 100 to 150 activities related to environment every year, but it's the first time that we are venturing into something of this sort. Films are an effective medium to send across the message of environment friendliness. Our motive behind organising this festival is to promote environmental awareness amongst both — filmmakers as well as viewers. The filmmakers while making the films have no option but to get into the minutest details about that particular subject and thus the subject is automatically given due attention," says Shantanu Rajguru, coordinator, Ecofest. He further adds, "You will be surprised to know that nearly 90 per cent of the filmmakers have handled this genre of films for the first time. Filmmaking is a passion and it is this passion that can help accelerate the cause."

Scheduled to take place on November 6 and 7 at S M Joshi auditorium, the Ecofest will showcase over 12 environmental films shortlisted from a total of over 25 entries. Varied topics like sea turtles, environmental pollution and so on will be handled by films — Ganpati Bappa Moraya, Have a Nice Day, Conserving Sea Turtles by Pugmark and so on. The shortest film in the festival is a 55 second film named Zindagi ka Saath with the lengthiest being a 12-minute film named Butterflies.

"While the filmmakers learn it while making the films, a serious involvement of the audience is important to spread the message and we have specially organised for interactions between the directors and audiences after screening of each of the films. This can also help the filmmakers come up with better and effective ideas the next time they think of making films based on environment. This festival is thus an opportunity for all to come together and discuss issues related to environment with filmmaking as the medium," says Rajguru.

In its first year, the festival also includes best film and runners up awards along with a special award for an out-of-the-box film.

Heading: Radio rampage - Indian Express
Content:
Paper Magic

Here is an opportunity to play with thin strips of paper to roll, mould and bend them into the reflection of your creativity. Finger puppets, fairies, paper jewellery, fridge magnet cartoons, floral designs all this and more can be your creations. A paper quiling workshop is being organised by Aperture India Gallery. The exhibition is on till November 6.

Dance your way

The ones clearing the auditions will get an opportunity to perform in live shows, music video albums, short films, documentaries and theatre plays after undertaking a professional training from AIPA. Heading: College bytes - Indian Express
Content:
Adding to the trend of campus radios, Radio Symbi is all set to go on air soon

It has not been long when films added glamour to this humble medium of communication. From the suave Vidya Balan to the naughty Preity Zinta radio has been the pet of all. Today when radio greets the world in its new avatar adding to efficacy of the good old radio is the glam quotient that owes its existence to FM channels. And when this age old mode of communication gets happening it glides its way straight to the colleges where the merger of the vivacious and the valuable takes place.

Coming up with campus radios, a concept where in house students of an institution control the console, the Symbiosis Institute of Media and communication, Lavale is the latest to go on air with its Radio Symbi in February 2009. With its youthful flavour and local touch the campus radio promises to be not only an infotainment medium but also a training ground to those who want to make it big in the radio industry.

Talking about the content, SIMC director professor Ujjwal K Chowdhury says, "The content target is three fold. It will focus on the rural crowd around, what's up in the college campus and will also feature programmes for the youth in general."

"Programmes on Radio Symbi will be an intelligent blend of educative and entertaing content. Apart from music programmes that will feature performances by local bands,there will be talk shows and panel discussions through which we plan to take up issues related to education and literacy, self employment, health and hygiene and civic issues of local concern," adds he.

The station will be operated from the SIMC campus in Lavale and would be encompassing an area of eight km radius initially, which might be extended to 16 km radius later. In other words it will be catering to listeners in SIMC, SIBM (Symbiosis college of business management), SITM (Symbiosis Institute of Telecom Management), SIT (Symbiosis Institute of Technology) apart from that ISBM, FLAME institute is also within seven km, new campus of Bharti Vidya Peeth and Lavle and other villages in the vicinity.

Planning to make it big with an eight-hour time slot on air initially, the five-student team of SIMC heading the project is exploring their creative best to give their campus radio an upbeat feel. " We want to launch Radio Symbi with a revamped and interesting format contrary to the element of boredom that is generally attached to campus radios," says Anand Jain, a final year student of SIMC and one of the team members.

Apart from English and Hindi, some programmes will be in Marathi to facilitate the understanding of the localites residing in the surrounding villages. With an estimated budget of around 50 lacs, Radio Symbi is a promising venture that will become the perfect platform for the students to voice their opinions on issues, exhibit their hidden talents and for that matter even sit back and listen to good music played by the college bands.

Workshops on radio production are being conducted for the upcoming batches so that they may take up the reins when the present batch leaves. Students are being trained in the nuances of programme production as well as the technicalities.

With an inherent connectivity and flexible format, campus radios offer new vistas to experiment with ideas and creative instincts. With a promising and well-researched content already in the pipeline combined with the expertise of dynamic set of minds working behind it, it seems that Radio Symbi is all set to keep its listeners tuned in.

Heading: 1,200 racehorses down with fever - Indian Express
Content:
Leadership Lessons

Indian cricket team captain, M S Dhoni visited the Foundation for Liberal And Management Education (FLAME) recently, where he interacted with the students of the institute. Dhoni also discussed various factors related to leadership. Talking on the change in his batting style from aggressive and flamboyant, to mature and controlled, Dhoni said, "As a youngster I wanted to go and destroy the opposition. But now, as a captain and a batsman,I have a different responsibility to shoulder, but nevertheless, I enjoy both the roles I play." Appreciating his humble behaviour, Parag Shah, chairman, FLAMES, concluded with the vote of thanks to the captain.

Marketing services seminar

A two-day national seminar on services marketing was recently organised by Jayawant Institute of Management Studies on the subject, Strategic Insights In Marketing Services. The objective of the seminar was to create awareness on the happenings in the service sector along with its importance in marketing those services and also to envisage the career opportunities available in various service industries. The seminar was inaugurated by Chandra Mauli, director, Pune Airport. In the inaugural address he emphasised on unique strategies used by various airlines to market their services in lieu of the staff competition so as to in the business. B G Piparaiya, general manager, Marketing, Bank of Maharashtra addressed the status of the Indian banking sector and the challenges in marketing their services.

Different Diwali

For these youngsters the festival was more than just partying or bursting crackers. Making Diwali special for the kids of Vanchit Vikas Sanstha, a NGO for the children in red light area, 25 youngsters celebrated the festival with them. "We looked forward to make the festival special for them. We gifted them clothes, food grains chocolates, biscuits, note books, story books, crayons, pens, toys and crackers and so on," said fashion choreographer, Sandeep Dharma who also joined the youngsters for the cause.

Chain Act 08

International School of Business and Media (ISB&M), Pune has organised Chain Act 08 a one-day symposium on Supply Chain and Operation Conference, to be held on November 8 at ISB&M Campus, Nande village, Pune. Speakers like C K Dave, vice president operations, Maruti Suzuki India Ltd, W S A Kanthiya, director operations, department of atomic energy and many more from leading companies across the country would be present to share their valuable experiences and address issues on the subject. During the one-day seminar recent research on the most critical supply chain issues and solutions adopted by industry leaders will be outlined and discussed. Presentations and stimulating panel discussion by experts in the field are other highlights.

MIT HR summit

The HR summit organised recently by MIT group of institutions at Dnyaneshwara Hall (MIT, Pune) concluded successfully after hosting two-days of focused discussions on contemporary aspects of the human resources function. The HR Summit structured as a series of corporate talks and panel discussions witnessed presentations and deliberations by Senior HR professionals and academicians on a wide range of emerging topics such as— Role of HR in times of inflation, War of talent - campus recruitment in India, Effect of global recession on Indian HR and B2E - Business to employee - Future trends. In his keynote address, Sunil Karad, executive director, MIT Group of Institutes said, "As a nation, we have a tremendous potential in the area of human resources. With this forum, we hope to inspire and support a new wave of ideas and thoughts needed to create the next generation of young leaders and managers."

Young and hopeful

Express Youth Forum had recently organised two events on the occasion of Diwali. The first one was at Army Paraplegic Center and EYF conducted a number of cultural activities along with antakshari and drawing competitions. The second event was scheduled in the evening at Savali, a home for the mentally retarded situated near Kothrud Depot. They distributed crackers and food items amongst the children. Vasant Thakar, president, Savali said, "These mentally retarded students are also a part of our society, they should not be left behind as destitute and the young generation should come ahead not just to give them a helping hand but also to bring them up to a normal way of life." The Event managers were Sonia Rodrigues, Sandip Vernekar, Ankit Shah and Rohan Jain.

IIJT centre inaugurated

The Indian Institute of Job Oriented Training (IIJT) at Aundh was recently inaugurated by advocate S K Jain, chairman, Khadaki Education Society. Alongwith Wasim Nirwan, support manager, IIJT, and Sushama Deshmukh, director, IIJT, former tourism minister and MLA, Chandrakant Chajed was present at the function. With its 275 centers across India, IIJT the centre at Aundh would be their new addition to accounts, finance and taxation course. Speaking at the occasion Sushama Deshmukh said, "The technical team of IIJT, Aundh, comprises of renowned academicians, industry professionals and personality development experts. It has launched its CBA course, which is globally recognised with Cambridge international examination certification." The curriculum involves classroom coursework and hands-on training as well as the practical workshops and Industrial training at various leading corporations, which gives the exposure to the areas of personality development and business knowledge. After completion of the above career program the student is awarded a Cambridge international examination certificate.

Heading: Mumbai racing season put off till January - Indian Express
Content:
Equine flu suspected as horses wheeze and sneeze; will not be able to race for at least a month

Nearly 1,200 horses at the Pune Racecourse are ailing and need a month's rest to recover from suspected equine influenza, or horse flu. Virologists at the Animal Husbandry department have collected 155 samples from 15 stud farms and will send these to the National Centre for Equine Research in Haryana on Tuesday for confirmation of the equine influenza virus. Pune last faced an outbreak of the disease in 1987.

The horses have been ill for more than a week, said Dr Ravi Reddy, secretary of the Indian Association of Equine Practitioners and a senior veterinary surgeon at Nanoli stud farm. The horses have high fever and are suffering from nasal discharge; some of them even have lung abscess, he said. Currently being treated at the stables at the Pune racecourse, some of the thoroughbreds have not responded to the first line of treatment and are on antibiotics for second bacterial infection, Reddy said.

The present outbreak has had the horses suffering from respiratory tract infection symptoms like fever and wheezing. The horses are kept at the stables of the Pune Racecourse and the handlers are also being given tips on maintaining hygiene. "We are restricting the movement of these persons from one farm to another," said Reddy.

Virologists with the Disease Investigation Section (DIS) of the state animal husbandry department pointed said such outbreaks also happened in Kashmir, Meerut and Rajasthan in June; last year the virus had even infected horses in Australia and Japan.

"We have surveyed 4,722 horses from 15 stud farms in Pune and surrounding areas. A total of 216 horses are ill and we have collected 155 samples out of which 27 are nasal swabs, 65 serum samples from healthy horses, 42 serum samples of horses who have recovered, 15 samples of presently ailing horses and six random samples," said P T Ganvir, joint commissioner of animal husbandry, DIS.

The Haryana research centre will isolate the virus from the samples, following which it will confirm whether it is equine influenza or not.

Virologists at National Institute of Virology in Pune said equine influenza occurs globally. The impact of an outbreak among horses can be devastating, with the ramifications most telling on the racing fraternity. The influenza has a high rate of transmission among horses and a short incubation time of one to five days. Affected horses, however, recover in three weeks.

Heading: Uniform jinx: Now, pupils’ parents can’t get cheques - Indian Express
Content:
The Royal Western India Turf Club (RWITC) held a special committee meeting with horse owners and trainers on Monday evening in Pune and decided that there will be no racing in Mumbai till January 15, 2009. The decision was taken in view of the mysterious fever that struck the stables at the Pune Racecourse due to which the Pune season ended on a sour note with mass withdrawal of runners on the last two days of the racing calendar.

Earlier the club had announced a three-week postponement, which has now been extended to over nine weeks. The Mumbai season was supposed to start on November 16. The meeting was presided over by Dr Cyrus Poonawalla and attended by a large number of trainers and owners of horses.

Behram Engineer, secretary of RWITC, said the club has also imposed a ban on the movement of the horses till the situation is under control. "We will review the situation of the horses week by week and if there is any change in these decisions the trainers and owners will be intimated," he said.

He confirmed that this is the first time ever that the Mumbai racing season has been postponed due to such a mass epidemic and that the club is likely to suffer major losses due to this delay.

Asked how many horses are down with the fever, Engineer said it was difficult to say as the figures changed rapidly. "You could have 100 horses inflicted with the fever in the morning and 400 by evening," he said.

Trainer Imtiaz Sait welcomed the decision and said that the well being of the horses was paramount at this stage. "It's a good decision because a horse takes about 3-4 weeks to recuperate after returning to normalcy and this time period will help them do that," said Sait who, like almost all other trainers, has most of the horses in his stables affected by the fever.

Heading: Bullets smuggled from ammo unit were sold to criminals - Indian Express
Content:
For children in schools run by the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), the academic year is well past the halfway mark but the drama over the uniforms that never reached them is still unresolved.

After activists blocked an attempt by the school board to give branded fabrics to over one lakh hapless children, the board has now cited difficulties in a plan to finance the purchase of uniforms by the children. It says payment by cheque or demand draft is impossible as most of these children hail from families where parents don't have bank accounts.

The payment aggregates Rs 4 crore, with each student to get around Rs 400. Now, with the fresh roadblock coming up, these impoverished students face the danger of not getting what they are eligible to as there are just four months to go this academic year.

One of the objections raised by activists was that the school board had bypassed the state-run textile corporation and gone for private companies for uniforms - in the process flouting a government regulation. Following these allegations the PMC appointed an inquiry committee; as per its recommendation, the civic body scrapped the entire tender procedure and instead decided to pay the children through DDs/ cheques so that they could buy school uniform on their own.

At a press conference on September 16, municipal commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi had told the media that in order to avoid delay in the retendering process, students would be given the amount through the school board. "These payments will be made in two installments. The first installment will be 60 per cent of the total and the remaining 40 per cent amount will only be made after the students produce evidence that they have really bought uniforms as per specifications," he had said.

Now, Pardeshi said, "We had decided to go for payment to the children through DDs or cheques, but the school board is opposing this move. If nothing works out, we will go for the textile corporation fabric." He said buying the fabric straight from the Maharashtra State Textile Corporation Limited could be an option.

School board chief Mahesh Ladkat told this newspaper that handing over the DDs or cheques was impossible due to the poor economic background of school students.

"We have over one lakh students studying in the civic schools and most of them are from measly financial backgrounds. We have found that their parents do not even have bank accounts, as they cannot afford the minimum Rs 500 opening balance. Giving these cheques is not practically possible. Therefore, we have conveyed this difficulty to the civic administration. However, a decision over this is yet to be made."

Heading: City’s pride boxes to gold in world youth championships - Indian Express
Content:
Two buyers in jail; former teacher absconding

Investigations into the recent smuggling of bullets from the Ammunition Factory, Khadki, (AFK), have thrown up startling revelations. The two accused, Bholu Bhegde and Sunil Pawar, arrested in the case, have reportedly told the police that more than 350 bullets had been smuggled out of the factory and some of them could have landed up in the hands of criminals. Some of the criminals who got their hands on the bullets are believed to be now behind bars.

The Crime Branch is now probing whether Bhegde, an employee of the factory, had any connection with anti-national elements or gangs. Bhegde was reportedly trying to sell cartridges to Pawar when they were arrested. On Saturday, police made two more arrests in the case. The duo, Sachin Dangat (33) and Rohidas Dangat (23), had criminal records and Dangat was the accused in a murder case, according to the police.

The four accused were produced in a Pimpri court on Monday and remanded to police custody till November 7.

Now, the Crime Branch radar is on a retired teacher staying in Pandharpur. "We sent a police team to Pandharpur to detain the teacher but he is absconding. We have launched a search for him. He is suspected to have sold over 125 bullets to criminals," said sub inspector Rajendra Bahirat.

So far, 29 bullets have been recovered, five of them from Dangat's farmhouse. "Many criminals to whom the bullets were supplied are now lodged in Yerawada Jail. We will question them too. Among them are Rakesh Phoolchand alias Mahakali of Dehu Road and Vishal Rajendra Banekar alias Papulya of Punavle," said Bahirat in the remand report.

"The number of bullets suspected to have been smuggled out from one of the premier ammunition factories in the country is very large. This is a serious security breach. We have to investigate whether Bhegde and Pawar had links with any anti-national elements," said Bahirat.

Meanwhile, it has been found out that there have been many cases of thefts from the factory in the past too. Besides, four employees having suspected links with the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) were under watch of the factory management. The factory sources said the four had been transferred to non-production departments after the tip-off against them.

Heading: Dead body lies outside the court for over six hours - Indian Express
Content:
When 17-year-old pocket-sized dynamite Nanao Singh stunned Cadet World Championship bronze medallist Grigoriy Nikolaychuk of Russia to clinch the gold at the inaugural AIBA Youth World Boxing Championships in Mexico on Sunday, his training officer and coaches at Army Sports Institute (ASI), Pune were not surprised. Anyone who pays a visit to the boxing training centre at ASI could fathom why. On a wall on the left side as one enters, a big board displays a list of probables for the Olympics 2012. Leading the list is 153-cm-tall Nanao Singh.

"I knew the boy could do it. He has that spark in him and he is never bothered about who his opponent is," said Lt Col S Jayakumar, training officer (boxing) at ASI.

This is not the first time the world has seen the confidence of little Nanao in the ring. Recently he out-punched Wales opponent Zack Davies 25-10 in the light flyweight (48 kg) category in the Commonwealth Youth Games in Pune to win gold.

"His opponent at the CYG was taller than him and his hand movements were also really good. But in the green room, Nanao was composed and focused and the way he started the bout showed his maturity," said Jayakumar.

Hailing from Manipur, Nanao joined ASI two years ago and since then has reaped many successes. Nanoa boxing glory days date back to his childhood and he got into the limelight by becoming the sub junior national champion in 2004, 2005 and 2006. He then went on to become national junior champion twice - in 2007 and 2008.

So far this year has been a dream run for Nanao. He won the gold and was acclaimed the best boxer at the Cuban National Games before continuing his blazing form to clinch the gold at the CYG and now again in Gaudalajara, Mexico.

The India team's chief coach, Capt G Manoharan, himself a former Olympic boxer and Arjuna awardee, said from Mexico that he was extremely pleased with the performances of all seven Indian boxers. "Nanao's performance was simply stupendous and the country can look forward to an Olympic Medal in 2012 from him," he said. Speaking about the prospects of the army lad winning a gold for India in the London Olympics, Jayakumar said, "He can do it. When he came to get my blessings before leaving for Mexico, I asked him to call me only after winning gold. He did call and I believe that he will do it again - at the Commonwealth Games and Olympics."

Heading: GLADA acts tough, warns illegal developers of action - Indian Express
Content:
The dead body of an unidentified man was found lying outside gate no 3 of the Shivajinagar district and sessions court on Monday. The body was spotted by the keeper of the Court.

Vikram Sonawane, the keeper of the Court, said, "I saw the body at 7.30 am, and I informed the police immediately.

However, nobody came in to pick the body. So at 11 am, I again called the Shivajinagar police station and they promised to reach soon. But the body was removed from the premises only at 2.50 pm."

When contacted, police inspector R. Yeole of the Shivajinagar police station said, "yes we did receive a call in the morning. But the municipality was unable to send anyone to pick up the body as they did not have any vehicles available at that time. As soon as they got a van they picked up the body."

Strips of medicines Vontac-150 and Ampicillin capsules were found near the body. The body has been sent to the Sassoon General Hospital for post-mortem.

The identity of the man has not been established yet. A case has been registered with the Shivajinagar police station.

Heading: 2,000 dengue cases later, national team comes calling - Indian Express
Content:
The Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA) is all set to serve notices to about 700 illegal colony developers to either stop construction or face demolitions.

Moreover, the authority is also preparing a second set of list of illegal colonies.

In view of the obvious action, the colony developers have sought a meeting with Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on November 9, to be arranged by Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda, to sort out this issue.

On Monday, after a delegation of these colony developers met GLADA Chief Administrator A K Sinha, they were given a 10-day period to sort out the issue themselves or face the music.

Kamal Chaitly, president of Ludhiana property dealers association, said: "The SAD-BJP government has changed the rules and now the approved colonies cannot be less than 75 acres in area. The development charges have also been raised from Rs 3.5 lakh per acre to Rs 35 lakh per acre. This has led to mushrooming of unapproved colonies. We have been requesting the authorities to look into our demands for more than a year but to no avail. For the last two years, no new approved colony has come up because it is not viable to have a colony on an area of 75 acres. Earlier, the limit was only 10 acres. The conditions, therefore, need to be relaxed because thousands of residents live in these colonies."

The GLADA had earlier asked the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) to stop electricity supply to the unapproved colonies. The decision was taken back after the residents met the chief minister in the recently held sangat darshan. The development authority had then put up notices outisde the unapproved colonies cautioning the buyers not to buy plots in these areas to avoid troubles in future. Sources revealed that sales of these plots had dipped drastically due to this action even as the step was taken only a few days ago.

Chaitly, meanwhile, said the GLADA can levy development charges on the unapproved colonies as a solution to this problem.

Heading: 4 yrs after missing deadline, work on Indoor Stadium to start again - Indian Express
Content:
Months after it reported the highest number of dengue cases in the country, a team of the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) visited the city on Monday to identify the technical reasons for the spread of the disease in the district and suggest preventive measures to check it.

The team, headed by Dr Kalpana Barua, deputy director of NVBDCP, told Newsline that since the district reported a large number of dengue cases, the team was here to enquire into the technical reasons behind it. The team, including regional director of the programme, Dr Amarjeet Kaur, visited the Civil Hospital and the Municipal Corporation to take stock of the measures being taken to prevent spreading of the disease. The NVBDCP team is learnt to have conducted surveillance drive in 137 hospitals across the country.

The number of dengue cases in the country has touched 7,600. Out of these more than 2,318 cases, including eight deaths, were reported from district.

Meanwhile, the visit of the NVBDCP team coincided with a meeting held by the district administration today along with officials of the Municipal Corporation, Health department and representatives of some city hospitals.

Those present at the meeting included Additional Deputy Commissioner Priyank Bharti, District Health officer Dr SS Dhir, BK Gupta, Joint Commissioner, Ludhiana Municipal Corporation (LMC) and Charanjeet Singh Uppal, Medical Officer of LMC.

Bharti said a plan has been put in place to control the further spread of the disease.

"The Municipal Corporation has acquired new fogging machines and a fresh schedule for fogging has also been prepared. We have now decided to create awareness by flashing the phone numbers of the nodal officers through advertisements so that people can contact them directly if fogging operation is not done in their areas," ADC Bharti said.

Notably, the LMC only had nine machines when the disease was spreading its tentacles in the district. It is only lately that it acquired 10 new fogging machines.

Heading: ‘Warring groups’ clash, 1 critical - Indian Express
Content:
The Indoor Stadium project, lying closed for more than two years, may finally see the light of the day. The work on the ceiling will be started soon, as decided in the Finance and Contract Committee (F&CC) meeting on Monday.

The members also gave the nod to extend the length of the Gill Flyover from Partap Chowk till Dholewal to ease the traffic on the route.

The Indoor Stadium project was scheduled for completion in mid-2004 at the cost of Rs 16 crore. Its estimated cost has now touched Rs 25 crore. Sources revealed that the committee is re-working on the project cost once again and it is likely to surpass its new estimated cost.

Moreover, despite a two-year delay, the committee has not laid down any fresh deadline for the project.

Senior deputy mayor Parveen Bansal said: "As of now, no fresh deadline has been set for the project. It was decided in the meeting today to start work on the ceiling. Deadline for the project will be set at a later stage."

Meanwhile, the Gill Chowk flyover, which was to end just before the Partap Chowk, has now been extended till Dholewal Chowk. Bansal said: "The cost of the extended flyover is still to be worked out and it is not necessary that the same contractor will be chosen for the work."

BJP councillors meet MC chief

The BJP councillors met MC Commissioner G S Ghuman along with senior deputy mayor Parveen Bansal on Monday. The councillors stressed that in tenders, the contractors be given a fare chance to apply and for every work one tender should be invited instead of a tender for a number of projects. Sources revealed that at present, tenders for development works amounting to Rs 25 crore each are being invited for various areas. Councillors said that a single contractor should not be allotted all the work. This delays projects and other contractors do not get a fair chance to apply, the councillors stated.

Heading: Museum of ‘king of hobbies’ has no visitors - Indian Express
Content:
The city, once known for its blood-laced gang wars, seems to be at it once again.

At Bhagwan Colony near Dholewal, a scuffle between two warring groups left one seriously injured. Jatinder Sharma, who received serious injuries in the lower parts of the body and a completely damaged eye, is currently undergoing treatment at the Christian Medical College and Hospital. The police, meanwhile, have launched a manhunt to nab the three named by the mother of the victim.

Santosh Sharma, Jatinder's mother said: "About two months ago, my nephew Vikas Sharma was shot dead by BSP youth wing leader Tarunjeet. We had all held rallies to protest against the cold-blooded murder. Probably people from the rival gang kept us on the target and found the time ripe to attack late on Sunday night."

Jatinder was unconscious till the filing of the report. His mother added: "After 11 on Sunday night, five persons attacked Jatinder while he was returning home. Before he could enter the home, the men pounced on him and stabbed him continuously. They even gauged out his eye which had to be stitched up."

"The police have not even arrested any one person who was involved in the murder of my nephew. His killers are walking free," Santosh said.

Gurtej Singh, Station House Officer, Division Number Six, ruled out the gang war theory and said: 'The allegations are not true. This is a completely new fight between the two groups and is evident from the fact that the people who have been named in the FIR by Jatinder's mother have no criminal background or anything to do with the BSP leader."

Those named in the FIR include Ashwani, Gaurav and Lali. No arrests have been made by the police so far.

Heading: Work on 5 hydel projects on Sidhwan canal grinds to halt - Indian Express
Content:
About ten years ago, Ludhiana got its first philately museum at the Head Post Office.

However, instead of attracting people towards what can be a wonderful hobby, the museum has hardly had any visitors. It remains closed for most time of the year and opens only on days when the Ludhiana Philatelic Club organises bal mela or a stamp exhibition.

In fact, only a handful of people in the city know about the museum's existence.

Yashpal Bangia, president of Ludhiana Philatelic Club, said: "The department does not bother much about the museum. We have often asked the Senior Superintendent Post Offices, Ludhiana (city division), to handover it to Ludhiana Philatelic club. We even offered our services for its proper maintenance as well as its regular usage for the public in general. We also proposed to open a small library here. The museum is opened only on three days — October 2, November 14 and once when a district-level exhibition of the Ludhiana Philatelic Bureau is organised."

Philately, the study and collection of revenue and postal stamps, is hobby to sharpen aesthetic tastes, especially for children. Ironically, students from very few schools across the city are asked to visit this place of knowledge.

Bangia said: "We do not feel like approaching more schools as the Postal department hardly takes any initiative."

Bangia, who has also written six books on philately, added: "If the Postal department hands over this museum to us, we will not only sit there, but also bring many positive changes. Many students from city schools will be made aware of this precious hobby."

Kuldeep Singh, SSPO, (Ludhiana Muffasil Division), who is also holds the charge of city division at present, said: "I enquired about this proposal with the dealing hand staff. They told me that the Ludhiana Postal department has forwarded the proposal to the Circle Office in Chandigarh thrice, where it is lying pending."

Heading: PAU inter-college youth festival to kick off on Nov 6 - Indian Express
Content:
City residents' hope of power crisis easing up in near future suffers a setback

There seems to be very little chances of the power crisis in the city easing in a near future. A Chandigarh-based textile company Winson Yarns has planned five hydel projects on Sidhwan canal with a total cost of more than Rs 25 crore. Though the projects are to be commissioned by March end, but work at all the sites has ground to halt, and curiously, the commissioning agency, Punjab Energy Development Authority (PEDA) seems to be unaware about the development.

Information revealed that a two hydel projects of 0.9 MW capacity each are coming up in Barewal and Issewal areas, one 0.75 MW project at Bharowal, one 0.85 MW project at Raowal while one 0.5 MW hydel project is coming up near Mansian village in Sidhwan Bet area. The company will also be giving rent of about Rs 25 lakh per annum to drainage department for using the canal area.

The company started work at all the sites about a year ago, but all of a sudden the work has been stopped at all sites despite the fact that deadline is approaching.

Balaur Singh, PEDA director, while talking to Newsline, said, "I am not aware that the company has stopped work. The contract was allotted to them on build, own and operate (BOO) basis and they have to complete the project by March 31. I will check up tomorrow the reason of delay. But I think the company may quicken the pace of work in the coming months."

The company, it may be mentioned, will be selling the power to PSEB at a rate of Rs 3.49 per unit and the power generated will be supplied to the nearest grid of PSEB, he added.

Sidhwan Canal will also get water supply for almost 10 months in a year, which at the moment is for not more than six months. For this, an escape channel has already been made from where the water supply would go to Sutlej river instead of being supplied for irrigation purposes during the months when water is not required by the crops, said Amarjit Singh Dullet, superintending engineer, Drainage Department.

Heading: Congress flays govt failure to check dengue - Indian Express
Content:
The Inter-college Youth Festival of Punjab Agricultural University will begin from November 6 and continue till November 19. "Preparations for holding the festival have been completed," said Dr Tejwant Singh, PAU Director Students Welfare, while adding that committees to handle different tasks have been formulated.

Dr Singh said that on the inaugural day, the cultural procession comprising contingents from different constituent colleges of PAU would start from the Museum of Rural Life of Punjab on the campus of College of Home Science.

The collage-making and cartooning events will take place on November 6. On-the-spot painting and poster making competitions will be held on November 7 while clay-modelling and Rangoli contests will take place on November 8. Dr Singh said creative writing competition would be organised on November 10, debate, elocution and extempore speech competitions on November 11 and poetic recitation and Haas Ras contests on November 12. All these events will be organised at the Students' Home.

The formal programme of inauguration, creative dances and folk songs would be organised in the open-air theatre on November 17 while all musical items will be held in the evening. On November 18, activities of Shabad Gayan (solo and group), quiz, one-act-play, mono-acting, mime and mimicry would be organised.

On November 19, the activities of classical dance, skits and folk dances would be held in the open-air theatre at 5 p.m., which will be followed by prize-distribution function at 7 p.m., said Dr Singh. Dr Tejwant Singh and Ramandeep Singh Grewal are the convener and co-convener, respectively, of the event.

Heading: Exhibition showcases photojournalists’ work - Indian Express
Content:
The AICC secretary and national spokesperson of the Congress, Manish Tewari today lashed out at the SAD-BJP government for its failure to contain the spread of dengue in the city.

Tewari also flayed Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal for his 'Sangat Darshans', which, he said, instead of solving the problems of the people were causing a lot of harassment to the ordinary people. In a statement issued after an extensive tour of the city and the surrounding areas, Tewari said he was shocked to learn that almost all the areas of the city were in the grip of dengue which, he claimed, had assumed epidemic proportions. He said the government had failed to respond to the situation and there was a panic among the people.

Tewari pointed out that no measure had been taken either for preventing the spread of the disease or providing any relief to the affected people. He said even the hospitals were ill-equipped to tackle the situation. He said the facilities at the government hospitals were very poor. He said while the Chief Minister had announced free treatment for the dengue patients, but there had not been any follow up action.

"I would ask CM to tell the public where should they go for the treatment of dengue; and where they would be treated for free?", Tewari said, adding that providing free treatment was a far cry too because even basic treatment was not available to the people.

Heading: College of Agriculture to hold convocation - Indian Express
Content:
It is for the first time that the photojournalists from the city have put up their works for display at the art gallery, Artmosphere. The youngest of the lot, Ravi Kanojia, who is a staff photographer with the Indian Express, along with Rakesh Bhambi from The Tribune and Vikas Kahol, special correspondent from The Mail Today, have put on display the works that they have shot over the period of their news gathering. The exhibition was inaugurated by city's leading businessman Balraj Bhasin.

Sukhvir Singh, owner of the gallery, said, "People see pictures in the newspapers daily. Our main aim in putting up this exhibition was to show people how each picture is a story in itself." About his work involving diverse fields Ravi Kanojia says, "The Indian Express provides me with immense opportunities to travel not only within the district but also outside, which in turn enriches my craft."

Vikas Kahol, who is also a reporter, adds, "My pictures are stories in themselves. The lone girl in a class full of boys shows the skewed sex ratio prevelant in the state. The old lady standing next to window is waiting for her daily doze of chemotherapy tells the tale of people suffering from cancer in the cotton belt of Punjab."

Rajesh Bhambhi, who has also worked for leading agencies like Reuters, says, "News photography is capturing a mood in a jiffy. So while I have tried to capture the expressions of Rahul, Priyanka and Sonia Gandhi as they take the ashes of Rajiv Gandhi, or the people shot dead by terrorists at Baddowal railway station or people tortured by the police lying on the ground. Each picture not only tells a story but also sends out a message for the society."

The exhibition is open for the next fortnight.

Heading: Zoology dept to hold national symposium from Nov 6 - Indian Express
Content:
The convocation and prize-distribution function of College of Agriculture, PAU, will be held on January 15 at the Pal Auditorium of PAU.

According to the College Dean, Dr Milkha Singh Aulakh, degrees for B.Sc (Agri) (Hons) and B.Ed courses in addition to awards and medals would be conferred on the students, who have successfully completed their courses during the academic years 2004-05, 2005-06, 2006-07 and 2007-08.

He said that Dr Gurdev Singh Khush, a world-renowned rice breeder from the International Rice Research Institute, and a recipient of World Food Prize would be the chief guest. Dr Aulakh said that students, who have to receive their degrees,

may contact the office of Dean, College of Agriculture.

Heading: 'Yahoo, Google revise deal in hopes of approval' - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Zoology, PAU, in collaboration with Indian Society of Life Sciences, Kanpur, Society for the Advancement of Academics, Sports and Cultural Activities (SAASCA) and Zoological Society, PAU is organising a two-day national symposium on "Recent advances in zoological sciences: applications to agriculture, environment and human health" from November 6. The event will be held at the Department of Zoology, Punjab Agricultural University here.

Giving this information, Dr Tejwant Singh, Dean College of Basic Sciences and Humanities at PAU, said many basic and applied zoological sciences had grown multi-dimensionally and were serving mankind in various ways, said Dr H.S. Sehgal, the chief organiser of the symposium.

He stressed that the study of behaviour, structure and function of various pest species and their complex relationship with environment had led to devise effective methods of minimising pest damage to crops. Elaborating on the basic sciences like animal molecular biology, biotechnology, nanotechnology, immunology, etc. in relation to their role in improving quality and quantity of animal products, Dr Sehgal said India ranked second in inland fish production, next only to China.

He however, mentioned that these developmental activities had had negative effects on environment. For example, intensive agriculture and aquaculture were responsible for poor soil health, water pollution of water bodies, environment-related human and animal diseases, etc., said he.

Several ethical issues connected to the developments made in the field of biotechnology, nano-technology, etc., were of present day concern, said Dr Tejwant Singh, adding that scientists in the area of basic sciences were continually working to address these issues and generating viable technologies.
