On its part, India Inc asked the government to pull out all stops to ensure availability of enough money to drive the economy on a high growth trajectory despite the global meltdown. CII President K V Kamath said, "If this country has to progress, we need to set what is the growth we want, and the growth rate clearly the government has articulated is around 8 per cent. If that is so, we need to work back (and see) what is the interest rate that will drive this growth."

FICCI President Rajeev Chandrasekhar said, "If we have to really address this issue (global crisis), the focus of the government without any ambiguity should be on driving growth and all the fiscal and monetary policies must be inclined to deliver growth."

Heading: Six ‘kidnapped’ pilgrims rescued; one abductor held - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: New lok adalat bench, mediation centre on High Court premises - Indian Express
Content:
Six persons, who were allegedly kidnapped on November 1 from near a bus stand in Phagwara, were rescued by the Jalandhar police on Monday. One of the abductors was arrested along with the vehicle, while five are absconding. The six persons included Suresh, his brother Varinder, Subhash, Rohtaf, Rakesh and Subhash.

They had gone to Vaishno Devi shrine and on way their back to Moth Lubari village in Sirsa district, they stayed at an inn at Hanuman Garhi Mandir in Phagwara, as they had to board a bus the next morning.

They were abducted by six persons and taken towards Tanda in Hoshiarpur district. The family came to know of the kidnapping when Kuldeep Kumar, father of Varinder and Suresh, received a call for Rs 2-lakh ransom.

The police asked Kuldeep to maintain contact with the kidnappers, while they kept a watch on their movement.

The place for delivering the ransom was fixed near Kala Bakra and a cop in plainclothes accompanied Kuldeep. However, the abductors fled in their two vehicles. As the police team chased them, they started pushing the abducted persons out of the vehicle, one by one, said Inspector Angrez Singh.

The police managed to surround one of the vehicles and arrested its driver, Jasbir Singh. The inspector said all the abductors, who were in their early twenties, were unemployed and belonged to good families of Khak village in Tanda.

Heading: ‘Every person we picked up turned out dead’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has decided to constitute benches for daily Lok Adalats on its premises. The new benches and the mediation centres will be inaugurated on November 8 by Supreme Court Judge, Justice S.P. Sinha.

Addressing a joint press conference here today, Justice K.S. Grewal, chairman of High Court Legal Services Committee, and Justice Mahesh Grover, chairman of High Court Mediation and Conciliation Committee, said three new benches of the lok adalats at the High Court have been constituted for expediting the disposal of cases by amicable settlement. Twenty counselling centres have been planned, 10 each for Haryana and Punjab. The mediation centres would save time and money and create goodwill, apart from reducing litigation.

Justice Grewal said a retired judge of the High Court will be the presiding officer and one retired judge of the District Court would be the member of the bench.

Justice Grover said the mediation will be a "voluntary, non-binding" process, in which an impartial and neutral mediator will assist the parties in reaching an agreement. He will not impose a solution, but create a conducive environment in which parties can resolve their disputes, he said.

The deliberations of the mediation centres would be kept confidential and would only be disclosed in the court, he said. The mediation centres will start functioning from November 9 in Punjab and Haryana. The mediation centre scheme has proved successful in New Delhi and Karnataka.

Heading: Environment fund gets rolling - Indian Express
Content:
BUS MISHAP: Rescuers say with 45 dead, there was no one to give first aid to

An uneasy silence prevailed at Kanohar Nullah in Kufri as bodies lay strewn along the the cold and rocky hillside. All were passengers on board the ill-fated private bus that rolled down 600 feet from Lambidhar, on National Highway 21, close to Kufri.

The bus also broke into several pieces after banging onto the rocks on the hillside. Forty five persons died in the accident.

"I could not hear a single cry. All that we saw were scattered bodies as the smell of human blood and flesh rose in the air," said D.D. Sharma, a member of the rescue team of Himachal Pradesh Fire Services.

The team reached the spot within half an hour, by which time local people had gathered at the spot and had rushed survivors to the hospital.

The private bus, Arun Coach (HP-63-3774) had started for Shimla from Kotighat in Kumarsain tehsil of Shimla district at 6.30 am. Two families on their way for a wedding in Shimla also boarded the bus along with other passengers.

Dharmor village in Narkanda suffered the maximum loss, with 14 persons belonging to a single clan dead.

"All the medicines and other aid rushed to the spot by locals and students from the nearby Kufri hotel management institute were not used at all. No one could believe that every person who was picked up for rescue turned out to be dead," said Rati Ram of Kufri.

One of the three passengers who boarded the bus at Fagu, just a kilometre before the accident spot, also died. She was identified as Draupadi.

Her sister, 35-year-old Anita, who survived, said, "The bus was moving on the left side, opposite to the side from where it went down and the road was very wide. The driver was moving fast and did not pay attention to the road, due to which the bus went out of control." Anita's husband also escaped with minor injuries.

List of deceased, injured

The deceased include Krishan Chand Kainthla, Lakshmi Kainthla, Tarachand and Paras Ram of Dhamod village, Narkanda; Mohanlal Bhardwaj, Mamta and Chand Devi of Batawada village, Kumarsain; Suresh Kumar of Bharana, Theog; Avdesh of Premghat,Theog; Sushil Kumar of Theog; Naresh Kumar of Panchayat Narkanda; Rajender of Bihar; Kamlesh Chauhan, Shanti Swaroop and Naresh of Badagaon, Kumarsain; Pradeep Kumar and Durga Nand of Bhuna village,Kumarsain; Draupda of Janedghat, Solan; Hiranand of Ujed, Narkanda; Prem Sukh, Vivek Bali and Chetan of Chamola, Kumarsain; Yoganand Bali of Ahar; Jogender (26-year-old bus driver) of Kathala; Gangi Devi of Matiyana village, Shilaru; Phuli Devi and Jeet Ram Shayam of Palvi, Theog; Prakash Chand of Shenal, Theog; Krishna and Brijlal of Kandayali; Durga Das of Kumarsain; Narender Kanwar of Kyara, Theog; Deewan Chand of Ghasni, Kumarsain; Kamla Devi of Gallu, Theog; Ramji of Theog, Lal Singh of Thatal, Theog; Pinki alias Lok Chand and Ghanshyam of Kangal, Kumarsain; Rajeev Kumar of Gharin, Theog; Nihal Chand of Nankhadi; Anil of Darog and wife of Naresh Yadav of Gurgaon.

The injured include Dhayan Singh and Anita of Kufar Faila, Narayan Dutt of Chehad, Lalita of Gullo and an unidentified 15-year-old Nepali child.

Heading: GAIL inks deal with Himachal to supply natural gas - Indian Express
Content:
In a first-ever initiative to make Himachal Pradesh a carbon neutral state, the government has set up an environment fund to be raised from all vehicle users and institutions contributing to environmental pollution.

The fund, to begin with, will be a voluntary contribution and the amount collected will be utilised only on checking pollution and its adverse affects.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, who had proposed the fund a fortnight ago, said the guidelines governing the fund have already been prepared.

"Principal Secretary (Environment) Sarojini Thakur has handed over the guidelines for the fund, which will have a separate account and not go to the government," Dhumal told mediapersons.

Contributions have already been made to the fund by the Chief Minister, Cabinet ministers and senior bureaucrats and officials. The CM has made an appeal to all vehicle users in the state to contribute to the fund.

Heading: Sukhna drowning: parents seek arrest - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh today signed a cooperation agreement with GAIL (India) for supply of natural gas to the state's industrial, transport and domestic sector consumers.

The agreement, signed by B.C. Tripathi, GAIL's Director (Marketing), and Manoj Kumar, Director (Industries) in Himachal, has cleared the decks for extending the proposed Dadri-Bawana-Nangal natural gas pipeline to the state. The work will begun in two years, after completion of an assessment on the demand potential and alignment of the pipeline. The 65-kilometre pipeline will require an investment of nearly Rs 3,000 crore, for which GAIL has already mobilised funds, said U.D. Choubey, chairman and MD, GAIL.

Choubey said the availability of natural gas to Himachal would enable the state to meet the additional energy demand of the industry, especially in Baddi, Barotiwala and Nalagarh and cut down vehicular pollution by switching over to CNG-based transport. The domestic consumers will also provided natural gas through a pipeline.

State's Resident Commissioner Ajay Tyagi termed GAIL's decision as a significant step to boost industrial development and reduce dependency on other forms of fuels and energy. Manoj Kumar, Director (Industries), said Himachal Pradesh will require at least 500 MW of power to be supplied to the new industrial units and once GAIL lays downs its pipeline, the industry will have surplus energy as a new substitute. In the transport sector, GAIL's entry into Himachal would help in curbing vehicular pollution, particularly in the cement sector.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, hailing the cooperation agreement, recalled his meeting with Union Petroleum Minister Murli Deora, when he asked for a project in Himachal to meet energy needs. He said the facility, after lying of the pipeline, would benefit the state even in generating tax revenue, since GAIL proposes to set up a petro-chemical plant.

Heading: Meat units in court for being health hazards - Indian Express
Content:
The parents of 20-year Ranjan Nelson, who drowned in the Sukhna Lake on Monday, protested outside the police post near the lake today against "police inaction" to arrest Yaman, the person accompanying Ranjan at the time of the alleged accident.

Ranjan had gone to the lake with his employer's son, Yaman yesterday. When they reached the regulator end of the lake, Ranjan asked Yaman to stop the Tata Indigo car (CH03V 5634) they were travelling in to answer nature's call. After about five minutes, Ranjan called Yaman, who was waiting in the car, and asked him to click his photograph.

"Ranjan sat on a tree and asked me to click his picture. The very next moment, he lost his balance and fell into the lake. He screamed for help following which I also jumped into the lake but failed to get hold of him. When I could not find any help nearby, I called the police," Yaman had told the police.

After a rescue operation by the police, Ranjan's body was fished out of the lake and taken to the Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16 for autopsy. The police had initiated inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC in the case and started investigations.

Ashok Nelson, the deceased's father, however, alleged that his son was probably murdered by Yaman and asked for his immediate arrest. He was also accompanied by a few local politicians, it was claimed.

Yaman's father also reached the police post and tried to convince the grieving parents.

The Station House Officer of police station, Sector 3, Inspector Har Sahai said they were investigating the matter and would take appropriate action in the case.

Ranjan's postmortem could not be conducted today as some formalities were yet to be completed.

The body would be handed over to his family after a postmortem on Wednesday.

Heading: Rural residents equally prone to cardiovascular diseases, says study - Indian Express
Content:
DERA BASSI: High Court pulls up PPCB for issuing no-objection certificates to two meat-processing plants

Pollution seems to have become an all-time companion of the people living in villages near Dera Bassi and the surrounding areas. Vomiting, nausea, loose motions are some of the common health problems reported by the residents, especially children, due to the pollution, which is blamed on the meat-processing industries in the area.

Highlighting the pitiable condition of the villagers, the principal of Government Senior Secondary School in Samgoli, Mohali, submitted medical reports prepared by various doctors to the Punjab and Haryana High Court on Tuesday. A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh took a strong note of the observations made by the doctors.

The reports were filed against two meat-processing units — M K Overseas and Abbott Cold Store Meat Plant — located in Dera Bassi. These units have come under the court's scanner for not maintaining effluent treatment plants (ETP) and adequate air pollution control devices. The doctors and the principal have sought immediate closure of the units. The villagers have also alleged that the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) is not taking any action against them. The Bench came down heavily on the PPCB for issuing no-objection certificates (NOCs) to such units.

"How are you issuing no-objection certificates and allowing electricity connections to these units without ensuring that they have installed effluent treatment plants. The PPCB has a very important role to play in protecting the environment. How did this unit get an electricity connection when it had not installed the treatment plant?" Thakur asked, referring to M K Overseas.

The Chief Justice emphasised the role of the PPCB, holding that before giving consent to any unit to set up or operate, it was its responsibility to ensure that adequate and effective pollution control devices had been installed by the unit.

He observed: "Either (PPCB) officers are issuing NOCs due to extraneous reasons or they are doing so under duress or pressure."

Explaining the problems faced by the PPCB, its counsel advocate A R Takkar submitted that it often happened that an industry changed its manufacturing process or technology later, in which case the PPCB was supposed to issue warning to the unit to update its pollution control devices. "Unless there are specific parameters of stink added by the Legislature, the PPCB is unable to legally stop an industry, except when air pollutants, including obnoxious gases and suspended particulate matter, is beyond parameters," he said.

The Chief Justice held that the board officer who visited an industry and submitted a report after inspecting it should be prosecuted if anything was found amiss with the unit.

The case has been adjourned to November 10, when the Bench will pass orders that would affect all the industries in Punjab.

The Bench will pass directions on the issue that only those industries should be given NOCs which have adequate and appropriate pollution control devices installed.

Heading: Youth shot at in Zirakpur - Indian Express
Content:
Emphasising that cardiovascular diseases are not restricted to the urban population, a recent study by the Department of Community Medicine, PGI, states that hypertension and the risk factors relating to lifestyle diseases have crept into the country's slum population and the rural areas as well.

The department has just finished collecting data for the study, said Dr J S Thakur. "We have surveyed 400 people in the city, the surrounding slums and nearby rural areas in Haryana. We found that the risk factors for CVDs are almost at par in the rural and urban areas. At some places, this traditional divide has also reversed."

Another study by the department titled 'Cardiovascular Disease Risk Management in a Primary Healthcare Setting of North India', published in the Indian Heart Journal 2008, also establishes the trend.

The study covered 1,010 people from eight selected pockets in Haryana and Chandigarh. Of those surveyed, 253 were from the urban areas, 375 from the rural areas and 382 were slum-dwellers. The study found that one of the major risk factors for CVD —hypertension or high blood pressure — has a similar prevalence among all categories.

"The burden of cardiovascular diseases is on the rise in developing countries. We found a high prevalence of hypertension among 30-year-olds not only in the urban population (36.4 per cent) but also among slum-dwellers (25.4 per cent) and in the rural areas (24 per cent). Therefore, the primary healthcare system should be empowered for management of CVDs," notes the study.

Smoking, a crucial factor putting the younger population at risk for heart attack, had a much higher incidence in rural areas (40.8 per cent) than in urban areas (15 per cent) and slums (32.2 per cent).

Also, 11.2 per cent of respondents from the rural areas were overweight, 4.2 per cent suffered from probable angina and 0.5 per cent from probable stroke.

Over 27 per cent in the slums were categorised as overweight while the overall rate of obesity in the general population was found to be over 23 per cent.

Explaining the trend, Head of the Cardiology Department at PGI, Dr Yash Paul said: "The upward graph of CVDs in rural areas signifies the changing lifestyle of the population. A few years ago, 2-4 per cent of the people in rural areas suffered from CVDs while this figure has now risen to 6-8 per cent. More and more of the youth re coming in. Our observations have found that CVD affects around 10-14 per cent of the urban population and the rural areas have started to match that figure now. This is due to less physical exercise, more calorie intake and smoking among the rural population."

Heading: Science exhibition exposes Internet dependence of students in schools - Indian Express
Content:
Two motorcycle-borne people open fired on a youth on Monday night, leaving him seriously injured. The incident took place in the Green City Colony. The bullet hit the youth in his waist. He is undergoing treatment at the PGI.

According to reports, Satvinder Singh, a resident of Mamta Enclave in Dhakoli, had gone to his friend Gurpreet's house in the colony late Monday evening. While the two were talking outside Gurpreet's house, two unidentified men came on a motorcycle and fired at Satvinder. The assailants fled after committing the crime, taking advantage of the darkness. The police have registered a case. SHO Ranjot Singh said an old enmity was likely to be the motive behind the attack.

Heading: Gang of domestic helps held for robbing houses - Indian Express
Content:
Gone are the days when students and their teachers brainstormed for hours to generate ideas and slogged hard finding material to prepare a project for science exhibitions. With access to the Internet, students have every information just a click away. The result: they don't need teachers' help any more. This was what people saw at the science exhibition held at the State Institute of Education (SIE) on Tuesday.

Almost all the students who displayed their projects said they had got the idea for it from the Internet. It's not only the ideas, but the guidance to set up the projects, too, came from the World Wide Web.

Piyuesh Bhardwaj, a student of Class X at Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 35, had made a project on the increasing population. "I got the idea from the Internet and it is from there that I got the relevant information to make the model. The topic is a part of my course too," he said.

Sharing similar thoughts, Deepak Jha, a Class XII student from GMSSS-46 who had made a project on the 'improving cure for cancer', said: "I wanted to make a project that was a combination of science and mathematics. My team and I got help from the Internet."

The students could be seen with projects with innovative ideas. Among them was a 'green house' that was on the theme of global warming and another was on organic farming, highlighting the use of bio-technology.

The exhibition was inaugurated by UT Adviser Pardeep Mehra and attended by Director, Higher Education, Raji P Srivastava and DPI (Schools) Samwartak Singh.

Organised in collaboration with the NCERT, New Delhi, the exhibition will remain open till November 7 from 8 am to 2 pm. In all, 60 schools from the city are participating in the exhibition.

Heading: Security still an issue on PU campus - Indian Express
Content:
The chandigarh Police on Tuesday claimed to have busted a gang of three thieves who used to loot household items after getting employed as servants in the houses.

Police officers said the modus operandi was to commit the theft within three days after being hired as servants to evade police verification. Police have also recovered four laptops, a DVD player, a mobile phone and a cycle from their possession.

The accused have been identified as Bhuvan (22), Kishan (21) and Ramesh Chand (23), all natives of Almora district. Bhuvan was leading the gang and is also said to be involved in several cases of theft and snatchings in the city. They all were residing in Nayagaon for the past few years.

Deputy Superintendent of Police J S Khaira said the accused used to follow the advertisements in the newspapers about the requirement of cooks and servants in houses.

"They used to identify families with three to four persons, so that their job is easy. They gained confidence of their masters and when the family members went out, they used to loot cash, valuables and other household items," the DSP said.

Station House Officer of Sector-39 Police Station Inspector Anokh Singh said a police party had set up a routine checkpost in Sector 42 on Monday night. "Police officers found that Bhuvan and Ramesh were coming on their cycle with a bag. They signalled them to stop and searched the bag. They recovered two laptops from their possession. Bhuvan could not justify the ownership of the laptops and was brought to the police station," he added.

During investigations, Bhuvan revealed the address of his brother-in-law, Ramesh Chand. Police raided Ramesh's place and recovered two more laptops, a DVD player and a mobile phone. Ramesh has also been arrested.

DSP Khaira said that after committing five to six thefts, they used to visit Uttranchal for easy disposal of the stolen items. "Also, they used to steal whatever they could find in the house without a lock. They never broke open any lock or an almirah. Usually people keep their mobile phones and laptops openly in their house," he said.

A week ago, Anokh Singh said that Bhuvan had committed a theft in a house in Sector 42, when the owners had gone to the Gurdwara around 11 am. He has various theft and snatching cases registered against him in CIA Branch, police stations in Sector 11, 17 and 34.

Police also managed to arrest two other thieves — Sandeep and Satish — and recovered six mobile phones and two earrings from their possession. They were arrested from their house after a tip-off, Khaira said.

Heading: Three convicted for murdering youth - Indian Express
Content:
Around 50 security personnel have already been hired and PU authorities seem to be keen on hiring more

Authorities at the Panjab University (PU), taking serious note of recent incidents of violence in the campus, held a meeting today to discuss the ways and means to buffer up security in the university.

In the meeting, it was decided that the campus would have at least five drop gates to prevent the entry of outsiders.

Also, a suggestion to have more CCTV cameras in different parts of the campus was made. Another move that the authorities decided upon was to hire additional security personnel.

Earlier, the university had hired private security guards, which is now being phased out after they failed to maintain a peaceful environment in the campus. Around 50 security personnel have already been hired and the PU seem to be keen on hiring more.

Talking to Newsline, a senior university official said, "Security has been one area where we seem to be lacking but now with new measures being adopted, we expect to see a change. Students without identity cards would not be allowed in the campus." The entry of outsiders has also been banned in the Students' Centre. The steps are likely to be implemented soon, he added.

Heading: Sharma writes to Gandhi to constitute experts’ committee to regulate growth in city - Indian Express
Content:
A lower court on Tuesday convicted three persons on charges of murdering a youth in 2005. The three accused — Mewa Ram, Sucha Singh and Darshan Singh — were convicted in the court of additional district and sessions judge, R S Attri. Two of the other accused, Raj Kumar and Maheshi, were acquitted.

There was high drama at the court when the judgment was pronounced as the families of the accused raised a hue and cry.

The quantum on the sentence will be pronounced on November 8.

On December 4, 2005, the bruised body of a youth was found by the police in Sector 39. The body, which had injury marks inflicted with sharp-edged weapons, was found in the bushes near a road from the Grain Market to Maloya village. The word 'Raju' was tattooed on the arm of the victim.

Later, four brothers, hailing from the Sansi tribe and living in a nearby orchard, were arrested by the police.

The police claimed that during the course of interrogation the accused had confessed to the crime.

According to the police, the deceased had illicit ties with the wives of two brothers of the tribe and Raju was put to death to reclaim the tribe's honour.

During the course of the court proceedings, Jagtar Singh, a witness, had stated that two of the accused - Mewa Ram and Sucha Singh - had made an extrajudicial confession before him.

All the accused were acquitted of another murder charge wherein a beheaded body was found near Maloya village in January 2007.

Heading: Management students with a heart of gold - Indian Express
Content:
The first Indian chief architect of the city, M N Sharma, has written a letter to UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi demanding formation of an experts' committee to regulate growth in the city.

The letter states that "the city has drawn attention for its famous buildings designed by Le Corbusier. Organisations like UNESCO and Foundation Le Corbusier are making efforts to preserve the heritage sites of the city. However, these efforts will be of no use if an experts' committee is not constituted till the formation of a Regulatory Planning Authority".

The committee should review the ongoing projects and those in the offing to preempt loss to the exchequer and conserve the remaining green belt to accommodate changing needs of the future.

He urged Gandhi to make use of her office to ensure that the committee is constituted.

Heading: MC to launch free garbage collection drive - Indian Express
Content:
The University Business School (UBS) in Panjab University has come up with a noble idea to make the management students more socially aware and responsible. The department has initiated a project in which the students are being involved in various kinds of social work.

Talking to Newsline, Chairperson of the department, Professor Dinesh Gupta said, "The initiative has been taken by the department to make the students aware of their social responsibilities and duties. Management students are usually too busy with their schedule and hardly have any time.We, at the department, are trying to aquatint them with the society around them."

To begin with, the department had launched a first-of¿its-kind project in which students were sent to different NGOs and institutes on the culmination of the Panjab University's Diamond Jubilee celebrations recently.

The students visited institutes including an old age home, Institute for the Blind and the Cancer Cell in PGI among others. As per the project, students have to prepare a report and give a presentation regarding the visit. Talking to Newsline, a student from the department, Nidhi said, "I had never thought that the department would give us such an opportunity. It is a very innovative step that the department has come up with."

Prof Gupta was hopeful that the move would bring about a change in the students and make them more aware of their social responsibilities. Adding he said, "When these students pass out from the department, they may or may not have time to interact with people from other sections of the society. So we, at the department, in our own small way have started this project to make them realise their social tasks." The department has adopted the project as a part of the curriculum.

Heading: MC may hand over upkeep of underground parking lots to market associations - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation (MC) has mooted the proposal of free door-to-door garbage collection from the colonies in the city.

The aim is to maintain cleanliness in the areas to prevent the outbreak of diseases.

The tenders for the same have also been invited. At present, the door-to-door collection of garbage is done in the sectors for which the residents have to pay an amount of Rs 30 per month. It was, however, observed that residents of the colonies did not pay even this amount. Instead, they dumped their garbage around their house and parks.

During monsoons, there had been an outbreak of cholera in the tricity. This raised concerns over the sanitation conditions prevailing in the colonies.

It was also seen that the areas lack basic hygiene. In fact, the outbreak of diseases like cholera, dengue is an annual feature in the slums and colonies. Generally, the authorities go into an overdrive once a problem arises. The colonies are then cleaned up and care is taken to provide better facilities.

Medical Officer Dr G Diwan said: "We feel that taking preventive action should be taken as it is better than cure. Door-to-door garbage collection will ensure that disposal is done properly. With the surroundings being clean, it would lead to improvement in health conditions as well."

He added that residents have been giving excuses that sweepers are not available in their areas. The proposal would solve some of these problems.

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra said: "Proper sanitation is one of our primary concerns. We want to ensure better health for all residents. It is felt that the residents of colonies were reluctant to pay even a small amount for garbage disposal. So, we will be providing the facility free of cost."

In the city, garbage is collected from every household and then taken to the Sehaj Safai Kendras. From here, it is moved to the dumping ground in Dadumajra.

Heading: CFSL to conduct inquiry against ‘errant’ official for not examining thumb impressions - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (MC) is contemplating handing over the underground parking lots to the market associations for maintenance. This issue had come up for discussion at the monthly coordination meeting of the Administration and the Municipal Corporation held on Tuesday.

The MC has underground parking lots in Sector 8 and 17. These are, however, not adequately used. While the underground parking lot in Sector 8 has been handed over to the market association, a meeting will be held with the market associations in Sector 17 to decide on the issue. The underground parking lots have never been very popular with the residents due to frequent thefts.

The meeting was held under the chairmanship UT Advisor Pradip Mehra, Mayor Pardeep Chhabra as well as senior officers of the Administration and MC.

The Mayor said that a scheme will be formulated for their development as a modern dairy complex, which includes facilities for residents, cattle sheds, gobar gas plant and milk plant.

The issue of Martyr's Gallery also came up for discussion. The design of pre-fab shelters for taxi stands has also been finalised.

The Mayor raised the issue of reviewing land price to be charged from allottees for religious spaces. An area of two acres has been allocated to PFA and the dog pound should be part of that project, he said. The MC would coordinate with PFA for constructing a dog pound in that area.

The issue of delay in the sanction of concept building plans from the office of the Chief Architect was also taken up. A meeting for clearing drawings for internal additions and renovation of Janj Ghar in Sector 47 will be convened soon.

The Mayor again raised the issue of space earmarked for a shopping centre in Mauli Jagran to be transferred to the Municipal Corporation.

The other issues raised included recarpetting of parking in Sector 38-C market, Dhanas Bridge, widening of road from Sector 39 to Maloya and construction of Sahaj Safai Kendras.

It was pointed out that there is a reserve land in front of Burail village, which should be developed otherwise it would turn into a dumping ground.

The demand for high mast lights in parks and green belts was also raised as the dimly-lit points are prone to theft.

Heading: Cops release accused on bail after court turns down plea - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Forensic Sciences Limited (CFSL), in Sector 36 in Chandigarh, has earned the wrath of the Punjab and Haryana High Court for not accepting court orders for conducting an inquiry into a land acquisition case.

A Division Bench headed by Justice Uma Nath Singh had directed the Registrar of the High Court to send a record pertaining to signatures of a few villagers from Haryana to CFSL.

The inquiry to ascertain as to whether thumb impressions of the villagers, which are alleged to be fake, were old or fresh. Justice Uma Nath passed the order and the record was to be sent to the CFSL. Surprisingly, one of the CFSL employee refused to take the record sent by the HC. Not only this, the employees also told the HC officer that the CFSL does not have the mechanism to examine thumb impressions.

When the officer demanded that the same should be given in writing, the employee reportedly refused to give the same.

Irked over this, the High Court summoned the CFSL director. Since he was on leave, the deputy director appeared in court and submitted that he will conduct an inquiry and initiate departmental proceedings against the employee.

The case pertained to a civil litigation in which a few villagers from Haryana, whose land had been acquired by HUDA for the construction of a drain, were allegedly not given compensation. The villagers had moved the High Court.

Heading: Elected Kharar councillors to finally take oath - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed a district court in Mohali to wrap up the ongoing trial proceedings in the infamous murder of QuarkCity engineer Sukhwinderjit Singh preferably within six months.

On Tuesday, the High Court (HC) denied bail to Sukhwinderjit's wife Neki Nalwa, who is one of the main suspects in the case, for the fourth time. Neki, who is lodged in the district jail in Patiala for the past almost three years, was given liberty to approach the HC again for seeking bail, if the trial doesn't end within the stipulated period of six months.

Justice Pritam Pal of the High Court pronounced this order while dismissing an application filed by Neki seeking bail in the murder and Arms Act cases lodged in Mohali on December 5 and 10, 2005.

After arguing the case for some time, the counsel for the petitioner stated that Neki is in custody for the last three years and material witnesses have already been examined in the case. He sought directions to the trial court to conclude the trial at the earliest, to which the counsel for the state raised no objection.

Taking into account the seriousness and gravity of the offence, the High Court Justice ordered to dismiss the bail petition at this stage "as the allegations of hatching out a conspiracy to commit murder are there".

After failing to get bail in three previous applications moved before the Sessions Court and another before the High Court, Neki had recently made another move to secure bail when High Court Justice Mehtab Singh Gill visited during the inspection tour of the Patiala Central Jail.

Treating Neki's hand-written application as a petition under Section 439 of the CrPC for regular bail, the High Court had heard the plea on October 22.

The resumed trial proceedings before the court of Mohali Additional Session Judge S K Garg are in advanced stage with almost 40 of the total 63 witnesses, including the complainant, his father and eyewitnesses, already been examined, while the process is on to examine the remaining witnesses, which mainly include the representatives of concerned banks, mobile phone companies and a

Amritsar resident, whose weapon was allegedly used in the crime.

The next date for hearing before the trial court is fixed for November 6.

Neki and her alleged paramour Himmat Singh Brandy were lodged in jail on charges of the murder and other relevant charges ever since Sukhwinderjit was shot dead when he was taking a stroll with Neki near their residence in Mohali on December 4, 2005.

While Punjab Police had recommended speedy trial in this case by referring it to a fast-track court, the trial proceedings before the Court of Additional Sessions Judge in Ropar had stalled for almost five months following a stay procured by Brandy from the Supreme Court on June 29, 2006.

The trial proceedings had resumed after the SC had on November 20, 2006, dismissed "as withdrawn" Brandy's Special Leave Petition (SLP), wherein he had sought a stay on the trial proceedings at Ropar Additional Session Judge's court. After a district court was set up in Mohali, the resumed trial proceedings were shifted here.

Recently, Sukhwinderjit's younger brother, Gurvinderjit Singh, who is the complainant in the case, had alleged threat from Brandy and demanded security.

Heading: QuarkCity engineer’s murder: conclude trial within six months, HC orders lower court - Indian Express
Content:
The long wait for the newly-elected 15 councillors of Kharar Municipal Council (MC) to take oath and charge of their new office seems to be over. Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who is also the convenor, has issued notices to all 15 municipal councillors and Kharar MLA Balbir Sidhu for the oath-taking ceremony to be held on Thursday at the MC office.

According to law provisions, the first meeting for the elected municipal councillors should be called within 14 days of notification of the election. But in this regard, the meeting will take place 53 days after municipal councillors were elected on September 14.

Earlier, the MC meeting was called on October 13, but it was postponed due to the "illness" of the SDM.

Meanwhile, the lobbying has once again intensified for capturing the coveted posts of president and vice-presidents of the Kharar MC.

While the ruling SAD-BJP combine, which had made a clean sweep by winning 10 of the 15 seats in the MC elections, is making all efforts to wrest control over the civic body. The Congress, which had won only 2 seats, is claiming the support of 3 independents and three from the SAD-BJP combine to form the United Front with majority of eight councillors, besides Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu, who being ex-officio member, has voting rights in the MC.

However, to come over the dissent in the ruling group and in a bid to reunite the "splintered or rebel" councillors, Punjab Cooperation Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh today held a meeting with 12 councillors.

Sources said that after detailed discussions, Captain Kanwaljit deferred the decision on the MC presidential candidate for Thursday morning, when he has again called a meeting of all municipal councillors, barring two from the Congress.

Sources said the independent candidates and rebel SAD-BJP councillors made it clear that they will support the ruling alliance, only if their choice of presidential candidate is accepted.

Heading: Housing society fined for not transferring flat - Indian Express
Content:
Panchkula gangrape: Police take u-turn, DSP says no girl brought to police station

In a major twist to the Panchkula gangrape case, a minor girl, allegedly involved in the crime, was brought to the city by the police for questioning on Tuesday. The accused is reportedly the daughter of a Mohali-based property dealer.

Later in the day, the police took a complete U-turn claiming that the victim did not identify any girl. DSP Ram Chander Rathi said: "Which girl are you taking about? No girl was brought to the police station today."

According to the 17-year-old victim's statement, the girl was her classmate in school and had introduced her to the two main accused, Jatin and Chhavi. "She was also involved in the making of my pornographic CD a year ago after which the accused youths started blackmailing me," said the victim. She added that the accused's name also is also mentioned in her statement recorded before the magistrate under Section 164 of the CrPC.

Meanwhile, the victim was made to wait outside the DSP (Headquarters) Office in Sector 1, Panchkula, for over two hours on Tuesday. DSP Rajesh Kalia had called the victim and her mother after their application demanding a CBI probe was forwarded to the district police but left without meeting them.

Talking to Newsline, DSP (Headquarters) Rajesh Kalia said: "We have received the victim's application forwarded by the DGP's office and it has been sent to the police station concerned. Also, today we were busy preparing for an important meeting on computerisation."

Heading: Ex-Dell employee to get Rs 25,000 from Citibank - Indian Express
Content:
Finding gross deficiency in its functioning, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the Industrial Cooperative Group Housing Society in Sector 51 to pay Rs 3.5 lakh as compensation. The society has been fined for causing grave mental harassment to a complainant after he was not allotted a flat despite a will favouring him.

The amount awarded as compensation includes Rs 50,000 as damages to be paid by the president of the society, Tejinder Singh, and a refund of Rs 94,740 wrongly charged as interest. Rs 5,500 have to be paid as the cost of litigation.

The complainant, Rajinder Singh, a resident of Sector 22, has stated that a shareholder in the society, Sudhir Kumar Jain, has executed a will and a sale agreement in 2002 in his (the complainant's) favour. The attesting witness to all the documents was Tejinder Singh, president of the society.

After the execution of the Will and the sale agreement dated December 3, 2002, Rajinder Singh paid the installments to the society on behalf of Jain. A letter was also issued that Jain had deposited Rs 1.75 lakh with the society and a further sum of Rs 1.5 lakh on account of cost of construction was deposited by Rajinder Singh.

After Jain died in 2004, the complainant requested the society to transfer the flat in his name. However, the society did not accede to his request owing to extraneous considerations, alleged Rajinder Singh. A cheque deposited by the complainant was rejected citing that he was not entitled to the flat, which had been transferred in the name of the nominee — Sudha Jain, wife of Sudhir Kumar Jain.

Then, Rajinder Singh approached the Assistant Registrar, Cooperative Societies, and a public notice was issued to the society. Only then, three years after the original owner's death, was the flat transferred in his name.

In its reply, the society pleaded that all payments were made in the name of Jain. "Anyone can deposit amounts on behalf of members, but that does not mean that the depositor is entitled for allotment of a flat. Flats of the society are not transferable before five years from the date of allotment as per Clause 6 of the Chandigarh Allotment of Land to Cooperative House Building Societies Scheme, 1991. In a death case, share is transferred in accordance with the provisions of Section 21 of the Punjab Cooperative Societies Act, 1961, as applicable to UT Chandigarh," stated the counsel.

The forum observed that that the complainant had been deprived of the flat for three years and lost a huge sum towards rent and granted him compensation.

Heading: Advocate to cough up Rs 20,000 for not filing case - Indian Express
Content:
Holding Citibank responsible for causing mental harassment to a former Dell employee after her provident fund was not released due to the bank's negligence, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum directed the bank to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation.

The complainant, Teena Goel, stated that she was employed with Dell International Services from July 2005 till March 2006. Every month, Rs 597 was deducted from her salary as provident fund. At the time of leaving the job, Goel filled all the requisite documents for the refund of her PF and was informed that the amount will be refunded within the next two months to her salary account in Citibank.

After the period expired, the complainant wrote to the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner who confirmed that the said amount was sent to her bankers through cheques. But when Goel checked her account, no amount had been credited. In its reply, Citibank said letters had been sent to the complainant requesting her to submit the requisite documents but they did not receive a response. Consequently, her account was closed.

The forum found that two cheques (Rs 6,334 and Rs 3,162) were issued in the name of the complainant to Citibank. On the other hand, the bank could not provide a courier receipt to suggest if a letter was sent by the bank.

"In any case, it was necessary for the bank to inform the complainant before closing her account. The complainant had to wait for her dues for over a year and write several e-mails to the authorities concerned. The bank was, therefore, careless and negligence in rendering proper service to the complainant," ruled president of the district forum, Jagroop Singh Mahal.

Heading: CHB razes 50 buildings in Sec 47 - Indian Express
Content: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed an advocate to refund Rs 10,000, taken as fee from a complainant for filing a petition which was never filed. Advocate Narinder Kumar Saneja has also been directed to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for harassment. The complainant, R K Goel, had approached Saneja in connection with a case booked by the Jagadhri police against his son Ajay Goel. Saneja informed him that the case was not under the jurisdiction of the Jagadhri District Court and advised him to file a Writ Petition in the High Court over the jurisdiction issue, for which a fee of Rs 10,000 was settled. Later, the complainant discovered that the case was indeed under the jurisdiction of the Jagadhri District Court. He asked for his money back from the advocate as the petition to be filed was of no use. But Saneja refused to refund the amount. In his reply, the advocate claimed a fee of Rs 20,000 had been settled upon and the balance (Rs 10,000) had not been paid. Also, the complaint was first filed with the Bar Council of India and the appeal is pending there, he added. The forum said: "Whether the advocate is entitled to retain the fee is a moot question as he did not perform the duty for which the fee was meant. By not refunding the amount promptly, he caused mental and physical harassment to the complainant and forced him to approach the forum."

Heading: Leopard skin seized from Himachal resident - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 50 illegal structures were demolished by the Chandigarh Housing Board in Sector 47 on Tuesday. Around 30 structures on government land were razed, about eight were newly constructed and ten others were removed.

The residents of Sector 47 pelted stones on the bulldozer of the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB), which was pressed into service to demolish the illegal structures constructed by them. But the police personnel deployed brought the situation under control.

The residents, while protesting against the anti-encroachment drive, deflated its tyres and snatched away the keys of the bulldozer. They protested for about 10 minutes.

DSP (south) J S Khaira said they had deployed enough police personnel to keep the situation under control. The woman police were also deployed to control women protesters.

"There were a few residents who pelted stones on the machine when it was bringing down an illegal structure. Nobody was injured. There was a minor incident of stone pelting. Only the windshield of the machine was broken," he said.

Police have arrested one resident, Maninder Singh of 2779/2, after a section officer section officer lodged a complaint with the CHB for creating disturbances while government officials were on duty.

Housing Board secretary Kamlesh Kumar was present on the spot as the duty magistrate

Talking to Newsline CHB secretary Kamlesh Kumar said: "None of the buildings confining to the norms were demolished. Only those constructions and buildings, violating the norms, were pulled down."

More such anti-encroachment drives are to be conducted next week in Sectors 38, 39, 41, 44, he added.

Heading: Hamish marshals Bengal Tigers’ win - Indian Express
Content:
A resident of Mandi in Himachal Pradesh, who was arrested on Monday night for possessing a leopard skin, was remanded in police custody for three days on Tuesday. Kaneshwar Singh claimed he had bought the skin from a poacher.

Deputy Superintendent of Police Jagbir Singh said the accused was trying to smuggle the skin into city. "On a tip-off, we set up a checkpost neat the IT park roundabout and arrested the accused. The skin is valued at around Rs 2.5 lakh," he added.

Kaneshwar, working as a salesman at a liquor vend in Sector 7, said he had bought the skin from Surinder Verma, a hunter, in Theog near Shimla for Rs 5,000. "I had come to city to sell it and was looking for buyers," he said.

Wildlife officials said the skin was of a young male leopard aged around three years. The length of the leopard was 7 feet and was estimated to have died around two years ago. DSP Singh added: "There was no bullet or stab wound. It seems the animal was either trapped and strangulated or poisoned."

Heading: 16 junior Indian golfers to attend camp in Scotland - Indian Express
Content:
An Unbeaten hurricane knock of 80 runs off 54 balls by Hamish Marshall saw Royal Bengal Tigers maul Chennai Superstars by nine wickets in the Indian Cricket League Twenty20 Tournament being played at Tau Devi Lal Stadium on Tuesday.

The New Zealander opened the Bengal Tigers' innings with Deep Dasgupta and the duo was involved in a century partnership (132 runs) for the first wicket. Dasgupta played a breezy knock of 54 runs off 46 balls with the help of four boundaries and two towering sixes. However, it was Hamish Marshall who dominated the bowlers right from the word go and played some scintillating strokes all over the ground. His unbeaten innings contained eight boundaries and three mighty sixes. Skipper McMillan joined Hamish at the fall of Dasgupta and the duo steered Tigers towards win with five balls remaining.

Earlier, Chennai Superstars made 161 in 19.5 overs. Andre Adams struck in the second over to remove Chennai Superstars' Hemanth Kumar when the team score was on 12. However, Vignesh didn't curb his attacking game as he smashed 22 runs off 13 balls before lofting a catch to Rohan Gavaskar off Adams. A disciplined bowling performance by Bengal bowlers saw the Superstars score run-a-ball. After the dismissal of Russel Arnold and Jesuraj, R Satish walked in and produced some fire-works with a blistering knock of 50 runs off just 25 balls. He smashed 22 runs off Upul Chandana's in the thirteenth over to get the Chennai side right back in the game. His knock contained five boundaries and three towering sixes. Giving him company at the other side was Hemant Badani who scored his third ICL fifty off 40 balls in the 18th over. Just when it looked that Chennai were heading towards a mammoth total, Upul Chandana scalped three wickets for just one run in the 19th over to bounce back into the game. Chandana took four wickets for 38 runs while Eklak Ahmid took three wickets for 21 runs.

Brief Scores:

Chennai Superstars: 161 all out in 19.5 overs (H Badani 55, R Sathish 50, G Vignesh 22, U Chandana 4 for 38, Eklak Ahmid 3 for 21) lost to Royal Bengal Tigers: 162 for 1 in 19.1 overs (H Marshall 80 no, D Dasgupta 54, C McMillan 21 no, Shabbir Ahmed 1 for 33).

Sidelights

Age gap hard to fill

Meanwhile, after losing six of their seven games, Rajesh Chauhan, assistant coach, Mumbai Champs reasoned that it was the age-gap between the players that is hindering players to gel well. The international players are more than 20-years senior to the local players

Tea or Coffee?

As the night got colder it was time for the spectators for a hot cup of tea or to warm up their bodies. The attendants at the coffee shop were kept pretty busy by the customers. With the mercury dipping down with each passing day, it seems that tea and coffee will be call of the day

Another entertainment

Just when the Chennai batsmen failed to entertain during the initial overs it was left to the audience to look for some other form of entertainment. Soon, paper planes started to hover over the stands.

Heading: Harmanpreet anchors St Stephen’s win - Indian Express
Content: Sixteen junior golfers from India will get a lifetime opportunity to learn the tricks of the trade from PGA qualified instructors in a six-day programme being organised at the prestigious St Andrews Links Academy in Scotland from June 20 next year. Apart from providing seven nights accommodation at The University of St Andrews halls of residence and meals, lessons in individual full swing and short game analysis using the latest coaching software technology, an e-coaching account, visit to The British Golf Museum, and an evening with a world renowned Golf Historian, the participants of the camp will also get a confirmed tee-off time on the prestigious 'The Old Course'.

Heading: Basketball tourney from today - Indian Express
Content:
Led by an all-round performance from skipper Harmanpreet Singh (81 runs and 3 for 19) helped St Stephen's School, Sector 45 blank Saupin's School, Sector 26 by 146 runs in the inaugural match of the fifth Molly Carver Cricket Cup for High Schools held at the St Stephen's School ground on Tuesday.

Harmanpreet elected to bat first after winning the toss and the decision proved fruitful as St Stephen's batsmen piled on runs and made 254 runs for the loss of six wickets in 30 overs. The openers Harmanpreet and Guraunak put the foundation for the big total as they put on 79 runs for the first wicket. Harmanpreet was in good nick as he hit six boundaries and four towering sixes during his knock. Guraunak's knock of 38 runs included two boundaries and two huge sixes. Karan Partap Singh bagged two wickets for Saupin's School.

In reply, Saupin's School were skittled out for just 108 runs in 24.5 overs. Anupam Saini top scored with 32 runs while Karan Partap chipped in with a useful knock of 26 runs. Left hand spinner (3 for 19) and medium pacer Talwinderjeet Singh (3 for 22) rocked Saupin's School batting with their accurate bowling.

Brief Scores:

St Stephen's-45: 254 for 6 in 30 overs (Harmanpreet 81, Guraunak 38, Japreet Singh 37 no, Karan Partap 2 for 46, Anupam Saini 1 for 45); Saupin's School-32: 108 all out in 24.5 overs (Anupam Saini 32, Karan Partap 26, Talwinderjeet Singh 3 for 22, Harmanpreet 3 for 19, Abhilash Sharma 2 for 18).

Heading: Kamal and Patel score upset wins - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Agricultural University today entered into an agreement with Mechanical Engineering Research and Development Organization (Merado), Ludhiana, an extension centre of the Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute, Durgapur, to collaborate on projects for design and development of farm machinery. An MoU to this effect was signed by the Dr. P.S.Minhas, director of research, PAU and Cdr V R Dahake, scientist-incharge of Merado.

Terming the event as a historic one, PAU V-C Dr Manjit Singh Kang, said thate he hoped that the partnership will greatly help Punjab's farmers in the long run.

Cdr Dahake said that with the signing of the MoU, the scientists of the two organizations would work jointly in the area of farm power and machinery.

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) will sponsor various research projects on development of farm machinery under this alliance, said Dr I S Dhaliwal, head, department of farm power and machinery at PAU.

Heading: National Forest Games from Dec 3 - Indian Express
Content:
Kamal Kishore Maderana, a trainee of Chandigarh Lawn Tennis Association, kept his winning spree by upsetting eighth seed S K Mukund in the Asian Juniors ATF Tennis Circuit at the Sector 10 Tennis Stadium here on Tuesday.

The second round-match was extended to three sets before Maderana from Rajasthan emerged winner. Kamal Maderana lost the first set at 4-6. However, he bounced back into the game by winning the second set before huffing a puffing at 7-6 (5) in tie-breaker. Kamal, who is a qualifier, gave a consistent display to end the challenge of Mukund who is ranked 113 in Asian Tennis Federation Order of Merit list, by 6-4. Wild card Atul Sri Patel also registered a mild upset as he stunned seventh seed and 123rd ranked in ATF AK Paradh Saradhi in straight sets 6-1, 7-5. Patel's next rival will be top seed Vishal Passi who ended the challenge of Jatinder Singh in straight sets 6-1, 6-3.

Local lad and third seed Digvijay Singh Naruka has so far justified his seeding as he defeated qualifier Ketan Tayal in straight sets 6-2, 6-1. Another local player and fourth seed Nischay Rawal had no difficulty in advancing to the next round as outplayed lucky Loser Dhruv Goel 6-0, 6-1. Second seed and wild card Nguyen Hoang Thien, the only foreign entry left in the boys' singles' category, moved into quarter-final by ousting Manish Kumar in straight sets 6-0, 6-1.

In the girls' singles' second round, qualifier Kavya Bharat shocked fourth seed and local player Bhavika Wadhawan 6-3, 6-4 on her way to quarter-final. Top seed Tarrannum Handa maintained her top form as she scored an effortless win over wild card Rajbir Kaur in straight sets 6-1, 6-4. Tarrannum is now pitted against fifth seed and wild card Rimpledeep Kaur who ousted Anushka Rajkumar 6-1, 6-1. Second seed Tamhita Nguyen of Philippines also had an easy round as she beat Roma Chandiran in straight sets 6-2, 6-0.
