Mukund 4-6, 7-6 (5), 6-4, Himanshu Sagar bt Aamirsohra M M 6-4, 6-0, Digvijay Singh Naruka bt Ketan Tayal 6-2, 6-1, Bhavtaranpreet Singh bt Dheer Anush Bhatti 6-4, 6-1, Nguyen Hoagan Thien (Viet) bt Manish Kumar 6-0, 6-1.

Heading: DAV College lifts overall title - Indian Express
Content:
The 17th National Forest Games being hosted by Punjab Forest Department will be held at Panjab University grounds from December 3 to December 7.

Announcing this in a press conference, Tikshan Sood, Forest Minister, Punjab said more than 2000 participants from forest departments all over India will take pat in the games.

The minister also informed that the Games were likely to be inaugurated by the Hon'ble CM Punjab in the Panjab University campus in the presence of many eminent personalities including Central and State Ministers and other distinguished persons from different walks of life.

As many as 121 events would be held in various sports and games disciplines including athletics, cricket, volleyball, hockey, football, basketball, weight and power lifting, badminton, tennis, table tennis, carom, golf, billiards, snooker, bridge, rifle shooting, swimming and kabaddi. The opening ceremony will consist of performances by military motorcyclists, tableaus, fireworks and other displays. In order to ensure proper coordination between the host State of Punjab and the 41 participating States / Forestry institutions, meetings with the nodal officers of the contingents will be held regularly

The minister also released the mascot 'Ena' which is the state animal of Punjab for the games.

Heading: For Daddy, with love - Indian Express
Content:
DAV College, Sector 10 claimed the overall team championship title in men's category with 81 points on the concluding day of the Panjab University Annual Athletics Meet being held at Panjab University grounds.

SGGS College, Sector 26 claimed the second spot with 76.5 points in the same category while JC DAV College, Dasuya grabbed the third spot with 15 points.

In the women's team championship, SGGS Khalsa College, Mahilpur emerged as the winners with 39 points while Khalsa College for Women, Ludhiana grabbed the second spot with 37 points. Guru Nanak Girls College, Ludhiana claimed the third spot with 26 points. Ravinder of DAV College, Chandigarh was declared as the best athlete in the men's category while Navjoban Kaur was declared the best athlete in women's category.

Earlier in the day, Ravinder claimed the gold medal in men's half marathon while Sukhdev Singh of DAV College, Chandigarh claimed the silver medal. Avtar Singh of SGGS College, Chandigarh grabbed the bronze medal. In javelin throw, Bhupinder Singh of SGGS College, Chandigarh claimed the gold medal with a throw of 65.15 meters while Hardeep Singh of GHG Khalsa College, Gurusar Sadhar grabbed the silver medal with a throw of 56.99 meters. Rohit of DAV College, Abohar claimed the bronze medal with a throw of 56.27 meters. In triple jump, Navjot Singh of DAV College, Chandigarh won the gold medal creating a new record with a jump of 15.29 meters. Manoj Kumar of SGGS College, Chandigarh grabbed the silver medal with a jump of 15.25 meters while Harvinder Singh of Panjab University Campus grabbed the bronze medal with a jump of 14.29 meters. In the women's category, Navjoban kaur of GTB Khalsa College for Women, Dasuya claimed the gold medal while Rajdeep kaur of SGGS College, Mahilpur claimed the silver medal. Kulwinder Kaur of SGGS College, Mahilpur grabbed the bronze medal.

In triple jump, Satwant Kaur of SGGS Khalsa College, Mahilpur claimed the gold medal with a jump of 10.70 meters while Shiksha of MCM DAV College, Chandigarh grabbed the silver medal with a jump of 10.15 meters. Talwinder of GGS College, Chandigarh grabbed the bronze medal with a jump of 9.97 meters.

Heading: into the light - Indian Express
Content:
Bindi Irwin pays a tribute to her legendary 'crocodile hunter' father in Animal Planet's one-hour special

For someone who lived his life surrounded by nature and a camera crew, this seems like a perfect tribute. Animal Planet, the entertainment brand dedicated to the unique relationship between people and animals brings a special show, 'My Daddy the Crocodile Hunter' hosted by Bindi Irwin, who is carrying on the legacy of her father - famed naturalist Steve Irwin, better known as The Crocodile Hunter who died in 2006. Ten-year-old Bindi Irwin will host an hour-long programme which will take viewers behind the scenes, on a very personal and private look at what it was like growing up with her famous dad. The show is interspersed with rare home movies of Bindi's birth, her early childhood and behind the scenes on-location shots of some of Steve Irwin's most exciting television shows and movies. "Besides capturing the father-daughter relationship, the show portrays Steve Irwin's vision, dedication and care for wildlife," spoke Rahul Johri, SVP & General Manager, India, Discovery Networks Asia-Pacific.

In this show, Bindi also shares anecdotes about how her dad taught her everything she needed to know about wildlife including never-seen-before footage of one of Steve's last crocodile research adventure in August 2006. This also saw Bindi assisting in some of the most amazing crocodile captures and wildlife experiences in the Australian outback. Bindi, who has grown up surrounded by animals, lives on the grounds of the Australia Zoo that Steve Irwin's family founded in Queensland. She is fast following in her parents' footsteps as an ardent animal and nature lover.

'My Daddy the Crocodile Hunter' will air on Animal Planet on Sunday, November 9 at 8pm.

Heading: Quick Check - Indian Express
Content:
A colourful peep into the mysterious, through the light of an artist's mind

They feel closest to the wanderer instinct in them, always on the move, hardly resting and always exploring. That's why this group of six artist friends calls themselves Bedouin. In their painting exhibition these Kolkata-based artists bring their visions of the world, each in his own distinct way.

The group has been brought to the city by sculptor P S Sawhney whose work is also on display. Malay Datta explores religion through mythology and spirituality. Devi's portraits show her in a subtle mood with Ganesha and her flowing hair play well against the trishul and flute. Lord Krishna's eyes show his innocence coupled with quest. It's Budhha's search for peace that stays with you. His body is like an old wall, cracked and fighting to keep the bricks of life together. Sarkar Bhowmick's imagination takes him into the woods, bright, red and warm with light and knowledge. The landscapes bare the veins of the earth. Tapan Karmakar attempts to bring alive the cultures and characters that are getting lost in modernity. And he ventures into different regions of the country - be it the tribal tiger dance of Orissa, Bengal's baul singer, horse riders of Rajasthan, folk singers that tell timeless tales, and monkey players.

Dipak Ghosh's canvas is a haven for tribal faces of India. A woman looks at herself in the mirror, a Christ like figure plays a musical instrument for a family of birds, Ghosh's subjects have a characteristic form. Tribals become the protagonists of Indrajit Ghosh's canvas as well. Painted in earthy colours one sees their lives, their relations, their jewels. Dino Nath Saha's geometric style presents a semi realistic view of life as he sees it, the masks one changes every day, the targets one builds to achieve.

On at Museum of Fine Arts, Panjab University, till November 8 from 10am to 5 pm.

Heading: Balle Baliye! - Indian Express
Content: Brainstorming came to its best when DAV College, Sector 10 played host to Satkal-CLA inter-college quiz contest. A total of six teams from different colleges participated juggling their memories for answers on questions related to science, art and literature, sports, business, music et al. And supporting the contestants were a eager audience who did get its share of chocolates for the correct answers. Prof Kushal Shante played the perfect quiz master giving quotable quotes like, "It's a difficult question but it's easy if you know it!" He had the teams guessing Harry Potter's middle name, BMW's full name, the name of the bank that fell due to recession and has the name of an animal in its name, the chess player who commented 'that hairy ape' referring to a competitor. At the end of the session of interesting questions the quiz ended in a tie but Dalbir Singh and Manmeet of Dr HSJ Institute of Dental Sciences and Hospital were awarded first prize as per the written score. Bracketed first was Government College for Girls, Sector 42 represented by Nidhi and Gunja. DAV college, Sector 10's Gurinderpal and Akshay were second. Punjab University campus was third represented by Arastu Chopra and Himanshu. "It is essential that we keep ourselves updated," remarked guest of honour Vipin Pubby, Resident Editor applauding CLA's role in organising events to help students excel in their capacity. Harinderjit Kaur, former Mayor also encouraged the students and urged them to contribute back to the society.

Heading: Green Gyan - Indian Express
Content:
City couple Savita and Jaspal Bhatti win gushing compliments on Nach Baliye 4

They are doing us proud. Well-known comedian from the city Jaspal Bhatti and his wife Savita who are one of the participating couples on Nach Baliye's Season Four are putting their best steps forward. And at a time when most of the couples on the dance reality show are complaining of injuries, Mr and Mrs Bhatti put up a fun-filled performance. Savita was dressed as a junior Sardar and introduced herself as Chhotu Ustaad, an apprentice to Jaspal Bhatti! The two danced with enthusiasm despite being one of the oldest couples on the show. And it all went down well with the judges. In fact, so impressed was Arjun Rampal that he called them the "fittest" on the dance floor. The model-actor has also promised Jaspal Bhatti training sessions including sharing his diet plan with the couple. Way to go!

Heading: Party Circuit - Indian Express
Content:
Get an overview of landscape designs

That Chandigarh is known as the green city is no news. But that the city is increasingly witnessing a large number of foreign architects flocking here to study its green landscape courtesy Le Corbusier, is news. Mapping the calendars this time round is the first of its kind international conference on 'Emerging Trends in Landscape Architecture'. To be held on November 9 at the Government Museum and Art Gallery Auditorium, Sector 10, "It is being organized by the Saakaar Foundation, an architectural organisation, in association with UNESCO, Swiss Arts Council, Archi Design Perspective, and Foundation for Architectural and Environmental Awareness," architect, author and the brain behind the project Sarbjit Bahga, tells us.

Eminent landscape architects from Switzerland, Turkey and the country are expected for the conference. "Salman Khurshid, former minister of State for External Affairs and a senior Congress leader will be the chief guest," adds Bagha. While HS Johl, President, Environment Society Punjab, will open the conference, Sudhir Sarup, editor, Archi Design Perspective and Dr SS Bhatti, former principal, Chandigarh College of Architecture, will also speak on the occasion. "Amongst the international speakers we will have Prof Günther Vogt, Practicing Landscape Architect of Switzerland, who will give an audio-visual presentation on 'European Landscape Architecture' and Dr Mustafa Var, Professor at Karadeniz Technical University at Turkey, who will talk about 'Urban Transformation Implementation', along with Andy Schonholzer from Switzerland," says Bagha.

Here, the landscape structure as pattern for a project, will also be deliberated upon along with age old dilemma of cities, open spaces and modernity. For more, visit the venue at 10:00 am on November 9. Don't be late!

Heading: sole interest - Indian Express
Content:
The city was party mode as folks flocked to Golf Club for the inauguration of the new bar and then, to Kirpal Singh of Gurudev Studio's exclusive party for the ICL players. The cricketers got a chance to let their hair down and enjoy interactions with other players and the local people. It was evening of smiles among music. Incidentally, Kirpal Singh's son Harpreet Singh is also an ICL player.

Remember we mentioned to you the other day that the Formal Bar at the Chandigarh Golf Club has got a facelift. To celebrate the re-launch and to get the members to check it inside out, the Club threw a formal bash on Monday evening. The party kicked off early on with the Club's president D S Bains formally inaugurate the bar. "Our next project is to renovate the gazebo," said Bains. Making it a perfect evening was Jacob and his band that kept everyone on the floor. Among those we spotted were R S Mann, Gen (retd) Himmat Gill, Gen (retd) Deepinder Singh, Bikramjit Singh, Brig (retd) J S Phoolka and Milkha Singh.

Heading: For art’s sake - Indian Express
Content:
Cute-meets-chic, practical-meets-pretty shoes this season that also brings with it a rainbow of colours!

The first time I saw them, it felt silly to wear them. That was until I slipped and let my feet into a pair of shiny purple patent shoes. Suddenly, the colour aubergine (read baingan!) didn't feel so uggh after all. Actually, they looked very chic, very fresh-off-the-ramp. "The colour is a hot-stepper internationally," spoke Shoe Rack's immaculately turned out merchandiser Kamal Singh as she listed out the glitzy options that went from blood-red to crocodile green at their Sector 8 store! Suddenly, black and brown seemed like staid choices. And that's been the case all of this season. Purple shoes, yellow pumps, peep toes, zip-up boots...there's enough and more to help you step out in style. "It's a colourful affair all the way. It's no longer about making do with black heels that will go with any dress. It is about matching your toes with your totes," city's own runway model Aanchal Kumar offers a style guide. When it comes to footnotes, Kumar puts the emphasis on patent. "There's a lot of gloss now and the bling effect has shifted from your outfit to your bag and shoes," she makes a point.

A quick recce of the burgeoning shoe stores in the city and we are convinced it's a full rainbow out there with no one particular style having a leg up, literally. "Yes, colours are really at play. I never thought yellow or blood red would sell in the city but I have been proven wrong. In fact three colours in one is a bestseller," tells Mohinder Singh Makkar, CEO, Makson Retailers who has brands like Momak (Sector 22) under his belt. Supplying to European stores, Makkar sure has an edge when it comes to shoe trends. And if you are thinking of flaunting your stilettos this season, Makkar doesn't think it's a really good idea. "The latest buzz are cone or kulfi heels. These are taller but broader making it a comfortable affair," he says. The peep toes and ballerinas are safe bets though.

"There were times when all one saw was heels but flats are now really popular and it doesn't have anything to do with height," mentions Ravijit Dhillon of '5 Knot 3' that's got on its racks a range of lie-lows in vibrant tones. As far as embellishments go, all that goes into your designer wardrobe is on your shoe too. Buckles, sequins, bows, satin ribbons, lace, stones...your shoe's equally well-dressed! Specially when it comes to wedding wear. "Dabka work is much in vogue along with sequins and stones," adds Makkar. Hop over to Sector 17 and the trends are for all to see in the back-to-back shoe stores. At Drishti we caught peep toes and ballerinas in all "shade card" colours. Black turns ash grey, brown goes copper, red is plum...you get the drift, right?

Heading: Portrait of an artist - Indian Express
Content:
Eight budding artists receive scholarships from Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi

It was a special moment and for most of the young artists an overwhelming one at that. Budding sculptors, painters and a caricature artist, eight talented students of the Government College of Art were selected for scholarships by the Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi, a novel endeavour. Selected by a panel of senior artists, the students will receive a monthly stipend of Rs 2,000 which has been sponsored by city-based companies. "Many of them are personal friends and were gracious and generous. We're setting a trend, one that will give many artists encouragement, promote research and quest for excellence in their fields. The choice was tough, but we found artists who are enthusiastic, energetic, have fresh ideas and have already done impressive work,'' Diwan Manna introduces the artists and adds that the scholarships are being named after eminent personalities like Amrita Sher-Gill, Tagore, Dr MS Randhawa, Le Corbusier...The amount agrees Diwan is not huge, but yes, it's a great start, "and a wonderful way to encourage us to work harder for it's a way of supporting us to see and research more, travel to exhibitions and even frame our work, which is also tough to do with our limited resources. These scholarships will set standards and aspire us for better work,'' Aishwarya Sultania, a painter is looking ahead.

For Ritu Raj Singh the fellowship's come at a good time, as his father retired this month, "and that means a little less burden on him.'' Amrit Pal Singh is a brilliant caricature artist, who believes you don't need words to support a caricature and agrees it's an off-beat field, which has a fantastic future, "Humour is close to my heart and I'm looking forward to some original work,'' says Singh. Get creative...

Heading: Save Rajasansi voices get louder - Indian Express
Content:
The lesser-known years of MF Husain is what the play Pencil Sey Brush Tak brings on stage

Ninety-three years of sheer genius and creativity is tough to envelop in a three-hour play, agrees Nadira Babbar here with Pencil Sey Brush Tak, a play based on MF Husain's memoir. The many unknown facets of the painter is what the director has strived to stage in the play, which is being organized by STEPS. "His struggles, growing up years, his Maharashtrian upbringing, relationships, especially the influence of his grandfather, there was so much to be explored,'' Nadira has known the painter since she was a child, as he would visit her parents' home often and was almost a family member. With a deep-rooted philosophy, the play charts how he was brought up in a home where all cultures and religions were respected and followed and how a painter from a small village rises above prejudices and with his art strives to bring harmony in diversity. "His series of paintings on Ramayana, Ganesha, history of Gulf countries are all brilliant pieces of art,'' Nadira has focused totally on the person, with Anup Soni playing Husain in his early 20s and Tom Alter in the role of senior Maqbool. "I completely depended on the text to shape my performance and the script conveys a lot, for not many know him how he was in that age,'' smiles Soni.

Juhi Babbar is in the role of Husain's wife and is thoroughly enjoying the experience, "I blindly trust my director with the roles she chooses with me and am happy doing theatre, as I'm not willing to struggle for Hindi film roles,'' Juhi is candid and says after her huge and successful Punjabi film, no other offer has come close to it.

"His grace, secular approach, art, and contribution to this country is what I have emphasised on and it's been a fulfilling experience,'' Nadira invites to see the life, time and work of MF Husain at Tagore Theatre on November 5 at 7 pm.

Heading: PUSA-1121 a money-spinner - Indian Express
Content:
JOINING FORCES: Travel agents protest; BJP to lead agitation today; Majithia asks leaders to rise above party politics to bail out the airport

Exporters, travel agents and businessmen today staged a massive protest against various airlines calling off their operations from the Rajasansi International Airport.

They submitted a memorandum to CM Parkash Singh Badal through the Deputy Commissioner's office, asking him to take up the matter immediately with the Centre to bail out the airport.

The issue also attained political colour, as a day after Majha leaders submitted their memorandum to the CM, the BJP declared that it would hold a protest at the airport tomorrow.

Hundreds of party workers are being mobilised to make the protest a major show, which is being led by BJP MP Navjot Singh Sidhu, who has held the UPA government responsible for the "early demise" of the airport, which was emerging as the backbone for region's economy.

Cabinet minister Bikram Singh Majithia, meanwhile, issued a strong statement, saying that parties should restrain from "politicising" the issue. He said leaders should sink their differences and work together to keep the holy city of Amritsar on international tourist circuit by saving Rajasansi Airport from pushing into oblivion.

Majithia, who had taken a team of MLAs from the region to the CM yesterday, said, "Every political party should join hands to convince the Centre to make flights from Amritsar viable for airlines. This is necessary to decongest the Delhi airport."

Traders and Industries' Association (TIA) (Border Zone) president Rajinder Singh Marwah said border areas have been adversely affected in the past due to terrorism and wars with Pakistan, but the airport gave some hope, which was now being dashed. "At present, only two airlines are suspending operations, but in future more will follow suit," said Marwaha.

Asserting that the airport and the Attari border were the only means of reviving the economic activities in the area, Majithia said the new trade routes had sent positive signal to the investors, international hotel chains and NRI pilgrims. "The area will suffer if the flights are suspended, as Indo-Pak trade through Attari is already witnessing a slump," he said, adding that PM Dr Manmohan Singh, who hails from the city, should take interest in developing the city as a hub of trading with west Asia.

He said the state government was doing its best to press upon the Centre to charge international travelling rates for domestic flights. "The Punjab government should also take up the matter with the Union Civil Aviation Ministry to computerise the cargo handling system at Rajasansi to encourage exports," he said.

Sidhu said he would not sit silent till the Centre intervened and his party would organise a rally to expose the UPA government's "discrimination" with the region.

Amritsar Vikas Manch, a local NGO, has also shot off letters to the PM and the Civil Aviation Ministry to ensure efficient use of funds for expansion project and pressing the airlines to continue services.

Sukhbir never flew from Rajasansi: MLA

Amid concerns raised by various political leaders over the reduction of flights from Amritsar's Rajasansi International Airport, Congress MLA from Kila Raipur Jassi Khangura accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of failing to lead by example when it comes to patronising the airport. In a letter to Sukhbir Badal, he said Punjab's aviation policy was in tatters. Khangura alleged that during the reign of the SAD-BJP, Sukhbir has not taken a single international flight from Amritsar, and preferred Delhi and other metros.

He said, "Notwithstanding claims to promote the interests of Punjab, the failure of the SAD president to fly from Amritsar shows Mohali and Bathinda are closest to his heart." The Congress MLA also claimed that not a single development initiative arising from SAD chief's numerous overseas visits has matured. "This government piloting the affairs of the state will ensure crash landing of Punjab's economy," he said.

Heading: Roadblock: Elevated project delayed by another 6 months - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after its notification as basmati, the PUSA-1121 has set the cash registers of Punjab farmers ringing.

While on an average this variety fetches Rs 3,000 to Rs 3,300 per quintal in almost all mandis, at Rajpura, it is being sold for Rs 3,500 per quintal. As per the official figures, 5.14 lakh metric tonnes of PUSA-1121 has already made its way into Punjab mandis, which is three times higher than last year.

The variety, which usually found buyers in big mandis, like that of Khanna and Rajpura, is selling like hotcakes even in Ludhiana and Moga. Narinderpal Singh Tiwana, chairman of the marketing committee in Salem Tabri grain market, Ludhiana, said, "Last year, only 26 quintals of PUSA-1121 was purchased, while this year we have already touched the 3,500 quintal mark. Farmers at our mandi are being given Rs 3,230 per quintal."

Ajmer Singh Lakhowal, chairman of the Punjab Mandi Board, says, "This is a long grain variety which is very good for Punjab, as its needs less water. Farmers in Punjab will be motivated to bring more area under this variety."

Manmeet Singh, a farmer from Amritsar who has about 20 acres under PUSA-1121, said, "Our average yield has been around 16 to 18 quintals per acre, which means I will make at least Rs 45,000 to Rs 50,000 per acre. This is almost Rs 10,000 to 15,000 more than the conventional paddy variety." As per figures provided by the State Agriculture Department, out of the total 24 lakh hectares of paddy in Punjab, nearly four lakh falls under basmati varieties.

B S Sidhu, Director, Agriculture, "PUSA-1121 is grown over almost one lakh hectares and great price this year will bring more area under it."

Heading: Bains will head panel to address scribes’ grievances - Indian Express
Content:
The multi-crore Central government-sponsored elevated road project of Amritsar Municipal Corporation, which was aimed at decongesting the city roads leading to the Golden Temple, seems to be a distant dream.

The lack of coordination between different departments to facilitate the ongoing work has being causing the delay. As a result, it will take a few more months before the road can be thrown open to the public.

The slow pace of work has made commuting difficult, causing bottlenecks at peak hours. Mayor Shawet Malik visited the site and pulled up the officials concerned. He also held meetings with various departments involved in the project and urged them to coordinate their working to ensure the work is completed soon.

"The work on laying the slab is in progress and a part of it has already been completed," he said. But the project might take another six months to complete, he added. The project, worth Rs 173 crore, is being undertaken by Gammon India. It was started in 2006 to provide a smooth access way to the devotees visiting the Golden Temple.

Sources said the delay has been caused due to the delay in shifting of high tension overhead wires by the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB), the underground telephone cables and the water supply and sewerage lines. Admitting that the project had been delayed, Executive Engineer of the Municipal Corporation R S Randhawa said the efforts were being made to speed up the work.

"We are trying to undertake several things simultaneously. It is not an easy job and requires disconnecting the power supply and the telephone lines," he said.

Heading: Meltdown hits state, Rs 800-cr citrus FDI in limbo - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today ordered the setting up of state and district-level joint committees of government and media representatives to look into the complaints by and against mediapersons in the state.

These committees would also advise the government on guidelines to be observed for greater media-government interaction and understanding, Chief Minister's media adviser H S Bains said here.

The committees would also keep the Minister for Information and Public Relations apprised of their suggestions and recommendations from time to time. Bains here today said similar committees would be set up at every district headquarter. While Bains would be the chairperson of the state-level committee, deputy commissioners would head the panels in their districts. Bains said the state-level committee would also have Principal Secretary, Department of Home Affairs and Justice, president or secretary general of Chandigarh Press Club, a representative of the organisation of the affected journalist or the aggrieved person and legal experts as members. Similarly, the district-level committees would have District Information Public Relations Officer, an accredited journalist, a representative of the organisation of the affected journalist and a nominee of the Chief Minister as members.

Meanwhile, a delegation of the Punjab and Chandigarh journalists met Badal here today and sought an impartial inquiry into alleged harassment of a private news channel journalist in Jalandhar.

Heading: ‘Maryada violated at Nanded’ - Indian Express
Content:
While India is still debating the impact of global economic crisis on its economy, Punjab is already feeling the heat. Even as its much-hyped public-private partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects are facing delay due to the liquidity crunch, the global meltdown has now hit Punjab's prospects of getting its first foreign direct investment (FDI) in agriculture.

Multi-national venture capital fund company, Cannizaro Holdings, has developed cold feet and is not coming forward to sign a MoU with the Citrus and Agri Juicing Council of Punjab. It was in February this year that a MoU was likely to be inked between the state government and Cannizaro, the biggest-ever foreign investment in agriculture sector in the country, with the firm expecting to invest a whopping Rs 800 crore.

Despite months of negotiations and Punjab changing its stand from no-guarantee to up to Rs 10-crore guarantee, the company, it was learnt, has expressed its inability to commit itself to the deal. While confirming the development, Punjab Financial Commissioner (Development) RS Sandhu said it was not the end of the road and the department was looking for other options.

The Punjab government had earlier offered a guarantee of Rs 20 crore to the Citrus Council-Pepsico project of bringing over one lakh acres under citrus cultivation in Punjab. But the council later ran into trouble with farmers owing to paucity of funds, as it could not pay them the lease money for the orchards.

With fund-starved Punjab too refusing to have any further stake in the programme, the council was given the option of roping in a venture capitalist.

Hope floats: Global vaccine giant submits Rs 500-crore proposal

Punjab today received a proposal of Rs 500-crore FDI from Merial for setting up a vaccine facility at Lalru. The US-based pharmaceutical giant today firmed up its $ 100 million (Rs 500 crore) FDI proposal for setting up a foot and mouth disease (FMD) vaccine manufacturing project.

Merial president Dr Jean-Loius Crosia had a breakfast meeting with Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal at his official residence today.

Crosia said they decided in favour of Punjab after studying other destinations such as Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka. This would be the fourth FMD vaccine manufacturing plant of the company in the country.

The first phase of the project would be completed by 2010 for which the company has already purchased 20 acres of land in Lalru.

"The new biotechnology facility with world-class process and standards for production and R&D will be comparable to our facilities in the UK, Brazil and France," Crosia said.

"The FMD vaccine project would give a boost to the dairy industry in the state, as Punjab has the highest per capita availability of milk per day, which is 3.88 times higher than the national average," Badal said.

Heading: Blind murder case solved; three held - Indian Express
Content:
Taking strong exception to the viewpoint of PS Pasricha, president of the managing committee of Takht Hazoor Sahib, published in a national magazine, Sikh radical body Dal Khalsa and SGPC member Manjit Singh Calcutta today sought apology from him for distorting historical facts.

They also criticised the honouring of Pasricha by Sikh high priests in the presence of SGPC chief Avtar Singh Makkar in violation of the maryada at Nanded during Guruta Gaddi Diwas celebrations. Calcutta said the assertion of Pasricha that "Guru Gobind Singh came to Nanded to ask Marathas to help him strengthen his forces in order to fight the Mughal empire, which at that time was under the supremacy of Aurangzeb" was wrong. Aurangzeb died in 1707 AD, long before the tenth Guru visited Nanded, he said, adding that Pasricha distorted facts to appease a Marathi lobby in the government.

"The second blasphemy that Pasricha committed was when he said that as per historians, Guruji was attacked by some of his own men and he died owing to severe injuries in his back," said Calcutta. "But the fact is that Wazid Khan, chieftain of Sirhind, was afraid of Guruji and sent one of his Pathan couriers to assassinate him and he was successful in the nefarious design. He attacked Guruji when he was resting at his camp in Nanded," he added. Dal Khalsa general secretary Kunwarpal Singh said that the five Takht Jathedars had accorded Pasricha a siropa during the celebrations, violating the moral Sikh code of conduct, as he dyes his beard.

Heading: 2,129 pirated CDs, DVDs seized - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of three persons, the Batala police today claimed to have solved the blind murder case of Gurbhinder Singh, alias Bhinder, a 22-year-old resident of Mehta village whose body was recovered from near Bolewal village.

The accused have been identified as Tarjinder Singh, alias Mithu, his brother-in-law Kulbir Singh, alias Sonu, and Onkar Singh, alias Happy. Batala SSP Dr Naresh Kumar Arora said the accused had called the deceased for drinking with them. "Later, they strangulated him with a dupatta,"he said.

The SSP said the accused killed Gurbhinder, as he allegedly used to force the sister of Tarjinder Singh to have relations with him. He added that further investigations were on.

Heading: ‘Unrestrained’ police force a nightmare for state govt - Indian Express
Content: Following a tip-off from the Indian Music Industry, Amritsar police recovered over 2,129 pirated CDs, DVDs and VCDs on Tuesday in a raid at two shops at Baba Deep Singh Market and Jail Road. Police seized 584 mp3 CDs, 1,018 movie DVDs, 342 movie VCDs and 185 song VCDs. Police have arrested Deepak Kumar and registered a case against him. Savio D'Souza, General Secretary, IMI, said, "IMI is committed in its fight against piracy."

Heading: Bhiwani ‘accident’: Prime accused in police custody - Indian Express
Content:
Bhiwani incident, Sarita case... police high-handedness has been too frequent

At a time when both Lok Sabha and state Assembly elections are nearing and the Congress government in the state is announcing all kinds of benefits, the unrestrained Haryana Police is a recurring nightmare for the Bhupinder Singh Hooda government.

The shooting down of an innocent student in Bhiwani yesterday by the police is just another blatant example of the brazen acts of the police force in the state. What made matters worse was the incongruous excuse that the "accidental" firing was because of a bump on the road!

Police brutality has been especially frequent this year and in all cases, the innocent have been at the receiving end. The Sarita suicide case is fresh in everyone's mind. Failing to get justice from the police and the administration, the hapless victim, raped by policemen, committed suicide outside the DGP's office at the Haryana police headquarters in Panchkula.

Just two months back, indiscriminate firing by the police upon a group of protesting guest teachers in Rohtak, the home district of the Chief Minister, led to the death of a woman teacher. The police went on to claim that she had been killed as a result of firing from the rampaging crowd, but the lie was nailed a day later when the post-mortem report proved that she died as a result of a plastic bullet fired by the police.

On June 18, the police shot down one Mahendra Singh of Garanpura village in Bhiwani after putting up a naka in Tosham to grab some criminals. They chased and killed the victim in the "encounter". The probe in this case is still on. In another incident on July 21, the Hisar police, led by SP Ashok Sheoran, shot dead one Sandip, alias Kalia. The SP's revolver was "lost" during the incident. Curiously, the same revolver was later used to murder encounter specialist from Delhi, ACP Rajbir Yadav.

Immediately after the Hooda government came to power in 2005, the brutal police lathicharge on protesting Honda workers in Gurgaon had hit national headlines. This was followed by the police inaction in the Gohana caste clash and the lathicharge on protesting Liberty factory workers in Karnal.

Earlier this year, there was the incident of a Yamunanagar nurse tearing off her clothes in protest against police inaction. She alleged she had been raped by some miscreants, but the police were not ready to investigate the case. On the lines of Sarita, a Muslim woman, Shamshida, too, tried to commit suicide in the DGP's office in Panchkula, but was saved by timely medical help.

Not that things were any better during previous governments. During the regime of Om Prakash Chautala, dozens of protesting farmers were shot dead by the same trigger-happy policemen in Kandela. Police firing and killing of farmers and others took place during Bansi Lal and Bhajan Lal's regimes as well. Surprisingly, despite all such violations and abuse of human rights, the state government has steadfastedly put down all suggestions to set up a human rights commission, with CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda claiming "there was no need for it in the state".

Haryana DGP Ranjiv Dalal was not available for comments, despite several attempts.

Heading: Funny side up - Indian Express
Content:
While no untoward incident was reported from any part of the district following the "accidental" death of 23-year-old Kuldip Singh, residents blocked a road in Kharak village and a complete bandh was observed in Satnali in Mahindergar district, a Rajput-dominated area.

Prime accused constable Karambir was remanded in two days' police custody by Civil Judge Shashi Chauhan after he was produced in the court today.

Taking no chances, the police have made elaborate security arrangements in the district. SP Sanjay Kumar said police force from four districts under Hisar Range has been deployed.

Accusing the police of delaying the arrest of the other seven accused, the deceased's uncle, Vijender, alleged that the police were trying to hush up the matter. "We will take legal action if the guilty are not arrested immediately," he said. A delegation of Sarva Jatiya Sangharsh Samiti met the SP, demanding immediate arrest of the guilty.

INLD general secretary Ajay Singh Chautala visited the house of the deceased and expressed his sympathy with the family. Condemning the police action, he said the Congress government had no control of law and order in the state and demanded President's rule in the state. Member of BJP national working committee Om Prakash Dhankar also criticised the Haryana government. HJC chief Kuldip Bishnoi also condemned the police action.

Heading: Sichuan, Again - Indian Express
Content:
Azhar Usman is called Osama Bin Laughin' for a reason

He's the man who had Pervez Musharraf in splits at a sit-down dinner in Dallas in September 2006. Azhar Usman, a 32-year-old, Chicago-based, stand-up comedian whom CNN recently named "American's Funniest Muslim", is preparing for his first professional outing in India and he is excited: "When I walk down the streets of Chicago I get dirty looks for being a Muslim. So in India, it'll be so nice to finally be hated for being an American. I feel so patriotic."

A Muslim and a comedian — it is an image that breaks away from stereotypes. Usman sticks to his carefully cultivated Muslim look — read heavy black beard — during performances. His brand of comedy is obvious in his wildly popular show "Allah Made Me Funny: The Official Muslim Comedy Tour" though he is sure he doesn't want to be "stuffed into some rigid box called Muslim comedy". "I am a comedian and I am Muslim and I think I understand what people mean when they call me a Muslim comedian. I hope that doesn't mean I can't be funny for funny's sake," he says.

On Saturday, Usman will hold fort at the American Center in Delhi. "The objective of this tour is quite simply to make people laugh," he says. It is a homecoming in many ways: Usman's parents moved from Bihar to Chicago in the 1970s, a few years before he was born. He went on to get a law degree and run his own dotcom before venturing into comedy. He was a hit from the word go — in one of his first shows, the emcee introduced him as the Ayatollah of Comedy and the name sticks to this day. "Now, I've been a full-time comedian for years and have performed in over a dozen countries in five continents," he says. In November 2005, he was called on to perform at the US-Islamic Word Forum in Doha. "My agenda has always been to wage peace through humour," he adds.

And about how Muslim clerics react to his jokes, Usman says they love it. "Every single Muslim cleric, scholar and imam who has watched my show has had nothing but praise," he says. This American traveller to India has packed his luggage, and airport security be warned — they could die laughing if they peep into his bag of tricks.

Usman will perform at the American Center on November 8. Time: 7 pm. Contact: 23316841

Heading: Ten Things To Do Before You Die - Indian Express
Content:
The usual flavours from China, but with some surprisingly good veggie dishes

Meher Fatma

We have had enough restaurants sautéing Sichuan peppers and dunking Hunan chicken, all in the name of China. If you haven't got tired of Chinese delicacies, then a new restaurant has joined the crowded food map of Noida's Sector 18 market. Mandarin Trail, an 80-cover diner on the third floor of The Great India Place mall, is set up by the RTC Group that runs the popular chain Ruby Tuesday. Decked with benches in bright reds and a lounge in black and white, Mandarin Trail sticks to serving the simplest of Chinese recipes — a fried Chinese cabbage for starters or a shredded lamb in hot garlic sauce for main course. Nothing adventurous, nothing deeply disappointing.

Must-Try

The menu seems to play with Chinese recipes that most Delhi restaurants chalked off theirs last season. A closer look, however, will introduce you to some interesting dishes, like fresh beans hakka style and a tangy eggplant for starters. We begin with eggplant with sesame seeds (Rs 175). Dices of eggplant in crispy skin and bathed in a delicious soy dressing make for a scrumptious mouthful. Apart from vegetables, seafood too is well-done here. We tried sautéed prawns (Rs 375). Finished with dry chillies, it was lip-numbing and needed a heady strawberry-soda mocktail to beat the heat. Golden Black Mushroom Bag (Rs 145) is artistically presented, with summery-yellow sheets of flour pouches filled with chopped mushrooms and knotted with a thin lace of lemon grass. In the main course, diced potato with corn kernels (Rs 185) is a vegetarian's delight. Served in hot garlic sauce, it is a refreshing shift from the usual veggie and tofu preparations that Indian restaurants churn out in the name of China. We also sampled Steamed Fish in Scallion Sauce (Rs 295). The fish complemented the subtle flavours of the sauce and we paired it with Yongchow Fired Rice (Rs 195), a mix-meat rice platter. The restaurant also offers braised whole pomfret (Rs 375) with a choice of dressings.

Give a Miss

Singapore Rice Noodles (Rs 195), in which we searched, in vain, for flavours.

Meal for two: Rs 1,000

Contact: 95120-4279322

Location: Third Floor,

The Great

Indian Place

Heading: Girls Just Wanna Have Fun - Indian Express
Content:
Actor Vinay Pathak explores his serious side with Dasvidanya

It has been a while since Vinay Pathak made us guffaw with his iconic film Bheja Fry. However, the actor says he has been grappling with being typecast as a comedian and insists that his versatility in front of the camera has yet to be revealed. "Ek Bheja Fry ne mera bheja kharab kar diya (One Bheja Fry has befuddled my brain). And I've played many character roles before it," says Pathak, promoting his latest film Dasvidanya (Russian for goodbye) at PVR Select Citywalk. Wearing aviator shades and dressed in a pair of denims and a crisp blue shirt, Pathak, who is also producing the movie, chats with the media, punctuating his answers with an occasional joke.

Dasvidanya is about the life of a simpleton, Amar Kaul, played by Pathak, who is told by the doctors that he has only three months to live. So he draws up a things-to-do list for 90 days. "My character looks back at life and sees that he hasn't done anything special. Nothing exciting has ever happened to him. So in the last three months he decides to make up for those lost years," says Pathak, who wears a sombre look in the film. The script, though, is eerily similar to the 2007 Hollywood flick The Bucket List, starring Morgan Freeman and Jack Nicholson. But Pathak is quick to deny this. "It's very different," he insists. "Kaul is an ordinary person who has to deal with unexpected news." The film also stars the hit duo of Ranvir Shorey and Rajat Kapur but only because they are the most appropriate for the script, says Pathak.

This might be his first film as producer but Pathak has been producing TV serials for the last four years. He will next be seen in SRK and Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi.

Heading: Mozart’s Last Note - Indian Express
Content:
Shireen Mehra cranks out women-only trips for safe, carefree journeys

Janak Sharma loved holidays with her family but there was always a missing ingredient. "I couldn't go for adventure sports, and there was always the hassle of looking after the children," she says. That was when a friend told her about Shireen Mehra and her Women on Clouds, a Delhi-based travel company by women, for women. Finally, Sharma went on her first ever holiday without her family and the 35-year-old housewife did all the things she always wanted to.

The six-month-old travel company of Mehra, 30, works on the idea that women can have a great time together. There have already been trips to Camp Red Stone in Dehradun and Ladakh, the itinerary filled with rappelling and rock climbing sessions and long walks on barren terrain. "Women can live without shopping," laughs Mehra, who began operating out of a basement office at Gulmohar Park. She was surprised at how popular her venture became even before they started advertising. "A lot of the callers are working women but there is a sizeable number of housewives as well. Clearly, it is fun to break away and just have fun with other women sometimes," she says. Groups comprise five-12 members and rates vary.

Mehra and her staff carefully go over the details, with safety and clean toilets being the biggest priorities. "Then, there is food. Since women are good cooks themselves, we have to ensure the meals are tasty," she says. After the first tentative steps, Mehra's company is now ready to fly, with future trips including foreign destinations.

Heading: 25-km hurdle: Dwarka-Gurgaon road hits legal block, no deadline in sight - Indian Express
Content: On Tuesday evening at Kamani, it was dark dreams that ruled the stage. Mozart's powerfully haunting last work, the Requiem, composed in 1791, was performed with febrile excitement under the baton of the French conductor Yves Parmentier. "The Requiem is one composition that summarises Mozart's works. And it was a great challenge to perform," said Parmentier, on his first visit to Delhi. The one-hour concert "Mozart's Requiem in Delhi" began on a sunny note though — the Delhi Chamber Choir conductor Gabriella Boda-Rechner marshalled 60 singers to crank out a cheery ABC song by Mozart, followed by Argentinean composer Raul Maldonado's stately Mi Canto del Sur. "The joy of doing Mozart is that his each line is joyful and precise and you can easily gauge the movement," said Boda-Rechner after the performance. Up next, the feisty conductor led the audience through a delicately nuanced composition, the biblical funeral cantata Gallia by Charles Gounod with soloist Aude Priya, who brought out a sense of immediacy to the composition. But it was the exacting Requiem in D minor, conducted by Parmentier with four soloists, which had the audience transfixed. The choir was accompanied by Hungarian-Moroccan pianist Marouan Benabdallah. Parmentier, who has directed the Requiem a dozen times, led the choir through the cohesive piece accentuated by soprano Sunanda Rao. The other soloists Shireen Sinclair, Prabhat Chandola and Antoine Redon also showed flashes of brilliance.   —Richa Bhatia

Heading: After 3-year scam hiatus, Noida plot draw restarts today - Indian Express
Content:
The construction of a 25-kilometre long road, which would have given direct access to Dwarka into Gurgaon, has hit a snag since a substantial stretch of land acquired for the project is dotted with widespread construction and is also awaiting a court nod for work to begin.

Envisioned in Masterplan 2021, this expressway — known as the Northern Express Road and undertaken by the Delhi and Gurgaon administrations — was to cut down travel time between the two states. Residents of Dwarka, who at present have to hit the NH-8 in order to reach Manesar and beyond, would have been saved the long detour once this 150-metre wide road came up — at a cost of Rs 90 to Rs 120 crore. Fifteen kilometres of this road would have run through suburban Gurgaon and the rest 10 through Delhi, sources said.

However, officials of the District and Town Planning (DTP) department of Haryana said that 242.55 acres of the total land acquired from 14 villages, have suddenly come under dispute because of existing buildings on it, mostly homes.

An official at the DTP department said a litigation on this stretch is also pending in the Punjab and Haryana High Court and possession can only start after the court gives its decision.

District Town Planner Madhusmita Moitra said: "There is a stay order on dispossession. The land has been acquired but the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) cannot take possession of the demarcated area till the court's final decision."

There is also the question of compensation to landowners. Official records show property owners in 10 villages of the 14 have been given compensation. The DTP official said: "Villages like Pawala Khasroorpur, Chauma, Gurgaon village and Kherki Dhaula are still waiting. Though the land has been acquired, these sprawling constructions remain the problem."

Once DTP gets possession of the entire 618.5 acres needed for the road, the estate officer of HUDA will begin issuing tenders. DTP's superintendent engineer Pankaj Kumra said: "There will be a toll plaza on this road as well like the other two on NH-8 at the Delhi-Gurgaon border and Kherki Dhaula." He, however, would not set a deadline for the finish, given the problems in land acquisition.

Meanwhile, villagers in Kherki Dhaula have said the authorities made several changes to the initial masterplan. Local Ramesh Yadav said: "The road was diverted from its original path after authorities found out that it would have otherwise run through a commercial plot. We have approached the High Court and have full faith in the judiciary."

President of the Gurgaon and Mahwat zila parishad Roa Abhey said, "The change in plan will affect over 1,000 villagers. The loss to property would have been much less if the road digressed an acre or two from the original blueprint. There is open space surrounding that plot. The road needn't have been taken out through residential areas."

Sources in Urban Development Ministry said the road will also connect areas in Gurgaon where development will now begin. "Such projects are usually undertaken by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). But they have a lot on their hands now. The two states have therefore gone ahead on their own," a senior ministry official said.

Heading: To make IGI safer in terror days, high-intensity bomb disposal machine soon - Indian Express
Content:
The draw for allotment of 1,250 residential plots, cancelled by the Supreme Court in July 2005 for alleged bungling in preparing the list of applicants, will begin afresh from Wednesday.

Following an Allahabad High Court order, the Noida Administration has beefed up security in and around Noida stadium where the draw will be held.

District Magistrate Shravan Kumar said on Tuesday that all necessary security arrangements are in place. "Officials from Hapur-Pilkhuwa, Meerut, Bulandshahar-Khurja and Ghaziabad development authorities have been called in to finish the draw with efficiency," he said.

The administration conducted a mock-run for the draw today.

According to officials, extra police personnel have been called from Meerut, Ghaziabad and adjoining areas. "In 2005, a group protesting against what they felt was unfair allocation of plots reached the spot where the draw was being held. We have beefed up security to avoid any such recurrence," a senior police officer said. CCTV cameras have been installed at various strategic points to keep the draw under close observation, the officer added.

The draw will take place under the observation of J B Patnaik, chairman of Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation, and Himanshu Kumar, IG (Registration).

The plots have been divided in four categories: 450 sq m, 112.5 sq m, 162-200 sq m, and 250-300 sq m. There are 128 plots for 450-sq m plots in both general and reserve categories, and 157 for general and 156 plots for reserve category in 112.5-sq m plots. The third category of plots will have 73 allotees both for reserve and general categories. For the plots measuring 250-300 sq m, there are 267 and 268 plots, respectively, under general and reserve categories.

There are 1,63,270 applicants for general category plots and 538 for reserve plots. The plots have been allotted in Sectors 44, 48 51 52 122, 46, 47, 54, 71 72 82, 90, and 93-B.

The Supreme Court had cancelled the draw of lots and ordered a CBI probe into the alleged bungling in preparing the list of successful applicants, which included VVIPs and their relatives.

Heading: AIIMS faculty up in arms over quota-job ad - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL), which is modernising the city airport, is in the process of procuring the country's second Total Containment Vessel (TCV), touted as the most foolproof bomb disposal machine.

The TCV is a spherical, vessel-like device, used for the first time by the National Security Guards to defuse a live bomb near Regal Cinema on September 13, when serial blasts rocked Delhi.

A TCV, CISF officials said, is now seen as a much-needed equipment to further secure the airport.

Sources said DIAL had ordered the TCV before the September 13 serial blasts and procurement is in final stages now. Delhi Police is also learnt to have ordered one such machine following the spate of blasts across the country in recent past.

The vehicle costs approximately Rs 3 crore.

The CISF is responsible for security inside the high-alert airport; Delhi Police mans security outside its premises. At present, a Bomb Disposal and Detection Squad (BDDS) is available with the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, headquartered at Mahipalpur near IGI, to take care of bomb threats.

While a TCV was first used in India during the Delhi blast, it has been extensively used by the US forces in Iraq, a CISF official. "The vessel has the capability to contain a blast without causing harm to surroundings."

Sources said the vessel, ordered from the US, can withstand a blast of up to 8 kg high explosives. "You cannot evacuate an area where you find an unexploded bomb," the official said, pointing out the necessity for the device. "It is also difficult for the bomb disposal squad to defuse a bomb at a crowded place like the airport. A TCV is the best solution in such emergency situations."

He said a retrieved bomb can be loaded into the vessel through an opening — approximately 2 feet in diameter — and the TCV itself can be loaded on a motorised palette that allows it to be moved to the scene of action, rather than moving the explosive to the vessel.

Dial has also procured two ground bomb killer blankets for use in terminal buildings. "This will take care of any explosive and minimise impact of an explosion," an airport official said.

Why Total Containment Vessel?

* Can withstand a blast of up to 8 kg explosives

* Retrieved bomb can be loaded into it

* TCV can be loaded on motorised palette and moved to spot, rather than moving explosive towards it

Heading: Sleek mantra: Parties rope in agencies, use ‘legal’ space for ads - Indian Express
Content:
An advertisement issued on behalf of the AIIMS director to fill up vacant posts for reserved category candidates is brewing another storm at the institute.

The advertisement, issued in national dailies on Tuesday, invites applications for 95 posts from SC/ST and OBC candidates, leaving out general category aspirants.

While the institute maintains that the step is to fill up the backlog of vacancies for reserved category candidates, resident doctors and faculty members say the vacancies advertised are only for SC/ST and OBC candidates. The step thus makes it 100 per cent reservation for the posts advertised, they contend.

"Even if this is a special recruitment drive only for reserved category candidates, all vacancies in the institute cannot be included in this," AIIMS faculty association president Dr Binod Khaitan said.

AIIMS faculty members now plan to move the court over the issue. "This is ridiculous," Dr Khaitan said. "How can reservation be applicable with a backlog when the institute hired SC/ST and OBC candidates in the past also through floating system? Another problem is that a Supreme Court order has forbidden reservation in specialty and super-specialty branches of medicine but in this case those seats have also been advertised only for SC/ST and OBC candidates."

Dr R C Deka, Dean, AIIMS, meanwhile said, "I have not seen the advertisement, and I do not have any idea about the details."

But the faculty association said that specialty and super-specialty branches such as cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery and others, which as per Supreme Court order are not open for recruitment through reservation, have been advertised.

Though the advertisement mentions that all recruitments will be only for temporary faculty posts, subject to outcome of the case in the apex court, the faculty association maintains that recruitment process is flawed considering that the matter is still in court. "In court, AIIMS authorities have given an affidavit saying recruitments only at the level of associate professor would be open for reserved category applicants. Then how can they advertise all posts for reserved category candidates?" Dr Kumar Harsh, president of AIIMS Resident Doctors' Association, asked.

Heading: Political bigwigs participate in Chhat puja, woo voters - Indian Express
Content:
With the war of words from above the new bus shelters and leaking public toilets intensifying on neon-lit hoardings, the Election Commission of India (EC) has directed municipal agencies to submit a report on the number of legal advertising sites in public spaces being used by political parties.

Thanks to the stringent laws imposed by the EC and municipal agencies, political parties are now using "legal" advertising spaces — like public utilities and bus shelters — for their pre-election canvassing, say MCD officials.

And that helps taking expenses into account. "It's an easy way to monitor expenditure on campaigning," says Amiya Chandra, head of MCD's remuneration cell. "We have been asked to round up all ad agencies that own the rights for providing legal advertising space and give an estimate of the amount spent on advertising."

Chandra says the report would be submitted to ECI within this week.

Though MCD has already filed about 1,000 FIRs against illegal hoardings since Monday, with parties like BJP and Congress hiring reputed advertising firms to design their election campaigns, officials claim the number of challans against illegal advertising has reduced considerably this time.

The Sheila Diskhit government had started a Rs 40-crore ad campaign in September, with slogans like "Har Din Hoti Behetarin, Dilli MereLliye" and "Mere Liye Sawar Rahi Hai Dilli" designed by agencies Dentsu, Crayon, Lintas and Triton along flyovers, bus stops and Metro stations. Sushil Pandit's agency The Hive, which did the campaign for Modi during the Gujarat elections, is churning out slogans for the BJP: "Congress Mehengi Padi", and "Sacrifice vs Sedition", over the Jamia Nagar encounter incident.

The Congress, which has hired Delhi-based ad firm Crayons for the Lok Sabha polls as well for a price of Rs 150 crore, is yet to kickstart its campaign in the final round of the Assembly polls.

Not willing to divulge campaign details, Rashpal Rana, in-charge of the campaign at Crayons, said, "We are still in the process of strategising but the campaign will start on November 15."

Heading: Poorvanchalis ask parties: observing Chhat alright but where is our ticket? - Indian Express
Content:
Independent candidates get the

Day 1 blues

The first day of filing nominations turned out to be a dampener for enthusiastic independent candidates, who turned up in full fervour to fill in their forms, courtesy ignorant election officers.

With political bigwigs like the BJP and the Congress yet to finalise their candidates, barely 15 forms were given out and many dejected candidates claimed the officers were clueless about these forms and the necessary details, resulting in no nomination forms being filled today.

Candidates kept running from pillar to post collecting information and passing it on to the deputy commissioners for the benefit of other candidates, who will turn up in the days to follow.

Heading: BSP confident of toppling Ram Babu Sharma in Rohtas Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
Even as politicians from both the Congress and BJP made a beeline to the ghats to celebrate Chhat and give news bites, it seems the Poorvanchali population in the Capital is miffed with both parties for not giving them minimal representation.

While the BJP has released its list, things are not yet clear for the Congress. And several Poorvanchali organisations have written to both parties complaining about the issue. The latest missive was fired by the UP Bihar Mahasangh, which was founded by BJP leader Lal Bihari Tiwari. Delhi has nearly 60 lakh Poorvanchalis. "In the BJP's first list, even in areas where there is a large population of Poorvanchalis, no person from the region has managed to get a ticket. The Congress, on the other hand, in the name of Poorvanchali representation, traditionally only gives a ticket to Mahabal Mishra," Uttam Tiwari, president of the UP Bihar Mahasangh, said.

There are at least seven seats in the Capital that have a predominantly Poorvanchali population. These include Patparganj, Burari, Dwarka, Sangam Vihar, Karawal Nagar, Kirari and Wazirpur. However, in the BJP's list, Poorvanchalis have been given representation only in Kirari, which will be contested by Anil Jha.

As far as the Congress is concerned, there is much uncertainty as the official list has not been declared. "Both parties demand votes in our name but they do not give us any representation. We have told them clearly that in case they continue to not pay any attention to us, we will boycott them," Tiwari said.

The BJP has given the Sangam Vihar ticket to Dr S C L Gupta. Gupta lives in Gurgaon and party insiders claim he got the seat because of his friendship with the Delhi BJP president, Harsh Vardhan. The name of retired IPS officer Amod Khanth is doing the rounds in Congress circles, although the seat has been allotted to Tek Chand Sharma in the initial list.

In Dwarka, which again has a sizeable population of Poorvanchalis, the BJP has given the ticket to Pradyuman Rajput. The Congress is planning to field Mahabal Mishra, although that remains undecided. In Karawal Nagar, the BJP has given the ticket to sitting MLA Mohan Singh Bhist, who is from Uttarakhand. In Patparganj, both the Congress and BJP remain undecided. The name of student leader Nakul Bhardwaj has been doing the rounds in BJP circles, even as candidates like Poonam Azad have been ignored.

Sitting MLA Mange Ram Garg has got the ticket from Wazirpur. He is a Haryanavi but his wife is from Jharkhand.
