Heading: ‘Just want to get out of hospital now’ - Indian Express
Content:
Promising an international gourmet experience to passengers using the Capital's Indira Gandhi International Airport, two brand new outlets offering a wide variety of food and beverage options have been opened at the airport's international terminal (Terminal 2).

Caffè Ritazza has opened in the visitor's lounge outside the departure concourse. It is an international coffee brand with a focus on "great coffee, fresh food and expert barista service, delivered consistently worldwide". "Taking account of the local culture and tastes, Caffè Ritazza can be adapted to deliver a coffee shop experience that's perfectly tailored to the local market," a DIAL official said.

The visitor's lounge also has a multi-cuisine restaurant, Food Village, which offers a wide range of Indian, Italian and Oriental cuisine. While there is an option for pizza lovers to dig into jumbo-sized pies and juicy pastas, others with a taste for noodles and dimsums can also indulge themselves here. Those with a taste for all things desi can choose between succulent kebabs and tikkas, or go for a wide range of vegetarian dishes. The restaurant also offers an array of sandwiches, submarines, salads and beverages."Since these outlets are located in the visitor's lounge, they can be accessed by friends and families seeing off or receiving their relatives as well," the official said.

People visiting these outlets, however, say the food is overpriced and not up to the mark. DIAL officials said their policy is to offer food for "all pallets and wallets". But consumers have complained about the quality of the food not being at par with the money charged.

"I had come to see off my daughter-in-law and we decided to eat before she took her flight to Mumbai. The food is overpriced and not up to any standard. We spent Rs 800 for a tiny meal for two, which tasted bad," Renu Sharma, a resident of Jungpura, said.Another visitor to the airport said the food was bland and extremely overpriced. "I ordered a dish of corn and carrot in lemon sauce, which had absolutely no hint of lemon in it. And I fail to understand why the staff is so rude. They just cleared my table before I had even finished," Dipanker Chatterjee said. A resident of Dwarka, he had come to pick up his brother.

Heading: Man arrested for ‘murder’ of street dog - Indian Express
Content:
Two weeks after the crash at Delhi Metro site, life has changed even for those who were 'lucky' to have survived the mishap

Just over two weeks after the accident at the Delhi Metro construction site near Laxmi Nagar in East Delhi claimed two lives, three victims continue to languish in the Orthopaedics ward of the Lok Nayak (LN) Hospital.

Nine victims were rushed to the hospital that day, among them 30-year-old bus driver Surender Singh who was declared dead on arrival. "Five patients have been discharged since then, while three are still recuperating," a doctor at the hospital said.

For Dhanu Mahato, 22, the days in the hospital have been excruciating. "He is just coming to terms with the fact that his leg had to be amputated," the nurse on duty in ward 5A said. A native of Bihar, Dhanu was employed with AFCONS, the firm that is building the Metro stretch on Vikas Marg where the accident occurred. Married recently, he was looking forward to a leave to meet his wife back in Bihar, elder brother Nitish Kumar said.

Mahato earned a little less than Rs 4,000.

Now, he just lies on his hospital bed and stares at the ceiling languidly. "He hardly talks; we don't know what to say to him either," Nitish said.

Mahato was working night shift at the site when the accident occurred early that Sunday morning, October 19. It left his right leg completely crushed.

For Shivesh Kumar, 19, meanwhile, it was just a case of being at the wrong place at the wrong time. Employed as a computer operator at a printing press in Paharganj, Kumar was on his way home when the debris fell on the bus he was in. "If he had taken the next bus, he wouldn't have been here, in the hospital," father Sita Ram said.

Kumar's injuries have affected his central nervous system and left him partially paralysed from waist downwards. Doctors are unsure whether he would walk again. "There's no pain as such because they give me painkillers every morning and evening. But I just want to get out of here now," the teenager said. He comes from Saharsa, Bihar.

"An official from Delhi Metro Rail Corporation came and told us that they (DMRC) will pay all medical costs and even left their card in case we need help," Sita Ram said. The family, though, has not heard from the Delhi government, which had also announced a compensation package for injured victims.

Hari Singh Meena, 22, was also employed with AFCONS and working the night shift. Post-accident, his right leg had to be amputated. In fact, his condition was extremely critical when he was bought to LN Hospital, the nurse on duty said. "He had lost a lot of blood and was critical. He is stable now but his injuries will take a long time to heal," she said.

Meena's elder brother Rajesh is also employed with AFCONS and they had been living in Karkardooma for the past two years.

DMRC committee files report

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has decided to take action against AFCONS, the agency responsible for carrying out construction work at Laxmi Nagar, the site of the accident that killed two on October 20.

While the firm has already been fined Rs 10 lakh, Managing Director, DMRC, E Sreedharan, said, "We have decided to issue a showcause notice to the contractor before blacklisting the agency from other DMRC contracts."

The MD has also decided to hold weekly meetings of all DMRC workers every Monday, according to a report submitted by the high-level committee formed by the DMRC on November 4.

Sreedharan admitted that the accidents in Laxmi Nagar happened due to the workers' failure to insert a minimum of 10 pins for each column in the liner supporting the girder.

Heading: Batla House encounter: RTI petitioner denied information - Indian Express
Content:
In a bizarre incident, a case under the IPC was registered against a man at the Seemapuri police station for the 'murder' of a street dog and injuring two others.

The incident occurred on Monday evening in N-block of Dilshad Garden area in the East District. A law student, Dhruv Mohan filed a complaint with an NGO and the police that few men were unnecessarily and brutally beating up a few dogs of the locality with iron rods.

Acting on his complaint, NGO members and local cops reached the spot at 8 pm. "We reached the spot and saw a man brutally beating the dogs. We immediately stopped him and took him into custody," a senior police officer said.

The dogs were immediately taken to Sanjay Gandhi Animal Hospital where doctors declared one dead, while two other animals were admitted in a serious condition.

"The dog that died had suffered severe blows on his head," the senior police officer added.

The police said the accused, identified as Kamal Maisi, was arrested by the police and an FIR under Section 428 of the IPC was registered at the Seemapuri police station. Kamal Maisi works with a government department.

Dhruv Mohan said the reason behind the attack was that the men didn't want these dogs to stay in their locality.

Police added that after the complaint they checked with the area residents about the fact whether these dogs had bitten anyone in the area, but residents had denied any such occurrence.

Heading: Sena hits back, torches Rashtravadi office - Indian Express
Content:
Petitions filed under the RTI Act in connection with the October 19 encounter in Batla House have generated more controversy than information. Information in the matter was sought from the NHRC, AIIMS, Delhi Police and the Supreme Court by petitioner Afroz Alam Sahil.

Afroz Alam wanted information regarding postmortem reports and the doctors involved from AIIMS, and also a copy of the postmortem reports. In a reply, officials from the AIIMS Trauma Centre stated they could not pass on information related to medico legal records under sections 8(1)b and 8(1)h of the RTI. These sections are meant for information expressly forbidden to be published by any court of law or tribunal, or the disclosure of which may constitute contempt of court. An irate Afroz Alam states in his blog, Soochna Express: "The denial of information by AIIMS is illogical. In this case, the court has not issued any orders regarding the Batla House case and we are not violating Section 8(1)b of the RTI. They said that information cannot be provided because it would impede the process of investigation or apprehension or prosecution of the offenders. I want to state that information we sought is not related to any police investigation."

The Delhi Police and Supreme Court have not replied to the petition till now. "If institutions like the Supreme Court do not take RTI seriously, then what is the use of having such an Act?" Alam asks. The information received from the NHRC states that 2,560 cases of police encounter/alleged fake encounters have come up and it has granted compensation in 16 such cases so far.

Heading: Mayor seeks apology from Oppn leader - Indian Express
Content:
A group of Shiv Sena activists set on fire the Rashtravadi Shiv Sena's office in Shahdara on Tuesday morning in retaliation to Monday's attack on Maharashtra Sadan by the Sena splinter group.

Five fire tenders were rushed to the spot after the blaze was reported at 9.10 am. No one was reported injured in the incident, the police said.

Owning responsibility, Shiv Sena's North India in-charge Sandeep Kulkarni said the attack was a "fitting reply" to the Rashtravadi party's attempt to "tarnish" the image of the Sena and its leaders. "It was a spontaneous reaction by Sainiks angered by the insult heaped on Sena leaders by Rashtravadi Shiv Sena," he said. "It was a befitting reply to those who attacked the Maharashtra Sadan."

Kulkarni also accused Rashtravadi Shiv Sena chief Jaibhagwan Goyal of trying to unnecessarily blame Shiv Sena in the ongoing attacks against North Indians, primarily migrants from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, in Mumbai and its suburbs.

On Monday, activists of Rashtravadi Shiv Sena, formed to counter Shiv Sena's anti-north Indian stand, attacked Maharashtra Sadan to press their demand for arresting Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray. Goyal has demanded immediate arrest of the MNS chief under the National Security Act (NSA), failing which, he said, the party would intensify its attack. Police officials said today's fire was of minor intensity and no one was injured since Rashtravadi Shiv Sena activists were not present in the headquarters at the time.

The police said local residents have reported that some 30 Shiv Sainiks were part of the arson this morning.

The police have begun an inquiry into the matter.

Heading: RAC officer commits suicide in Chanakyapuri - Indian Express
Content:
Mayor Arti Mehra has threatened to move the court against the leader of Opposition Jai Kishan Sharma for passing an 'insensitive' comment on her at a press conference on Monday. Sharma had said, "She is a blot on the race of women." Reacting to Sharma's comment, the Mayor said he was an insensitive man and that she would take him to court if he does not issue an apology.

"I have already written to the President, Prime Minister, the UPA chairperson, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi and the chairperson of the National Commission for Women," said Mehra.

Mehra, along with other BJP councillors, will also take out a protest march against Sharma on Wednesday.

"After submitting my complaint tomorrow, I will wait for 48 hours for Sharma to give me a written apology. If he fails to do so, we shall meet the UPA Chief Sonia Gandhi to file a complaint against him. Women councillors will go also go on a hunger strike if Sharma fails to issue a written apology," said Mehra.

Heading: Woman attacked with acid, 6th case in 15 days - Indian Express
Content:
A 55-year-old Assistant Commandant of the Rajasthan Armed Constabulary (RAC) shot himself with his service pistol at Chanakyapuri here on Tuesday. He was posted with the 12th battalion of the RAC.

According to the police, Mahender Singh Chaudhary, a native of Bharatpur in Rajasthan, was found dead in a chair in his room with his service pistol in his right hand by the police at the battalion camp on Tuesday afternoon.

Police officers said a suicide note was found in the room which stated that he took the extreme step as he had failed to perform his duty towards his family, parents and siblings. The note mentioned that no one was to be blamed for his death.

The police added that Singh reached the battalion camp around noon and asked for his service pistol. After a few minutes he went back to his room saying that he was not feeling well," the police said. Later, a constable went to check on him and found him dead.

"We informed the police immediately. Around 6 pm his body was taken out after the DCP, New Delhi district, visited the spot along with other senior officers," an RAC officer said.

Heading: CAMPUS NOTES - Indian Express
Content:
A 20-year-old woman was allegedly attacked by an unidentified assailant who threw acid on her in the New Usmanpur area of the Northeast district on Tuesday. This is the sixth such incident in Northeast Delhi in the past fortnight.

According to the police, the incident took place around 7.30 am in the Brahmpuri locality of New Usmanpur area. The victim, Amreen Nasim Siddqui, a teacher at Navjeevan School in the same area, was going to her school when the attack took place.

Police said Siddqui, in her statement, told them that she was crossing a narrow lane near her house when a youngster came up behind her and threw acid on her back. The assailant fled the spot before she could react. She also described her attacker to the investigators. "The victim received burn injuries on her back and was taken to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital for medical treatment and is still admitted there," the senior police officer added.

The victim's father works with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) while her brother Nadeem Akhtar Siddiqui works as an interior designer with an Ahmedabad-based firm in Saket.

Despite claims by the police that they are trying to trace the accused as soon as possible, the local residents continue to live in a state of terror. Kehekasha, a local resident said, "The area is becoming highly unsafe for women and we are apprehensive of stepping out of our homes after six in the evening."

Secretary of the RWA in the area Purushottam Rawat said, "The law and order situation has worsened in our locality. Despite our complaints, no strict action has been taken yet."

Javeria, an 18-year-old girl who is the victim an earlier acid attack, said, "Last month, I was going to a local shop when a man threw acid at me."

Deputy Commissioner of Police, Northeast district, Surender Yadav said that the chemical being used by the assailant is not exactly acid and does not leave permanent scars. "A sketch has been prepared of the serial attacker using the victim's description. We have launched teams to nab this serial attacker and will arrest him soon."

Past incidents

Three of the six incidents have occurred in the same street in Gautam Puri area and the remaining three in Brahmpuri area. All attacks reportedly are similar.

* October 11: a 16-year-old girl attacked in Gautampuri.

* October 20: a 17-year-old girl attacked in Brahmpuri

* October 28: an 18-year-old girl attacked in Gautampuri

* October 30: a 12-year-old girl attacked in Brahmpuri

* November 1: an 18-year-old girl attacked in Gautampuri

Heading: The Kauls of Punjab: Siblings of the first-class - Indian Express
Content:
JNU organises alumni meet

Jawaharlal Nehru University is organising its first ever alumni meet, AAJ-08 (Alumni Association of JNU-08), from November 5 to 8 at its campus. The university expects approximately 700 alumnus to attend.

Pearl announces admissions

Pearl School of Business, Gurgaon, has announced admissions to its two-year full-time MBA programme for 2009-11. Last date for submitting applications is January 31 — the programme commences in June 2009.

DU teachers protest

Democratic Teachers' Forum for Social Justice on Tuesday organised a massive protest march and demonstration in North Campus to demand social justice for SC/ST/OBC categories at all levels and the proper implementation of UGC guidelines on reservation of teaching posts.

IIFT organises workshop

The Indian Institute of Foreign Trade organised a workshop focussing on helping Indian food processors meet competitive export standards at their institute on Tuesday.

JNU celebrates CIL Foundation Day

For the first time in its 34-year-old history, the Centre of Indian Languages at JNU celebrated its Foundation Day on October 31. On the occasion, Professor S R Kidwai, a noted Urdu scholar was honoured by the Centre.

Heading: Tripura take firm control - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab team mates and brothers Uday (21) and Siddharth Kaul (18) have so far played two Ranji ties together and have already made significant contributions. Last season Uday, in his third season for Punjab, played a vital role to help the team avoid relegation while medium pacer Siddharth snared a five-for against Orissa, on debut.

And on Tuesday, the brothers shone again to help their team inch closer to the 400 run mark. Even though Uday was unlucky to have missed out on a deserving century, he was happy that his season was beginning with a good score.

"I fell short by five runs, but I am not complaining. Rather, I am happy that I have started the season with a good score," Uday said about his knock.

The Kaul brothers added brisk 42 runs for the ninth wicket with Siddharth finishing off with an unbeaten 34, his highest first class score till now.

"I may be a bowler but I have to contribute with the bat every now and then," Siddharth added.

Ironically, Uday credits ICL for his consistency. "Before the ICL exodus, I was batting lower down the order. When a lot of senior players left, I got promoted. Batting higher up has made me a better player," he said.

Siddharth, with only two first class games against his name, already has adjusted mentally for the long haul.

"I have realised that I have to be patient as a bowler. I can't complain about the nature of pitches. If I'm good I should be able to take wickets even on placid tracks," he said.

Before their Ranji partnership, the Kaul brothers have played four under-22 matches together. So, any talk of rivalry or awkwardness in sharing the dressing room is not a problem for them.

"We are team mates here and brothers at home. And there's no rivalry between us as our roles are very different. I'm a bowler and he (Uday) is the keeper-batsman for the side, there can't be any comparisons between us," Siddharth quipped, adding, "We keep an eye on each other's performance."

Interestingly, both find talking about cricket all the time, boring."We only talk about the game during team meetings. Once we are done with the match or training, we don't utter a word about this. Life will get boring if we talk about cricket all the time," the Punjab keeper said.

Heading: Third new taxiway at growing airport - Indian Express
Content:
Visiting bowlers rule on Day Two asServices go into self-destruct mode

Abhijit Dey was only into his second over of the day when Tripura coach Sameer Dighe got up from his seat, almost superstitiously, as if to make things happen. With Services at 88 for four at tea, Tahir Khan and Madhushudan Reddy had already gone into a shell, playing a streak of maiden overs.

However, there couldn't have been a better coincidence for Tripura than Dighe's change of position and Khan's dismissal — Rajib Saha taking a sitter at silly point off Dey's second ball of the over. Khan, after facing 190 deliveries on his way to a solid 52, failed to negotiate the extra bounce. Reddy, in Dey's next over, tried to do things different in his 37-ball 6 but scooped one straight into the bowler's hands.

A bunch of Services officials were still unsure if the floodgates had actually opened, pinning their hopes on three all-rounders in their squad — debutant Abhishek Sinha, AK Mohanty and Suvra Karmakar. But then, Tripura are not a team of individuals.

While all the bowlers had their wickets' column ticking by then, spin spearhead Jayanta Debnath's was reading zero. Sinha, after a 42-ball 26, became Debnath's first victim, edging one to Rajesh Banik at slip. Before his second wicket that concluded the Services' innings for 138 — a classical off spinner that castled Rakesh Kumar — Vineet Jain did the same to Mohanty, while Dey had Karmakar caught at short-leg.

The second day's play clearly livened up the match when batsmen, eyeing a big first-innings total, threw away their wickets. Services, having scored 138 off 75 overs, had an innings run rate of less than two runs an over.

The dismissal of Yashpal Singh early might have cost them dearly, but he also, like Nishit Shetty on Monday, tried to accelerate when the road was getting slippery — failing to clear mid-on taking the aerial route, right after lunch when his team were precariously placed at 49 for 2. The reason, according to coach Jai Prakash Pandey, can be his uncharacteristic 34-ball 9.

"When you are playing out so many deliveries without scoring a run, you are bound to get out, with the bowler clearly on top. The boys failed to rotate the strike, inviting pressure. This is why singles are so important on a track like this," said Pandey.

Tripura's late fightback on Monday ended early on Tuesday with the remaining three wickets accounting for only 17 more runs. For Services, Rakesh Kumar and Suvra Karmakar took five wickets each, but the former had the distinction of claiming a third consecutive five-for after making his debut against Assam with five wickets last season.

The new ball for Tripura's second innings, however, was given to Karmakar who finished with a run-less over.

Tripura virtually ended the day at 85 for no loss, thanks to their even bowling card that displayed two wickets each for Vineet Jain, Tushar Saha and Jayanta Debnath, one more and one less for Abhijit dey and Timir Chanda, respectively.

The lead might amount for a win while Services have only one way out — bowl out the visitors and chase down the target.

Brief scores: Tripura 223 and 0/0 in 1.0 over lead Services 138 all out in 75 overs (Tahir Khan 52; Abhijit Dey 3/16, Jayanta Debnath 2/22, Tushar Saha 2/40, Vineet Jain 2/33) by 85 runs.

Heading: Woman’s rotting body greets joggers on Carter Road - Indian Express
Content:
An unemployed man, Raju Adangale (32), tried to commit suicide by jumping from the sixth floor of Mantralaya on Tuesday. The building houses the offices of the chief minister, deputy chief minister and other senior ministers.

Adangale, a resident of Ghatkopar, hails from Niphad in Nashik and was peeved at not getting a job despite registering himself in the state employment exchange. He tried to commit suicide by jumping from the window in the lobby, but was stopped by bystanders.

Speaking to the media, Adangale alleged that officials had demanded a bribe of Rs 2,000 from him to send a call letter and he also had to face such demands when he had appeared for the police recruitment process.

Heading: After pay-up notice, excise official shown as call girl on website - Indian Express
Content:
Lay by the sea for two or three days

The decomposing body of a woman greeted early morning joggers on Carter Road in Bandra (West) on Monday morning.

The dead woman, in her forties, was clad in a jogging track suit but barefoot. Marked with blunt injuries, her body had lain beside the sea near the Arts Club for two or three days, yet no one had noticed it till Monday.

"Our police station received the information from the control room, which must have been contacted by some pedestrian. We immediately rushed to the spot and recovered the body. The primary injuries were on her hands and torso and she seemed to be in her forties," senior police inspector Prakash George of Bandra police station said.

The police admitted they were puzzled by the fact that the body, though decomposed, had gone unnoticed so long. "It is really very surprising. It was only on Monday morning that it got noticed and the police were informed. The body has been sent to Bhabha Hospital for an autopsy," said George.

Identifying the body is proving difficult as no missing complaint on any woman of such a description seems to have been filed in any police station.

"From the quality of the jogging track suit she was wearing, one would assume that she came from a middle-class, if not well-to-do, family. In such cases, there should have been a missing complaint filed by the family as it is evident that the body had been lying out for at least couple of days. Yet there appears to have been no missing complaints on any woman in her thirties or forties. We contacted all police stations near Bandra area. It is surprising," said George.

Heading: 2nd Metro route on track: Centre okays VGF - Indian Express
Content:
Defaulting father, avenging son

A youth created a sleazy profile of a female excise official, posted it on Orkut and used it to harass her, his revenge for a notice the official had sent his to pay up dues amounting to several lakh rupees, the police said.

The profile on Orkut portrayed the excise official as a call girl and she got to know of it when she started receiving calls. "She complained to the police, a case was registered at Dindoshi police station on Monday and the cyber crime cell started a probe. The profile on Orkut showed her as a call girl soliciting customers and even mentioned her mobile number on the website. She started receiving calls from strangers at odd hours of the day; that is when she realised what had happened," said a police officer.

The cyber crime investigation cell (CCIC) of the crime branch tracked down the culprit by tracing the Internet protocol address he had used while posting the profile.

Kovid Patil (20) of Goregaon (East) was arrested on Monday. The cyber crime investigation cell (CCIC) of the crime branch booked him under the Indian Penal Code for acts intending to outrage the modesty of a woman, and under relevant sections of the Information Technology Act. He was produced at Esplanade Court on Tuesday and remanded to police custody till November 10.

"The motive was to create pressure on the excise official and harass her. In her capacity as an excise officer, she had served a notice to Kovid's father Hemant Sadanand Patil, asking him to pay up Rs13 lakh. Hemant Patil runs a company called Technocrat India that manufactures components for the automotive, agriculture, earth moving and defence sectors. His son helps in the business and tried to stall the payment of the dues. When this failed to deter the excise official, he posted the sleazy profile," said the police officer.

Heading: Jobless man attempts suicide from Mantralaya - Indian Express
Content:
In a boost to the state government's plans for the Charkop- Bandra-Mankhurd metro Railway corridor, the Centre has approved the Rs 1,532-crore viability gap funding (VGF) for the project.

The 38-km route is to be built at a projected cost of Rs 6,192 crore and the availability of the VGF will ensure that it can be built through the public private partnership (PPP) route. The project is expected to be complete in four years' time, once it takes off.

The corridor will have 27 railway stations and provide north- south and east- west connectivity.

The financial bids for the Charkop-Bandra-Mankhurd corridor, for which seven consortia are vying, are expected to be in by mid-December and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) is confident that construction work on the line will begin by January-end.

"We are having a pre-bid meeting on Wednesday and expect that the work on the second corridor to start by the end of January," said Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner.

The groups in the fray for what will be the city's second Metro Rail corridor are Essar, Alstom and Lanco Infratech; GVK Power and Infrastructure Ltd, Yeoh Tiong Lay and Bombardier Transportation; IL&FS , Transportation Network Ltd, Punjlloyd Ltd, and Soma Enterprises; L&T , IDPL, GE India, IIPL and CAF; Tata Power, Pioneer and Mitsubishi; Reliance Energy, SNC Lavalin; and Reliance Industries, Siemens AG and Gammon India Ltd.

Meanwhile, the MMRDA is still to decide on the model of implementation for the third metro rail corridor that will run from Colaba to Bandra. "We will start deliberation on the model for the third corridor after we finalise the second corridor," Gaikwad stated. The third corridor mainly underground and thus involves a huge cost of construction and therefore an inordinately large viability gap funding, which may force the state government to go in for a state-funded model and opt out of the Public-Private Partnership model.

Heading: MNCs to go slow on their expansion plans in Asia after global meltdown: report - Indian Express
Content:
Rabale police claimed to have cracked the murder case of Sena leader and real estate agent Nitin Prabhu with the arrest of his former business partner Sanjay Jadhav and one Sachin Sane on Tuesday. According to the police, the duo were arrested from the Vashi Railway Station premises while they were planning to flee to Nashik.

When contacted, DCP (Zone 1) RD Shinde said, "The deceased had some fallout with his former business partner Sanjay Jadhav an year ago due to disputes in a mobile business that they were running . They also had an argument around 15 days ago over some issue during which Jadhav had allegedly threatened Prabhu. Based on this, we suspected Jadhav and started gathering information about him."

As Jadhav was originally from Nashik, a team of policemen was sent to gather information about his possible whereabouts and another team was also operating in Mumbai to gather information from friends and acquaintances of the deceased and accused. "During the investigation, we initially arrested on November 3 one Avish Pawar (26) who confessed his role in the conspiracy to kill Prabhu and Sanjay Jadhav," said Shinde.

Based on Pawar's confession, the Rabale police started tracing Jadhav and arrested him along with another co-conspirator who is identified as Sachin Sane. Sane also confessed to have played a role in the conspiracy to murder Prabhu due to personal rivalry. "These three men have been taken into custody for further inquiry. We are also tracing the the identities and whereabouts of the two men who were hired to shoot Prabhu," said Shinde.

On November 1, while Nitin Prabhu was going to his real estate office along with his friend Aniruddha Samant on the latter's motorbike, Samant received a call on his cellphone. "After receiving the call, Samant pulled over to the side of the road, just outside the Asha Hospital in sector 7. While he was talking, two unidentified men approached the duo, fired three to four rounds at them and ran away," said Shinde. The duo then fled the spot on a motorbike, which they had parked around 50 to 60 ft away.

While Prabhu succumbed to his injuries on the spot, Samant sustained an injury after a bullet grazed his neck and was recuperating in the Indravati Hospital in sector 8 of Airoli.

Heading: ANC requests chief public prosecutor to appear in - Indian Express
Content:
The impact of the global meltdown, which is gradually being felt on Indian shores, will further affect the already-declining demand for on commercial real estate market in India.

According to a report by Jones Lang LaSalle, several multinational occupiers in Asia, who were optimistic about their expansion plans at the beginning of the slowdown, are now planning to go slow on their expansion plans.

The report is based on a survey of 30 leading multi-national companies carried twice— one at present and the other seven months ago— when the Asian economy had begun to brace itself for the impact of the subprime crisis.

These companies together occupy 200 million sq ft of space in the continent. Still very buoyant about the market, more than 40 per cent of MNCs had said they would expand their presence in Asia. However, seven months down the line more than 50 per cent of the MNCs that were once looking at aggressive expansion, have said they will "now grow less in the region than they had previously intended".

The companies surveyed are mostly those from the financial services industry, technology sector and consumer goods/manufacturing sector. The report stated that by the time the second survey was carried out, "one international bank said it was too buffeted by the current turbulence to have any clarity of planning. The other— a financial services firm— no longer exists as a going concern."

According to Anuj Puri, chairman and country head, JLLM, the corporates surveyed were those with a very strong presence in Asia, the purpose being understanding their appetite for Asia as a market.

"The good thing is they have not written Asia off. Though the growth will be muted, commercial real estate can find solace in the fact that most companies might look at shifting their back office work that occupies more space than front office, to India as a cost cutting measure," said Puri.

Only 15 per cent of the companies surveyed said that they would grow more than previously planned. However, the report clarified that in "all of these cases, off-shoring was the principal driver of the incremental growth, not market opportunities."

Heading: Radio channel, ACB come together to observe Vigilance Awareness Week - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti Narcotics Cell (ANC) of the Mumbai Police is leaving no stone unturned in securing conviction of the drug peddlers who supplied contraband at the rave party busted in Juhu. The ANC has approached Chief Public Prosecutor R V Kini requesting him to appear as special prosecutor in the case.

A team of ANC sleuths had on the night of October 5 raided a pub in Juhu and detained 239 youths for participating in an alleged rave party. Nine of the detained were later arrested on charges of possession, sale and consumption of narcotics. The police had seized as many as 104 tablets of Ecstasy, 850 drops of LSD and charas worth around Rs 9.6 lakh. Deputy Commissioner of Police (ANC) Vishwas Nangre Patil wrote a letter to Kini on Tuesday requesting him to appear in the case.

When contacted, Patil said, "It's a case which is both sensational and complicated. Therefore, we have asked a senior public prosecutor to handle the matter." He also said, "Since we prefer a smooth trial, we want a senior prosecutor to appear in the case."

Other than the nine accused, which includes a woman too, all the detained are out on personal bond till reports of the chemical analysis tests carried out after their detention is received by the police. If the tests show positive results, they would also be taken into custody and booked under the Narcotics Drug and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.

Prosecutor Kini said, "I will be taking up the responsibility of conducting the trial and hopefully we shall secure a conviction of the guilty."

The next hearing in the case is on November 6. The court will hear bail applications of two accused and cancellation of bail of seven others on the same day.

Heading: Nursing college at JJ Hospital to be revamped - Indian Express
Content:
This year the officials from the State Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) will not be alone in organising the Vigilance Awareness Week. Thanks to the efforts of the Public Concern for Governance Trust, the ACB has managed to rope in the radio channel Red FM for its awareness campaign in a bid to reach a wider audience.

The Vigilance Awareness Week started on Monday and will continue till November 7.  The first day of the week saw government offices observe an oath taking ceremony. The officials solemnly vowed 'not to bow to corruption of any kind and fight it in every way possible without any bias or favour.'

Sanjay Parande, additional deputy commissioner of police, ACB said, "While lectures and banners are effective, the audio-visual media has a wider reach. Last year we made a silent film on the topic which was widely appreciated. This time unfortunately the week will be observed at a time when the schools and colleges are still in vacation. But that's when we decided to rope in a radio station as its reach would be immense owing to its popularity." Parande added, "While the tenure of the week remained restricted to a few days, our aim is that its impact continues for a long time.

Our awareness campaigns have always stressed on the agenda that the people should be aware of their rights against corruption and that they should be aware of our existence."

While Parande argued that there was no specific study on the trend of corruption cases, he stressed that awareness levels have considerably increased. "Statistics may reveal that most of the cases being investigated by us are against the police or the BMC officials but that does not necessarily mean corruption is high in these sectors. It indicates a probability that cases go unreported in other sectors."

Mumbai-specific statistics from the ACB reveal that it registered 47 cases from Mumbai, till October this year and arrested over 60 persons in connection with the cases. 17 police personnel and 23 BMC personnel have been booked in these cases. Last year's figures show that the ACB registered 72 cases till October 2007 and 80 till the end of the year, with 121 persons having been arrested. Cases against 47 police personnel and 33 BMC personnel were registered last year.

Statistics for the whole of Maharashtra reveal that the ACB has arrested 304 persons after laying 231 traps between January and August this year. Of the accused, 73 are from the revenue department, 72 are police personnel while 23 are from the Municipal Corporations.

Heading: Vice President presents Jamnalal Bajaj Awards - Indian Express
Content:
Kalam emphasised the need for specialised courses for nurses and urged them to take care of rural patients with dedication

The nursing college in the state's biggest hospital will soon be revamped to bring it at par with world-class medical colleges like All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). The central Government has sanctioned Rs 120 crore for the upgradation of JJ Hospital, of which Rs 7 crore will be utilised for upgrading the nursing college. The city can also look forward to more nursing colleges soon.

Speaking at the centenary celebration of the Trained Nurses Association of India (TNAI), T Dileep Kumar, advisor to the Government of India, said more nursing colleges will be opened across the country to address the problem of acute shortage of nurses.

"There is a shortage of one million nursing staff in our country. The nurse to patient ratio is very high and that's needs to be corrected. For this purpose the Government of India has earmarked Rs 3100 crore for the nursing sector in the 11th plan. A centre of learning and excellence costing Rs 20 crore would be built in each state," said Kumar, who is also the president of Indian Nursing Council.

He added that the focus would be on states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Chattisgarh and the North East, where there are very few nursing colleges.

Present at the event, India's former president A P J Kalam talked about the dedication of Florence Nightingale and urged all nurses to render medical services with a similar dedication. Juggling from past to present, Kalam also talked about the importance of technology and the need for specialized courses for nurses. "Blending care with knowledge is important in the 21st century. Nurses should be technologically savvy in order to complement super specialty doctors," he said.

"In Philippines there is a nursing college offering PhD programme in nursing, so qualified nurses from this programme can practice independently in rural areas. A similar concept should be there in India to take care of National Rural Health Mission. I strongly advocate postgraduate nursing courses for working nurses through distance education," Kalam added.

Besides more nursing colleges, Kumar and Kalam also stressed on the need for public-private partnership. "Three days ago, the foundation stone was laid for the Indian Institute of Advanced Nursing with the help of private partners like Clinton Foundation, Apollo hospitals and others to train nurses in super specialties. Many such centers are needed and partnerships should be encouraged," said Kumar.

Heading: Chhat puja celebrations carried out smoothly at Juhu Chowpatty - Indian Express
Content:
The Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation awards were given away on the 119 th birth anniversary of industrialist and philanthropist Jamnalal Bajaj on Tuesday. Vice President Hamid Ansari, Maharashtra governor SC Jamir and former Maharashtra governor and council of advisors of the foundation, PC Alexander, were present at the function.

The awards were given away in four categories. Award for outstanding contribution in the field of constructive work was given to Biswanath Patnaik of Orissa-based Banabasi Seva Samiti, who has worked in the field of development of scheduled castes and scheduled Tribes, education and upliftment of downtrodden women, children, abolition of dowry, prohibition etc. He has also started welfare schemes, primary, secondary schools and non-formal education centres. His model has been prescribed by the Central Government for social welfare schemes for other states.

Tushar Kanjilal of West Bengal received the award for application of science and technology for rural development. Kanjilal elaborated on his experiences as an active campaigner for the protection of Sunderbans for thirty years.

Phoolbasan Yadav, a Chattisgarh native, was the recipient of the award for outstanding contribution for the upliftment of women and children. Yadav, who has studied till the seventh standard, formed self-help groups like the Pragya Mahila Samooh, Kiraya Bhandar and the Bazar Theka with the help of other women of her village. She has been actively involved in abolishing child marriage and dowry in around 65 villages of her state.  

Gandhian Louis Campana of France was given the International award for promoting Gandhian values outside India. Campana took up the mission of promoting non-violence in Europe after meeting Gandhi in 1937 in India. Since then, he has led several non-violent demonstrations in France and elsewhere.

Heading: School not paying as per 5th Pay Commission, says teacher - Indian Express
Content:
The Chhat puja celebrations in Juhu Chowpatty went ahead without much disturbance on Tuesday. Fear of violence among devotees was unfounded as the police kept a vigilant eye on the celebrations. Following the recent incidents of violence against north Indians led by the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, the police had stepped up security for the festival.

"We have had no problems and the crowd has been very co-operative," said senior police inspector Gaekwad of Santacruz police station.

"The pooja went flawlessly," said A Yadav, a devotee. "The police arrangements are very good and I feel very secure," he added. Bhola Gupta, a vegetable vendor from Kandivali said, "I am very happy as the Chhat Puja went well with all the tension in the past months."

However, there was a marked decrease in the number of devotees at the beach as compared to last year. The police estimated that around two lakh devotees turned up at Juhu Chowpatty although four lakh were expected. "This is only 50% of the crowd that was there last year. I guess people were a little afraid due to the past incidents" said Shanbhu Jha, another devotee. "I think that only 25% of last year's crowd is present today. But it may get better in the morning," added Gupta.

"We were getting calls till 4 pm about the situation here. We told everyone to come but still the crowd is a little diminished" said Professor A K Jha, a pandal organiser.

Heading: Portion of 100-yr-old building collapses - Indian Express
Content:
Years after the Bombay High Court and education officer ordered a trust-run school at Nallasopara to pay a primary school teacher according to the 5th Pay Commission, the school has not yet acted upon it.

Vilasini Retnakar, a teacher at a primary school run by Tulinj Education Trust since 1993, was handed over a termination letter by the school in 2000 as she was an untrained teacher.Following her termination, Retnakar moved the High Court which ordered the school to take her back and asked her to complete her D.ED.

Retnakar completed her D.ED in 2004 and again moved the High Court alleging that she was not being paid as per the Fifth Pay Commission.

The court then directed the education officer (EO) to pass an order within six weeks. The EO directed the school to pay Retnakar according to the 5th Pay Commission along with the arrears.The school, however, did not reciprocate and instead challenged the order passed by the EO.

A division bench of Justice S B Mhase and S S Shinde was then informed by the EO that he will withdraw his earlier order and pass a reasoned order to the parties concerned.

The court then set aside the earlier order and directed the EO to pass another order within four weeks and disposed of the petition in April 2007.

The EO then passed the order in favour of Retnaker and also wrote two letters to the school in April and June this year directing them to pay her as per the Fifth Pay Commission scale.

Retnakar claims that even after all these months of passing a reasoned order, the school hasn't paid her accordingly. She also said that her letters to the school demanding the pay has not been replied to by the school.

"Now we are contemplating to move the court against the trust for contempt," Retnakar said.

When contacted, Secretary of the trust Umesh Naik alleged that the EO did not follow the procedure as directed by the High Court before passing a reasoned order Naik, who is also the President of the Nalasopara Municipal Council, contends that the EO did not hear the school authorities before passing the order. "Now we will move a fresh application challenging the EO's order," Naik said.

However, HC while disposing the petition had clearly stated that they did not find it necessary for the EO to hear the parties as the same officer had heard the matter earlier.

Heading: Robbery at Hanjur Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
A portion of the 100-year-old Maharashtra Housing & Area Development Agency (MHADA) owned Chowgade building in Mukhwada lane collapsed on Tuesday morning leading to panic among the residents.

At around 9:50 am a portion of the second floor of the building collapsed. Though around 33 families live in the building, there were no casualties reported. Residents alleged that internal repair work conducted by a ground floor tenant caused the accident.

"There is a wheat grinding shop on the ground floor. The owner of the shop was carrying out some repair work due to which the wooden beams supporting the building got disturbed. We think that is what triggered the accident," said Prakash Verma, a resident of the second floor of the building.

"It all happened very suddenly. One minute the floor was there and the next minute it had given way. Some of our belongings got damaged but thankfully no person was injured, by sheer luck no one was present near the site when the accident occurred," added Verma.

MHADA officials said that they will soon carry out repair work for the building. "This is an old structure supported by wooden beams. The beams had been corroded and this caused the accident. We have evacuated the building and will carry on a detailed inspection of the place after which we will carry on the repair work of the building," said a MHADA engineer present at the side on condition of anonymity.

Heading: Two years on, MC finally decides on the design of indoor stadium’s ceiling - Indian Express
Content: A Co-operative Credit Society was robbed on Monday afternoon by four men, in the Andheri pump house area. The incident occurred at 2:30 in the afternoon. The men forced an entry into the office of Datta-Digambar Co-operative Credit Society in Hanjur Nagar. They  tied Rajaram Pawar(43) a collection agent for the society and one Vishnu Dhonde (45) and Sopan Supde (28) . The robbers fled with Rs 1,03,140 in cash. A case of robbery has been registered at the MIDC police station. Senior police inspector Pradeep Sonawane, MIDC police station said, "Even if they were threatened with a knife they could have made some noise as the thieves left."  He added, "Only their hands were tied not their legs. It is surprising they didnt shout as this is a crowded area."

Heading: Woman dies, in-laws booked in dowry case - Indian Express
Content:
Construction work to resume at an escalated cost of around Rs 32 crore, deadline not fixed yet

The Finance and Contract Committee (F&CC) of the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation has finally decided to give approval to a design of the ceiling for the indoor stadium coming up in the city. It took the MC more than two years to finalise the design. Due to the delay, the construction cost of the stadium that was Rs 16 crore in 2006 has shot up to almost double.

Though Senior Deputy Mayor Parveen Bansal said the cost of the project would come to around Rs 25 crore, sources said if the stadium were to be made air-conditioned the expenditure would not be less than Rs 32 crore.

The construction of the stadium had started in January 2003. With an 18-month deadline, it was supposed to be completed by June 2004. The MC's failure to provide the designs to the contractor in time delayed the project and jacked up the cost.

Deepak Singhal, the contractor who has been awarded the work, told Newsline, "I have heard that work on the project will resume soon. From the day I get the drawings, it will take another year to complete the project."

Set to generate revenue from the venture, the MC has planned to build around 70 showrooms within the stadium, which will be auctioned once the project is ready.

The sources said while the work was lying incomplete, a payment of Rs 16 crore, according to the earlier estimate, had already been made to the contractor.

Taking a strict note of the pending project, the vigilance cell of the local bodies department had asked for a status report of the indoor stadium. According to the sources, however, the MC had sent a wrong report, saying more than 70 per cent work was complete, while the actual work done on ground was not more than 50 per cent.

Following this, eight employees were suspended, it is learnt.

The project has got a green signal once again, but with the MC neither fixing any deadline for the completion of the work and nor working out a new estimate, it is not clear yet as to when the stadium will see the light of day.

Heading: Defying V-C order, PAU non-teaching staff to go ahead with today’s rally - Indian Express
Content:
Victim's father says she was starved to death

The Sadar police booked the in-laws of a woman and rounded up her husband on charges of dowry harassment after she died on Tuesday. Her father alleged that Hardeep Kaur died due to starvation as her in-laws did not give her food for many days and burdened her with household work.

The actual cause of her death is not known yet as the police are waiting for the postmortem report.

Hardeep was admitted to

the local Civil Hospital on

Sunday after her father Sadhu Singh brought her from her in-laws' house when she reportedly complained that she was sick and was being denied medical

attention.

A resident of Guru Nanak colony, Sadhu Singh works as a labourer in a local factory. In his statement to the police, he blamed his son-in-law Ravi and his mother Kanta Rani for Hardeep's death.

Sadhu said the accused used to starve her and did not give her any break from the household work. He said Hardeep's husband Ravi sold chana bhaturas and tea on a rehri for a living.

Sadhu said his daughter married Ravi around three years ago, adding that due to his poor economic condition he had taken financial help from his neighbours for the wedding. Ever since, he alleged, her in-laws had been harassing her for dowry.

Hardeep leaves behind her one-and-a-half-year-old son.

Ravi, meanwhile, denied all the allegations and said though he was financial position was not sound he was doing every thing to get medical help for an ailing Hardeep.

Sub Inspector (SI) Mukesh Kumar, in-charge of the Merado police post, said they were looking into the matter. He said no arrest had been made so far.

Heading: ‘Failure to check larvae formation at initial stages spread disease - Indian Express
Content:
Buckling under pressure from the non-teaching employees, Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang withdrew on Tuesday the advisory letter that he had sent to all heads of the departments, asking them to take action against those employees who had participated in a recent rally. The move, however, failed to pacify the PAU Non-Teaching Employees' Union. Defying Dr Kang's orders against holding rallies on the campus, the union has decided to go ahead with its November 5 rally as planned.

The union had a two-point agenda for the protest rally — withdrawal of the advisory letter and the issue of filling the post of Dr Kang's secretary from the teaching cadre. The non-teaching employees claim that this post belonged to the non-teaching cadre.

After almost day-long meetings and brain-storming sessions, the union decided not to cancel the rally, saying though the letter had been withdrawn the issue pertaining to the appointment of a secretary from their cadre had not been addressed yet.

Union president Harbans Singh Mundi said: "Only one thing can defer our rally and that is if the V-C announces a new name from the non-teaching cadre for the secretary's post on Wednesday morning." The rally is scheduled to start around 1 pm.

Mundi claimed: "Dr Kang had told us earlier that he had to make this appointment very suddenly as he needed a secretary after the former incumbent was transferred two months ago. He has been assuring us that this post will be reverted back to our cadre soon. He had promised to appoint a new secretary in 15 days' time. It has been two months now and all we have got from him so far are assurances. We want action now."

Heading: Students protest fee hike at GNGC - Indian Express
Content:
'Dengue attack: National health team chief says fogging alone is not the solution, more awareness required

The national health team visiting the city in the wake of the spread of dengue in the district blamed it on the failure of the authorities to reduce the source of Aedes aegypti mosquito in the initial stages when the disease was setting in.

Giving details about the observations made so far during the visit, Dr Kalpana Barua, deputy director of the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, said fogging alone could not be taken as the only solution to contain the disease.

Speaking to Newsline, the expert in vector-borne diseases said: "Fogging is conducted on the roads while mosquitoes breed in areas in and around human habitats. And notably, the mosquito develops in small water containers and therefore the lack of awareness among the people is also to blame. Besides, the source of the mosquito may develop even a few days after fogging."

Dr Barua added that the authorities could not effectively put in place the disease management expertise in 'source reduction'. "The Municipal Corporation has minimal staff of four inspectors and 20-odd other workers to cover such a large city," observed Dr Barua, who visited the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) on Tuesday. The hospital has registered the maximum number of patients (nearly 2,000) so far.

Headed by Dr Barua, the national health team is on a three to four-day visit to Ludhiana and has been visiting various areas across the city, besides hospitals, to check the reasons of the formation of the larvae. Dr Barua will submit her observations and analysis of the data collected from here to the Ministry of Health, Government of India.

She said the civic authorities had been lacking in eliminating certain factors that led to larvae formation. "The health department should have also spread community awareness, one of the factors that has been lacking. But it is also difficult in such a large city to visit each and every household, where people are not doing anything to save themselves from the disease."

Dr Barua also observed that though the civil hospital had been marked as a sentinel surveillance hospital, there should have been efforts to keep track of the disease to ensure non-transmission of the disease.

Heading: PAU sex scandal: Brar refuses to record statement, again - Indian Express
Content:
College extracting money in the name of 'extra fees', allege students

Students of Guru Nanak Girls College protested today in the college campus alleging unreasonable hike in the last installment of fees.

Fearing the news of protests would spread, the students were allegedly confined into college premises later and were not allowed to leave as the college gate was locked.

For over two hours, the college authorities tried to hush up the matter and did not let the students leave the college premises or allow those standing outside to enter the college. Many students complained they had been waiting for over an hour but the college authorities did not open the gate for them though they had to attend lectures.

Students alleged the college management has demanded extra charges in the second installment of fees on various pretexts including parking fee and library fee and various 'extra fees' to recover the costs of building of the auditorium constructed recently.

A student of BA final year, requesting anonymity, said, "We were protesting against the fee hike but they locked us inside the college premises and classrooms and did not allow us to leave the premises for over an hour."

She added,"The college used to charge Rs 360 per scooter or moped earlier but they have increased it to Rs 540 now. Apart from this, we have been asked to pay many other charges for which the only reason they have given is 'extra fee'."

"Earlier, we knew that we were supposed to pay Rs 3,500 as the second installment of fee but now we have learnt that the second installment will be Rs 7,000. Besides, they are charging us separately for practicals," complained another student of BA final year.

A female journalist of a Hindi newspaper, who entered the campus, was also rashly pushed out by the gatekeepers at the college gate.

When questioned on the whole matter, the principal of the college refused to comment while the president of the college management, Gurbir Singh, said he nobody was locked inside the college. "Students were not locked inside the college and the fee that the students have been asked to pay is as per the university guidelines. The fee structure is higher than expected in some courses and the principal can give concessions on certain conditions in that case," he said.

Heading: Colonisers thank CM for planned - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Agricultural University seems to be grappling with the inquiry into the sexual harassment case, which began almost a month-and-a-half back, with Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, director, student welfare, refusing to record his statement with the committee for the second time.

While in his first appearance before the committee Dr Brar had registered his refusal in person, this time he has sent a letter. This meeting, it has been learnt, was scheduled for November 3 and had to be postponed after Dr Brar refused to come for the meeting.

A member of Dr Brar's family, who did not wish to be named, said,"Dr Brar was not in town when he was called for the meeting. He was not informed about the date. He however received the letter today and has sent back his reply saying that till the time he is given all the relevant documents that he has demanded, he will not record his statement."

Dr Brar had asked for the copy of the original complaint made by the complainant with her signatures.

"The first time we asked for the copy of the complaint, a computer print out with no signatures was handed out to us and the same thing has been sent to us second time too," the family member said.

When contacted, dean, college of home science, Dr Neelam Grewal, who is enquiring the matter, said, "I have not seen Dr Brar's reply." When asked as to how does the university plan to break this dead lock, Dr Grewal said, "I have discussed the issue with the V-C and we are working out the way." The committee has already recorded the statement of the complainant and her witnesses.

Heading: ‘We need to review question of freedom for women’ - Indian Express
Content:
Colonisers and Property Dealers' Association, Punjab, has thanked the Chief Minister for announcing setting-up of a new sub-registrar office in Ludhiana. The members also thanked the CM for allowing PSEB to given connections in the unapproved colonies for the time being.

Kultar Singh Jogi, president and Jatinder Pal Saluja, general secretary of the association, said that these demands were presented before the CM in the sangat darshan programmes. This will reduce the rush at other sub-registrar offices, added Saluja.

Heading: Agri varsity, Merado to develop farm machinery - Indian Express
Content:
A one day UGC-sponsored national seminar on 'Indian women writers: A feminine perspective' was organised by the English department of Khalsa College for Women, Civil Lines here today.

Dr Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU, inaugurated the seminar.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Kang said that the status of women all over the world, particularly in India, has been undergoing a rapid change in the recent decades. He named some of feminist novelists and socialists who carved a niche for them, including Arundhati Roy and Anita Desai.

The one-day seminar focussed on the feminine concerns of Indian women writers and the emphasis was on the change which has occurred in the interests of women writers due to the encounter between South-Asian society and the west.

The keynote speaker, Dr N K Ghosh, head, PG department (English), Agra College, said that Indian women writers have made a significant contribution with their depiction for social realities and portrayal of feminine sensibilities.

Dr TS Anand, senior faculty, Guru Nanak Dev Engineering College, spoke on issues in Indian diasporic writing after 9/11, in special context with Chitra Banerji, Divakaruni and Kiran Desai. Dr Rupinder Kaur, head, English department, Punjabi University, stressed the question of freedom for women should be reviewed.

Heading: Centuries-old wada collapses on residents, five injured - Indian Express
Content:
DAV College, Sector 10 claimed the overall team championship title in men's category with 81 points on the concluding day of the Panjab University Annual Athletics Meet being held at Panjab University grounds.

SGGS College, Sector 26 claimed the second spot with 76.5 points in the same category while JC DAV College, Dasuya grabbed the third spot with 15 points.

In the women's team championship, SGGS Khalsa College, Mahilpur emerged as the winners with 39 points while Khalsa College for Women, Ludhiana grabbed the second spot with 37 points. Guru Nanak Girls College, Ludhiana claimed the third spot with 26 points. Ravinder of DAV College, Chandigarh was declared as the best athlete in the men's category while Navjoban Kaur was declared the best athlete in women's category.

Earlier in the day, Ravinder claimed the gold medal in men's half marathon while Sukhdev Singh of DAV College, Chandigarh claimed the silver medal. Avtar Singh of SGGS College, Chandigarh grabbed the bronze medal. In javelin throw, Bhupinder Singh of SGGS College, Chandigarh claimed the gold medal with a throw of 65.15 meters while Hardeep Singh of GHG Khalsa College, Gurusar Sadhar grabbed the silver medal with a throw of 56.99 meters. Rohit of DAV College, Abohar claimed the bronze medal with a throw of 56.27 meters. In triple jump, Navjot Singh of DAV College, Chandigarh won the gold medal creating a new record with a jump of 15.29 meters. Manoj Kumar of SGGS College, Chandigarh grabbed the silver medal with a jump of 15.25 meters while Harvinder Singh of Panjab University Campus grabbed the bronze medal with a jump of 14.29 meters. In the women's category, Navjoban kaur of GTB Khalsa College for Women, Dasuya claimed the gold medal while Rajdeep kaur of SGGS College, Mahilpur claimed the silver medal. Kulwinder Kaur of SGGS College, Mahilpur grabbed the bronze medal.

In triple jump, Satwant Kaur of SGGS Khalsa College, Mahilpur claimed the gold medal with a jump of 10.70 meters while Shiksha of MCM DAV College, Chandigarh grabbed the silver medal with a jump of 10.15 meters. Talwinder of GGS College, Chandigarh grabbed the bronze medal with a jump of 9.97 meters.

Heading: Crematorium mishap: share blame, civic body tells pollution board - Indian Express
Content:
A nightmare came true for people living in Kasba Peth on Tuesday morning as the third floor of Mote Mangal Karyalaya, a 250-year-old wada, caved in. Five people were injured.

A large number of families lived in the wada. They knew it was so dilapidated it could cave in any day. They had, in fact, been served several notices to leave but could not do so because they could not afford accommodation elsewhere.

The city has around 18,000 wadas, most of them very old, particularly those in Shaniwar Peth, Budhwar Peth, Kasba Peth, Bhavani Peth, Narayan Peth and Ganj Peth.

"We have been serving notices for demolition of this wada but the occupants did not vacate it," Pune Municipal Corporation ward officer Madhav Jagtap said.

The wada is in the heart of the city, within 100 metres of Shaniwar Wada that is a heritage structure. So, structural changes to the wada cannot be made without the permission of the Union archaeological department, the Pune Municipal Corporation and the landowners. The wada cannot be repaired either as the Mote family, the owners of the wada, are involved in a dispute. In the police complaint Gajanan Dattatray Mote of Budhwar Peth was named as the owner.

The injured belonged to the Satpute and the Potnis families: Nilima Shirish Potnis (35), her husband Shirish Gajanan Potnis (45) and mother-in-law Neela Gajanan Potnis (65), along with Mahesh Dhindiba Satpute (31) and Dhondiba Bhaguji Satpute (70).

"I was in the bathroom when the collapse happened. I heard a loud noise and came out. Initially it was all dust and I could not see anything. My husband and son, who were in the hall, were injured," said Chitra Satpute (65), who lives on the second floor.

Two fire engines and an ambulance were pressed into service. The police admitted the injured to Surya Hospital in Shivajinagar.

"Nearly 45 families lived in constant fear in the 15,000-square-foot wada. The wada was declared a dilapidated structure in the early 1990s and we have been receiving notices from the Pune Municipal Corporation since then. The last notice came around four months ago, asking us to vacate the wada. The 45 families pay rent ranging from Rs 4 to Rs 100. All of us are poor and had to live here knowing it could collapse anytime," said advocate Omkar Arun Deshpande.

Deshpande said Sahukar Dixit, a moneylender during the Peshwa era, built the wada around 250 years ago. Then it was known as Teen Chowky Wada. The wada only had a ground floor then. The Mote family bought it 80 years ago and built the upper floors.

Tenant Sudhir Joshi said, "Three generations of my family have spent their lives in this wada. We requested the Mote family that they demolish the structure and make a new building. But he does not give us permission to repair the wada."

Heading: Who will make the customer pay farm labourers’ PF? - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), while admitting to its shortcomings, has trained guns on the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) for not sharing the responsibility for the accident that killed seven at the biomedical waste disposal plant in Kailash crematorium on September 11.

The MPCB is the licence-issuing authority to the contractor who has been arrested for disposing of aerosol cans illegally on the crematorium premises.

"There has been negligence from the civic staff as the incident took place in an area under the PMC jurisdiction, but the MPCB should also be held accountable as it is the licensing authority and its officers were visiting the plant every month," Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said.

The PMC would take action against its staff, he said, adding the civic administration would also put on record its views on the failure of MPCB to keep a check on the illegal activity carried out by the contractor.

The MPCB, for its part, says it cannot be held responsible. Regional officer of MPCB P K Mirashe said, "The incident took place outside the incinerator and the board officials cannot be held accountable for negligence in the duty as is being alleged by the PMC."

He conceded that there had been illegal activity on the plant premises by the contractor and the board officers visiting the plant every month were unaware of it; this he attributed to lack of information from the PMC.

Asked why the plant was shut down, Mirashe said the contractor was using his employees for illegal activities and had appointed a sub-contractor without taking the approval of MPCB.

"A police complaint has been filed against the contractor and PMC officials for the incident," he said, adding the board would have initiated action against its officer if the incident had taken place in the plant.

Meanwhile, the PMC, with the concurrence of MPCB, has appointed Passco Environment Solutions Limited on a temporary basis for the disposal of biomedical waste at plants in Talegaon and Satara. It has also invited parties to restart the incinerator at the Kailash crematorium.

"We had asked the PMC in September to appoint a new agency within two months for the disposal of biomedical waste in the city. We will assess the progress and based on that we will decide whether to extend the two-month deadline," Mirashe said.

The MPCB, as per a Supreme Court directive, will appoint an agency to monitor biomedical-waste-generating units in the state.

Heading: Mahasabha chief fails to meet blast suspects - Indian Express
Content:
About 3,000 labourers with the Agriculture Produce Market Committee (APMC) are waiting to see if the wholesale customer will shell out money for their provident fund and gratuity aggregating Rs 30 lakh. The levy charged is 30 per cent of the labourers' aggregate salary, which works up to Rs 90 lakh-Rs 1 crore a month.

On Wednesday, it will be known if commission agents have submitted the levy along with the salary of the labourers, done on the fifth of every month. Till September, the security net for the labourers came from farmers, who decided to stop paying last month on the basis of a High Court judgment of 2004. The commissioning agents, who till now used to collect this levy from the farmers, have refused to recover dues from customers as they will not be able to enforce it.

"We have not yet started charging our customers, a difficult task. We want the labourers to recover these dues themselves," said president of APMC commissioning agents, Shivlal Bhosale. He argued that the labourers at the APMC should collect the levy charge from customers on their own.

"Commission agents have been collecting the levy charges from the farmers. After farmers refused to pay it, they were given the liberty to collect it from customers. Why should our labourers collect the dues from the customers? According to our law, the agents have to do it," said Anil Lakaswar, chairman of the Pune Mahtari Mandal Board where salaries of the labourers are deposited.

The APMC is clear on recovering the dues from the commissioning agents. "If they do not pay the levy charges on November 5, we will either revoke the licenses of these agents or recover it via arrears of land revenue (recovery by attaching individual property)," said APMC administrator B J Deshmukh.

"Customers will refuse to pay the levy; then we will have to foot the bill. We are already paying one per cent market cess, which should technically be paid by our customers," said another agent.

Pune APMC will be the second after Ahmednagar to tap the customer for the labourers' security net, for whom the additional cost will not be more than Rs 150 per tonne.

On October 19, the government appointed a committee headed by principal secretary of cooperatives S K Goel, which decided on an interim basis that the consumer would pay the levy to the commission agent, who in turn would deposit it with the board.

Heading: Cong student leader murdered - Indian Express
Content:
Hindu Mahasabha president Hemani Savarkar, who had planned to offer free legal aid to the Malegaon blast suspects, failed to meet them at Nashik court on Monday.

"We were not allowed to meet the suspects. We would soon call a press conference to announce our further course of action," said Savarkar, who is also the national president of Abhinav Bharat.

The state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) has so far arrested eight persons in connection with the blasts, four of them from Pune. Of the four, three have links with Abhinav Bharat - Maj (retd) Ramesh Upadhyay was the working president, Ajay Rahirkar the treasurer while Sameer Kulkarni the organisation's point man in Bhopal. The fourth accused, Rakesh Dhawade, is an arms expert. Investigations have revealed that Pune was the headquarters of Abhinav Bharat.

Savarkar has earlier said that if it was proved that Malegaon blasts was executed by Hindus, she would consider it a reaction to Islamic terrorism. "It is but natural that some Hindus might believe in a 'bomb for bomb' strategy because of the failure of government in tackling Islamic terrorism in Hindustan," she had said.

Heading: PMC mulls octroi on sales tax returns of gold - Indian Express
Content:
A leader of the Congress student wing was murdered in broad daylight on Tuesday. Pravin Pramod Jagdale, Pune vice-president of the National Students' Union of India, was stabbed to death around 4.40 pm at Shirole Vasti near Fergusson College Road.

Jagdale (27) lived at Anand Nagar on Sinhagad road.

The police said he was on his way to Shirole Vasti when he was murdered. He was passing by a vacant plot when six unidentified youths attacked him with sharp weapons. He suffered grievous injuries and died on the spot.

He had been the vice-president of NSUI for four years. He owned a cyber café at Anand Nagar.

Jagdale's family had shifted to Anand Nagar some years ago from Shirole Vasti. According to the police he was on his way to meet a relative in Shirole. The Deccan Gymkhana police have registered a case against six unidentified assailants.

Heading: After twelve years, workers become owners of Garware Nylon - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to increase its revenue in view of the global meltdown, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) is toying with the idea of charging octroi on the sales tax returns of gold. According to the present system, two and a half per cent octroi is charged on the value of gold.

The jewellers are also in favour of this plan and deny any scaling up of gold prices and thus not have any adverse impact on gold buyers.

Municipal commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi on Tuesday held a meeting with jewellers and octroi chief to tap additional sources of income. Later, while talking to media, he said, "In order to enhance PMC's revenue, in the wake of the global economic crisis, we are trying to tap more sources of income. The amount of octroi generation through gold is just Rs 1.5 crore at present. But considering the business in Pune, the octroi collection should ideally touch Rs 8-10 crore, which is not happening due to a number of hitches."

"Hence, we are now planning to levy octroi on the sales tax returns of gold submitted by jewellers. Gold traders should pay money in lieu with the sales tax returns. However, we are just thinking in that direction and nothing has been finalised. Once we draw up a proposal, we will table it before the civic standing committee for approval," he said.

Supporting this move, Fatehchand Ranka of Pune Jewellers Association said, "If it materialises, it will be a very positive move. This kind of system will be beneficial to both- PMC as well as jewellers. Through this system, PMC will be able to generate ten times more revenue than the present practice. This additional money could then be utilised for the development of city." He added that this system would also reduce risks for gold traders.

Civic octroi chief K C Karkar said, "At present, we charge 2.5 per cent octroi on the value of gold. But as per the new consideration, octroi will be charged on the Value Added Tax (Vat) returns of gold sales. This will bring in a lot more transparency and better revenue for PMC."

Apart from the gold items, PMC is also planning to charge the telecom and other public utilities money in the form of royalty for the usage of land for the laying cables. "At present we charge only for excavation for laying cables. Now, we are considering charging money from these utilities for utilising our space."

The PMC is also planning to raise the charges for advertising hoardings within the PMC limits.

Heading: Medihope brings hope to cancer patients - Indian Express
Content:
After over12-year-long struggle, the ex-workers of the Garware Nylon who lost their jobs in 1996, became owners of the company's land by paying the last installment of Rs 92 lakhs on Monday.

The cost of the land, after the bid, was Rs 6.01 crore. The bidding was carried out after high court directed the workers to get better bidders.

The deadline for the payment was on November 7, but workers decided to make the final payments a few days in advance. This brings an end their struggle of over 12 years after they lost their jobs with the company owing them a lot of money in gratuity.

Out of the 1,200 workers who lost their jobs, around 210 came together under the Common People's Front to bid for the land.

It happened in February, when workers found out that the land was being sold to businessmen for a paltry price of Rs 2.35 crore - this was below the reserve price of Rs 5 crore for the nine acres. When workers protested, the court asked them to get better bidders. This was when they decided to bid themselves.

For many of these workers, raising the bidding amount meant mortgaging a lot of their belongings. However, owing a stake in the company was as much an emotional decision as it was a financial one. Workers expect the company unit to start earning money as soon as they start leasing out the built up office space in the 9-acre land.

Heading: Two new awards introduced in Pulotsav - Indian Express
Content:
