Medihope-a product from city-based Ayurvedic medicine manufacturer Ram Katkar — brings hope to those suffering from the excruciating side effects that come with chemotherapy, treatment for the noxious disease of cancer. After receiving patents from the central government last year, the company, Hope Ayurvedic Medicine Pvt Ltd, has now registered in 108 other countries for patenting the product as a special Ayurvedic medicine.

According to Katkar, chief executive officer, Hope Ayurvedic Medicine, Medihope will reduce the side effects of chemotherapy, in which anti-cancer (cytotoxic) drugs are used to destroy cancer cells during the course of treatment. "After getting the patents last year, we had to wait for another year for the rains to come. The herbs used in the medicine grow only after monsoon; so now have now got all our required raw material," Katkar said.

An engineer by profession, working in government services, Katkar took a five-year break from his profession to develop this medicine. "When I discovered this formula, I wanted to use it for the benefit of the common man," he said.

Having researched on the medicine for more than a decade, Katkar said, "The medicine was developed after several lab tests and over 3,000 trials. Medihope is effective on the body in just two to four days. If supplemented with cancer drugs, it expedites recovery. The course of treatment depends on the type and severity of cancer and the cost would be around Rs 4000-7000."

"Unlike the metallic Bashm, the key ingredients, Saptrangi and Tantani, being extracts of leaves, are completely herbal. Medihope is not a cure for cancer, but an effective medication that helps reduce the side effects of various radiation therapies used in cancer treatment," said Katkar, adding, "Medihope helps heal blood-related disorders and prevent nausea, weakness and depression. Along with general health, urine problems and other blood-related disorders like anemia, that is largely found in women, it also helps in curing diabetic wounds, which if not treated, can get gangrenous," said 48-year-old Katkar, an alumni of Walchand College, Sangli. Medihope will be launched in the market in early 2009 and the company will have offices in Mumbai, Delhi and Ahmedabad, with their head office in Pune, Katkar said.

Heading: ISRO to launch remote sensing, information portal by 2009 - Indian Express
Content:
PulotsaV, the 13-day cultural extravaganza that begins on Saturday will mark the introduction of two new awards –Pu La Krutadnyata Sanman for outstanding social work and Pu la Jeevan Gaurav Sanman for veteran artists. This year, Dr Prakash and Dr Mandakini Amte, will receive the Pu La Krutadnyata Sanman for their work in Gadchiroli and Bhamragad, while veteran actress Sulochana Didi, who recently celebrated her 80th birthday, will receive the Jeevan Gaurav Sanman.

"Pu La and Sunitatai have always been generous in doing charity without publicity. The Pu La Krutadnyata award is a way of acknowledging their gesture," said Virendra Chitrav, secretary of Aashay Sanskrutik –the organisers of the festival. The award consists of memento, citation and Rs 25,000 cash. Aparna Velankar will hold an open interview of the Amte couple after the award presentation on November 18 at Yashwantrao Chavan auditorium at 5 pm. There will also be an open interview of Sulochana Didi by Sudhir Gadgil after honouring her with Pu La Jeevan Gaurav Sanman on November 19 at 5 pm in the venue.

This year, film director Vijaya Mehta will be awarded the Pu La Smruti Sanman consisting of a citation, memento and Rs one lakh cash prize. The award presentations on November 08 followed by her open interview by journalist and author Ambarish Mishra and actor Neena Kulkarni. A major attraction of this festival will be screening of original recordings of three plays directed by Vijaya Mehta viz. Shakuntal, Wada Chirebandi and Hamidabai ki Kothi.

Other than that, Pu La Sparsh, where veteran theatre personalities, littérateurs and artists will share their experiences about Pu La and revive his contributions to the art field. An interview with leading radio jockeys in the city is also an added feature of this year's Pulotsav.

The annual feature –Paalvi, where young talent is given a chance to participate is being turned into a competition from this year.

Hence, the 10 nominated participants from various cities in Maharashtra will compete with each other in classical singing and three winners will perform on November 12. Also, the Pu La Tarunai Sanman, where audience vote and decide the winners from nominated participants, will take place on November 20. Pulotsav will be concluded at Yashwantrao Chavan auditorium with a performance by winners of the Pu La Tarunai Sanman.

Organised by Aashay Sanskrutik and Paranjpe Schemes, Kirloskar Proprieties and Lagu Bandhu, the festival will be inaugurated by veteran poet Vinda Karandikar.

Other than documentaries, films and drama, the festival will also have book exhibition, painting exhibition. Pulotsav be held at National Film Archive of India (NFAI), Yashwantrao Chavan Natyagruha and Pathfinder.

Heading: Economic slump hits Gujarat hard - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) will launch an IRS (Indian Remote Sensing) image portal called "Bhuvan" and an information portal called "Bhu Sampada" by March 2009. The "Bhuvan" portal is expected to be more powerful and efficient than the popular "Google Earth."

This was announced by ISRO Chairman G Madhavan Nair while delivering the Todar Mul Lecture on "Benefits of Space to the Society," organised at the inaugural function of the Indian National Cartographic Association (INCA) Congress in Gandhinagar on Tuesday.

Nair said that upon being integrated with application-specific Spatial Decision Support (SDS) tools, these two unique portals would open up a new era of collaborative mapping in the country. "These are not mere image or information browsers, but are the mechanisms for providing satellite images and thematic maps to the user community for the purpose of development planning," he said.

He added that the "present day requirement as well as the trend of meeting multiple information demands at different levels of details, dynamically, and with specific analysis and synthesis capabilities, has prompted ISRO to launch these two portals."

Since the late 1960s, India has achieved enhanced agricultural produce through intensive irrigation, genetically improved crops, use of inorganic fertilisers and chemical pesticides. But, this has also unfortunately led to water logging and salinity in irrigated areas resulting into depleted irrigation efficiency.

"In this context, remote sensing based studies using IRS data has been carried out to arrive at solutions for enhancing the water use and reclamation of degraded lands," Nair said.

He added that about 16 per cent of the country is characterised by wastelands which is not under optimal use. Reclamation of such lands is a must for enhancing agricultural productivity and improving ecology. He further said that mapping and monitoring of wastelands in the entire country has been carried out using satellite sensing data. The Ministry of Rural Development, at whose behest this exercise was carried out, has been using this information for planning and implementing various reclamation activities, he added.

"It has been seen that during 1998 to 2005, about eight million hectares of wastelands have been reclaimed, and the National Wastelands Atlas has brought out the fact that about 35 Mha of wastelands can be reclaimed and made suitable for cultivation, especially agro-horticulture, coarse grains, bio-fuel plantation, among others, with appropriate intervention," Nair said.

He also called for scientific means to manage the natural resources and environment for the future generations, adding that increasing soil erosion is a major concern.

Annually, dwindling groundwater potential, lack of infrastructure, both physical and social, and increased frequency of disasters, are also matters of concern, he said. Therefore, there is an urgent need to reverse the effect of degradation with proper use of appropriate technology, he added.

400 delegates from country and abroad to deliberate at ISRO congress

As many as 400 delegates from India, the US, Australia and Germany will deliberate over Satellite Image Technology and Collaborative Mapping for the next three days at an annual affair of the Indian National Cartographic Association (INCA). It is being hosted this year by the Ahmedabad–based ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC).

ISRO Chairman G Madhavan Nair also elaborated on the role played by Space Technology in societal development. "The use of satellites in communications, in remote sensing, in GIS, in tele-education and in telemedicine should not be underestimated. EDUSAT has created more than 30,000 virtual classrooms while about 300,000 patients have been benefited by use of telemedicine. About 450 Village Resource Centres in 22 states have also become operational," he said.

Nair also enumerated on the role played by space technology in forecasting crop production, in urban morphology, in remote sensing of gases, in identifying the potential fisheries zone and prospective ground water, in watershed development and in wasteland mapping.

Heading: Loss of money, job causes strife, couple consumes poison - Indian Express
Content:
Three TRAGIC incidents, one common cause: Unemployed youth hangs to death, farmer, couple attempt suicide
In debt, crop failure forces couple to attempt suicide

Mounting debt coupled with crop failure led a young farmer couple in Amreli district to attempt suicide. The couple from Lakhapadar village in Chalala taluka were admitted to the Amreli Civil Hospital hours after they consumed pesticide on Monday.

According to the police, Pravin Patolia (35), a cotton grower, had taken a bank loan, which he had calculated to repay through farm income. But total failure of the cotton crop forced the couple to attempt suicide. They consumed the pesticide used for cotton crop when they realised their inability to clear the debt. They could be saved because of timely treatment made available to them after Pravin's brother rushed them to the hospital. Their condition is now stated to be stable.

Chalala police officers said: "Last year, Patolia took a bank loan of Rs 50,000. He had been paying the debt through monthly installments. But it became difficult for him to pay the monthly installments following crop failure this month." They said Patolia even took a loan to build a house.

Cotton crop in Patolia's 5.3 bigha failed following erratic monsoon coupled with pests attack.

Heading: Unemployed youth hangs himself from ceiling fan - Indian Express
Content:
Unemployment, market crash led to extreme step; couple had a petty quarrel over purchase of household item

The recent crash in the share market and months of unemployment forced a couple to consume poison in Bhavnagar in the wee hours of Tuesday. The condition of the Shah couple who are under treatment at the Bhavnagar Civil Hospital, is critical, said sources.

According to preliminary investigation, Paresh Shah (30), who worked at a local studio, had remained jobless for over four months. Shah reportedly also lost money in the recent crash in the share market.

"They consumed DDT," said an official at the Bhavnagar B-Division police station where the case has been registered.

Reportedly, a petty quarrel between Paresh and his wife Puja over the purchase of a household item led the couple to take the extreme step.

"Their condition is said to be critical," said the police.

"According to some reports, Paresh also lost money in the share market following the global slowdown. We are investigating about his investment details," said the police.

Heading: AMC to hold its weekly meeting in China - Indian Express
Content:
A 26-year-old unemployed youth committed suicide by hanging himself with a bed-sheet from the ceiling fan of his house on Monday night.

The Amaraiwadi police have registered a case of accidental death.

The police said Abhishek Chauhan alias Sunny, a resident of Sadguru Apartment in Khokhra, was a graduate and had been unemployed for a long time.

They said he was living along with his widowed mother and younger brother.

His mother works as a nurse at the V S Hospital in Ellisbridge area.

Head constable Balwansinh Bhavansinh, who is investigating the case, said the incident occurred in the evening when Abhishek was alone at home. The body was found by his brother who returned home at night.

Balwansinh said: "Abhishek's family has said that he was disturbed for the past many days as he was not getting a job."

The police have not recovered any suicide note so far.

Heading: Struggling model ties knot with lifer, hopes for his early release - Indian Express
Content:
The municipal corporation standing committee will hold its next meeting on Thursday in the distant land of Nanjing, China, where its members have gone to attend the World Urban Forum (WUF) conference.

The WUF conference, which started on November 3, will continue till November 6 with its focus on urban issues. It is being sponsored by HUDCO. The standing committee meeting, on the other hand, will take up routine issues. The objective is to meet the statutory compulsion of holding a meeting every week without failure.

Criticising the venue for holding the meet, senior Congress councillor Liyaqat Ghori said in an acidic tone: "The members want to give the impression that they are so concerned about the welfare of the city that they have not forgotten its residents even in a foreign land." He said the timing of the meeting could have been adjusted so as to convene it before going to China or after returning from there.

He said the decision to hold the meeting in China was an attempt to gain cheap publicity. "It will be worthwhile if the visit reflects in some meaningful study made during the World Urban Forum," he said. The committee members will return on November 9 after visiting Shanghai.

Apart from committee chairman Asit Vora and ruling BJP leader in the AMC, Dr Kamlesh Patel, some Congress members of the committee are also in China apart from the regular members and deputy commissioners M S Patel and Capt. Dilipkumar Mahajan. AMC Congress leader Surendra Baxi defended the move saying that in the past, the then committee chairman Jayantilal Parmar had held a committee meeting in the US.

"There is nothing wrong if the cost of the visit is borne by a third party, other than the AMC and the participants," he said.

HUDCO is learnt to have sponsored the meeting as part of its programme to build the capacity of the councilors in running the daily affairs of the municipal corporation.

Heading: One dies, two injured in a freak accident - Indian Express
Content:
Locals say the marriage was planned to increase her clout in the chawl and nearby area

"Partners in crime" — Bonnie and Clyde were names synonymous with this phrase. Adding a new flavour to the legendary romance of this notorious couple, Mushtak Alam Parmar (35), a convict with a lifer and Mehjabeen (22), a small-time model, tied the knot on October 31 in Ahmedabad.

Coming from an economically weak background, Mehjabeen took to small-time modelling after working in a beauty parlour for sometime. With a retired father who was serving in the Railways and a mother who is now working as a social worker, Mehjabeen also acted in some low-grade films in order to become famous.

Apparently, Mehjabeen met Mushtak when he was a guest at her home with a few other BJP candidates. He met her again a couple of times and proposed marriage and the couple tied the knot a year later.

Mehjabeen affirms to have met him secretly before marriage and also whenever he was on medical examination at the Civil Hospital or when she was allowed to meet him in jail.

She said her three-day marriage event was wonderful. "We were together all the time, but couldn't go out much as we were surrounded by the police."

The marriage took place at the Shah Abbas Masjid in Jamalpur with great pomp and show and a large number of family and friends visited them. The marriage was conducted amidst heavy police security, though.

According to residents of Chote Lal ki chali, where Mehjabeen has a large number of houses, the marriage was planned to increase her clout in the chawl and the nearby area. A few residents said the family is a nuisance as Mehjabeen's brother has often been found to indulge in violent incidents in a state of drunkenness. Besides, several strange people visited her at late hours and when the people objected to this, her brother troubled them, they said.

Incidentally, only last month, Mehjabeen was reportedly charged with injuring a man in her chawl. Overlooking the charges and allegations of her neighbours, Mehjabeen is now looking forward to her newly married life with Mushtak. She has dreams of having a perfect family and a cosy home with her husband.

"I am not afraid of anything. Whether he stays in jail for the next four years or 10, I will wait for him. I like him and that is why I got married. I knew everything about him and he also never hid anything from me. He supports me mentally and financially. I have no issues that he is in jail. I am confident about the success of our marriage," she told Newsline.

Incidentally, Mushtak, a convict with a lifer, is lodged in the Vadodara Central Jail, where he is serving his term since 1992.

Mehjabeen is now working hard for her career and also taking rounds of the court to shorten Mushtak's term. She said: "We have appealed to the High Court. There are four more years left for his penalty. But I am positive about him getting released soon."

Heading: RMC’s re-plantation project succeeds; trees have sprouts - Indian Express
Content:
Two cars collide when a boy mistakenly releases the ignition lock, minor arrested

The Rajkot city police on Tuesday arrested a minor boy for allegedly killing a man and injuring two other persons in a reckless driving case. The 16-year-old boy's attempt to play the music player in his uncle's Scorpio car turned into a freak tragic accident.

The boy accidentally unlocked the steering wheel of the MUV leading to its collision with another car parked nearby which in turn hit Feroz Savan (28) and two other bystanders on Monday afternoon. Feroz later succumbed to his injuries at the Rajkot Civil Hospital.

Bhaktinagar police produced the accused, a Class VIII student of V V Virani High School, in the juvenile court, today. A case of murder through reckless and negligent driving has been registered against the boy, a resident of Babariya Colony. The boy's father Kumuddin is a retail scrap dealer.

"A case under Section 304(a) of the IPC and Section 3 Article 181, 184, 134 and 177 of the Motor Vehicle Act has been registered against the boy," said the police.

Rajkot Police Commissioner Sudhir Sinha said there was some discrepancy about boy's age. "But from his school certificate we have found that he is 16 years old," Sinha said.

According to the police, the accused, who wanted to play the music player, inserted the key into the steering wheel of the car and instead of turning it once, turned it thrice, releasing the ignition lock.

The accused also applied pressure on the accelerator leading to the collision of the MUV with another parked van. The victims who were standing nearby were hit by the van.

The police investigation revealed that the accused took the keys on his own and got into the MUV. Investigation also revealed that the boy had never learnt to drive a four-wheeler.

The Scorpio belonged to the boy's maternal uncle, a resident of Mumbai, who had come to visit the family during vacation.

Heading: Rape and murder: find the culprit or resign, Patels tell Kundaria - Indian Express
Content:
The experiment by the Rajkot Municipal Corporation to re-plant more than 350 trees, which will be shifted from the 150 feet Ring Road, to construct the city's first flyover, has received tremendous success. More than 24 trees, which were re-planted by the Corporation's Garden Department at the D H College campus, have developed new sprouts. The trees were planted on the Ring Road some 10 years ago and the RMC decided to transplant them rather than chop them.

The Corporation received several offers and finally awarded the contract to a local contractor for transplanting trees at a cost of Rs 1,500 apiece under its own supervision and technical guidance.

RMC Garden Superintendent Dr K D Hapaliya said: "This was my first experience to transplant more than 350 trees from one location to another. For experiment, we uprooted around 24 trees and replanted them at the D H College campus and surprisingly, we received very good results. As per my knowledge, this project must be the first in the state in which a government body is transplanting trees in such huge numbers. We are taking personal interest in the supervision of each tree here."

He said the entire staff of the Garden Department is busy in this activity. "Till now we have shifted more than 175 trees to a new location. Fortunately, the D H College ground has black cotton soil, which is very good for re-planting trees," he said, adding that every tree requires more than 500 litres of water initially.

He added that in order to save the uprooted trees from fungus and other infections, they are spraying a mixture of blue copper to act as a fungicide and growth hormones to the roots, so that the trees are protected from infection, and grows faster at the replanted place.

After this successful experiment, many local residents as well as other municipal corporation have also started approaching the RMC Garden Department to take guidance for their re-plantation projects.

"Our aim is to educate the people with this new technique and it has been very successful as many local residents who want to expand their property, but are facing problems because of trees, have started calling us for help," he said.

He said their project will take many weeks to complete because each tree requires personal care during uprooting and re-plantation.

Heading: Land dispute leads to murder of two brothers - Indian Express
Content:
Community leaders give 48-hr ultimatum to BJP MLA

The rape and murder case of a mentally challenged girl in Tankara taluka has taken a political turn after the Patels, traditionally staunch supporters of the BJP in Saurashtra, started agitation against its party legislator Mohan Kundaria following the administration's failure in the case.

A 19-year-old mentally unstable Patel girl was allegedly raped and murdered at Sajjanpar by an unidentified person.

The girl's body was found from the outskirts of the village. The inability of the police to find and arrest the culprit even 20 days after the incident, has irked the local Patel community.

Agitating under the banner of the Umiya Sena, the Patels have demanded either the arrest of the culprit or the resignation of Kundaria.

Kundaria has been the MLA of Paddhari-Tankara for four consecutive terms.

The Patels from the area assembled at Tankara on Monday and gave a 48-hour ultimatum to Kundaria.

Dhiru Bhimani, a leader of Umiya Sena, said: "The people of Tankara would want Kundaria to resign as the police have failed to arrest the culprit of a crime of such a heinous nature even after 20 days. It's a case of utter inaction on the part of the local administration."

Addressing a gathering of over 1,000 people at Takara, Bhimani said: "We have given a 48-hour ultimatum. The agitation will be intensified if the culprit is not arrested by then."

The agitation has refreshed the memory of the Chandni rape and murder case. A minor Koli girl from Rajkot was raped and murdered at the Datar Hill in Junagadh in 2007.

The incident had led a widespread protest by the Kolis against the Narendra Modi government and had created a division among the Koli leaders of the region on party lines.

Heading: VHP leader sent to judicial custody - Indian Express
Content:
Two brothers living in Gitanagar slums in the Katargam area, were killed by their cousins over a land dispute on Monday night.

The Katargam police have arrested Kashinath Hingraj Pradhan and Kanaiya Hingraj Pradhan for the murder. The police said the murders were the fallout of a land dispute in their native Sama village in Ganjam district of Orissa.

Bhagirath Karunashankar Pradhan (28) and Shyam Karunashankar Pradhan (22) , both loom workers, were fast asleep when Kashinath and Kanaiya attacked them with knives.

"We kept a watch at the railway station and the bus depot, as we knew that they would try to escape from the city. We arrested them just when they were about to leave the city," said a police officer at the Katargam police station.

Heading: Anti-cervical cancer vaccine launched in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The court of Additional Senior Judicial Magistrate — First Class — in Gandhinagar has sent Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) leader Ashwin Patel to judicial custody after his extended police remand ended on Tuesday. Patel has been arrested by the Gandhinagar police under charges of sedition for sending anti-government SMSes from a mobile phone.

Patel's advocates had submitted a bail application before the court of Justice N G Dave.

The court, however, rejected it on the ground that it is not authorised to hear a bail application for an offence which carries a sentence of life imprisonment.

Advocate Deepak Shukla, the convenor of the legal cell of the VHP, who appeared before the court for Patel, said: "We have submitted the bail application to the Gandhinagar District and Sessions Judge and the hearing for the same will take place on November 6."

Patel's arrest has evoked a lot of anguish among the VHP cadre, which has taken to the streets as a mark of protest.

Heading: Aviation industry sees downturn in corporate bookings - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat welcomed the launch of Gardasil — a vaccine to prevent cervical cancer and other cervical and vaginal diseases —at a function here on Tuesday.

Manufactured and distributed by MSD Pharmaceuticals (India), it is the first vaccine against cervical cancer to be launched in India.

Two years ago, the vaccine was launched in the US, Europe and Australia.

Though no official survey has been carried on the incidences of cervical cancer in the state, vaccinologist Dr Baldev Prajapati and paediatrician Dr Raju Shah of two different medical colleges here said at least four cases of cervical cancer were diagnosed in the state daily.

They said, at present Gardasil is the only vaccine that protects against Human Papillomavirus, which causes cervical cancer, abnormal and pre-cancerous cervical legions, vaginal legions, vulvar legions and genital warts.

According to reports, over 74,000 women die of cervical cancer every year in the country. This is one-fourth of the total cervical cancer deaths in the world. In other words, eight women die of cervical cancer in the country every year, making it the commonest cause of cancer deaths among Indian women.

According to vaccinologist Dr Atul Munshi, at least two cases of cervical cancer are diagnosed every day in Ahmedabad alone. Almost all the cases are in tertiary stage. Seventy to 80 per cent of them die due to the disease, said Dr Munshi.

Dr Prajapati and Dr Shah said the Indian Association of Paediatricians has recommended the use of Gardasil to all eligible girls/ women in the age group of nine to 26 years.

According to Dr Shah, the success rate of the vaccine is as high as 98.5 per cent. He said the vaccine is more effective if given at an early stage. Given in three doses, each dose costs Rs 2,800, said company officials.

Heading: Gujarati Diaspora wants Obama at the White House - Indian Express
Content:
The economic slump has not spared any business and has driven almost every corporate into cost cutting. The aviation industry, which has seen the immediate effect, has now registered a downturn in the number of corporate bookings in the domestic sector.

Executives entitled to travel by flight are now travelling by train after the market crash, as companies are making major efforts in cost cutting.

While the substitution can only work for certain domestic destinations, other long distance travel hasn't seen much of an effect. Moreover, the withdrawal of commission to travel agencies by airlines from November 1 has resulted in major loss of revenue to the agencies.

While all airlines have seen an increase in the fares due to increase in taxes, the airlines have witnessed a sizeable dip in reservations as compared to last year. Airport Manager Suhas Jadhav said: "The fares have shot up significantly this year, because of which people who are entitled to air-travel can now no longer afford it."

While the aviation industry in general has seen a massive downturn in business, Gujarat, which is a price sensitive market, has also seen a dip to the tune of 20-25 per cent in the number of passengers in general.

Corporate bookings have gone down to a sizeable amount as well, said Dena Gochrewal, Travels Head, Green Channel corporate travel agency.

"The corporate bookings have reduced to the tune of 20 per cent. For city-based corporates, travel to Mumbai has been particularly affected as a morning flight can easily be substituted by a night train at one fourth of the cost," she said.

Viraj Broker, proprietor of Suvika Corporate Travel agency, said: "While corporate travel to major destinations has been affected by at least 40 per cent, the loss of revenue for the agencies has been even bigger. It is to the tune of 50 per cent; and especially after all the airlines have decided to withdraw any commission to agencies, the loss is expected to rise."

Gorchewal said: "We are contemplating on increasing the amount we charge per ticket. The Rs 350 that we charge per ticket now, seems to be too high, and Rs 150 will be too little. But we will have to reduce the charge."

Heading: Dalit front to launch campaign from Dec - Indian Express
Content:
Gujaratis, one of the most influential and populous Indian Diaspora groups, remained glued to their television sets watching the United States vote for its next President.

Cutting across the racial barrier, they seem to have made their choice for Democrat candidate Barack Obama.

Praful Nayak, the chief executive management committee of the Association of Indian-Americans of North America told Newsline, "There are around 10 lakh Gujaratis in the US and this time everyone is excited."

Rushikesh Vyas, a Master of Tele-Communication student in Rochester, New York, said: "I have been to several debates here and observed that Democratic Party candidate Barack Obama will take the post of the president. It is not because he is black, but because of his policies and the way he wants to lead the US."

Krishnakant Vakharia, President of the Vishwa Gujarati Samaj said: "As of now, there are around 2 lakh Gujaratis in the US who are eligible to vote for the United States presidential elections, and in some parts of the country they will play the key role."

He added: "Citizens here know very well the policies of the Republican Party candidate John McCain, which are very much similar to those of George Bush. People know what Bush did. They are frustrated after looking at the economic meltdown. After 8 years of Republican Party rule, we need a new party and new policies."

Hitesh Savla, an executive in a financial firm in New Jersey said: "There is a need for a change in the US political wings. I cannot see hope for John McCain this time. It is Barack Obama all over. The way he talks, his polices and his positive attitude has made him everyone's favourite."

"Compared to McCain, Obama better understands the requirements of the Spanish people in the US. Along with the Spanish, Obama also has the support of the African-Americans,"said Vimmi Surti, who recently completed her Bachelor's in English Literature from Albany, New York and returned to Ahmedabad.

"There is no doubt that the US will be re-shaped after Obama takes the post of President," she added.

'Obama will solve issues of racism, meltdown'

"It's not just mine, but everyone's dream to see Barack Obama win. His leadership skills and confidence has attracted everyone. He can change the overall scenario of the state and can take the US to a new level," said Leah Martin, model and singer of New York, who is now at Ahmedabad.

Martin, also the brand ambassador of a fashion garment product of SEWA, added, "Seeing Obama as the first African-American President is a signal of global unity being followed in the US too. The issues of racism, prejudice and economic meltdown will be solved soon after Obama steps into the White House."

Heading: BSP, BJP hold meetings on RS poll candidates - Indian Express
Content:
The National Dalit Front (NDF) comprising three Dalit political outfits, floated to counter the growing influence of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), will soon launch its campaign in Uttar Pradesh by holding series of rallies beginning December.

Udit Raj, the general secretary of the NDF, announced this on Tuesday. The Indian Justice Party headed by Raj is one of the constituents of the NDF. The Ram Vilas Paswan-led Lok Janshakti Party and Ram Das Athwale-led Republican Party of India are the other constituents.

"In December, our national president Ram Vilas Paswan, working president Ramdas Atwale and other leaders will address a Khatik, Balmiki, Paswan rally at Allahabad, Fatehpur and Pratapgarh," Raj said. "In the coming days, several Dalit leaders, who have been associated with Dalit leader Kanshi Ram and Mayawati will join the NDF," he added.

Criticising Mayawati, Raj said the Front will expose her for compromising on the "Bahujan Hitaya" principle which has been changed to "Sarvajan Hitaya" by colluding with "Manuvadi" forces. "Mayawati is no longer working for the poor, downtrodden, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. She is enjoying the fruits of power and working for those who have oppressed of the Dalits," he added.

Reiterating the Front's agenda of forging unity among Dalits, backward castes and tribals in the country, Raj said it will strive to become an alternative platform for the Dalits and the other oppressed sections of the society.

The NDF will work to ensure reservation for Dalits in the private sector and set up a national development authority to ensure that funds allocated for Dalits and tribals are not used for other purposes.

Other demands of the front include setting up of a national judicial service on the lines of IAS/IPS and reservation for Dalits in it.

"The front will uphold the ideology of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. It will also work towards ensuring quality education for Dalits," Raj said.

Heading: Congress seeks Bundelkhand package - Indian Express
Content:
The political scenario in the state is heating up over the selection of candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections. On Tuesday, the ruling Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) held a meeting of its legislators and senior leaders to finalise candidates for the polls.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) too, in a meeting of its elections committee members, authorised state president Ramapati Tripathi to discuss the names of the candidates with the Central leadership.

The probable candidates discussed in the BSP meeting were Dharmveer Ashok, sitting member Veer Singh, Gaya Charan Dinkar and O P Tripathi.

The name of BSP general secretary Akhilesh Das, who was formerly with the Congress, is also doing the rounds in the political circles as the fifth candidate. With its strength in the Assembly, the BSP can outright win 5 seats and with the help of six more MLAs, it can grab the sixth seat too.

The Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress, meanwhile, are yet to meet on the polls issue.

While the SP is likely to field its sitting MPs Amar Singh and Abu Asim Azmi, the party is yet to discuss the third seat with the Congress —whether the SP will transfer its surplus votes to the Congress or the Congress will support its third candidate.

The last date for filing the nominations is November 10 and the last date of withdrawal of names is November 14.

The Rajya Sabha members whose term is expiring on November 25 are Rajnath Singh, Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi (both BJP), Amar Singh, Shahid Siddiqui, Abu Asim Azmi, Uday Pratap Singh (all SP), Esam Singh, Veer Singh, Gandhi Azad (all BSP) and Akhilesh Das (Congress). However, the seats of Esam Singh and Akhilesh Das had been vacated.

Heading: Killer weed spreads to Bijnor, six children die, three critical - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) has demanded a special relief package for people of the Bundelkhand region.

On Tuesday, state party president Rita Bahuguna Joshi met Union minister for Agriculture Sharad Pawar in Delhi and requested him to approve the package. The UPCC delegation, including Congress leader in legislative council Ranjit Singh Judev and member of legislative Assembly Vivek Singh, was assured that the package was ready and awaiting the Cabinet nod.

In a letter to Pawar, Joshi wrote: "Needless to impress upon you that the situation is becoming embarrassing for the Congress Party in UP, which is spearheading the movement for adequate relief package for Bundelkhand region. Though, it is already late, further delay would aggravate the miseries and sufferings of people of Bundelkhand."

The leaders of UPCC had met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in January and submitted a memorandum informing him about the poor condition of the people in Bundelkhand due to drought.

Talking to The Indian Express from Delhi, Joshi said: "The situation is obviously embarrassing because Bundelkhand is spread in Madhya Pradesh as well. They have got the relief package a long time ago. But the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh is still waiting for it."

When asked why the UPCC was demanding something which Chief Minister Mayawati has been demanding for a long time, she said: "We have been demanding the package since Rahul Gandhi visited the Bundelkhand region last year. Our first demand to the Prime Minister was made in January. After that we have met him at least thrice and the Union Minister for Agriculture six times."

"We are certainly not speaking on the lines of Mayawati as she had demanded a package for the entire state," the UPCC president added.

Heading: Kanpur V-C who stopped Rahul from holding meet quits - Indian Express
Content:
Exactly a month after the poisonous weed Cassia occidentalis or Kasaundi claimed lives of two children in Saharanpur and left seven other ill, the weed has started spreading itself in adjoining districts.

In Bijnor, six children have died in the last three days and the condition of three others is critical. Some of the affected areas are Chandpur, Ganj and rural areas in the Kotwali block. Nine cases have already been reported in Saharanpur in last 15 days.

Bijnor-based Dr Vipin M Vashistha, who is conducting research on the weed for the last few years, said: "All reported patients are in the age group of 2 to 6 years and majority are between 3 and 4 . The cases have seen a sudden increase in the last three or four days and we are still trying to find out the reason."

He added: "Due to the sudden fall in temperature, children have started roaming around in fields during daytime and might have consumed the weed."

Dr Vashista, also a member of the Indian Pediatrics Association, said: "Mortality rate of the reported cases has shot up to 70 per cent. I have put the district authorities on alert and asked them to take immediate steps."  District Immunisation Officer of Bijnor, Dr Brij Bhushan, said: "We have put all our community health centres and primary health centres on alert. They have been asked to immediately report the cases because right treatment at right time can save the lives of affected children."

He added, "We have also asked the centres to destroy the weed in areas from where the cases are reported."

Saharanpur administration has devised a unique way to curb the disease. District Immunisation officer Dr O P Singh said: "Following the inability of the Health department to remove the wild weed, we have motivated gram pradhans of a few villages to take up destruction of the weed as a social work."

He added: "Some gram pradhans have ensured that the weed will be removed from their villages and villagers made aware of its effects. We are planning to implement it in other villages as well."

Heading: Delhi Police in Azamgarh to quiz blast suspect kin - Indian Express
Content:
The vice-chancellor (V-C) of a Kanpur university, who had prevented Congress leader Rahul Gandhi from holding a meeting in the unversity premises, resigned on Tuesday. Governor T V Rajeswar has accepted his resignation.

V K Suri, the V-C of the Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology, had hit the headlines when he denied permission to Gandhi to hold the meeting in the university's auditorium in October. He was scheduled to address the students of the university. At the last moment, Suri cancelled the meeting citing security reasons. The governor, apparently miffed over the treatment meted out to the Congress leader did not participate in the university's convocation ceremony scheduled for the same evening. He was the chief guest.

The governor had sought explanation from Suri for not permitting Gandhi to address the students. The V-C, in his reply, had said the university authorities had not granted any formal permission to Gandhi to hold the meeting.

The Raj Bhawan had said Suri had cancelled Gandhi's meeting under pressure from the UP government. The Mayawati government had denied the charge, saying the state had nothing to do with the matter as it was an issue between the university and the Congress. The governor has ordered the registrar of the university to assume charge till a new V-C is appointed.

Heading: Monkey business on as forest dept lacks infrastructure - Indian Express
Content:
A Crime Branch team of the Delhi Police reached Azamgarh on Tuesday to record statements of the relatives of the serial blast accused.

The team will interrogate the relatives on Wednesday in the Sanjarpur and Saraimeer area of Azamgarh.

Fourteen people belonging to the area have been identified as accused in the Delhi blasts. Of these, two were killed in the Batla House encounter in Jamia Nagar.

Till date, while six have been arrested, the rest are absconding.

Heading: Smart carts to replace vegetable thelas soon - Indian Express
Content:
Owing to the lack of infrastructure, the state forest department has been unable to control the monkey menace in the city.

Divisional Forest Officer (Lucknow) Ashok Mishra said: "Despite receiving 162 complaints of monkey menace on Monday, our officials could not catch a single monkey. Instead, they used langurs to scare them off, as we do not have the required infrastructure to control monkeys."

The department has now asked the Lucknow Municipal Corporation to provide animal catching vans and staff to control the menace.

The department is also clueless about the rehabilitation of monkeys. "Even if we catch monkeys, where will we keep them? There are no rehabilitation centres in the city," Mishra said. The civic body's plan to construct a rehabilitation centre near Amausi has already missed the deadline.

"The proposal to construct a rehabilitation centre of mokneys was approved a year ago and it should have been completed by now. However, the deadline has been extended till March next year," said Mayor Dinesh Sharma.

In the absence of monkey catchers, the Forest Department is in talks with monkey catching squad from other cities. "Due to dearth of monkey catchers in Lucknow, we are in talks with teams from Kanpur, and Gurgaon who will work along with the Lucknow team to help us catch monkeys," Mishra said.

At present, the department has only one four-member team to catch monkeys in the city.

Heading: Prime accused in Archana murder case arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government will take the help of the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIM-A) to introduce "hand-held smart vegetable carts" in the state. Lucknow has been identified as the venue for the pilot project. The Rs 49-lakh project is expected to be implemented in nine months.

A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the IIM-A and the Mandi Parishad of the state government will be signed next week in this connection. The project has already been successful in Bihar where Kaushlendra Prasad, an IIM-A topper, has come up with the smart cart system. Prasad and his guide, Professor P K Sinha — Chairman of the Centre of Retailing in IIM-A — will visit the state to sign the MoU.

Under the project, a federation of farmers will be constituted. "These farmers will be asked to divide their agricultural land into two portions. In one part, they can cultivate regular vegetable crops and in the rest, they will grow vegetables according to the specifications of international market," said Rajesh Kumar, Director of Mandi Parishad, the nodal agency which will provide logistic support to the project.

At present, UP exports branded mangoes and potatoes. "But the export is limited to East Asian countries as there are stringent specifications for the European and the US markets. We are trying to grow vegetables and fruits as per their standards and ensure exports to Europe and the US," Kumar added.

The vegetables grown according to the specifications of international market will be made available on these smart hand-held carts. Sold at lower rates, the vegetables at these carts will compete with vegetables sold at stores like Reliance Fresh, Spencers or Big Bazaar.

The project gives a farmer the leverage to carry on with his existing business of selling usual vegetables, but at the same time, get better prices for those grown as per specific standards. The amount of vegetable grown will depend on the demand to ensure constant supply of fresh vegetable.

IIM-A has also chalked out means to meet the cost of the smart carts. The cost of a cart is Rs 45,000. Following Prasad's model, the smart carts will have billboards, each side of which will fetch a minimum of Rs 15,000 from advertisements.

Prasad said: "We have conducted the baseline survey of Lucknow and its surrounding areas."

"We have gathered information like per head consumption, coverage area for a vendor, which vegetable comes from which state and so on. We are now preparing a model based on the data collected," he added.

Heading: Railways to phase out trains from wildlife reserves - Indian Express
Content:
Ending the four-day long hunt, the Uttarakhand Police on Tuesday afternoon arrested the prime accused in Archana Sharma murder case. Ashok Kumar, on the run since the murder was reported on Friday night, was arrested from Nai Tehri under Muni ki Reti police station in Tehri district.

Station Officer Muni ki Reti, Surendra Bhandari said: "We had been trying to trace call details of Ashok. On Tuesday we came to know he was hiding somewhere in Tehri."

Ashok was on the run after allegedly killing Sharma (30), who was working as a junior lab assistant with the State Public Analyst Laboratory (SPAL) in Lucknow. She was found dead in an ashram, Shivnandan Bhawan in Rishikesh on Friday. According to the Uttarakhand Police, she had checked in on Thursday with Ashok, whom she had introduced to the bhawan authorities as her husband.

The postmortem report had confirmed strangulation as the cause of the death. The body had marks of injuries that showed scuffle between the deceased and the assailant before the incident.

Suspecting Ashok to be hiding in Lucknow, a police team from Uttarakhand had reached Lucknow on Sunday and raided his residence in Alambagh but he was not found there. Ashol worked in railway coach and wagon factory as an air-condition assistant.

Tehri SP Mohan Singh Bangyal, said: "Preliminary investigations revealed that illicit relationship between the accused and the victim might have caused the murder. Exact motive for the murder can be known only after interrogation." In 2001, Sharma was married to one Alok Kumar, who had also suspected dubious relationship between his wife and Ashok.

Heading: Missing Lucknow youth found shot dead in Barabanki - Indian Express
Content:
To avoid accidents with animals, the North Eastern Railway (NER) has agreed to phase out trains running at night through Katerniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary and Dudhwa National Park with immediate effect. Besides, speed of the trains passing through the area during the day will be reduced soon at specified points, where maximum animals are sighted.

Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, V K Patnaik said: "Nearly 70 animals, including four tigers and three elephants, have died in the area in the last decade due to train accidents. At present, two trains are operating on the stretch and the NER has agreed to reduce it to one and then finally to zero."

Ner Divisional Railway Manager Ashima Singh said: "We will phase out these trains during night and will reduce speed of trains at certain places from 15 to 30 kilometers."

Heading: Hail UP! - Indian Express
Content:
A Lucknow youth, missing since Monday, was found shot dead in Jehangirabad area of Barabanki on Tuesday. Bike of Shyam Kumar Gupta (21) was recovered from Fatehpur area of the same district. His body bore three bullet injuries, said the police.

Gupta's father is a leading jeweller of Sarrafa market in Alambagh.

Inspector General (IG) Lucknow Zone, A K Jain said the deceased was a former student of the Lucknow University and was last seen with some youths in a car in Barabanki on Monday. The police also recovered photographs of some girls from the deceased.

Enmity with a group of expelled students of the university and dispute related to some girls might be a possible motive of the murder, the IG said.

Jain added Gupta, a resident of Ram Nagar, had left home on his bike on Monday noon and primary investigations have revealed that he regularly visited the university even though he had left his studies last year.

He was close to the former general secretary of the Lucknow University students' union, Vinod Tripathi, who was shot dead in Gomti Nagar a year ago, said the police officer.

Earlier, Gupta had a clash with Tripathi's rival group led by Anil Baba and Pawan Dubey, who were expelled by the university for their involvement in criminal activities, the IG said.   

Residents of the area, where bike of the deceased was recovered, told the police that they had seen him getting into a car leaving the motorcycle on Monday.

Heading: Handy Craft - Indian Express
Content:
An 8-day event dedicated to Uttar Pradesh misses the local crowd while stalls are vending stuff from as far as Jammu & Kashmir

Sponsored by Pragati Paryavaran Sanrakshan Samiti, the eight-day 'UP Mahotsav 2008 is waiting for visitors at Chandrashekhar Azad Park (Gole Market, Mahanagar) in the State capital.

While cash boxes at various stalls are not jingling, the cultural stage is abuzz with activity. "There has been enthusiastic participation in the cultural events from across the State," informs media in charge Vinod Kumar Singh.

The highlight of the third day of the event was a Kavi Sammelan, prior to which Abhishek Tripathi, Shashank Shukla, Pradeep Kumar, Shweta Tiwari adn Anuja Maurya from Barabanki presented a dance programme.

In the poets' meet conducted by Shyam Srivastava 'Rohit', there were recitals by Lavlesh Premi from Allahabad, Shivanshu Patel and Gaurav Maurya from Barabanki.

Apurva Srivastava and Harshita from Lucknow took part in the flower decoration contest.

Fancy dress and painting competitions were other features of the eventful day.

Heading: Another malaria death in state, second in North Dinajpur - Indian Express
Content:
In these times of cash crunch and post-Diwali smog, news about an exhibition-cum-sale may not be welcome...not unless it is about one that offers exotic stuff at throwaway prices.

A stroll to Lalit Kala Akadami's Regional Centre at Aliganj becomes worthy, in this respect. It is venue for 'Purbashree', a festival to showcase handicraft of not only the North-Eastern States but also Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Orissa. The highlight is a range of goods with price tags that are easy on the pocket.

Prices begin at as low as Rs 40 and the discounts make even the higher-priced items a deserving proposition. For example, a bedcover from Bhubaneswar could be yours for as less as Rs 140, while another splendid spread from Rajasthan may seem a tad exorbitant at Rs 620 but becomes a rich acquisition after a chunky discount.

"It's a Shillong government initiative but craftsmen from other States have joined in too," says BC Kalita, manager of the event, being held under the aegis of Development Commissioner (Handicraft) of the Ministry of Textiles.

Temptations include batik art dress material, bamboo and cane furniture, lamps, planters, besides bags, table mats, and decoration objects made of jute and a host of artefacts that amaze as much with their beauty as their price.

From frugal doormats to dressy durries and from sarees to tops representing Varanasi, Shillong

Jewellery from Rajasthan comprises necklaces made of jade, sandstone and other rocks. Trinkets abound at every stall and there are keyrings, hair clips, bangles, rings and belts aplenty to put you in a to-buy-or-buy-more dillemma. Dry flowers, agarbatti, terracotta and leather goods of utility and delight are all there up for grabs.

Artisans from different states manning the different stalls are not quite enthused to see the poor footfall, but hope the prices would attract crowds.

Heading: Funds lying unutilised in civic body’s health department - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another malaria-related death in West Bengal, Swapan Barman (23) died at the North Dinajpur district hospital at 3 am on Tuesday. This is the second malaria death in the district. Barman, a resident of Sherpur, was admitted to the hospital with fever on November 2 and tested positive for falciferum malaria.

Nearly a month ago, a death was reported in the Karamdighi block of the district.

It is, however, alleged that the civic bodies are suppressing the actual number of reported cases.

Chief Medical Health Officer of North Dinajpur, Sudhanshu Shekhar Sahu said: "It is difficult to give a count of malaria cases because most people do not report it to the hospital. They prefer local treatment and only a few, whose condition gets worse, come to the hospital."

He added: "Both the persons who died in the district had reported to the hospital, so we know about it. At present, no other malaria patient is admitted at the hospital."

District Magistrate of North Dinajpur Sukumar Bhattacharya had earlier blamed a few nurses for the spread of malaria.

The nurses were, however, found infected with dengue at Lady Dufferin Hospital in Kolkata and had returned to their homes in north Bengal.

Medical Superintendent of Lady Dufferin Hospital Tanya Mondol confirmed that after the nurses were tested positive for dengue, she had asked them to remain in the hospital for the fear of spreading the virus. Sahu said that some of these nurses had been kept under surveillance.

"Though the nurses came back to north Bengal, many did not return home. We kept track of nearly 25 nurses, who have now recovered and reported to their duties. The recent deaths in the district had nothing to do with dengue because the men died of malaria," said Sahu.

Heading: Hospitals blame KMC for unclean premises - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when city residents are finding it hard to fight vector-borne diseases, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has failed to utilise the fund allocated as health budget for checking the rise of these diseases.

The KMC records show Rs 72.59 crore had been earmarked as health budget for the current financial year, of which around Rs 10 crore is spent on the salary of the health workers, said a senior civic official. Rest of the amount is allocated for the vector-borne disease control programme and polio, leprosy and tuberculosis eradication programme. The eradication programmes are partly funded by the Centre.

Interestingly, the health budget keeps on increasing every year, but even those services which used to be provided earlier have been curtailed.

Earlier, the KMC used to operate some mobile blood test vans, which moved around the city to examine blood samples if a vector-borne case was suspected.

These vans no longer operate. Moreover, malaria clinics often go without doctors and instead laboratory technicians run the clinics.

"At the time of the outbreak, people require at least one clinic that remains open for 24 hours. There was a clinic at the SSKM Hospital that used to operate round-the-clock, but it has been closed down. The option of mobile clinics is also no longer exists. The existing malaria clinics are also not reliable and remain closed most of the time in my ward," said Javed Ahmed Khan, leader of the Opposition.

He added the distribution of medicines in slums is also not satisfactory, as very few people in the Darapara slum area receive medicine, though huge consignment of medicines, worth Rs 60 lakh, have been procured by the civic body for distributing them in slum areas.

"We have not been able to distribute the medicines in all the wards uniformly and could not collect the active data, as we are facing a severe shortage of health workers. Many posts are lying vacant. Moreover, there is no one to supervise the work at the ground level," said a senior health official of the KMC.

The civic body waits for the health department to sanction the required malaria and dengue test kits instead of procuring them by spending a few lakh. "We needed blood-test kits for all the wards under my borough, but we are yet to receive them the kits even after asking for them repeatedly," said Firhad Hakim, chairman, Borough IX.

A senior KMC health official, however, said they do not have the funds to procure blood-test kits. The civic authorities also denied they have enough funds to take all the measures.

Joint Municipal Commissioner Sahidul Islam, on the other hand, said: "We do not have any shortage of funds. We will do everything that is needed to check the outbreak. Whatever has been asked by the health department, we have sanctioned."

Ratna Sur, chairman of Borough 13, meanwhile, said: "We do not have larvicide — 'Pyrithrium' — in our stock. The KMC sent bleaching powder for sprinkling. Our health executives, however, said bleaching powder should be sprinkled during an enteric outbreak, it has nothing to do with vectors."

The civic body has even lagged behind in creating awareness against the diseases.

In November, when the outbreak has taken the worst shape, the KMC has allocated Rs 2 lakh for printing leaflets to spread awareness. That too when the diseases may be on their way out with the coming of winters.

Heading: Cop held for selling ammunition to criminals - Indian Express
Content:
While the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has been issuing notices to leading hospitals in the city to clean up their premises, in a reverse situation of sorts, two hospitals are now blaming the KMC for not taking adequate action to clean up their premises.

LK Ghosh, medical superintendent of NRS Medical College and Hospital, said that in spite of sending letters to the KMC, health officials were yet to visit the hospital premises for spraying mosquito repelents.

"The corporation asked us to clean up stagnant water, which we have done and we have also been spreading bleaching powder within the premises, but the KMC authorities are yet to take any action. We sent them a letter nearly a week ago asking them to start spraying, but we are yet to receive any response from the department," Ghosh said.

At the SSKM Hospital, the situation is not very different. While the bleaching powder is evidently spread all over the hospital, there has been little effort to clean up the accumulated garbage.

Hospital staff allege that the roads are barely swept once a day and most of the members living on the premises make an effort to clean up their own area. They allege that an employee was diagnosed with dengue and was sent to ID Hospital for treatment.

Ashok Ghosh, deputy superintendent, however, said that insufficient staff made it difficult to clean up the premises and the KMC should take more effort to do so. "It is the duty of the civic body to clean up, as we do not have enough people for the purpose. How can the hospital staff be expected to clean up the premises?" he asked.

Heading: Travel agents face uncertainty over transaction fee issue - Indian Express
Content:
A sub-inspector of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has been arrested for allegedly selling ammunition to criminals while he was posted in the armoury section of Nadia Police Headquarters at Krishnagar from 1979 to 1989.

Shankar Chakraborty, who was on general duty and not attached to any particular branch of the CID, was arrested by a team from Bhawani Bhaban on Monday evening.

Chakraborty's involvement came to light after the police arrested two criminals, Surajit Mullick and Asim Das, from Machlandapur in Habra and seized 84 rounds of ammunition from them. During interrogation, the duo confessed that the ammunition was supplied to them by one Madhab Das, who was later arrested from Titagarh.

"During interrogation, Das told the police that Chakraborty used to sell police ammunition to criminals while he was posted in Nadia," said a police officer of South 24 Parganas. "An inquiry has been ordered against Chakraborty. He was transferred to the CID from Cooch Behar four years ago," said Sanjoy Mukherjee, Special IG (CID). —ENS

Heading: ‘US investors keeping a close watch on land acquisition issue’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the Calcutta High Court passed an interim order lifting the status quo on airlines stopping the commission of travel agents, uncertainty and confusion looms large on their fate.

A few weeks ago, travel agents and airlines had discussed the possibility of introducing a transaction fee on the ticket price once the commission system is scrapped.

The transaction fee could range from Rs 350 to Rs 2,500 depending on the cost of the ticket.

"From November 1, four airlines —- Jet Airways, Air India, Kingfisher and Singapore Airlines —- have added transaction fee as a ticket component which will be given to us," said Anil Punjabi, chairperson, Travel Agents Federation of India (Eastern India).

While Air India has already started charging the fee at its counters and website, Kingfisher, Singapore Airlines and Jet Airways have not introduced the new system on their websites yet, Punjabi added.

"Airlines have said that they will keep transaction fee equivalent to travel agents till December 31, 2009. After that, tickets purchased directly from airlines and the ones purchased from travel agents will be of different rates," Punjabi said.

Travel agents fear that the new system might go the US way where agents were forced to keep higher fee, while airlines came up with lower fares on their websites.

"Of the 15 airlines who had decided on the zero per cent commission, only six have agreed to the transaction fee system. We might have to stop selling tickets of a few airlines soon," said Punjabi.

Air France, Northwest Airlines and KLM are some of the airlines that have not agreed to follow the new system.

"There is no system of commission anywhere in the world. We have decided to charge the transaction fee only for 14 months to give some time to travel agents. We cannot do it for ever, as zero commission is a major cost-cutting method for airlines," said an Air India official.

Heading: Govt to upgrade security for VIPs - Indian Express
Content:
United States investors are keeping a close watch on how the West Bengal government deals with the problem of land acquisition for large investment projects in the state.

Speaking at an interactive session organised by the Merchants' Chamber of Commerce, Beth A Pyne, US Consul-General in Kolkata, said that no US firm has yet expressed its desire to leave West Bengal due to land acquisition issues. But she also added that investors would like to see that future investment projects in the state would not be affected by political controversies.

"US businessmen know that West Bengal has a lot to offer. But investors are watching closely that how the state government resolves land acquisition issues for large investment projects," said Pyne.

"In the last few years, the economic policy adopted by the state government has encouraged private investments, which has attracted US investors to the state," she added.

With trade in manufactured goods between India and the US estimated to grow over $50 billion this year, Pyne stressed on the importance of good relations between the US and West Bengal. "Despite the present global economic crisis, the state has a lot of economic potential and the government has shown interest in foreign investments. We would like to work with the state government. With the end of the Cold War era a long time ago, we do not label any government as Communist or non-Communist," Pyne said .

According to the US consul-general, investors believe that services, particularly information technology, banking and financial services, offer opportunities for economic cooperation between the US and West Bengal.

Apart from these sectors, Pyne said US firms would like to work in West Bengal in sectors like infrastructure, especially airport modernisation and port development, power, food processing, chemical industries and biotechnology.

With rising concern over the ongoing financial crisis in the US, Pyne reassured that her government would handle it, though it might take some time.

"The crisis will not be resolved overnight, as it took nearly a decade before we reached this situation. We have recovered from such crisis earlier also, and the present situation is not an exception," said Pyne.

Heading: Seven Salboni blast accused, three in their teens, will be in police custody - Indian Express
Content:
The state government is going to overhaul the entire VIP security system to ensure that incidents like the landmine blast in Salboni on Sunday are not repeated.

The pilot car of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjees's convoy was damaged in the blast. Bhattacharjee, along with Union Minister for Steel, Chemicals and Fertiliser Ram Vilas Paswan and Union Minister of State for Steel Jitin Prasad had gone to Salboni to attend the foundation ceremony of Jindal Group's steel manufacturing unit. Six policemen were injured in the blast.

"The incident has proved that the degree of threat, as well as its reach has increased significantly and we have to act according to that. We have held several meetings and decided that the entire security system has to be upgraded so that this kind of incident does not happen again," Director General of Police (DGP) A B Vohra said on Tuesday. The measures to be introduced include purchasing new mine detectors and other electronic devices.

The DGP, who once again admitted that there was a security lapse on Sunday, said nobody will be spared if found guilty of dereliction of duty.

"I have already said that it was a clear case of security lapse. We have all the equipment to detect such kind of devices. We have suspended three police personnel and if we find anyone else responsible, we will take action against him, regardless of the position he is in," Vohra added. He admitted the police have not yet been able to ascertain which group was behind the incident. "It looks like some Left wing extremist group was behind the explosion. But till the investigation is over, we cannot say anything," the DGP added. Vohra further said he was not sure who was the target of the miscreants. "There were so many people in the convoy. It could have been anybody," he added.

Heading: Decomposed body of student found in coaching centre - Indian Express
Content:
The seven accused, who were allegedly involved in the Salboni blast were produced before the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM), West Midnapore on Tuesday. The CJM, Narendranath Das Gupta, remanded them in police custody for 10 days.

After the explosion, the Salboni police had raided the local hideouts and arrested six persons on Sunday night. Another arrest was made on Monday.

Gopal Karamnga (45), Dipak Pratihar(37), Gautam Patra, Buddhadeb Patra and Eban Murumu were arrested from different villages of Lalgarh in West Midnapore, a stronghold of the Maoists, nearly 35 km from Salboni.

Among the five, three are school students. Another two — Lakhiram Murmu and Sahadeb Mahato — were arrested from a nearby village of Birbhanpur.

Gautam, Buddhadeb and Eban — all aged between 16 to 17 years — are students in Lalgarh. While Buddhadeb is a student of Class VIII, Gautam is a student of Class IX and Eban of Class VII.

Charges of undertaking anti-national activities, possessing illegal explosives and hatching a conspiracy to organise an attack on the convoy of the chief minister have been brought against the seven accused.

Public Prosecutor Ardhendu Saha said all the accused were involved with the CPI-Maoist group and carrying on their activities for a long time. "Except the students, the four others had visited the base of the Maoist camp at Jharkhand," he added.

Lakhiram and Sahadeb were arrested in 2006 for their involvement in a blast allegedly masterminded by the Maoists.

A chargesheet was filed against Lakhiram and Sahadeb, but were released on bail, said the public prosecutor. Dipak Pratihar was also arrested in April by the Lalgarh police but was later released on bail.

Heading: Maoists order private owners not to rent out vehicles to forces - Indian Express
Content:
The decomposed body of Anusree Pal, a student, was found inside a coaching centre in the Kamdohori area of Regent Park on Tuesday morning. The teacher, Kuntal Ghosh Dastidar, who owned the centre, had committed suicide on Sunday.

According to the police, there were strangulation marks on Pal's body. A first-year student of Basanti Devi College, Pal was murdered at least three days ago, said an officer.

The police have recovered Pal's identity card and a letter that points towards Ghosh-Dastidar's involvement in her murder.

Separated from his wife, the police suspect Ghosh-Dastidar was having a romantic relation with the Pal. He could have murdered Pal after she put pressure on him to marry her, said an officer.

On Tuesday, after completing the last rites, when Ghosh-Dastidar's wife came to the coaching centre to collect some articles, she found a foul smell emanating from the building.

She informed the police, who broke open the door and found Pal's body. The police are questioning the relatives of both the deceased.

Heading: Another tiger captured near populated area in Sunderbans - Indian Express
Content:
Maoists have instructed private vehicle owners not to rent out their cars to security forces or the police.

A spokesperson of the CPI (Maoist), Surya, had issued the statement on October 25.

The direction came shortly after the Maoist cadres informed their top party leaders that instead of using government vehicles, security forces are using a large number of private vehicles to carry out sudden raids in villages known to be strongholds of the CPI (Maoist).

This instruction has put the police in trouble because the security forces use several private vehicles to conduct raids in the Maoist-infested blocks in Midnapore West, Bankura and Purulia.

Earlier, cadres belonging to the Peoples' Liberation Guerilla Army (PLGA), military wing of the CPI (Maoist), had blown up a Tata Sumo in Belpahari killing three health department staff, including a doctor.

Seeking an apology for the killings, the Maoist group claimed that its cadres had blown up the vehicle as they had information that policemen were travelling in the car.

"The medical staff boarded the Tata Sumo with dark glasses, making themselves vulnerable. The blast unexpectedly killed them instead of the CRPF or police forces," said the statement issued by Surya.

It added: "The green Tata Sumo with a dark glass and no red-cross symbol affixed bore a striking similarity with the vehicle regularly used by the armed forces."

Refusing to give much importance to the statement, senior state police officers said that Maoists are trying to create panic among the villagers in order to create pressure on the state government to stop a counter-insurgency operations.

Heading: Suit-able Men - Indian Express
Content:
The state Forest department officials captured a tiger from a village outside the big cat's core habitat in Sundarbans on Monday night.

The reason behind the straying of the tiger into the village is yet to be known.

According to the forest officials, the animal will be released into Kendo Islands, a deep core area of the Sunderbans Tiger Reserve.

"We captured the tiger by using a trap cage and bait from Rajat Jubli village in the Gosaba area. We will release it very soon," said West Bengal Principal Chief Conservator of Forests Atanu Raha.

The Forest department officials said the tiger was spotted while it was trying to jump over the nylon net encircling the Sunderbans Tiger Reserve area on Sunday night.

"There are a number of reasons why this particular tiger strayed into the village. It might have developed a taste for the cattle or has become too old to hunt. It may have also strayed in search of a tigress because of the on going mating season," said Raha.

"When the tiger was captured, a tigress was also spotted in the vicinity, but was shooed away by villagers," he added. The Sundarbans, which comprises about 10,000 sq km of marshlands and mangrove forests along the Bay of Bengal coast, is one of the last natural habitats of the big cats.

This is the fourth instance of tiger straying into Gosaba. In October, locals had to chase away a tiger, which had swum across the Bidyadhari river to enter the area. The tiger was spotted while it was dragging a cow from a cowshed of Purba Sonargoaon village. In September, another tiger, which had strayed into Jameshpur village of Gosaba, was captured by the Forest department.

Heading: Hollywood Calling - Indian Express
Content: Alessio Nebiolo was in school when he first heard Isaac Albeniz, the Spanish composer's ever popular "Sevilla". There was something about the modal sound that entranced the Italian. Now, 31, Nebiolo is a classical guitarist who cranks out heady classical pieces with dazzling inventiveness, coupled with a feisty manner. "I had my first concert at the age of 14 and dabbled in rock music as well. But, it was classical music that enthused me more," says Nebiolo, who is based in Switzerland and teaches at the Conservatoire de Musique de Geneve. On Friday evening at Delhi, Nebiolo, with his 34-year-old German guitar, enthralled a mixed audience with Dances from Terpsichore by German composer Michael Praetorius. The India-wide concert "The Guitar Among Centuries" organised by the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, Switzerland, and the Italian Embassy Cultural Centre, saw the feisty Italian play old tunes with feverish excitement. Nebiolo began with a bluesy sonata by Domenico Scarlatti in the first half of the performance and moved to a selection from Etudes and Préludes by self-taught Brazilian composer Heitor Villa-Lobos. The second-half of the performance saw him stirring up a romantic tune Tarantella by Italian composer Mario Castelnuovo Tedesco. But, it was Isaac Albeniz's Sevilla Asturias played with beautiful symmetry that floored the audience. He capped the performance with a shimmering Brazilian sonata in Opus 47 that had shards of folk melody. "It is not a popular South American tune like the samba or tango. It is essentially tribal music composed by Alberto Ginastera," shared Nebiolo, who accentuated the acoustic with a swoop of the string and an occasional thumping.

Heading: Kumble’s job was tougher: Chandra - Indian Express
Content:
When the International Dance Festival 2008 organised by German choreographer Pina Bausch kicks off this month, it will feature just one Indian dancer. Arushi Mudgal (in the picture), 22, daughter of vocalist Madhup Mudgal, will be the first Indian to feature in this prestigious festival's roster. A sociology student, Mudgal switched to a correspondence course in her final year to focus on dance. "I practise almost every waking hour," says Mudgal.

She grew up in the rich cultural atmosphere of Gandharva Mahavidyala, the institute founded by her grandfather Pt Vinay Chandra Maudgalya in 1939. The piece that Bausch wants Mudgal to perform is her self-choreographed Bageshri, a series of pure dance movements that have no literal meaning or narration. "It is a very strenuous piece that requires minute attention to detail as well as stamina and energy," she says, before adding that it was her first choreographed piece, so it's all the more special.

Her performance in the German festival on November 16 will be followed by several performances in India and will culminate with her first visit to Pakistan in December. "Apart from the chance to take Indian culture abroad, foreign performances are also rewarding because all the tickets fly off months before the show. It's a wonderful experience," she says, stressing that Indian traditional culture will always find some admirers among the youth.

Heading: Stop! Plate Group boys practising... - Indian Express
Content:
The statistics notwithstanding, the debate remains interesting. The legendary Indian spin quartet or Anil Kumble — who has had the bigger influence on Indian cricket?

"You can't compare between 200-odds and 600," said Sourav Ganguly the other day.

Today, a member of the quartet, Bhagwat Chandrasekhar, who has 242 wickets in 58 Tests, gave his thumbs up to his junior while saluting him for an outstanding career.

"You can't compare between two generations. But I think Kumble's job was tougher. He had to adapt to two different formats of the game. We didn't have one-dayers during our time and the pressure was less. Nowadays there are so many matches, it's too much stress on the cricketers. Kumble played for 18 years and was a champion in both forms of the game," Chandrasekhar told The Indian Express.

There were lots of similarities between the two. Both of them bowled fastish leg-break, both had to prove their critics wrong time and again. People often said about Chandra that he didn't know what he was bowling. In Kumble's case, it was turn or rather the lack of it.

"At the end of the day it's wickets that matter. His record speaks volumes for his achievement. He is probably India's greatest match-winner. If one can have 900-plus international wickets without turning the ball, so be it." Kumble, incidentally finished with 619 Test and 337 ODI wickets.

During his last press conference in India colours, Kumble said that when he first came on the scene, people said he wouldn't last more than a couple of Tests. As a former player from Karnataka, Chandrasekhar saw Kumble grow up in front of his eyes. What was his initial assessment when he first saw Kumble bowling?
